These Black Friday deals are like music to our ears
Black Friday has finally arrived! And good news: we've spotted some absolutely scorching Black Friday deals to upgrade your music-listening experiences. Prices are crashing hard, and now really is the perfect time to pick up a new set of cans for you or a loved one.
I'm here to help you make the most of this annual super-sale, and have collected a healthy selection of discounts on headphones for everyone — with options for all budgets.
• See all of today's best early Black Friday deals
My favorite deal in the US? It simply has to be the Bose headphones below, which only released in August 2026 but already have a sizeable discount — even in the limited-edition green colorway.
Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen): was $359 now $199 at Amazon
How about another? Well, a close second for me is an offer on the excellent Nothing cans listed below, which are an absolute steal at this lowest-seen price.
Nothing Headphone (a) : was $199 now $109 at Amazon

More Black Friday headphones deals, US
This is a record-low price for the new version of the flagship Bose QuietComfort Headphones — and, yes, the limited-edition greens are in the deal (as is a lovely 'Hazelnut Taupe' finish). These continue the manufacturer's reputation as an industry leader when it comes to sound quality and noise cancellation, while also offering a comfortable fit and all-day battery life. Although they were a harder sell at full price, this massive $160 discount for Black Friday makes them a much better buy if you want some affordable premium over-ear headphones.
Read moreRead less▼
What a deal! I loved these cans at $79, and I adore them for this crazy money. The design is a joy and you also get hearing tests, to tailor the sound — which is unheard of at the level. OK, the 'Energy Slider' may not be to everyone's taste, but the zealous audio sounds just fine without it, and this is their lowest-ever asking fee. Highly recommended for a dollar under 50 bucks.
More info: see my full CMF Headphone Pro review
Read moreRead less▼
An immense (and immensely exciting) deal! These on-ear headphones only arrived in September 2026, but they promptly received a glowing 4.5-star review from my colleague Harry Padoan. He says these new Sony cans "sound superb for the price and the level of comfort genuinely surprised" him — which is all the more reason for this massive 46% saving genuinely surprised me! There are some fun colorways to choose, too. The only thing you can't have here is ANC, but if you're someone who finds that surplus to requirements, you may have found your ideal headphones deal here. Another Sony scorcher of a deal? Yes please!
Read moreRead less▼
The second-generation model has now been revealed, but the original Bose QuietComfort Headphones remain a top choice if you want quality noise-cancelling headphones at a budget price. I've been using a pair for a long time now and rate them highly, while our expert testers also scored them an impressive four stars in our review. You get excellent noise cancellation, top-tier audio quality, and 24 hours of battery life for an all-new lowest-ever price. Note: not all finishes are discounted (Twilight Blue might be my fave of those that are available for this fee). I mean, what a discount, eh?

This isn't quite the cheapest these have been — they hit $399 previously — so we understand if you want to hold for another drop. But it's a great price for the best sound you can get from AirPods. Our AirPods Max 2 reviewer Becky Scarrott has been using them daily since they arrived — and as our Audio Editor, she has a lot of nice headphones she could use…

They're class-leaders for a reason, folks. These flagship Sonys really are the best that the Japanese brand can offer: think supreme comfort, big cosy ear cups and a cocoon of silence ANC. Oh, and a whopping $112 off!
Read moreRead less▼
Still the flagship Bose ANC cans to beat and, I have to say, if you own an Android and you just want noise to be canceled, they're your best bet. This saving is the lowest they've ever been by $20, too, which helps ease that still-significant asking fee. A worthy pair of cans, though, if you can afford them…
Read moreRead less▼

I was hesitant to recommend them regularly in the past due to their steep asking price, but with this deal, I think they're well worth snapping up.
Read moreRead less▼
It seems that Soundcore's over-ears are $10 cheaper than they've ever gone before. Symbolically dropping into double-figures, that makes them seem like a real bargain, especially now that they're half the price of the Pro sibling.
Read moreRead less▼
We raved about the Sennheiser Accentum Plus when we reviewed them a couple years back, talking up their punchy, assertive sound, strong battery life, and quality build. At almost 50% off, this deal almost feels too good to be true too.
Read moreRead less▼
What a saving! They're less than half price, folks! OK, they're a 2020 set of cans (superseded by the Crusher ANC 2, which arrived in August 2023) but if you just want some Skullcandy headphones, this is a discount that's impossible to ignore, especially with their 40-hour battery life and Personal Sound curation in the Skullcandy app.
Read moreRead less▼
The newer set to the Skullcandy Crusher Evo above — and this time, you get active noise cancellation! We gave them a very respectable four stars under intense review back in 2023. And now they're a whopping 50% off?! Black Friday deals really are in a different class. Oh, and several other shades are available at this lowest-seen price, including this 'Primer' taupe finish, 'Hazard' orange, Black and, bizarrely, a shade Skullcandy is calling 'Drab' but is actually a lovely racing green hue.
Read moreRead less▼
A 2026 release date? Check. Glowing 4.5-star review? Indeed. Weren't they a cheaper model to the inaugural, flagship set anyway? Yes, and when we reviewed them, we enthused "Now THAT's how you do a second version". There's ANC, great sound quality, a gloriously off-the-wall aesthetic, great battery life, fantastic on-ear controls and now, a huge 45% off, which makes them the cheapest we've ever seen them sell for. Hurrah!
Read moreRead less▼
Now that their successor has launched, it's perhaps unsurprising to see the Sennheiser Momentum 4 get a juicy discount for Black Friday. These five-star headphones offer spectacular, impactful audio, huge battery life, and a timeless design that we can't get enough of. And at more than 40% off, it feels like the perfect time to snap up some of our favorite wireless headphones that Sennheiser has ever put out.
Read moreRead less▼
Already, Sony, are you sure? Well, if you insist! This updated version of the five-star Sony WH-1000XM4 has only been on the market for two months — we haven't even reviewed them yet — but they're already $100 off. That's a third off the beloved XM4s, plus their more modern trappings.
Read moreRead less▼
These are Sony's cheapest noise cancelling phones, and they're almost half off. They're quite a new pair of headphones, only having launched in September, so a massive discount like this is pretty surprising. We have a full Sony WH-CH730N review if you'd like to know more.
Read moreRead less▼
Who needs wireless? At nearly 60% off, these open-back wired headphones are perfect for audiophiles who don't want to spend loads of money. They're a fair few years old now, and they've been discounted before, but they're a change from the many wireless ANC models you see on sale all the time.
Read moreRead less▼
The new Beats 360 are already $100 off. They've only been on sale for two months now, which is about half as long as Beats was teasing them for. We've yet to review them, but our tester found them incredibly comfortable.
Read moreRead less▼
A 'mere' 15% discount might not sound like much, but on expensive headphones, it's still welcome. The Momentum 5 are Sennheiser's newest premium cans, released in June, and in our Sennheiser Momentum 5 review we sung the praises of the soundstage.
Read moreRead less▼
More Black Friday headphones deals, UK
The best headphones Sony makes, at the best price they've ever been. That's it, peak Black Friday achieved. You don't need me to tell you any more about them — you see them on most people's heads every day! They're fantastic. What you may not know is that until now, they've only ever dropped to £298, so this is £48 cheaper than they've ever been. Highly recommended.
Read moreRead less▼
They may not be Sony's newest flagship model, but the Sony WH-1000XM5 still have an awful lot to offer, with amazing ANC, exciting and punchy audio, an attractive look, and no end of features to play around with in Sony's Sound Connect app. At less than £200, they are an unbeatable value-for-money option.
Read moreRead less▼
Know this, dear reader — I loved these cans at £79, and I adore them for this silly money. The design is a delight and you also get hearing tests, to tailor the sound, which is unheard of at the level! OK, the 'Energy Slider' may not be to your tastes, but the zealous audio sounds just fine without it, and this is a return to their lowest-ever asking fee. Highly recommended for a pound under £50.
More info: see my full CMF Headphone Pro review
Read moreRead less▼
I love the expansive sound signature of the Sony 1000X The Collexion, as well as their incredibly comfortable fit, luxurious looks, and gigantic feature-set. Now, you can net a massive £120 off Sony's most premium wireless headphones ever, making them a must-buy for anyone that wants the ultimate blend of premium sound and design. This is the cheapest they've ever been by some margin, too.
Read moreRead less▼
Double-figure pricing on these reliable over-ears is great, especially because it puts them at the same price point as many tempting rivals. All the color options are reduced, too, so you could get the lovely blue version I use, maybe…
Read moreRead less▼
We're huge fans of the Sennheiser Accentum Plus here at TechRadar, and continue to recommend them regularly, even a fair few years after their release. They offer punchy, assertive audio, plenty of playtime, and a stylish look that already felt like great value for money. So now, at less than £92, it would be impossible for me not to advise you to snap these up!
Read moreRead less▼
I adore the look and feel of these headphones, which sort of have a teardrop-shaped ear cup. I also love this lavender shade, but other options are just as discounted. If you love bass, they could be the pick for you and, while I think the treble is a little undercooked, for this money it's churlish to complain. Oh, and the deal? It's a whopping 50% off! Huge! Need to know more? See our full, in-depth JLab Jbuds Lux ANC review.
Read moreRead less▼
Ooh, what a lovely finish! And these cans are just stunning generally, to be honest. Still the flagship Bose ANC cans to beat — and, if you own an Android and you just want noise to be eliminated, they're still your best bet. Still a relatively significant asking fee, I grant you — but they're so worth it, if you can afford them…
Read moreRead less▼
These are Nothing's inaugural headphones, launched in June 2025. I love the design (this is the set that looks most like cassette tapes over your ears, of Nothing's three options) but they're a little heavy and the audio is a touch compressed against Nothing's more recent releases. That said, the deal is just £8 off their lowest-ever asking fee, so if they drop to £141 again, they're worth that every day of the week — see our full Nothing Headphone (1) review for the full scoop.
Read moreRead less▼
Finally, a set of audiophile-grade wired headphones in the Black Friday sale — behold, the Sennheiser HD 660S2! Our Reviews Editor, Josh Russell, always speaks highly of his pair, which offer satisfyingly neutral, insightful sound as well as an ergonomic fit and eye-catching design. A tidy saving only adds another reason to grab these, whether you enjoy making music or you're a hobbyist audiophile.
Read moreRead less▼
It's crazy when a price of £59 feels kind of just OK in a headphone roundup, no? But such is the nature of these incredible deals — and at 34% off, they have never dropped lower, according to our price trackers! We called the Space One 'Beats alternatives' under intense review, which kind of puts things into perspective; I don't see any ANC-toting Beats cans for anywhere near this money. And you can check out our full Anker Soundcore Space One review for more.
Read moreRead less▼
Sony's most recent on-ears are cheap enough that even £18.50 off is an incredible saving. It's not just the price, though: in our Sony WH-CH530 review we praised the comfortable fit and strong Sony sound quality. There's no ANC, but if you don't need it, they're a great pick.
Read moreRead less▼
These are new enough that I'm surprised they've seen any discount, albeit a modest one. Released in September, these are a modernised version of the beloved XM4s, with some new features but the same design people still love. If you want premium cans, they're a solid pick with this discount.
Read moreRead less▼
Want an alternative to Sony or Sennheiser's premium picks? The Crusher 1080 are Skullcandy's most premium headphones in ages. Expect that Skullcandy goodness, like a bass slider and warm sound, but with Bose smarts, like tuned audio and spatial sound. The discount is better than some other premium rivals are getting.

These slightly older headphones were replaced by newer ones earlier this year, but our five-star Sennheiser Momentum 4 review still shows they're worth buying thanks to their fantastic sound and ANC. Oh, and the discount means they're now way cheaper than the Momentum 5, for if you don't need the top-end features.
Read moreRead less▼
Bose's recent premium (but not Ultra premium) headphones are enjoying a solid little discount. In my Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) review I said that they were a discount away from being must-buys, so if you were on the fence with them, this price cut could sway your hand.

There's no discount on the new Beats headphones, sadly, but the older Beats Studio Pro are now a lot cheaper than their lowest-seen price to date, if you buy the Khaki model. This means they're less than half the price of the Beats 360, so if you don't mind the slightly older design, it's a much cheaper alternative.

Dutch ace Wessel Nijman is the top seed after winning six events this year

articles.title: Científicos del MIT desarrollan un modelo de IA que puede diseñar chips como un ingeniero y con una fracción de recursos
articles.text:
Investigadores del Instituto de Tecnología de Massachusetts (MIT) desarrollaron SLIC, un método de inteligencia artificial para diseñar circuitos integrados analógicos con modelos de lenguaje pequeños que pueden ejecutarse localmente. La técnica podría acelerar el diseño de chips utilizados en funciones como las comunicaciones y la gestión de energía, sin exponer datos confidenciales de empresas y fundiciones a servicios externos en la nube, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
El sistema, descripto en arXiv, obtuvo resultados cercanos a los del modelo GPT-6-Astra en pruebas de diseño que exigían cumplir métricas específicas de rendimiento, aunque utilizó una fracción de los recursos computacionales. También conservó su desempeño frente a estructuras de circuitos que no había visto antes, nodos tecnológicos más avanzados y procesos comerciales reales.
La investigación será presentada en la Conferencia sobre Sistemas de Procesamiento de Información Neuronal de 2026. El método busca que un modelo reducido pueda diseñar circuitos analógicos con un nivel comparable o superior al de sistemas de mayor escala. Estos chips permiten que los dispositivos electrónicos procesen señales del mundo físico, como las comunicaciones inalámbricas de un teléfono o las mediciones de temperatura del motor de un automóvil.
Un modelo local para datos industriales confidenciales
El diseño de circuitos analógicos suele depender de ajustes manuales entre numerosas variables y objetivos que pueden entrar en conflicto. Los ingenieros deben definir parámetros para alcanzar un rendimiento determinado y, a partir de una configuración inicial, modificar componentes hasta aproximarse a las especificaciones requeridas.
Yan Xu, estudiante de posgrado de Ingeniería Eléctrica y Ciencias de la Computación del MIT y autora principal del trabajo, explicó que el procedimiento no admite una fórmula única: “Para diseñar un circuito, los ingenieros encuentran un buen punto de partida basándose en su intuición y luego, a partir de sus conocimientos sobre diseño de circuitos, ajustan algunos controles hacia el rendimiento que buscan. No hay una forma universal de resolver todos los problemas de diseño de circuitos”.
Los modelos generativos de gran tamaño pueden automatizar parte de esa tarea, pero su uso suele requerir infraestructura remota y grandes recursos de cómputo. Para las compañías del sector, enviar datos específicos de una fundición o diseños propietarios a proveedores externos de inteligencia artificial puede representar un riesgo de privacidad.
SLIC permite entrenar y desplegar el modelo dentro de la propia organización. Xu sostuvo que el sistema ofrece “una opción alternativa para automatizar el diseño de circuitos analógicos” y añadió que las empresas pueden usar sus propios datos confidenciales para entrenar un modelo local y conservar sus activos protegidos.
El modelo empleado utiliza unos pocos miles de millones de parámetros, una escala de varios miles de veces menor que la de los sistemas de frontera, que pueden operar con billones de parámetros. Esa reducción permite ejecutarlo en una computadora portátil, con menores costos y consumo de recursos.
Simulaciones, ajustes y mejoras después de cumplir la meta
El método reproduce una parte del aprendizaje de un ingeniero. Primero, un modelo de mayor tamaño genera varias demostraciones del proceso de diseño de código abierto para un problema de optimización analógica; luego, esas demostraciones sirven para orientar al sistema pequeño.
Después de esa etapa inicial, el modelo enfrenta por sí solo un nuevo problema de diseño. Propone valores para los parámetros del circuito, realiza simulaciones, evalúa los resultados y ajusta de forma iterativa sus decisiones con el conocimiento adquirido durante el entrenamiento.
La técnica utiliza aprendizaje por refuerzo de múltiples etapas con recompensas verificables: el sistema recibe información del entorno durante una tarea compuesta por varios pasos y adapta su conducta a partir de esa respuesta. Cuando ya encuentra un diseño que cumple los objetivos definidos por el usuario, continúa buscando mejoras marginales de rendimiento.
Ruonan Han, autor principal sénior del trabajo, profesor de Ingeniería Eléctrica y Ciencias de la Computación del MIT y miembro del Laboratorio de Investigación en Electrónica de la institución, señaló que los modelos pequeños especializados pueden aproximarse a los resultados de sistemas mucho más grandes: “Mediante entrenamiento especializado e investigación en áreas específicas, podemos usar modelos mucho más pequeños, que consumen muchos menos recursos, para lograr casi los mismos resultados que los modelos insignia en el diseño de circuitos analógicos”.
El proceso también puede ser interpretado por el usuario porque los modelos describen su razonamiento en lenguaje natural. “Aunque todo el proceso está automatizado, el usuario puede ver qué ocurre dentro del modelo”, afirmó Han. Esa visibilidad puede aportar ideas sobre el diseño y aumentar la confianza en las decisiones del sistema.
Aplicaciones en chips de radiofrecuencia y microondas
Las empresas pueden adaptar el modelo entrenado por los investigadores a sus propios datos mediante un proceso de ajuste posterior o utilizar el método para construir una versión propia. Como enseña un procedimiento general de diseño de chips, SLIC no queda vinculado a una compañía determinada y puede aplicarse a distintas clases de circuitos.
Wenjie Lu, exinvestigador posdoctoral del MIT y ahora científico principal de investigación en Analog Devices, Inc., indicó que la demanda de chips analógicos crece mientras la velocidad de diseño no ha seguido el mismo ritmo. “Esta investigación intenta aportar nuevas capacidades a la inteligencia artificial para resolver un problema en el que la industria lleva décadas estancada”, añadió.
Zhang consideró que el modelo local puede aprender comportamientos de diseño transferibles y perfeccionar un circuito mediante un simulador, lo que reduciría los ajustes manuales repetitivos. Añadió que la línea de trabajo podría conducir a diseños personalizados más complejos, incluidos circuitos de radiofrecuencia y microondas.
Los investigadores planean estudiar modelos capaces de mejorar de manera autónoma para abordar topologías y objetivos de diseño más variados. También buscan crear una arquitectura con varios modelos pequeños, cada uno dedicado a una parte distinta de una tarea compleja de diseño de circuitos.

articles.title: I test over a dozen coffee makers every year, and these are the top 3 affordable espresso machines I recommend for beginners
articles.text:
If you're shopping for your first coffee maker this Black Friday, the choice might be overwhelming. That's why I'm here. As TechRadar's resident coffee expert, I test over a dozen coffee makers every year, and I've put together a shortlist of my three favorite options for beginners — all of which are on sale in the US and UK for Black Friday. In the US, for example, the Philips Baristina Latte is $399.99 at Amazon (was $499.99).

There are huge discounts on entry-level coffee makers in the UK as well, where the fabulous Lavazza Tabli is now only £99 at Amazon (was £199). Both options are two of the best I've tested this year, and come highly recommended. Curious? Read on for my full thoughts on both, plus one other coffee maker for beginners who feel ready to try a manual espresso machine.

Philips Baristina

If you want to brew your coffee with fresh beans but you find the idea of using a manual espresso machine a bit daunting, the Baristina is the machine for you — and I've been heartily recommending it to anyone who'll listen since I tested it in February this year.
This is a bean-to-cup coffee machine, meaning it does all the work for you, but it's a lot more affordable than most, and because there's no case covering everything up, it's much easier to clean. Just push the portafilter handle into place and slide it to the right, hit the brew button, and the Baristina will grind the ideal dose of coffee into the filter basket, tamp it down, then slide it over to the left automatically and brew your espresso using perfectly heated water at the optimum pressure.
I've become quite a coffee snob during my time as TechRadar's Homes Editor, and I was seriously impressed by the Baristina's performance. The only catch is that you can't adjust the grind size, so you may have to experiment with a few different coffees until you find one that works well with the machine. I was lucky enough that my usual beans (Honduran Swiss Water Decaf from Wogan Coffee, if you're curious) were ideal.
Read my full Philips Baristina review
This updated version of the Baristina includes an automatic milk frother for foaming dairy or plant-based milk, addressing my only real criticism of the original brewer. It's a record-low price at Amazon for Black Friday, with $100 off.

The Baristina Latte isn't available yet in the UK, but you can grab the original machine with a generous £50 Black Friday price cut. If you want to make milky coffees, the Baristina is also available bundled with a standalone milk frother for £299.99 (was £379.99) at Amazon.
Read moreRead less▼
Capsule
Lavazza Tabli

Lavazza's Tabli machine, which launched a few months ago, promises the convenience of coffee pods without the plastic and metal waste — and after thorough testing, I'm happy to report that it delivers. It uses pucks of compressed ground coffee with no individual packaging, which you insert into the top of the machine before selecting your brew size (single or double). The used coffee drops into a bin in the bottom of the machine, which you can empty directly into your household food recycling or compost heap. Easy.
Most importantly, the coffee tastes delicious. In fact, I used three full boxes of tabs while testing the machine, and found myself using it rather than my usual espresso machine.
You can control the Lavazza Tabli through a mobile app if you like, and it has some smart home connectivity features, but in my experience it works best as a no-frills espresso machine that's beginner-friendly, affordable, and really delivers on flavor.
Read my full Lavazza Tabli review
The superb Tabli coffee maker only launched a few months ago, but has already received a generous 38% price cut for Black Friday at Amazon.

If you're in the UK, you can grab the Tabli for half price in Amazon's Black Friday sale. There's 20% off my favorite Qualita Rossa coffee tabs as well, so I'd recommend stocking up while the deal lasts.

For the slightly braver home barista, the De'Longhi Dedica Duo is a superb little manual espresso machine that will have you brewing like a pro in no time — and is surprisingly affordable. Usually, espresso machines in this price bracket are pretty poor quality, but De'Longhi has a reputation to maintain, and although the little Dedica Duo is cheap, it's just as well-made as the brand's full-size coffee makers.
That means it maintains steady heat and pressure, so you get consistent results with every brew. Once you've found the right grind size for your beans, you will be able to make great-tasting coffee every time with this little wonder. Its steam wand is excellent as well, and every component from the tamper to the milk pitcher feels reassuringly robust.
The 'Duo' in the name refers to the fact that this little machine also offers cold extraction, bypassing the boiler and making espresso using water directly from the tank. It takes a little longer than brewing hot, but the result is a smooth, rounded shot that's a great foundation for an iced latte or an espresso martini. Cheers!

articles.text:
Save a huge $1,020 on a 240Hz OLED gaming laptop from Lenovo with an RTX 5070 Ti, now just $1,999 — portable Legion 5i rig features an 18-core Intel CPU and a 1TB SSD
Serious gaming performance for a brilliant Black Friday price
An OLED gaming laptop, fitted with an RTX 5070 Ti, and all for less than $2,000? That's a deal you don't want to ignore. Lenovo has slashed $1,020 off this Lenovo Legion 5i OLED gaming laptop, dropping the price down to just $1,999.99 for Black Friday. While the RTX 5070 Ti is a powerhouse, it's the 16-inch OLED display with its 240Hz refresh rate that makes a real difference here.
● Check out this OLED gaming laptop at Lenovo
Choosing OLED over a basic LCD means you're getting a display that'll give you perfect blacks and almost infinite contrast, while that 240Hz refresh rate is ultra-fast and ideal for smooth, blur-free motion in games. The top resolution here is 2,560 x 1,600, and with the RTX 5070 Ti at your disposal, you won't struggle to hit high frame rates with ultra graphics presets switched on at 1600p. You've also got the option to hook it up to an external display over HDMI if you want to go bigger.
This Lenovo Legion 5i gaming laptop sports an Intel Core Ultra 7 251 HX, RTX 5070 Ti GPU, 16GB of DDR5 and 1TB of NVMe storage. This is an OLED gaming laptop with a 1600p top resolution and a 240Hz refresh rate.
The gaming credentials, though, are confirmed by the RTX 5070 Ti. Yes, it's the mobile version, so it isn't a like-for-like with its desktop equivalent, and instead ships with a set of 5,888 CUDA cores and 12GB GDDR7 VRAM. At 1600p, though, that won't be much of a problem. DLSS support, meanwhile, means you've got breathing room, with multi-frame generation able to cut some of the slack with AI-generated frames to give you an uplift in the most power-intensive games.
Coupled with the GPU is the Intel Core Ultra 7 251HX as your processor. It has 18 cores, comprised of six performance cores and 12 efficient cores, with a max boost clock on the p-cores of up to 5.1 GHz. Again, a more than formidable option for the kind of gaming or productivity work you'd be expected to do on a laptop like this.
Elsewhere, you're getting a 1TB SSD offering Gen 4 speeds, so enough space for a couple of big game installations there. A small compromise is on RAM, with only 16GB of DDR5 included here. While 32GB would be better, the price is good, and you've got the option to upgrade later down the line. articles.title: Por qué iCloud sigue lleno al borrar fotos: el truco de respaldos y carpetas ocultas
articles.text:
Borrar fotografías del iPhone no significa que ese espacio se libere al instante en iCloud. Apple separa la biblioteca fotográfica activa de las copias de seguridad y de las carpetas de retención temporal, y esa división es la razón por la que el contador de almacenamiento apenas se mueve tras una limpieza masiva de imágenes.
El truco está en entender que, además de la papelera de eliminados, existen respaldos de aplicaciones, documentos en iCloud Drive y álbumes ocultos que siguen consumiendo gigabytes sin aparecer en la vista principal de Fotos.
La confusión es habitual entre usuarios de iPhone y iPad, que cada semana eliminan decenas de archivos pesados esperando ver un cambio inmediato en los ajustes de almacenamiento.
El problema no suele ser un fallo del sistema, sino un diseño de Apple pensado para evitar pérdidas accidentales de información y para repartir los datos entre distintos servicios dentro de la misma cuenta.
Eliminados en iCloud: la papelera que retiene archivos 30 días
Toda fotografía borrada de la galería pasa primero a una sección llamada Eliminados, que funciona como una papelera de reciclaje. Durante 30 días, esos archivos permanecen almacenados y pueden recuperarse con un solo toque, lo que explica por qué el espacio ocupado en iCloud no desciende de inmediato.
Solo cuando se vacía esa carpeta de forma manual o cuando se cumple el plazo de un mes, el sistema borra definitivamente los archivos y libera el almacenamiento real. Muchos usuarios ignoran este paso y asumen que el borrado desde el carrete principal es suficiente, cuando en realidad la eliminación completa requiere una acción adicional.
A este retraso se suma el tiempo que tarda la sincronización entre dispositivos. Si el borrado se realiza con poca batería, sin conexión wifi estable o con el modo de bajo consumo activado, la orden puede quedar en cola antes de reflejarse en los servidores de Apple y en los demás equipos vinculados a la cuenta.
Respaldo en iCloud y Fotos en iCloud no son lo mismo
Uno de los errores más frecuentes es pensar que el respaldo del dispositivo y la fototeca sincronizada funcionan como un único bloque de datos. En realidad, operan con reglas distintas dentro del ecosistema de Apple.
Cuando la fototeca está sincronizada en iCloud, el respaldo del dispositivo suele omitir esas imágenes para no duplicarlas. Sin embargo, ese mismo respaldo sigue conservando ajustes del sistema, datos de aplicaciones y archivos asociados a cada app, lo que puede mantener ocupado un volumen considerable de espacio aunque el carrete esté vacío.
Esta diferencia explica por qué, incluso después de borrar fotos y vaciar la papelera, el almacenamiento total de la cuenta no refleja una baja proporcional. El consumo de espacio depende de varias categorías que se gestionan de forma independiente.
Aplicaciones, documentos y álbumes ocultos que consumen gigabytes
Buena parte del espacio que parece “desaparecido” está repartido entre funciones que no se muestran en la pantalla principal de Fotos. Revisar estas categorías es clave para entender el consumo real de almacenamiento:
Las aplicaciones de mensajería, los editores de video y los juegos suelen guardar adjuntos, archivos de caché e historiales dentro del respaldo del dispositivo, incluso después de haber limpiado por completo el carrete fotográfico.
Los documentos descargados, los adjuntos de correo electrónico y las carpetas del sistema asociadas a distintas aplicaciones en iCloud Drive también ocupan espacio de manera independiente, sin que esos archivos aparezcan nunca en la app Fotos.
Por último, los álbumes marcados como Ocultos y las copias vinculadas a varios dispositivos conectados a la misma cuenta pueden generar la sensación de que el espacio no se reduce si no se revisa el desglose detallado por categoría.
Pasos para verificar y liberar espacio real en iCloud
El camino más directo para salir de dudas es ingresar a Ajustes, tocar el nombre de usuario y entrar en la sección iCloud, donde aparece una barra de distribución por categorías.
Esa vista detallada permite distinguir con precisión cuánto espacio corresponde a Fotos, cuánto a Respaldo, cuánto a iCloud Drive y cuánto a Mensajes, en lugar de depender únicamente del contador que muestra la app Fotos.
Si el objetivo es recuperar gigabytes sin perder recuerdos, conviene seguir tres acciones concretas. Primero, vaciar de forma manual la carpeta Eliminados dentro de la app Fotos para forzar el borrado definitivo. Segundo, entrar en Administrar almacenamiento dentro de los ajustes de iCloud y desactivar el respaldo de aplicaciones que no necesitan guardar datos en la nube.
Tercero, comprobar si existen copias de seguridad antiguas de dispositivos que ya no se utilizan, ya que esos respaldos inactivos siguen ocupando espacio dentro del límite contratado de la cuenta.

articles.title: Google veut publier l'adresse personnelle des développeurs, bien au-delà de ce qu'exige l'Europe
articles.text:
À partir du 1er mars 2027, Google affichera l’adresse et le téléphone des développeurs « marchands » sur le Play Store, dans le monde entier. Les indépendants qui travaillent depuis chez eux n’ont guère d’échappatoire.
Le Digital Services Act européen impose bien une transparence sur les vendeurs en ligne, mais pas à l’échelle planétaire. Google a choisi d’appliquer la règle partout, et c’est là que le bât blesse pour les petits studios.
Une obligation européenne, une application mondiale
Google justifie ce changement par le passage de Google Play à un modèle de place de marché en ligne dans l’Espace économique européen et au Royaume-Uni, afin de respecter les règles locales de protection des consommateurs. Selon Heise, tous les comptes développeurs actifs devront déclarer avant le 1er février 2027 s’ils sont « traders » (marchands) ou non, quel que soit l’endroit où ils distribuent leurs applications.
Les indices du statut de marchand incluent des revenus réguliers : publicité, applications payantes ou achats intégrés. Ceux qui se déclarent marchands verront leur adresse et leur numéro de téléphone affichés publiquement, partout dans le monde. Les développeurs qui ne distribuent pas dans l’EEE ni au Royaume-Uni peuvent se déclarer non-marchands et échapperaient ainsi vraisemblablement à cet affichage. Le texte européen n’impose donc rien de tel au reste du monde : c’est un choix de Google.
Pas de boîte postale : l’adresse perso ou un prestataire payant
L’adresse affichée provient du profil de paiement du compte développeur, et les boîtes postales y sont interdites. Un indépendant sans bureau a donc deux options : exposer son domicile ou payer un représentant, ou un prestataire, qui lui fournit une adresse professionnelle.
Plusieurs développeurs s’en agacent : l’un d’eux, cité par le magazine coréen The Elec, envisage de louer un local rien que pour protéger ses données personnelles. Le dirigeant juge utile de fournir un contact aux consommateurs en cas de litige, mais pointe les risques d’atteinte à la vie privée et d’usage abusif de ces données, avec une exposition possible des proches qui vivent sous le même toit.
Apple limite l’affichage à l’UE et tolère les boîtes postales
Le contraste avec Apple est net. Dans le cadre du DSA, la cuisine de Cupertino restreint l’affichage des adresses et numéros aux 27 États membres de l’UE. Elle autorise aussi les développeurs individuels à indiquer une boîte postale sur l’App Store, après vérification de justificatifs (reçus ou factures de location de la boîte). L’adresse exigée pour l’identité est ainsi séparée de celle que voit le public.
Apple avait en outre demandé dès 2024 aux développeurs de se déclarer marchands le cas échéant : Google arrive tard, et plus strict. Reste à voir si la pression des indépendants suffira à lui faire assouplir sa copie avant mars 2027. Pour l’instant, la protection de la vie privée des petits studios passe par leur portefeuille.

articles.title: Meta añade su IA Muse a los mensajes de Instagram: ayudará a hacer compras y otras rutinas
articles.text:
Meta ha comenzado a integrar a Muse, su agente de inteligencia artificial, directamente en los mensajes directos de Instagram, de manera que los usuarios pueden conversar con el asistente sin salir de la aplicación.
La novedad elimina la necesidad de alternar entre Instagram y la app propia de Muse para pedirle ayuda. Desde ahora, el asistente puede ofrecer contexto sobre una publicación, armar itinerarios de viaje o convertir contenido guardado en listas de tareas concretas.
Cómo funciona la integración en los mensajes directos
La conversación con Muse aparece como un hilo más dentro de los DMs de Instagram. Según detalló Meta en su anuncio, los usuarios pueden compartirle publicaciones para pedirle más información sobre lo que muestran, ya sea un lugar, un producto o un tema puntual.
Las conversaciones iniciadas desde Instagram no quedan aisladas: también se reflejan como un chat lateral dentro de la aplicación principal de Muse, de modo que es posible continuar la charla en cualquiera de las dos plataformas.
El despliegue de esta función en mensajes directos comenzó el 24 de noviembre para usuarios de iOS y Android en Estados Unidos, Canadá, México, Japón y Singapur, según precisó TechCrunch.
Qué puede hacer Muse con el contenido guardado
Más allá de la conversación directa, Meta presentó nuevas formas de trabajar con las publicaciones y los reels que cada usuario guarda en Instagram. El asistente puede organizar ese material en carpetas personalizadas llamadas Colecciones.
Entre los ejemplos difundidos por la compañía figura convertir un video de una receta en una lista de compras, o transformar publicaciones de viajes guardadas en un itinerario para una próxima salida. En moda, Muse podría sugerir ideas de atuendos a partir de los reels que el usuario haya recopilado.
La empresa también mostró casos de uso ligados a una publicación puntual: agregar una cafetería a un itinerario en Ciudad de México o buscar una oferta de Black Friday para un par de zapatos. Son ejemplos que ilustran cómo Meta busca conectar el descubrimiento de contenido con una acción práctica, aunque la compañía no detalló comercios participantes ni criterios de búsqueda para las compras.
A partir del lanzamiento, cuando un usuario guarde una publicación en Instagram verá una sugerencia para pedirle a Muse que la organice. Esta función de Colecciones, a diferencia de los mensajes directos, se limita por ahora a Estados Unidos y Canadá, sin fecha anunciada para su expansión a otros mercados.
Cómo será el control del usuario sobre las acciones del asistente
Meta sostiene que las personas mantienen el control sobre su experiencia con Muse en Instagram. Según la compañía, nada se comparte, publica o envía sin aprobación previa, y los usuarios pueden pedirle al asistente que olvide información o deshaga acciones en cualquier momento.
Las páginas de ayuda de Instagram explican que Muse puede solicitar confirmación antes de ciertas acciones, como compartir información o visitar un sitio web desconocido, cuando el usuario tiene esa opción configurada. Esto implica que no todas las funciones requieren necesariamente el mismo tipo de aprobación.
El antecedente más reciente en materia de privacidad llegó en octubre. Infobae informó el 21 de octubre de 2026 que Meta suspendió la posibilidad de compartir conversaciones con Muse después de que se detectara la exposición de información sensible.
Ese episodio se refería puntualmente a compartir conversaciones y no implica que el asistente publique contenido de forma automática en Instagram, aunque resulta pertinente al evaluar las funciones de intercambio de información que ahora se suman a la red social.
La disponibilidad de Muse en un país tampoco garantiza que todas sus funciones estén activas allí. Wired en español informó que el asistente está disponible para mayores de 18 años en México a través de su sitio web y de aplicaciones para iOS y Android, mientras que TechCrunch confirmó que ese mismo mercado forma parte del despliegue de mensajes directos, aunque queda fuera, por ahora, de las nuevas funciones de Colecciones.

articles.title: Which all-in-one Black Friday VPN bundle is really worth it? I compared NordVPN Prime, ExpressVPN Pro, and Proton Unlimited — all under $7 a month — to decide
articles.text:
Which all-in-one Black Friday VPN bundle is really worth it? I compared NordVPN Prime, ExpressVPN Pro, and Proton Unlimited — all under $7 a month — to decide
From encrypted cloud storage and AI credits to cyber insurance, the real test is knowing which extras you’ll actually use
VPNs used to be basic, single-purpose tools built only to encrypt and reroute your internet traffic. Now, they’ve evolved into all-in-one digital privacy and cybersecurity suites.
While you can get a solid VPN with extra security tools from as low as $2.29/month thanks to Surfshark’s Black Friday deal, flagship bundles like Proton Unlimited, NordVPN Prime, and ExpressVPN Pro go the extra mile. These products include encrypted cloud storage, identity monitoring, and password managers all on top of the basic VPN.
The benefit is managing everything under one subscription. However, they don’t come cheap.
Out of the three tiers currently on offer for less than $7 a month, I’d go with Proton Unlimited. It has the lowest monthly rate ($6.49/month) and only locks you into a one-year commitment.
Proton Unlimited: The all-rounder
Proton has faced its fair share of scrutiny in recent weeks, but if you’re looking for a genuine all-in-one privacy toolkit, Proton Unlimited is worth a look.
It’s currently available for $6.49/month, or $77.88 upfront for a one-year subscription — nearly $60 less than the $134.85 upfront price you’ll pay for ExpressVPN Pro or NordVPN Prime’s 15-month plans.
With Proton Unlimited, you get 500GB of encrypted cloud storage alongside Proton Mail, Proton Calendar, and Proton Pass, the company’s well-respected password manager.
Proton Unlimited: 1-year all-in-one privacy bundle
Now: $6.49 per month ($77.88 upfront) 
Proton’s Black Friday deal drops its flagship bundle to $6.49 per month. The plan includes one of the best VPNs on the market alongside private email, 500GB of encrypted cloud storage, a password manager, and ad-free access to a full suite of encrypted office apps.
ExpressVPN Pro: AI, eSIM, and dedicated IP
ExpressVPN Pro is currently on sale at $6.99 a month for a 28-month subscription totaling $195.72, or $8.99 a month for a 15-month plan at $134.85.
While that’s a steep jump over Proton on a shorter commitment, you get several perks Proton doesn't match. First, it includes a dedicated IP, which is genuinely useful for remote work and avoiding relentless CAPTCHAs while browsing. It also throws in a complimentary eSIM via its partner, Holiday.com.
Finally, Pro bundles 2GB of encrypted vault storage and 500 credits for ExpressAI. While the assistant hasn’t wowed our reviewers, this could be a tidy consolidation play if you want to merge a private AI tool with your VPN, password manager, and identity monitoring.
ExpressVPN Pro: dedicated IP and AI bundle 
Now: $6.99 per month ($195.72 upfront) 
ExpressVPN Pro includes useful extras like ExpressAI credits and a complimentary Holiday.com eSIM. Its most valuable addition, however, is a dedicated IP address, which helps eliminate some of the most irritating parts of using a VPN.
NordVPN Prime: Complete identity and malware protection
NordVPN Prime is NordVPN’s flagship tier, combining antivirus, ad blocking, NordPass, and 1TB of NordLocker encrypted cloud storage on top of specialist identity tools — including bureau credit monitoring, credit score tracking, and up to $5,000 in cyber insurance (US-only).
It’s currently available for $6.99 a month for 27 months, paid $188.73 upfront. Its shorter 15-month plan bumps the price to $8.99 a month.
Its anti-phishing and malware protection has performed well in recent independent testing, blocking 92% of scam websites in AV-Comparatives' latest Q4 2026 audit — a solid layer of defense over Black Friday weekend when there’s always a spike in fake retail scams.
NordVPN Prime: identity and malware protection 
Now: $6.99 per month ($188.73 upfront) 
NordVPN’s flagship tier includes everything you need to keep your identity safe online and your devices protected from malware. It includes Threat Protection Pro, call and message scam protection, NordPass password manager, and 1TB of encrypted cloud storage. If you’re in the US, you can also get Coveron data removal and cyber insurance.
The verdict
The best option here really depends on what you need from your subscription.
If price, an alternative to Google, and a shorter commitment are your top priorities, I’d recommend Proton Unlimited. Thanks to its Black Friday deal, it’s considerably cheaper upfront than the alternatives and still includes encrypted email, calendar, password management, and 500GB of cloud storage.
However, if private AI access or a dedicated IP is your main priority, go with ExpressVPN Pro. And if you want maximum identity defense — including data removal and cyber insurance — NordVPN Prime is the stronger two-year choice, as long as you’re in the US.
Each of the plans also offers shorter-term billing starting at just one month alongside a 30-day money-back guarantee, so if you’re unsure, you can test them out and see which of these features you’ll actually use.

Sam is VPN Managing Editor at TechRadar. He has worked in the VPN industry since 2018 and has previously written for CNN, Al Jazeera, WIRED, and Deutsche Welle as a freelance journalist. He focuses on VPNs and digital privacy, cybersecurity and internet freedom.
Before joining TechRadar, Sam carried out research on global digital rights issues at Top10VPN. His research has been cited by the United Nations and UK Parliament, as well as publications such as The Guardian, Washington Post and BBC.

articles.title: Hallaron más de 12.000 sitios hechos con ChatGPT abiertos a cualquiera, algunos con datos de clientes
articles.text:
La empresa de ciberseguridad Pluto Security detectó 16.666 sitios web creados con ChatGPT Sites, la función de OpenAI que convierte unas pocas instrucciones en una aplicación publicada en internet. De ese total, 12.830 (77%) se mostraban a cualquier visitante sin pedir inicio de sesión, según el informe que la firma publicó el 23 de noviembre.
Los investigadores revisaron a mano una parte de esos sitios y hallaron información sensible de 27 organizaciones. Pluto afirma que no vulneró ningún sistema: usó herramientas gratuitas y fuentes públicas, como buscadores, archivos web, repositorios de código y datos de rastreo de internet. Según la firma, el conjunto se reunió en unos 10 minutos.
Pluto aclara que el 77% no equivale a filtraciones: son sitios accesibles sin registro, y algunos pueden estar abiertos a propósito. Las filtraciones confirmadas son las de las 27 organizaciones.
ChatGPT Sites está disponible para los planes Plus y Pro, y para los espacios de trabajo Business y Enterprise, según el centro de ayuda de OpenAI. El usuario describe la aplicación, ChatGPT escribe el código y la publica, con alojamiento incluido. Cada dirección termina en chatgpt.site.
Ventas, cotizaciones y datos de residentes
El caso más sensible, según Pluto, fue el panel de ventas de una empresa de la lista Fortune 500 (las 500 mayores compañías de Estados Unidos por ingresos). Mostraba 207 reuniones comerciales con nombre y cargo de cada prospecto, entre ellos directivos de hospitales, y el resultado de cada cita.
El mismo panel incluía indicadores de desempeño de cada vendedor. Pluto sostiene que un competidor podría usar esa información para ir tras los mismos clientes durante una negociación, o que un atacante podría hacerse pasar por un vendedor y escribir a un directivo que acababa de reunirse con él. Tras el aviso de la firma, la empresa restringió el acceso.
Una empresa de transporte de carga dejó visibles 1.185 cotizaciones a clientes desde 2023, con tasas mensuales de conversión, cuentas principales y un mapa de dónde guarda sus datos internos. Un sitio de un complejo residencial exponía nombre de lote, teléfono, correo, cumpleaños y aniversario de boda de 425 residentes.
Un cuarto hallazgo no provino de la empresa afectada. Un proveedor de sensores armó una presentación de ventas para una cadena minorista europea y la dejó pública. Ahí figuraban la cantidad de tiendas por país y los cierres que la cadena aún no había anunciado.
Una pantalla de contraseña no protege los datos
Según Pluto, muchos sitios tenían una pantalla de acceso creada por la propia IA que no protegía nada. Si la aplicación envía los datos al navegador antes de que el visitante ingrese la clave, cualquiera puede descargarlos sin conocerla. La contraseña solo oculta lo que ya llegó a la computadora.
Ehud Melzer, investigador de seguridad del equipo fundador de Pluto, explicó al medio israelí N12 que antes los equipos de desarrollo y de sistemas participaban en decidir quién accede a la información de la empresa. Ahora, dijo, esa decisión recae en el empleado que sube el archivo y publica la aplicación, y el área de seguridad puede enterarse tarde.
El centro de ayuda de OpenAI indica que un sitio nuevo queda limitado a su dueño y a los administradores del espacio de trabajo hasta que se cambia el acceso. Publicarlo para cualquier persona de internet exige que la función de publicación pública esté habilitada. En los planes Enterprise, esa opción viene desactivada y debe activarla un administrador.
La documentación también advierte que, si el sitio incluye su propio sistema de acceso, ese sistema tiene controles propios, y recomienda revisar el contenido y el público elegido antes de publicar. Los administradores pueden decidir quién crea sitios y quién publica.
Qué recomienda la firma a las empresas
Pluto aconseja localizar los sitios que los empleados publicaron, revisar qué datos contienen y limitar la publicación abierta salvo que haya una razón. Para herramientas internas propone compartir con personas concretas o con el espacio de trabajo, usar el acceso “Sign in with ChatGPT” (iniciar sesión con ChatGPT) y borrar los sitios en desuso.
Pluto vende servicios de seguridad para este tipo de herramientas y el informe forma parte de su difusión comercial. Los datos de 16.666 y 12.830 sitios provienen de la propia firma y no figuran verificados por un tercero. La búsqueda no encontró una respuesta pública de OpenAI al informe.
La empresa de carga y la compañía de la lista Fortune 500 no fueron identificadas por Pluto. Tras el aviso de la firma, solo la segunda confirmó haber restringido el acceso a su sitio, según el informe.

articles.title: Un prototype de processeur Intel Razor Lake-AX en fuite confirme la mémoire intégrée
articles.text:
Sujet délicat que celui de l'intégration de la mémoire vive aux processeurs. Intel a déjà tenté l'expérience par le passé, mais Razor Lake pourrait marquer un changement plus durable.
L'année 2027 d'Intel promet d'être riche en nouveautés processeurs. D'un côté, le retour de Raptor Lake avec une petite (et ultime ?) gamme de puces. De l'autre, l'entrée en scène de Nova Lake et, sans aucun doute, des informations complémentaires autour de Razor Lake qui fait déjà parler de lui.
Razor Lake, pas avant fin 2027 ou début 2028
Selon les dernières informations que nous avons pu recueillir, Intel aurait bel et bien dans l'idée d'organiser un événement autour de son architecture Nova Lake fin février à Berlin.
Un événement qui sera logiquement l'occasion de présenter en détail cette nouvelle gamme de processeurs et, pourquoi pas, de commercialiser les tout premiers modèles dans la foulée. Mais nous ne sommes pas là pour parler de Nova Lake, quand bien même Intel joue gros sur ce dossier. Non, c'est la génération d'après qui nous intéresse aujourd'hui, Razor Lake.
Pas attendu avant, au mieux, la toute fin d'année prochaine et, plus sans doute de manière plus vraisemblable, début 2028, Razor Lake devrait notamment être l'occasion de présenter un APU redoutablement équipé. On parle ici d'une puce dotée de 16 cœurs CPU avec une répartition estimée en 4 cœurs performants (P), 8 cœurs efficaces (E) et 12 cœurs basse consommation (LPE).
Plus important encore, la partie GPU devait être représentée par 12 cœurs qui, en plus d'être plutôt nombreux, devaient se reposer sur la plus moderne des générations Intel, les Xe3P. Mais Razor Lake, c'est aussi l'hypothèse d'une puce orientée gaming, un CPU avec 12 cœurs Coyote Cove (P-cores), sans aucun cœur efficace (E-cores) et un supplément de cache « bLLC ».
Razor Lake serait aussi l'occasion de reposer la question de la mémoire vive intégrée – ou non, donc – au package du processeur. Une question à laquelle ont déjà répondu des entreprises comme Apple ou Qualcomm, mais qui semble diviser chez Intel.
Jusqu'à 128 Go de LPDDR5X intégrés à la puce
Plusieurs gammes de processeurs Intel sont déjà commercialisées avec de la mémoire vive intégrée au package. C'est notamment le cas dans les branches dédiées aux puces pour ordinateurs portables.
Les empreintes pour quatre puces de LPDDR5X sont bien visibles. © VideoCardz
À la manière de Lunar Lake sur les Core Ultra 200, Razor Lake pourrait donc bien aussi avoir sa composante « memory-on-package » avec de la LPDDR5X intégrée au package de chaque puce. La confirmation nous est venue tout récemment avec la diffusion de deux clichés par nos confrères du site VideoCardz, deux clichés d'un prototype de CPU Razor Lake-AX.
Bien sûr, il est encore trop tôt pour conclure de manière définitive, d'autant que les deux clichés sont « incomplets ». On y voit bien la puce Razor Lake-AX et son package, mais il n'est pas question de puces mémoire sur ces photos : on ne voit que l'empreinte laissée pour chaque chip. Quatre empreintes pour un maximum de quatre puces.
Des informations qui collent avec des précédentes rumeurs et semblent venir confirmer qu'un processeur Razor Lake-AX pourra être accompagné de 32 à 128 Go de mémoire vive LPDDR5X. Notez que de telles configurations sont là pour confirmer que Razor Lake-AX serait bien vu par Intel comme un possible concurrent aux solutions Halo d'AMD.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: Por qué GTA 6 no permite volver a jugar las misiones
articles.text:
Rockstar Games confirmó que GTA 6 no incluirá una función para volver a jugar misiones ya completadas, una herramienta que sí estaba disponible tanto en GTA 5 como en Red Dead Redemption 2. La decisión responde a un conflicto directo con la estructura narrativa del juego, según explicó el estudio.
El director sénior de diseño de Rockstar Games, Scott Butchard, abordó el tema en una entrevista con Kotaku. Según su relato, la posibilidad de repetir misiones estuvo sobre la mesa durante las primeras etapas de desarrollo, pero el equipo decidió no incorporarla a medida que el proyecto avanzaba.
“La repetición de misiones fue sin duda algo que barajamos en las primeras fases del desarrollo, pero actualmente no la ofrecemos”, declaró Butchard en diálogo con el medio. “A medida que el juego iba tomando forma, nos pareció que entraba en conflicto con la historia que intentábamos contar”, agregó.
Las decisiones del jugador pesan sobre la trama
El argumento central de Rockstar gira en torno al peso de las decisiones del jugador dentro de la historia. Butchard sostuvo que volver a jugar misiones de forma aislada “restaba importancia a las decisiones” tomadas a lo largo de la partida, al describir esa dinámica como “quedarse al margen del juego”.
GTA 6 permite ramificaciones narrativas significativas: los jugadores pueden decidir si matan o perdonan a ciertos personajes, completar objetivos de distintas maneras y moldear el vínculo entre Jason y Lucía según sus propias acciones. Estas variables generan opciones de diálogo y escenas cinemáticas diferenciadas, un nivel de ramificación que explicaría la complejidad de implementar un sistema de repetición de misiones equivalente al de entregas anteriores.
El precedente de Red Dead Redemption 2
Red Dead Redemption 2 también ofrecía variaciones que afectaban el carácter de su protagonista, Arthur, aunque con un alcance menor al de las decisiones presentes en GTA 6. Ese título sí contaba con un menú de repetición de misiones, lo que marca una diferencia respecto al funcionamiento actual del nuevo lanzamiento.
Rockstar no descarta cambios futuros
Butchard fue preciso en su formulación: el juego “actualmente no admite” esta función, una frase que deja abierta la puerta a una eventual incorporación mediante una actualización posterior. Sin embargo, el estudio no confirmó ningún plan concreto en ese sentido.
La ausencia de esta herramienta generó controversia entre los jugadores, en particular porque GTA 6 incluye algunas de las misiones mejor valoradas de la franquicia, como la misión final del Capítulo 1. Dado que completar el juego puede demandar entre 50 y 100 horas, resulta poco probable que la mayoría de los usuarios reinicie la partida completa solo para revivir una secuencia puntual.
Aun si Rockstar no incorpora la función de manera oficial, existe la posibilidad de que la comunidad de desarrolladores de mods encuentre una solución alternativa cuando se lance la versión para computadoras, un paso que la compañía no ha confirmado todavía pero que se considera habitual en sus títulos anteriores.
El avance de la adaptación no oficial para PC
Entretanto, una versión no oficial de GTA 6 para computadoras continúa en desarrollo pese a los intentos de Take-Two Interactive y Rockstar Games por frenar su distribución, que ya incluyeron el cierre de más de 3.000 repositorios vinculados con el proyecto.
Según información difundida por comunidades de jugadores, la iniciativa, basada en una copia filtrada para Xbox Series, trasladó parte de su desarrollo a espacios privados y ya cuenta con las primeras modificaciones creadas por usuarios, además de un lanzador propio en preparación para facilitar su ejecución a quienes no tienen conocimientos técnicos avanzados.

articles.title: Denny’s touts renewed support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following reinstatement — says ‘some things you just don’t take off the menu’
articles.text:
Denny’s touts renewed support for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following reinstatement — says ‘some things you just don’t take off the menu’
Denny's posted a 200-word statement to its X social media account, ignoring the fact that Huang resigned from Nvidia after admitting he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Following his recent resignation from the company and his return as CEO earlier this week, Jensen Huang has received a glowing statement of support from Denny's, the chain where he famously began his working life before founding Nvidia. The diner chain Denny's posted a 200-word statement to X in which it sought to maintain its links to the Nvidia founder, saying that there are "some things you just don’t take off the menu." Denny's, famously, is the diner where Huang came up with the idea for Nvidia before founding the then-GPU company, now an AI server outfit.
Notably, the chain also noted that it has restored a plaque commemorating the occasion to "where it belongs," days after it was removed amid growing controversy over Huang and his affair with former Megaspeed employee Alice Huang. Megaspeed is now under criminal investigation over its involvement in bypassing U.S. export controls relating to Nvidia's advanced AI chips. It's also believed that Alice Huang's husband, Kang Wei, may also be a spy with connections to China's Ministry of State Security.
Despite all of that, Denny's has very much hitched its trailer to Huang and his reputation, for better or worse. The diner's statement ends by reminding him that his booth "is always waiting and the coffee's on," although it's unclear whether he'll be able to make time for a visit between his upcoming visit to Congress to discuss the last few weeks' goings-on and joining board meetings with U.S. President Donald Trump. There is good news for Huang, though, even if he's found to have broken the law during his trysts with the suspected spy. Trump says that a pardon is "always an option," meaning Huang could be free to visit all the Denny's diners he wants to in the future.
As for Nvidia, its share price has suffered the same fate as other tech stocks in recent weeks. It rallied after initially nosediving around the time of Huang's resignation, but has since continued its downward trajectory, having fallen almost 2.4 percentage points in the last five days and over 30 points in the last month.

articles.title: 5 free tools to keep you scam safe from fake shops on Black Friday
articles.text:
5 free tools to keep you scam safe from fake shops on Black Friday – how to protect your email address and track prices properly too
Tips, downloads and some useful online retail common sense around email addresses, price tracking and the signs that you're looking at a fake shop
I'm going to level with you here, I'm old. Yesterday I had a neck ache that, as far as I can tell, was the result of having gone to sleep. That's right, my own neck was furious that I'd got a solid seven hours rest. While that's not ideal, my advanced years mean I've been around for a while and I've seen the internet evolve.
In the late 90s most people would have never trusted the internet for shopping, but back then the sort of scams and fraud that exist today were less of an issue. But like anything, when the money shows up, so do the criminals looking to make a fast buck, and those criminals have got really good at making fake shops since AI turned up and made generating almost identical replicas of the real deals ridiculously easy.
The positive side is that the internet has evolved to take security much more seriously and there's plenty you can do to beef up your own resilience online. So here are some free tools and tips worth trying out, to not only keep you safe from fake shops, but also ensure you're not overpaying this Black Friday.
Don't use your real email address
Let's start at the beginning, with arguably the simplest of all our tips. Our email needs to be treated a bit more like personal information.
Because most online stores and services use an email to identify you, it can be used by criminals if it leaks online. An example:
Let's say you shop at retailer A, make an account using your email address and do the same at retailer B. If retailer A gets hacked or compromised then your email may end up being revealed, which is helpful for hackers who want to know active email addresses, so that they can then get into B, C, D and all the other places where you have the same credentials which, hopefully, don't all use the same password. (You don't don't do that, do you? I've warned you about this one already.)
So by using a more disposable set of email addresses is a good idea. It also means that if a shop or service does get compromised, you can cancel that address and you won't lose much or receive endless spam messages, and potential invitations to be defrauded.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It's also useful for getting introductory discounts, where you may not want to use the company again so don't want to be constantly emailed about new offers. Think of these as burner email addresses.
How do you do this then? Well, good news for Apple customers who are paying for iCloud+ because hiding your email is included. When you register a new account, your phone, tablet or Mac will just ask you if you want to hide your real email.
Google is apparently working on a similar feature, but it's not built in to Android yet. So for people who don't want to use Apple's service, or use Android, we can turn to other companies.
If you use Firefox as your web browser (and you should, for a number of reasons) then the option is built in for free. When you see a "sign up with email" option, Firefox will add "use an email mask" option for you to use.
The alternative too Google Search, DuckDuckGo also has a free option for email masking. It uses a brower plug-in which does the same thing.
Proton Email (which is excellent in its own right) also has the option, but you will have to pay for the service. Although, now is a good time to subscribe, while Black Friday deals are live.
However I want to stress, please do NOT use any old email mask app from your phone or browser app store. Giving your real email to an unknown company is just as bad as using your email to sign up for things.
Get a price-tracker, and ensure you're not paying over-the-odds
Laws around the world differ greatly on how "sales" are handled. In the UK there are rules on sale prices that should help to ensure that retailers can't just slap a "deep discounts" label on something they just added 30% mark-up to before the sale started.
When it comes to Amazon deals, they're generally not bad for authentic price drops – at least in the UK. If you're in the US, it will vary and other countries have their own rules and considerations.
However, extensions for your browser like Keepa and CamelCamelCamel are a good way of seeing price history on Amazon. I use Keepa, which adds a nice price history chart on every Amazon item page. You can even set up alerts to tell you if something you want is getting a discount.
Of course, when it comes to spotting good deals, it would be daft of me not to mention that we have a whole team of people spotting the best prices and sharing those deals with you – so make use of our dedicated Black Friday page to track down deals.
Use a malicious ad block
Adverts are part of life these days, and let's be honest they keep a lot of the internet free for us to use. The problem is, not all ads are created equally and there are times when ads can be used to compromise your computer. This is a rare problem, but it's called Malvertising and sits in the same sort of space as viruses.
Fraudsters can deliver a small program via adverts that can then do things using your computer. That might be something like cryptocurrency mining, generating money for them but slowing down your computer and increasing your electricity bill. For the most part, your anti-virus software, either the built-in version or something you pay for, will detect these and remove them. But it's much better to avoid it in the first place as they can potentially steal account details and other personal information.
When it comes to selecting a malicious ad blocker we suggest something like uBlockOrigin or Adblock Plus to prevent these sort of attacks. It's also worth remembering that you can exclude some sites from ad blockers, which can be useful as they do also block links for legitimate shopping links sometimes, which can make for a confusing experience.
Even so, the advantages of keeping yourself safe online outweigh the mild inconvenience.
Check that Amazon reviews are legitimate
Amazon's changed a lot over the years, and when it became a marketplace offering both products it stocks, plus third-party sales it also introduced the possibility of companies selling through the platform using fake reviews to make their particular product seem better than the rest.
This matters, because so many of us use the wisdom of the crowd to decide if product A or product B is better, and if we can't rely on that review process then we may end up wasting money on inferior products. This, in turn, can make decision paralysis worse, and if you've suffered through that, you'll know it's annoying.
So make use of some review checkers. These tend to use AI to determine if the reviews for a product are genuine. RateBud has both a website you can use, as well as Chrome and Firefox browser extensions. When you install, and visit, Amazon, it will show you a score based on its confidence that the reviews are genuine.
If you're a Google Chrome user, Surevett does the same thing, but obviously only works if you're using that specific browser.
For reviews outside the world of Amazon, it's a lot harder to check. However, you can spot fake reviews yourself.
Look for a very high percentage of five star ratings, but read the specifics of the review itself. Does it mention the specific product you're buying, or is it very generic "this product is excellent, really useful" could be for anything, and perhaps not the specific product you're buying.
Keep an eye out for "verified purchase" too, as that means the user has an account which shows as having actually bought the item, so that can help.
But be aware, some companies do incentivise legitimate purchasers to leave a good review, and can sometimes offer gift cards if you do – this is bad too as it can conceal the true feedback.
Do some homework on the retailers
It would be great if there was a universal way to check a retailer before you buy, but I've spent some time looking and there's not much that works universally. F-Secure has an online shopping checker, but you'd need a subscription to get the full story.
There are some things you can do though, that might help keep you safe. For example, seen an interesting product on TikTok? Does the link open to a store you've never heard of? Those are generally good warnings.
So, if you haven't heard of the retailer before, check sites like TrustPilot, Yelp or Google Reviews – and, ideally, several of them for each site you're not sure about. If you can't find much evidence of the shop existing, or having any reviews, then you might want to rethink buying from them.
Check the registered address too. Most companies will have an "about" section, and reputable ones will make it really easy to work out where they are based. So have a look for that, and plonk the address into Google Maps. Does it look like a business, or someone's house? That might not be an issue in itself, lots of small businesses operate out of homes – but what are you buying – is it a bespoke piece of craft, or a television. The type of product can help inform how credible the business is.
I've recently encountered some stores offering Christmas products that will have a US address, alongside one in China's industrial cities. These products are advertised with AI videos, which offer a lot of implausible functionality and I deeply suspect the product you get will be quite disappointing in comparison.
So bear that in mind, Chinese products are often excellent and sites like AliExpress are pretty reputable. But there are also products made to a low price, that may not be either safe or useful – so it is worth thinking carefully about what you splash out for.
If this all feels like a bit of a headache then you could try paying for someone, or, in fact, some thing, to do it for you. Some security software does come with a fake shop detector for your browser. NordVPN's Complete plan is a good example of that. You can take a look at NordVPN's Black Friday deal here.
And finally...
A word of reassurance as I wrap up, and start my own shopping quest for "a pillow that doesn't make me wake up with a sore neck". If you happen to end up with a product that isn't as described, there are things you can do.
The first port of call is to complain to the business itself. If you get nowhere, then you can speak to your bank and start a dispute, this can often be done through your banking app too. Mastercard, Visa and Amex all offer good consumer protection, for credit card purchases there's a law backing it up, but only for transactions over £100.
In most countries, a debit card has the same protection as a credit card. It may not be enshrined in law, but the scheme operators (Mastercard, Visa) enforce it through their own rules.
The exception to this is the U.S. where debit does not get treated the same. So, use credit if you're one of our cherished American readers. Amex has slightly different rules and procedures, because it is a bank – but the principal will be the same.
