articles.title: Cómo programar mensajes en WhatsApp sin usar apps de terceros
articles.text:
WhatsApp sumó una función nativa para programar mensajes, sin depender de aplicaciones externas. La herramienta permite redactar un texto en cualquier momento y fijar su envío entre 10 minutos y 14 días después, tanto en chats individuales como grupales.
La novedad acerca a la app a opciones ya conocidas en plataformas de correo electrónico como Gmail y Outlook, y resuelve situaciones en las que el contenido está listo pero el horario no es el adecuado: un saludo de cumpleaños a la medianoche del país donde vive el destinatario, un recordatorio laboral o un mensaje de aliento antes de un examen, sin necesidad de permanecer pendiente del reloj.
Pasos para programar un mensaje en WhatsApp
Para activar la función, el proceso comienza en el chat individual o grupal elegido, donde se escribe el texto que se quiere enviar. Luego, en lugar de tocar el botón de enviar de forma habitual, se debe mantener presionado ese mismo botón. Ahí aparece la opción para seleccionar la fecha y hora de la entrega.
La aplicación admite un rango de programación de hasta 14 días, con un mínimo de 10 minutos de anticipación. Una vez confirmado el horario, el mensaje queda en espera dentro de la plataforma y se envía de forma automática en el momento definido por quien lo creó.
El envío de contenido de una sola vista, para fotos y videos, mantiene el mismo mecanismo de siempre y no se modifica con esta incorporación.
Chats individuales y grupos: dónde funciona la programación
La función de mensajes programados está disponible tanto para conversaciones entre dos personas como para grupos, lo que amplía su utilidad.
En el plano individual, permite preparar un saludo privado con anticipación. En comunidades, familias o equipos de trabajo, administradores o integrantes pueden dejar listos avisos para que lleguen a todos en el horario acordado.
En los grupos, en particular, la herramienta evita depender de que alguien esté conectado a una hora determinada para compartir información. Un recordatorio de reunión, una fecha límite o una convocatoria puede redactarse con anticipación y quedar previsto para el momento oportuno, sin alterar el funcionamiento habitual de la conversación.
Textos, fotos y videos: qué formatos admite la herramienta
La programación no se limita a los mensajes de texto. La función también admite fotos y videos, por lo que es posible dejar lista una felicitación acompañada de una imagen o un aviso audiovisual dirigido a familiares, compañeros o integrantes de una comunidad.
Cuando el contenido llega al destinatario, se visualiza como un mensaje corriente. No incluye ninguna marca especial que indique que fue preparado con anticipación ni exige una acción adicional de quien lo recibe.
La diferencia se concentra del lado de quien envía el mensaje, que organiza la entrega para una fecha posterior sin que eso se note del otro lado de la conversación.
Cómo revisar o eliminar un mensaje programado antes del envío
Quienes utilicen esta función pueden consultar los envíos pendientes antes de que se cumpla el horario elegido. Esa posibilidad permite controlar los mensajes ya previstos y modificar la decisión si las circunstancias cambian, por ejemplo, si una reunión se cancela o un saludo deja de tener sentido.
También es posible eliminar un mensaje programado antes de su envío. La eliminación evita que el contenido llegue al chat seleccionado, siempre que se realice antes del momento fijado.
Esta gestión de pendientes ofrece una alternativa para corregir errores o retirar información que ya no deba compartirse, sin necesidad de recurrir a herramientas externas.
Entrega garantizada aunque el teléfono esté apagado o sin batería
Uno de los aspectos que la compañía remarcó es que la entrega del mensaje no depende de que el teléfono permanezca encendido, con batería o conectado a internet en el horario previsto.
Según explicó WhatsApp, el mensaje aparecerá en el chat elegido aun si el dispositivo está apagado o se quedó sin carga en el momento en que estaba programado el envío.
La empresa señaló además que estos mensajes mantienen el cifrado de extremo a extremo que aplica a las conversaciones personales. Esto implica que el contenido permanece protegido durante todo el proceso y que terceros, incluida la propia compañía, no pueden acceder a su contenido.
Con un límite de hasta dos semanas de anticipación, la función suma una herramienta de planificación a una aplicación utilizada para conversaciones personales, grupos familiares y coordinación laboral, y permite dejar listo un mensaje apenas surge la idea para que llegue en el horario más conveniente para cada destinatario.

articles.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
articles.text:
Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday.
Three of the attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major disruptions reported. The victims have not been named, and it is not known who is behind the attacks.
Florian Schütz, who directs Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre, gave the figures in an interview with public broadcaster SRF.
All five cases were reported in recent days. Small and medium-sized companies were among the organizations hit, and they came forward voluntarily.
The agency's first notice, a security advisory published on Tuesday, said the agents had compromised the victims' IT systems in every case known at that point. Neither the notice nor yesterday's broadcast interview explains why the count changed.
"These cases represent a shift in the cyber threat landscape," the advisory said.
The targeted operators are in at least two sectors. Electricity, drinking water, and telecommunications suppliers are examples of what Switzerland counts as critical infrastructure, according to a news agency report on the interview.
The attacks involve what the Swiss agency calls agentic offensive frameworks, AI agents that find security weaknesses and carry out attacks on their own. Its advisory named ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI as examples of agents reachable over the internet, not as the tools used in the five cases.
The agents are often used to scan for known, unpatched weaknesses and can run many attacks in parallel, the agency says. When defenses respond, the agents switch methods, leaving companies significantly less time to detect an intrusion and respond.
The number of AI attack tools freely reachable online has nearly doubled since October, according to the agency. The figure counts available tools, not attacks or victims.
Raphael Reischuk, co-founder of Switzerland's National Test Institute for Cybersecurity, expects a larger wave of attacks and says companies underestimate the risk.
Italy's national computer security incident response team, CSIRT Italia, described mass compromise campaigns in an official bulletin this week. In the cases it observed firsthand, AI-directed autonomous agents broke into a large number of systems within a few hours.
The agents adapt their actions within seconds, run in parallel without human input, and chain vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and compromised credentials together, the bulletin says. It names ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI, and DeepSeek Harness, an open-source agent whose Red Team Mode uses a built-in prompt to get past the underlying model's safety limits.
Each action on its own looks like normal user or API traffic. Detection depends on context: where requests come from, how often they arrive, how much data moves, and the order in which things happen.
Britain's National Cyber Security Centre reported the same pattern in agency guidance this week. "Since September 2026, the NCSC has seen a marked rise in AI-assisted cyber attacks," it said.
Some incidents caused downtime on internet-facing services, and others gave attackers a foothold for further agent-driven activity. The weaknesses are old ones: credentials committed to code repositories, misconfigured infrastructure-as-code, default or missing authentication, and weaknesses in APIs.
What has changed is the speed, persistence, and low cost of the attacks, the British agency says. The frameworks are also noisy, which makes them easier to detect.
The European Commission has already been hit. Attackers using ARTEX broke into its human resources, medical reimbursement, and translation systems, the Commission has confirmed, in an earlier intrusion first detected on October 22.
What Defenders Should Do
The strongest common advice from the three agencies is to shrink the time attackers have. Their recommendations overlap:
- Install critical security updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours of release (Switzerland), and patch flaws already being exploited first (Italy).
- Disconnect or isolate internet-facing systems that cannot be patched quickly (Italy).
- Reduce what is reachable from the internet, using geo-blocking, allow lists, and authentication in front of services (Switzerland, UK).
- Require MFA or passkeys on everything reachable from the internet, and grant the lowest privileges that work (Switzerland).
- Watch for unusual behavior and data volumes (Switzerland), and correlate logs: agent activity shows up as bursts of requests and high error rates (UK).
- Put bot challenges on high-value endpoints, and use decoys such as honeytokens to catch and slow agents (UK).
- Load Italy's published indicator feeds into monitoring tools, noting that the indicators change quickly and are valid only for their stated timeframes (Italy).

articles.title: Black Friday : 15 PC portables à moins de 500 €, jusqu’à -50 %
articles.text:
Ce vendredi 27 novembre, jour J du Black Friday, Amazon, Boulanger et Cdiscount font baisser le prix de leurs PC portables d’entrée de gamme. Nous avons retenu 15 modèles de marque pour les petits budgets, de l’écran OLED au Chromebook, en vérifiant sur chaque fiche le prix de référence affiché par le marchand.
Aucun de ces 15 PC portables n’est passé entre les mains de notre rédaction : chaque section s’appuie sur la fiche du marchand et du fabricant, et signale ce qu’il faut vérifier avant d’acheter. La sélection couvre les PC Windows, Intel, AMD ou Snapdragon, et les Chromebook, avec des remises de 21 % à 50 % sur le prix de référence. Les plus fortes économies en euros reviennent au Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 Ryzen 5 et au Dell 15 Core i5, 400 € de moins chacun, la plus forte en pourcentage au Lenovo, à -50 %.
- HP OmniBook 3 16 pouces OLED (Snapdragon X, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 469,99 € au lieu de 799,99 € (-41 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 (Ryzen 5, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 399,99 € au lieu de 799,99 € (-50 %)
- Dell 15 (Core i5-1334U, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 449 € au lieu de 849 € (-47 %)
- HP OmniBook 3 16 pouces (Ryzen 5 7520U, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 479,99 € au lieu de 839,99 € (-42 %)
- ASUS Vivobook S14 (Snapdragon X, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 449,99 € au lieu de 699,99 € (-35 %)
- HP 14 pouces (Snapdragon X, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 499,99 € au lieu de 849,99 € (-41 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 15 pouces (Snapdragon X, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 499,99 € au lieu de 799,99 € (-37 %)
- ASUS Vivobook 15 (Core 5 320, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 449,99 € au lieu de 699,99 € (-35 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces (Core 3, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 429,99 € au lieu de 549,99 € (-21 %)
- HP OmniBook 3 17 pouces (Core 3 100U, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 479,99 € au lieu de 799,99 € (-40 %)
- Dell 15 (Ryzen 5 130, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 449 € au lieu de 629 € (-28 %)
- ASUS Vivobook Go 15 (Intel N150, 8 Go, 128 Go) à 299,99 € au lieu de 499,99 € (-40 %)
- Lenovo Duet Chromebook 11 pouces (8 Go, 128 Go) à 299,99 € au lieu de 499,99 € (-40 %)
- Acer Chromebook Plus 514 (Core 3 N355, 8 Go, 128 Go) à 299 € au lieu de 399 € (-25 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 Chromebook 14 pouces (4 Go, 128 Go) à 164,99 € au lieu de 249,99 € (-34 %)
HP OmniBook 3 OLED : un écran OLED de 16 pouces sous les 500 €, à 469,99 €
Ce HP OmniBook 3 associe une dalle OLED de 16 pouces en 1 920 x 1 200 pixels à une puce Snapdragon X, avec 8 Go de LPDDR5x et un SSD de 256 Go, pour 1,7 kg. Boulanger reprend l’autonomie annoncée par HP : 1 jour et 19 heures. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un écran OLED : des noirs profonds et un contraste élevé, propres à la technologie OLED.
- Une autonomie annoncée hors norme : 1 jour et 19 heures selon la fiche constructeur reprise par Boulanger.
- À savoir : le chargeur n’est pas inclus, selon la fiche Boulanger, et la puce Snapdragon X fait tourner Windows sur Arm, avec lequel certains logiciels et jeux restent incompatibles.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 : un PC portable Ryzen 5 à moitié prix, à 399,99 €
Ce Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 (15AMN8) embarque un processeur AMD Ryzen 5, 8 Go de RAM et un SSD de 256 Go, derrière un écran IPS Full HD antireflet de 15,6 pouces. Il pèse 1,62 kg, passe au Wi-Fi 6 et répond à la norme militaire MIL-STD-810H. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 400 € de moins : sur le prix barré de 799,99 € affiché par Amazon.
- Robuste et bien équipé : certification MIL-STD-810H, Wi-Fi 6, HDMI, USB-C et cache pour la webcam.
- À savoir : il est vendu sans chargeur, comme l’indique le titre de la fiche Amazon.
Dell 15 Core i5 : 400 € de remise sur ce PC de 15,6 pouces, à 449 €
Le Dell 15 (DC15250) associe un Intel Core i5-1334U à 8 Go de RAM et à un SSD de 512 Go, sur un écran de 15,6 pouces avec pavé numérique. Dell y ajoute la recharge rapide ExpressCharge et deux ans de service sur site après diagnostic à distance. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 512 Go de stockage : le double des modèles en 256 Go de cette sélection.
- Deux ans de service sur site : Dell intervient à domicile après un diagnostic à distance.
- À savoir : 8 Go de RAM suffisent à la bureautique, mais limitent le multitâche sous Windows 11.
HP OmniBook 3 16 pouces : 360 € de moins chez Cdiscount, à 479,99 €
Cette version de l’OmniBook 3 embarque un AMD Ryzen 5 7520U, 8 Go de LPDDR5 et un SSD de 512 Go, derrière un écran antireflet de 16 pouces en 1 920 x 1 200 pixels. Elle pèse 1,64 kg et HP annonce jusqu’à 9 h 15 d’autonomie selon le protocole MobileMark 25. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un grand écran 16:10 : 16 pouces en 1 920 x 1 200 pixels, plus haut qu’une dalle 16:9 classique.
- 512 Go de SSD : de la place pour les documents, les photos et les logiciels.
- À savoir : Cdiscount affiche sur la fiche un code 50D449, qui retire 50 € dès 449 € d’achat. Il n’est pas inclus dans le prix de cette sélection.
ASUS Vivobook S14 : un 14 pouces Snapdragon X perd 250 €, à 449,99 €
Ce Vivobook S14 (S5408QAB) repose sur une puce Snapdragon X à 8 cœurs, avec 8 Go de LPDDR5X et un SSD NVMe de 256 Go. Son écran de 14 pouces passe au format 16:10 en 1 920 x 1 200 pixels, et son châssis répond à la norme MIL-STD-810H. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une connectique complète : deux USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 et deux USB-A, malgré un profil fin.
- Un format 14 pouces : un écran 16:10, plus facile à glisser dans un sac qu’un 15,6 pouces.
- À savoir : il est vendu sans chargeur, et Windows sur Arm reste incompatible avec certains logiciels et jeux.
HP 14 Snapdragon X : 1,4 kg et 512 Go de SSD, à 499,99 €
Ce PC portable HP (14-hz0037nfx) mise sur la légèreté, avec 1,4 kg sur la balance, et sur une puce Snapdragon X épaulée par 8 Go de RAM et un SSD de 512 Go. Son écran de 14 pouces affiche 1 920 x 1 200 pixels, et Boulanger reprend l’autonomie annoncée de 1 jour et 8 heures. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Léger : 1,4 kg sur la balance, facile à emporter au quotidien.
- Une grosse autonomie annoncée : 1 jour et 8 heures selon la fiche constructeur reprise par Boulanger.
- À savoir : le chargeur n’est pas inclus, selon la fiche Boulanger, et certains logiciels restent incompatibles avec Windows sur Arm.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 Snapdragon X : 300 € de moins chez Boulanger, à 499,99 €
Cette version de l’IdeaPad Slim 3 (15Q8X10) passe à la puce Snapdragon X, avec 8 Go de LPDDR5x, un SSD de 512 Go et un écran de 15,3 pouces en 1 920 x 1 200 pixels. Elle pèse 1,6 kg, et Boulanger reprend une autonomie annoncée de 18 h 30. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 18 h 30 d’autonomie annoncées : de quoi tenir une journée de cours ou de travail.
- Un pack avec sac au même prix : Boulanger propose aussi cette configuration avec un sac à dos, à 499,99 €.
- À savoir : le chargeur n’est pas inclus, selon la fiche Boulanger.
ASUS Vivobook 15 : un Intel Core 5 à 6 cœurs, à 449,99 €
Le Vivobook 15 (X1504MA) embarque un Intel Core 5 320 à 6 cœurs, qui grimpe jusqu’à 4,6 GHz, avec 8 Go de DDR5 et un SSD NVMe de 256 Go. Son écran IPS Full HD de 15,6 pouces est certifié TÜV Rheinland, et son châssis répond à la norme MIL-STD-810H. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un processeur Intel x86 : une compatibilité totale avec les logiciels Windows.
- Un cache pour la webcam : un volet physique masque la caméra 720p.
- À savoir : il est vendu sans chargeur, comme l’indique la fiche Amazon, et 256 Go se remplissent vite.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces : un châssis alu et un clavier rétroéclairé, à 429,99 €
Cet IdeaPad Slim 3 (14IWC11) réunit un Intel Core 3, 8 Go de RAM et un SSD de 256 Go dans un châssis en aluminium gris, avec un écran WUXGA de 14 pouces et un clavier AZERTY rétroéclairé. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un clavier rétroéclairé : pratique pour taper dans la pénombre.
- Un format compact : 14 pouces au format WUXGA, en 1 920 x 1 200 pixels.
- À savoir : le titre de la fiche Amazon annonce un écran OLED, sa description une dalle IPS. Vérifiez ce point avant d’acheter. Le chargeur n’est pas inclus.
HP OmniBook 3 17 pouces : le grand écran perd 320 €, à 479,99 €
Cet OmniBook 3 (17-dk0049nfx) offre le plus grand écran de cette sélection, 17,3 pouces, avec un Intel Core 3 100U, 8 Go de RAM et un SSD de 512 Go. Il pèse 2 kg, et Boulanger reprend une autonomie annoncée de 10 h 18. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un écran de 17,3 pouces : confortable pour la bureautique et les films, sur un bureau.
- 512 Go de SSD : un stockage confortable à ce prix.
- À savoir : la définition se limite à 1 600 x 900 pixels, moins fine qu’un écran Full HD, et le chargeur n’est pas inclus selon la fiche Boulanger.
Dell 15 Ryzen 5 : un écran antireflet de 300 nits, à 449 €
Ce Dell 15 (D15265) associe un AMD Ryzen 5 130 à 8 Go de RAM et à un SSD de 512 Go, avec un écran Full HD WVA antireflet de 15,6 pouces annoncé à 300 nits. Il pèse 1,66 kg, embarque le Wi-Fi 6 et une touche Copilot. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une recharge par USB-C : compatible USB-C Power Delivery, en plus d’un adaptateur 65 W.
- Deux ans de service sur site : Dell intervient après un diagnostic à distance.
- À savoir : aucun adaptateur secteur n’est fourni, précise la fiche Amazon.
ASUS Vivobook Go 15 : un PC Windows de 15,6 pouces sous les 300 €, à 299,99 €
Le Vivobook Go 15 (E1504TA) vise les usages simples avec un Intel N150 à 4 cœurs, 8 Go de LPDDR5 et 128 Go de stockage UFS 2.1, derrière un écran IPS Full HD de 15,6 pouces. Il pèse 1,63 kg et dispose d’un volet de confidentialité sur la webcam. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 200 € de moins : sur le prix barré de 499,99 € affiché par Amazon.
- Léger pour un 15,6 pouces : 1,63 kg, facile à emporter en cours.
- À savoir : 128 Go de stockage se remplissent vite, et le processeur N150 se cantonne à la navigation et à la bureautique. Il est vendu sans chargeur.
Lenovo Duet Chromebook : un 2-en-1 tactile avec clavier inclus, à 299,99 €
Ce Chromebook 2-en-1 de Lenovo prend la forme d’une tablette de 11 pouces en WUXGA, avec un support folio et un clavier inclus dans la boîte. Il embarque une puce MediaTek Kompanio 838, 8 Go de RAM et 128 Go de stockage, sous ChromeOS. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Tablette et PC : l’écran tactile se détache, le clavier et le support sont fournis.
- 8 Go de RAM : une configuration confortable pour ChromeOS.
- À savoir : ChromeOS ne fait pas tourner les logiciels Windows ; il s’appuie sur les applications web et Android.
Acer Chromebook Plus 514 : les outils IA de Google sur un 14 pouces, à 299 €
Ce Chromebook Plus de 14 pouces en WUXGA embarque un Intel Core 3 N355, 8 Go de LPDDR5X et 128 Go de stockage eMMC. Le label Plus de Google lui ouvre des outils comme Gemini ou la gomme magique de Google Photos, et son clavier est rétroéclairé. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Le label Chromebook Plus : des performances minimales garanties par Google et ses outils d’IA.
- Un clavier rétroéclairé : pratique pour taper dans la pénombre.
- À savoir : le stockage eMMC est plus lent qu’un SSD, et ChromeOS ne fait pas tourner les logiciels Windows.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 Chromebook : le moins cher de la sélection, à 164,99 €
Ce Chromebook de 14 pouces (14M868) affiche un écran Full HD antireflet, une puce MediaTek, 4 Go de RAM et 128 Go de stockage, pour 1,3 kg. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Le prix : 85 € de moins que le prix barré affiché par Cdiscount.
- Léger : 1,3 kg et 1,86 cm d’épaisseur.
- À savoir : avec 4 Go de RAM, il se destine à la navigation, aux mails et aux documents en ligne.
Black Friday et Cyber Monday : les dates et le code à connaître
Le Black Friday tombe ce vendredi 27 novembre, et le Cyber Monday suit le lundi 30 novembre. Chez Cdiscount, le code 50D449 affiché sur une partie des fiches retire 50 € dès 449 € d’achat : les prix de cette sélection, relevés le 26 novembre, ne l’incluent pas. Les autres offres que nous suivons sont réunies sur notre page Black Friday.
PC portable à moins de 500 € : que vérifier avant d’acheter ?
Trois points départagent les modèles de ce budget. La mémoire vive d’abord : 8 Go suffisent à la bureautique, 4 Go cantonnent un PC à la navigation. Le stockage ensuite : 128 Go en eMMC ou en UFS se remplissent vite, un SSD de 512 Go laisse de la marge. Le processeur enfin : une puce Snapdragon fait tourner Windows sur Arm, qui n’accepte pas tous les logiciels, et un Chromebook ne fait tourner que des applications web et Android. Vérifiez aussi la présence du chargeur dans la boîte : plusieurs modèles de cette sélection sont vendus sans.
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Comment profiter des offres du Black Friday ?

articles.title: Black Friday is the perfect time to pick up a new 3D Printer — these are the best deals we've spotted so far
articles.text:
Black Friday is the perfect time to pick up a new 3D Printer — these are the best deals we've spotted so far
Save money on a new 3D printer.
Black Friday sales season is in full swing, and there are a host of great 3D printer deals on offer, both directly from all the main manufacturers and from retailers such as Amazon. We've sourced some of our favorite deals from around the web and collated them all here in this handy 3D printer deals roundup to help save you some money if you're in the market for a brand new 3D printer or looking to upgrade. So grab yourself one of the best 3D printers and a few rolls of filament to start you on your printing journey.
Amazon and manufacturers such as Anycubic, Elegoo, Bambu Lab, and more have plenty of deals on mainstream FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling) printers that utilize common filaments such as PLA and PETG, and also great offers on Resin, SLA (Stereolithography Apparatus) 3D printers, which utilize layers of cured resin to produce highly detailed prints. All you need to do if choose which method of printing you prefer.
Many of the current deals that we've featured in this roundup have detailed reviews available, and some may be included on our lists of the best 3D printers, best multi-color 3D printers, or best budget 3D printers. We also have an extensive library of 3D printer reviews to support our picks.

articles.title: Epic Games Store regala Bread and Fred y un paquete de Firestone hasta el 3 de diciembre
articles.text:
Epic Games Store regala dos propuestas para computadora: el juego cooperativo de plataformas Bread and Fred, que cuesta USD 14,99, y un paquete de objetos del juego de rol Firestone. Ambas están disponibles hasta el 3 de diciembre a las 16:00 UTC (11:00 en la costa este de Estados Unidos).
Los datos de fechas y precios figuran en el catálogo de promociones que la propia tienda publica para su página de juegos gratis. Según ese registro, las dos ofertas empezaron el 26 de noviembre a las 16:00 UTC y terminan el 3 de diciembre a la misma hora.
Quien reclame un juego antes del cierre lo conserva en su biblioteca de forma permanente, aunque la promoción termine y aunque no lo instale de inmediato. Reclamar no exige ningún método de pago: el total del pedido aparece en cero.
Qué se puede reclamar esta semana
Bread and Fred es un juego para dos personas en el que dos pingüinos van atados por una cuerda y deben escalar una montaña nevada. La cuerda sirve para balancearse sobre huecos, pero un salto fallido puede arrastrar al compañero hacia abajo, según la descripción del sitio de videojuegos Nerdzap, que lo cataloga como “jugable” en la consola portátil Steam Deck.
El medio citado también señala que las reseñas en la página del juego en Epic son mixtas: a algunos jugadores les gusta la física de la cuerda y a otros les parece frustrante la escalada. El juego no tiene versión nativa para Android ni iOS, de modo que la oferta aplica a la tienda de escritorio.
Firestone es otra cosa. Se trata de un juego de rol en el que los héroes combaten solos, incluso cuando el jugador no está conectado. El juego base ya era gratuito, por lo que lo que Epic regala es un paquete de contenido que la tienda valora en USD 100.
El paquete incluye 200 gemas, 30 cofres con equipo y joyas para los héroes, un aspecto exclusivo llamado The Gladiator para el personaje Talia, además de polvo, pergaminos y fichas. Para obtenerlo hay que instalar Firestone desde Epic y entrar al juego antes de que termine la promoción.
El sitio Pro Gamer agrega una condición para las cuentas nuevas: deben llegar a la etapa 15 del juego para que el paquete llegue de forma automática al inventario. Ese requisito no figura en el catálogo de la tienda, por lo que conviene revisarlo en la página de Firestone antes de instalarlo.
Cómo canjearlos paso a paso
El proceso es el mismo para cualquier juego gratuito de la tienda, según las guías de los sitios GhostKeys y Times of Games, que coinciden en los pasos. Epic puede modificar los textos de los botones, así que la redacción exacta puede variar.
Primero, abrir la página de juegos gratis de Epic Games Store, desde el navegador o desde el programa de escritorio, e iniciar sesión con una cuenta de Epic. Si no se tiene, se puede crear una sin costo.
Segundo, elegir el juego y entrar a su página. Allí aparece el botón “Obtener” (“Get” en la versión en inglés) junto al precio habitual tachado. Al pulsarlo, la tienda lleva a una pantalla de pedido con total de cero.
Tercero, pulsar “Realizar pedido” (“Place Order”). Con eso el juego queda en la biblioteca de la cuenta y puede instalarse en ese momento o más adelante. En el caso de Firestone, además hay que instalarlo y abrirlo desde Epic para activar el paquete.
Epic suele anunciar los títulos de la semana siguiente cuando arranca cada rotación. El catálogo de la tienda muestra que Strange Antiquities, un juego que cuesta USD 17,99, pasará a ser gratuito el 3 de diciembre a las 16:00 UTC, cuando termine la promoción actual, y seguirá disponible hasta el 10 de diciembre a la misma hora.

articles.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
articles.text:
Details have emerged about a new zero-day vulnerability in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution.
The proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, which has yet to be assigned a CVE identifier, has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT.
"I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests," a security researcher who goes by the online alias "ek0ms savi0r" said. "No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface."
The shortcoming affects Cacti Core 1.2.31, the latest version, when the guest account is enabled. It's worth noting that the guest account is disabled by default starting with Cacti version 0.8.7.
At a high level, the vulnerability allows an attacker to abuse the guest access to write an unvalidated value (i.e., non-numeric text) into a setting called "preview_graphs_per_page" via "auth_profile.php?action=update_data." The configuration parameter controls how many graphs are displayed per page when viewing graphs in Preview Mode.
The crafted value takes the form of arbitrary SQL strings that can be turned into a second-order SQL injection by taking advantage of the fact that Cacti does not validate that the user-provided input is actually an integer value. This, in turn, opens the door for arbitrary SQL query execution when the graph preview page ("graph_view.php") is loaded with default filters.
The SQL query demonstrated by "ek0ms savi0r" is an UPDATE statement to modify a record in Cacti's poller table. In the final stage of the attack, the realtime poller endpoint ("graph_realtime.php") is invoked from the same guest session, which causes the modified row from the poller table to be read and passed as input to PHP's popen() function without any allowlist or sanitization checks.
The researcher has pointed out four failures that ultimately make it possible to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution -
- The guest can write a numeric setting as an arbitrary string
- The stored default bypasses request validation
- Cacti's PHP PDO database driver accepts stacked statements through the SQL LIMIT clause
- The poller executes a database-stored command string
Successful exploitation of the flaw can allow an attacker to compromise the Cacti server and provide a pivot point to the target network as it exposes sensitive data, or even suppress alerts by modifying the poller table.
"Because Cacti often stores credentials and connection details for routers, switches, servers, and other devices across a network, an attacker who reaches this level of command execution can gain a foothold reaching far beyond the monitoring server itself," watchTowr said in an advisory.
In the absence of a fix, users are advised to disable the guest account and restrict access to the Cacti web interface to mitigate potential risks. It's also essential to review poller configuration entries for unexpected command values and apply the fixes as soon as they become available.

Ele soma conectividade tripla (Lightspeed sem fio, Bluetooth e USB-C com fio), teclas double-shot em PBT, placa superior em alumínio escovado e mapeamento avançado com o recurso KEYCONTROL.
Para quem busca o topo de linha sem fio da marca com perfil baixo e acabamento reforçado, é uma opção direta e versátil. O uso simultâneo durante o carregamento via cabo evita interrupções em sessões longas.
O Logitech G915 TKL Lightspeed oferece mobilidade e resposta sem atrasos perceptíveis em uma estrutura metálica compacta. A ausência do bloco numérico facilita setups com menos área livre e torna o transporte mais prático para eventos ou mudanças de bancada.
A ficha técnica destaca a transmissão sem fio Lightspeed de 1 ms, corpo com estrutura em liga de alumínio e base reforçada, roda de volume dedicada e teclas de mídia de toque suave. Também permite operar conectado via USB para carregar a bateria enquanto você continua jogando.
Ainda que tenha sido sucedido pela geração G915 X em recursos mais recentes, o G915 TKL permanece relevante quando surge com preço competitivo. É indicado para quem quer um teclado sem fio de perfil baixo e visual sóbrio sem abrir mão de controles de mídia físicos.
O Logitech G515 TKL Lightspeed combina digitação silenciosa e conforto em um corpo fino voltado a jogos e trabalho. Seu design tenkeyless de 22 mm de altura reduz o cansaço e abre espaço na mesa para gestos largos de mira.
Por dentro, o modelo reúne switches mecânicos GL de perfil baixo pré-lubrificados de fábrica (com opções tátil ou linear e atuação a 1,3 mm), teclas PBT de dupla moldagem e camadas internas com redução de ruído. A conectividade tripla traz Lightspeed de 1 ms, Bluetooth, uso com fio USB e pareamento 2:1 para compartilhar receptor com mouse compatível, além de bateria de até 36 horas e suporte ao KEYCONTROL.
Ele funciona como um meio-termo inteligente dentro da linha sem fio de baixo perfil da Logitech G. Entrega boa parte da experiência moderna de customização e acústica mais contida com proposta mais acessível que o G915 X TKL.
O Logitech G Pro prioriza portabilidade e precisão direta para quem joga títulos competitivos com foco em desempenho. O formato compacto sem teclado numérico e o cabo removível facilitam levar o periférico em mochilas para campeonatos ou encontros presenciais.
O teclado utiliza switches mecânicos GX Clicky com feedback tátil e sonoro marcante, além de 12 teclas F programáveis via G HUB e memória integrada para perfis de iluminação. O cabo destacável conta com encaixe de três pinos para manter a conexão firme durante partidas intensas.
Trata-se de um modelo com fio focado no essencial competitivo, sem distrações extras na carcaça. Vale a atenção apenas ao conector micro USB removível e à preferência por switches com clique audível antes da compra.
O Logitech G713 aposta em conforto prolongado e estética clara para setups que valorizam visual e ergonomia. O apoio para pulsos macio incluso e o formato TKL ajudam a manter as mãos relaxadas em maratonas de jogo ou digitação.
Na parte técnica, o modelo traz conexão USB-C com fio destacável, controles de mídia dedicados, iluminação RGB Lightsync por tecla e no perímetro, além de opções de switches mecânicos GX (tátil, linear ou clicky). Integrante da linha Aurora, ele também aceita keycaps e placas superiores intercambiáveis vendidas separadamente para mudar o visual.
É uma escolha indicada para quem prefere conexão com fio estável, apoio acolchoado de série e forte apelo estético. Atende bem tanto a quem joga quanto a quem passa horas digitando textos.
O Logitech G413 SE entrega durabilidade e simplicidade para quem quer um teclado mecânico direto ao ponto. O layout completo com bloco numérico atende bem quem alterna entre jogos e planilhas ou digitação frequente sem depender de atalhos.
Ele conta com switches mecânicos táteis, keycaps em PBT resistentes ao desgaste e ao brilho, iluminação em LED branco e anti-ghosting com sobreposição de 6 teclas. A proposta dispensa RGB colorido e recursos extras para focar na resistência estrutural e no funcionamento plug-and-play.

É uma alternativa coerente para quem não faz questão de switch mecânico e prefere silêncio, apoio integrado e preço mais contido. Funciona bem como primeiro teclado gamer ou para quem divide o PC com outras tarefas.
Comece definindo o espaço disponível na mesa e os gêneros de jogo que você mais joga. Modelos TKL liberam área para o mouse, enquanto teclados full-size mantêm o bloco numérico útil para produtividade e planilhas.
Em seguida, avalie a conexão (sem fio Lightspeed ou cabo USB), a altura das teclas (perfil baixo ou tradicional) e o tipo de resposta do switch (linear, tátil ou clicky). Também vale conferir o layout das teclas (ABNT2 ou padrão internacional) e a presença de controles de mídia dedicados.
Lightspeed é a tecnologia de conexão sem fio de 2,4 GHz da Logitech G desenvolvida para entregar baixa latência e estabilidade de sinal em jogos. Na prática, ela busca aproximar a resposta sem fio da experiência de um cabo USB, evitando atrasos perceptíveis em comandos rápidos.
O melhor teclado custo-benefício depende do seu orçamento e do tipo de uso: o G515 TKL Lightspeed se destaca entre os sem fio modernos de baixo perfil, enquanto o G413 SE atende quem busca um mecânico durável mais acessível e o G213 serve a quem quer gastar menos com foco em silêncio e conforto. Avalie o preço promocional no momento da compra e se você precisa de conexão sem fio ou se o cabo resolve bem o seu setup.
O Logitech G Hub centraliza a configuração de efeitos de iluminação RGB Lightsync, perfis por jogo, macros e atalhos das teclas. Em modelos compatíveis com o recurso KEYCONTROL, o software também permite criar camadas e atribuir múltiplas funções por tecla.
Teclados mecânicos costumam oferecer resposta mais consistente, durabilidade elevada dos switches e variedade de sensações (linear, tátil ou clicky) para jogos mais exigentes. Teclados de membrana, como o G213 com teclas Mech-Dome, entregam toque mais silencioso e preço menor, sendo suficientes para jogos casuais e uso misto.
A sigla TKL significa Tenkeyless, ou seja, um teclado sem o bloco numérico à direita. Remover essas teclas reduz a largura total do periférico, dando mais espaço para o movimento do mouse e deixando a mesa mais organizada.
Os teclados da linha Logitech G são compatíveis com Windows e macOS, variando conforme o modelo e o software de configuração. Em consoles como PS5 e Xbox, a conexão USB ou sem fio básica pode funcionar em jogos que aceitam teclado nativamente, mas recursos avançados como macros e perfis completos do G Hub dependem do computador e do suporte de cada jogo.

A great selection of soldering tips, a large LCD screen, clear controls and a bonus hot air rework wand make the Yihua 995D+ the best option for those who solder for a living.
Read moreRead less▼
The Yihua 995D+ can reach temperatures of 480 °C (896 °F), which gives more than enough heat to solder and reflow even the heaviest solder joint. This soldering station has excellent thermal properties, letting you start soldering speaker wire with ease.
The stand is compatible with right and left-handed users, as it's separated from the main station, so you'll have free access to the soldering iron while reducing the number of cables trailing across your workbench. It has three preset channels to let you switch between jobs quickly, and it feels great to handle, thanks to a non-slip coating and flexible silicone cord to stop any melting accidents. You've also got a good number of tips, from precision tips to heavy tips for large projects.
The hot air gun has a similar cable for protection and is easy to handle. You'll need to select the correct controls before using the central knob to handle temperature and airflow. After that, it's easy to control both.
The Yihua 995D+ is an excellent soldering station for both beginners and pros alike. It gets the job done, looks good, and keeps more cash in your pocket.
Don't need hot air but need a desktop soldering station? The Yihua 939D+ is for you.
If all you need is a reliable and compact desktop soldering station, then the Yihua 939D+ is a good option. This compact soldering station comes with a temperature range of 392°F to 896°F (200°C to 480°C) and ships with a selection of soldering tips to cover many different use cases, from precision to bulky solder joints.
A solid and dependable soldering station that reduces the cost by omitting hot air rework functionality. This is a soldering station that I could personally use all day, everyday!
Read moreRead less▼
It comes with 75W of power, making it suitable for heavier solders like speaker cables. Use the dial to control your settings and the LED display will update accordingly.
Helping hands for successful soldering
Soldering can be a tricky task to complete, and an extra pair of hands is always welcome. Luckily, you don't need a pair of human hands to get the job done, as this helping hands tool can substitute perfectly.
Soldering veterans will know the less-than-glossy metal armature and magnifying glass combos that are available, but this set of helping hands is a little bit different. It comes as a magnetic base, clips, and posts that help to grip your circuit boards as you solder.
With five alligator clips and six posts designed to hold your PCB firmly to the magnetic base, your hands are free to concentrate on soldering up your next project.
Read moreRead less▼
Measuring 11.41 x 7.08 inches (29 x 18 cm), this magnetic helping hands kit is sturdy for holding your PCBs while giving you a choice as to how it holds them. The five flexible alligator clips are used to clamp and hold circuit boards a little nearer to the user. The flexibility of the armatures means that both sides of the PCB can be seen, remaining accessible for soldering either way.
If you need more rigidity, the six posts are used to clamp to the edge of the board you're soldering, which is useful if you're soldering just one side. This is ideal for a maker with plenty of tasks on his sheet.
Keep soldering on, with lead-free and leaded solder.
You'll want lead-free solder if you're planning on soldering. It's the gold standard, it's safer, and it avoids the environmental issues that come with traditional leaded solder.
Lead-free solder is the gold standard these days. Any modern electronics will have components soldered using lead-free solder. It's safer than traditional leaded, and avoids the environmental issues, such as lead leakage during bad disposal. It's the safest option if you're planning on making anything you go on to sell, too.
Lead-free solder is better for the environment, and it means you can build and sell products that are made using it.
This 0.6mm diameter solder has a flux rosin core so it flows neatly around your solder joints.
Read moreRead less▼
That said, there's still a case for leaded solder, especially if you're using it for yourself (and you take precautions).
The solder below is worth considering if you need it. It's a mix of 63% tin to 37% lead, which is a decent mix, and should produce good solder joints.
Lead solder is still great for personal use, and this 0.8mm rosin core 63/38 tin / lead mix will melt great and produce shiny and reliable solder joints.
Read moreRead less▼
Keep your workbench safe from hot soldering irons
Every maker is going to have a workbench that has seen one or two accidents. If you want to avoid any permanent damage, you'll want to pick up one of these sillicone soldering mats.
This silicone repair mat will keep your workbench free from scratches and soldering iron burns. The included magnetic notches and slots will make sure every screw goes back in at the end.
Read moreRead less▼
Silicone soldering mats are an essential buy for a hobbyist. They'll keep the heat from your soldering iron away from the workbench, and often have extra positions to keep screws in one place and to stop magnetics from falling off your bench.
Good for taking apart a laptop, for instance. It'll keep your screws safe, the bench burn-free, and it'll help you from scratching the chassis, too. When you're done, you can just roll it up and put it away.
Stay safe soldering with a fume extractor
Lead-free or not, you're going to see fumes when you're soldering. It isn't a great idea to breathe these in, so a fume extractor can help you to improve the air quality around you as you work.
Keep your lungs healthy by removing the flux fumes and solder smoke from the air. This tiltable solder fume extractor works from up to five inches away and pulls the offensive fumes through an activated carbon filter to keep the air fresh. You get extra filters in the box
Read moreRead less▼
Extractors work, as you'd expect, by using a fan to suck smoke and fumes from the air, directly into an activated carbon filter, with clean air passing through the back of it. This extractor uses a high-speed fan to do it, keeping high suction from up to five inches away: plenty of space for you to solder in comfort.
This extractor comes with four rubber feet, so it won't move around, and the locking tilt mechanism helps you point it to the right places as you work. It also has fenders on both sides of the fan to stop any breezes from moving fumes away from the unit, as it keeps you safe.

articles.title: Près de la moitié des boutiques SFR attaquent l'opérateur en justice
articles.text:
Les distributeurs indépendants de SFR, qui exploitent près de la moitié des boutiques de l'enseigne, assignent l'opérateur en justice. En cause, selon eux, les effets du rachat de SFR par Orange, Bouygues Telecom et Free sur leur activité.
Le rachat de SFR se retrouve devant la justice par un nouveau biais, cette fois celui des distributeurs indépendants de l'opérateur au carré rouge. Ce vendredi 27 novembre, 84 sociétés réunies au sein de l'ADIES ont annoncé avoir assigné SFR devant le Tribunal des activités économiques de Paris, où une audience est prévue le 10 décembre. Elles réclament une révision de leurs contrats et une indemnisation, dans un réseau déjà fragilisé par l'annonce de la vente, à laquelle elles ne s'opposent pas frontalement.
Près d'un magasin SFR sur deux est entre leurs mains
Derrière ces 84 sociétés, on trouve l'ADIES, l'Association des distributeurs indépendants de l'enseigne SFR, créée en août 2025. Elle rassemble aujourd'hui la quasi-totalité des indépendants du réseau, soit 55 chefs d'entreprise qui exploitent environ 250 points de vente, installés en centre-ville, dans des zones rurales ou dans le périurbain. Leur devanture affiche bien le carré rouge, mais leurs boutiques n'appartiennent pas à l'opérateur. Elles lui sont liées par un contrat de distribution et consacrent l'essentiel de leur activité à vendre ses offres, forfaits mobiles comme box.
Ce réseau représente à lui seul près de la moitié de la présence physique de SFR en France. D'après l'ADIES, ses difficultés se sont nettement aggravées depuis le 6 juin 2026. Ce jour-là, Orange, Bouygues Telecom et Free ont signé avec Altice le protocole d'accord pour racheter SFR à 20,35 milliards d'euros. La disparition programmée de la marque entame la confiance des clients, et la fréquentation des magasins s'en ressent. Qui a envie de s'abonner chez un opérateur dont on connaît déjà la date d'expiration ? Les distributeurs, eux, attendent toujours qu'on leur trace une perspective.
Les chiffres avancés par l'association décrivent un réseau à bout de souffle. Une vingtaine de sociétés sont aujourd'hui en procédure collective. Leurs difficultés financières sont désormais placées sous le contrôle d'un tribunal, qu'il s'agisse d'une sauvegarde, d'un redressement ou d'une liquidation judiciaire. Treize magasins ont déjà baissé le rideau et d'autres fermetures sont annoncées. L'ADIES redoute que la situation empire dans les prochains mois. Quant aux salariés de ces boutiques, ils restent exclus des engagements de maintien de l'emploi pris lors du rachat, qui garantissent jusqu'à début 2029 un poste aux salariés de SFR concernés par la reprise.
Devant la justice, les boutiques SFR veulent se faire entendre, sans remettre en cause la vente
Les distributeurs réclament deux choses auprès de SFR. D'abord, un rééquilibrage de leurs contrats, pour les adapter à une situation bouleversée par l'annonce de la vente. Ensuite, la réparation du préjudice qu'ils estiment avoir subi. L'ADIES assure avoir sollicité SFR pendant plus d'un an sans obtenir de réponse, avant de saisir le Tribunal des activités économiques de Paris. Pour information, c'est le nom que porte l'ancien tribunal de commerce de la capitale, à titre expérimental, depuis janvier 2025. Rien n'est gagné d'avance, puisqu'en février, la cour d'appel de Paris avait donné tort à un autre distributeur indépendant, qui réclamait 300 000 euros à l'opérateur.
Pas question pour autant de jouer les saboteurs. « Nous ne sommes pas opposés à la vente de SFR. Mais notre réseau représente près de la moitié des magasins de l'enseigne et ne peut pas être la variable d'ajustement de cette opération », insistent les membres du bureau de l'association. Le recours au juge ne ferme pas la porte au dialogue. L'ADIES veut toujours construire, avec SFR comme avec les trois acquéreurs, des solutions pour que ses magasins restent ouverts.
Ce recours intervient dans une procédure de rachat déjà bien chahutée. En juin, on apprenait que plus de 400 boutiques SFR devaient fermer. Sur les 530 du réseau, seules 120 seraient reprises, une quarantaine par repreneur. Fin octobre, Orange visait toujours une finalisation au second semestre 2027, tout en reconnaissant attendre l'issue de procédures engagées par les représentants des salariés. L'ADIES mise sur le fait que ses boutiques entretiennent au quotidien la relation de proximité avec une part importante des clients SFR. Selon elle, leur affaiblissement modifie déjà la distribution des offres télécoms, alors que l'Autorité de la concurrence, saisie du dossier en juillet, ne s'est pas encore officiellement prononcée de manière définitive. Le 10 décembre, le tribunal ne se prononcera pas sur la vente de SFR, mais sur les contrats qui lient l'opérateur à ses distributeurs.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time Remake se actualiza en Nintendo Switch 2: las novedades del nuevo parche
articles.text:
Nintendo lanzó la actualización Ver. 1.1.2 de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para Nintendo Switch 2, un parche que soluciona un error crítico detectado en la misión «El amigo de Malon». La descarga, gratuita, está disponible desde el 25 de noviembre y representa el primer ajuste del remake desde su lanzamiento, ocurrido el 5 de noviembre.
El fallo afectaba a Link niño durante la secuencia en la que Malon, el personaje del rancho Lon Lon, le enseña la Canción de Epona. En determinadas circunstancias, la combinación de botones necesaria para tocar la ocarina dejaba de responder justo después de que Malon transmitiera la melodía, lo que impedía avanzar en el episodio.
El problema desaparecía si el jugador abandonaba la misión, pero reaparecía al intentar completarla desde el inicio. Nintendo no detalló qué originó el error ni en qué punto exacto se producía el bloqueo.
El acceso a Epona quedaba comprometido
Sin la resolución de este episodio, los jugadores no podían obtener a Epona, el caballo que acompaña a Link a lo largo de la aventura. Aunque no resulta indispensable para completar la historia principal, contar con el animal reduce los tiempos de traslado por Hyrule y habilita el acceso a misiones secundarias adicionales. Quienes ya habían topado con el bloqueo pueden retomar el episodio sin inconvenientes tras instalar la actualización, según las notas de parche oficiales.
El documento también menciona la corrección de «varios problemas» orientados a mejorar la fluidez general del juego, aunque la compañía no especificó cuáles. Tampoco se informó el peso de la descarga de la versión 1.1.2.
Cómo instalar la actualización
El parche se aplica de forma automática al iniciar el título si la consola está conectada a internet. De manera alternativa, los usuarios pueden forzar la búsqueda de la actualización desde el menú HOME, al pulsar el botón + sobre el icono del juego.
Antecedentes del remake y su soporte técnico
La versión 1.1.2 llega después de la 1.1.1, una actualización de 343 megabytes publicada el 4 de noviembre, un día antes del estreno oficial. Aquel parche había habilitado la compatibilidad con Zelda Notes, el servicio complementario disponible en la aplicación Nintendo Switch, que ofrece un cuestionario diario con 2.000 preguntas y una ocarina virtual vinculada al remake. Para activar esta función, los jugadores deben seguir las instrucciones que aparecen en pantalla tras actualizar el título.
Las notas de la actualización no hacen referencia a otros fallos detectados por la comunidad de speedrunners desde el lanzamiento, entre ellos saltos infinitos y supersaltos que permiten a Link saltearse secciones completas del juego.
Un remake exclusivo que acompaña el aniversario de la saga
El remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time es exclusivo de Nintendo Switch 2 y tiene un precio de 59,99 dólares en formato digital y 69,99 dólares en edición física. Nintendo reconstruyó el título original de 1998, lanzado para Nintendo 64, con incorporaciones como saltos manuales, posibilidad de esprintar, control libre de cámara, doblaje completo y un nuevo registro de misiones. El lanzamiento se anunció durante el evento The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, celebrado el 8 de septiembre.
El estreno del remake coincide con la celebración por el 40º aniversario de la franquicia, que incluyó además el lanzamiento de ocarinas físicas oficiales a través de My Nintendo Store.

articles.title: Over 500 shoppers have already snapped up this £160 Lenovo Chromebook on Amazon this Black Friday
articles.text:
Less than half price: Lenovo's gorgeous 14-inch WUXGA Chromebook with Wi-Fi 7 is just £160 for Black Friday
A 1920 x 1200 screen, Wi-Fi 7 and a #1 Best Seller badge, now £190 off
I've found a Chromebook with a WUXGA screen and Wi-Fi 7 at less than half price: the Lenovo Chromebook 14 is £159.99 (was £349.99) at Amazon. That's 54% off, and it's currently the #1 Best Seller in Traditional Laptops on Amazon UK, with 500+ bought in the past month.
The 14-inch IPS screen runs at 1920 x 1200 (WUXGA), a taller 16:10 shape that shows more of a document or web page than a standard 1080p panel. This device runs on a MediaTek Kompanio 540 processor supported with 4GB of LPDDR5 RAM and 64GB of UFS storage. It is available in a Cosmic Blue body.
This is a 14-inch WUXGA (1920 x 1200) IPS Chromebook with a MediaTek Kompanio 540, 4GB RAM, 64GB UFS storage, Wi-Fi 7, an HD webcam with privacy shutter, and stereo speakers.
Why we recommend it
A 14-inch IPS panel running at 1920 x 1200 offers 120 more rows of pixels than a standard 1080p display; therefore, more of a document, spreadsheet, or web page fits on screen before you scroll, which helps with essays, research, and long reading. Wi-Fi 7 brings faster downloads and steadier video calls on a Wi-Fi 7 router, and on an older router it still connects at that router's speed.
A physical shutter covers the webcam lens between calls, and the stereo speakers are tuned for clear voices in lessons and meetings. At 1.36kg, it's light enough to carry to lectures or the office every day, making it suitable for students and mobile businesses. The full-size keyboard has responsive keys, and the large touchpad makes navigation easy. ChromeOS adds automatic updates, built-in security, Google services, and Android apps from Google Play. In all, the price is a major point of attraction.
What to know before you buy
This is a Chromebook, so it runs ChromeOS, not Windows or macOS. Most everyday tasks happen in the browser or in Android apps, but desktop software and specialist programs won't run natively.
Memory and storage are modest: 4GB of RAM suits light multitasking, and 64GB of UFS storage fills up quickly if you download large files, so the 128GB model at £255 is worth considering. The keyboard is not backlit, the screen is a 60Hz panel, and the warranty is one year.
Price Context
£159.99 is £190 below the £349.99 RRP. If 64GB feels tight, the 128GB model is £255. Amazon also lists £119.99 with a gift card if you're approved for the Amazon Barclaycard (representative 28.9% APR variable), which only makes sense if you were going to apply anyway.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Lenovo Chromebook 14 if... you want a light, affordable laptop for study, browsing, documents, and video calls, and a taller, sharper screen matters more to you than raw power.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions, AI Server Hijacking + 17 More Stories
articles.text:
A website can look perfectly fine to the person running it. Log out, visit the same page, and things might look different. Something similar is happening with browser extensions, where even the way you find and install one can change what it does. Checking whether software works as expected only tells you so much.
Then there’s the question of who gets to use what. Stolen logins are opening doors across connected systems, while some AI servers are sitting online for anyone to use at someone else’s expense. Even software responsible for keeping the power on has found its way into an attack.
Meanwhile, authorities are taking down large scam operations, extortion gangs are making comebacks, and ransomware activity is picking up. Some of the more worrying findings this week involve things most people would have little reason to suspect. The details are worth a look.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  Stolen credentials expose customer data Todoist has disclosed that an attacker gained unauthorized access to its production systems and retrieved some customer information on November 23, 2026. The incident affects 6% of its users. "Between November 22 and 23, an attacker used a stolen credential associated with our version control system to modify automated workflows in three repositories and obtain additional credentials," it said. During this time, they could also read our source code. Our investigation found no changes to application code. One of the credentials they obtained allowed them to change how employees access our internal systems. The attacker used it to take over an employee’s work account and gain access to our cloud infrastructure. On November 23, the attacker downloaded a file containing account information for some early Todoist users whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method. They also made targeted queries for account tokens, searched some customer content for credentials, and accessed email information through connected Todoist for Outlook accounts."
- 
  
  Record cybersecurity acquisition CrowdStrike said it will acquire Zscaler in a deal worth $43.9 billion, making it the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record. "Security used to be about keeping the adversary out. Today, safety is required to let AI in," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said. "The network used to connect people to places. Now it connects agents to data. With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely. We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen."
- 
  
  Paid ads activate hidden payloads Microsoft's Edge Extensions Security Team has documented SleeperWidget, a set of over 250 extensions across Microsoft Edge Add-ons, Chrome Web Store, and Mozilla Add-ons that work as advertised unless installed through a paid search ad. Once installed that way, they collect browsing data, inject ads, and change shopping links. "Its extensions pose as maps, recipe finders, package trackers, and other everyday tools. Most deliver the features they advertise, which makes hidden behavior easier to miss," it said. "In the extensions we analyzed, installation through a paid-advertising funnel also activated browsing-data collection, ad injection, and shopping-link modification."
- 
  
  LLMjacking without exploits An analysis of 20,354 internet-facing hosts has revealed that thousands of servers where AI services or notebook APIs have been deployed and left accessible without authentication, potentially enabling attackers to abuse them for their own purposes. "More than half of the exposed Ollama servers in this scan have already been touched by someone who is not the owner," Rapid7 said. "79% of exposed Ollama hosts list at least one :cloud model, mostly GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Kimi variants. An exposed, signed-in server can provide access to someone else's paid subscription, with the bill landing on the owner. This is the self-hosted version of LLMjacking, and it requires no exploit at all."
- 
  
  Blockchain-backed malware delivery SonicWall Capture Labs has disclosed details of a Java-based loader from SilentNet, a Java-based remote access trojan and infostealer sold as a malware-as-a-service offering that's advertised on YouTube. The JAR masquerades as a mod for Minecraft Fabric and targets players who download mods from external sources. "Once loaded by the game, it pulls the player's Minecraft session token from memory. It then gets its command-and-control (C2) address from a smart contract on the Polygon blockchain, and downloads a portable Python runtime hidden inside a PNG image to run a second-stage infostealer," SoniWall said. "Every string in the JAR is hidden by per-character arithmetic; it resolves hostnames through DNS-over-HTTPS, and it talks to its C2 through a custom HTTPS client that skips certificate validation."
- 
  
  AI-powered phishing infrastructure Threat actors are using DeepSite, Hugging Face's AI website builder, to create dozens of phishing and credential-stealing pages on Hugging Face Spaces impersonating 28 brands, including Microsoft, Google, PayPal, Chase, and Coinbase. "29 of the pages were built with DeepSite, Hugging Face’s AI website builder," Aikido said. "One Microsoft login clone took about 90 minutes of plain-language prompts, and other operators asked the builder to hide their pages from crawlers or send stolen logins to Telegram."
- 
  
  Credential theft spans 127 CVEs According to VulnCheck, requests to steal credentials made up 13% of all vulnerability exploitation recorded between January and November 2026. Credential-harvesting attempts appeared across 127 of 694 CVEs observed in its honeypot network, with open-source software and AI developer tools like Apache, Laravel, Langflow, Flowise, MLflow, and n8n taking up 61% of the CVEs associated with credential-harvesting attempts. "Attackers search application files, logs and environment variables for database passwords, cloud credentials and API keys, with file-read and SSRF vulnerabilities providing opportunities without code execution," VulnCheck said, adding it "observed 1,756 attempts targeting AI provider and coding agent credentials from 406 IP addresses across 27 CVEs."
- 
  
  Ransomware disrupts critical services A previously unknown ransomware and data-extortion group calling itself BYOD has claimed at least nine organizations between October 5 and November 9, 2026. "Its attacks have had real-world consequences, including ambulance diversion, more than 30 clinics closed, and campus-wide device shutdowns," TrendAI said. "BYOD runs a pressure campaign alongside the intrusion: audio messages on infected computers, public leak-site posts, statements framing its attacks as holding organizations accountable, and outreach to individual victims." Although the complete intrusion chain remains to be analyzed, evidence points to credential compromise and a remote access trojan on an employee's computer for initial access.
- 
  
  Malicious JavaScript delivery platform A malware campaign has been observed installing a fake WordPress plugin built almost entirely by a name generator, including its title, directories, files, and functions (e.g., trijavascriptly, ultravueal, maxdataic, and quadmicroservicesion). "Behind the generated names is a second-stage delivery platform that runs arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of every anonymous visitor to an infected site, routes that traffic through the victim's own domain, and lies dormant for logged-in users," Wordfence said. The malware has been discovered twice, once in January 2026 and another in September 2026. Exactly how the plugin is installed is not known, but investigation shows that it's likely via a compromise of an administrator account.
- 
  
  Global scam networks disrupted The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) has announced that over 17.3 million scam accounts have been deplatformed on Meta, 700 fraudulent crypto investment websites seized, and 12 U.S. arrest warrants issued as part of efforts to tackle foreign and domestic scams over the past six months. The Strike Force has traced and restrained $1,082,260,156.82 in cryptocurrency stolen from U.S. victims. "Our Scam Center Strike Force has continued its work investigating cyber-enabled fraud perpetrated against Americans by transnational organized crime groups, emanating out of Asia and attacking America's main street," said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. "The Strike Force teams focus on identifying and pursuing key leaders — including Chinese organized crime affiliates operating in Cambodia, Laos, and Burma, and rapidly expanding around the globe — to bring them to justice." FBI Director Kash Patel said the Operation Blackout scam demolition initiative has "seized nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, taken more than 14,000 digital devices, directly warned over 11,000 Americans from scam attempts, and prevented more than $690 million in potential victim losses." Over 29 scam compounds operating across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East have been dismantled and more than 2,200 trafficked workers have been repatriated. The U.S. State Department has also worked with U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement to facilitate the freezing of more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency, the takedown of over 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts, and several arrests. Earlier this month, the U.S. Attorney's Office also filed a civil forfeiture action to recover 456,602 USDT (Tether) that's alleged to be proceeds of romance fraud schemes targeting individuals in Massachusetts and elsewhere on online dating sites and Facebook.
- 
  
  Billion-dollar crypto recovery bid The Justice Department has filed a civil action to recover over $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency that was illicitly obtained from Binance by North Korean actors in a major hack last month. "To date, the United States has assisted in the freezing, seizing, and/or the return of almost $3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from multiple sources since the theft from Binance on or about October 29," the DoJ said. Brett Leatherman, Cyber Branch Operations Director of the FBI, said, "North Korea depends on sophisticated laundering techniques to convert stolen cryptocurrency into funds that support the regime's illicit activities," adding, "Following the Binance theft, the FBI and our partners moved quickly to trace and freeze stolen assets and share critical information with virtual asset service providers."
- 
  
  Extortion gang resurfaces after arrests The ShinyHunters extortion gang claims to have returned on a new data leak site following a series of arrests targeting alleged members. The new TOR site, launched on November 23, features messages in both Russian and English announcing the group's return, while denouncing a former member, Rey (aka Saif), who was reportedly arrested and is "actively cooperating" with law enforcement. "We want to let you know that from now on we will only be using our account on Exploit, which we've held since 2020," the group said. "We won't be active on any other BF-style forums anymore." They also concluded the statement with a shout-out to two other arrested members, Umbreon and Ed Dubrovsky. "Thank you for being with us all this time," the group said. "We won't forget you, and we might even send you a couple of postcards to your rat-infested cells. It was a pleasure working with you. And it's truly a shame that our guys got caught because of such silly mistakes, ones that could easily have been avoided if you fools hadn't gotten involved with the wrong people."
- 
  
  AI misuse detection without data retention Anthropic has launched a public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), allowing organizations to detect potentially harmful AI activity across multiple interactions while maintaining zero data retention (ZDR). The protection employs a second defensive layer, known as automated safety monitoring, that looks for patterns of misuse across multiple requests to provide automated safety monitoring without storing any customer data. "Instead, our automated safety monitoring system analyzes data stored entirely on infrastructure controlled by our customers," Anthropic said. "When automated safety monitoring finds a risk, it creates a Safety Case for you to review. These cases can be read from your cloud storage or through an API, and can be integrated with security information and event management systems. They do not include inputs and outputs. Once it's set up, automated safety monitoring can help your team detect intentional misuse that could lead to serious harm (like offensive cyber operations). It can also help detect agents that take actions beyond a user's intentions."
- 
  
  Ransomware activity jumps 23% NCC Group has revealed that ransomware attacks surged 23% in October 2026 compared to September, with 1049 claimed incidents. The Gentlemen, N0n, Qilin, Akira, and Silent Ransom have claimed the most victims. Top targeted verticals included industrials, consumer discretionary, healthcare, IT, and consumer supplies. Check Point Research has reported a record 2,830 ransomware victims in Q3 2026, claimed by 117 ransomware brands, up from 91 in the previous quarter. Of these, 42 are new. "Ransom payments continued to diverge: average payments fell 45% quarter over quarter to just over $1 million, while the median rose 167% to $400,000," Check Point said. "The top 10 groups accounted for just 49% of victims, the first time groups outside the top ten collectively represented the majority." Qilin, The Gentlemen, and INC Ransom emerged as the most active groups during the period. Interestingly, while the top 10 groups accounted for 71% of victims in Q1 2026, the figure has declined to 58% in Q2 and only 49% in Q3, indicating a fragmentation of the threat landscape.
- 
  
  12,200 online stores compromised A new analysis from Guardio Labs has revealed that one online shop in 195 (i.e., about 12,200 of the 2.38 million stores) was hijacked in October 2026. The phenomenon has been codenamed CartJacked. "Three schemes go straight after shoppers: hand-offs to gambling and scam pages, fake 'I'm not a robot' checks that tell you to paste a command (about 900 shops), and card skimmers," Guardio said. "Of the ten commands the fake checks handed out, three still delivered malware, including a stealer for passwords and crypto wallets."
- 
  
  €26 million crypto trail uncovered A Europol-led operation along with authorities from 11 countries has disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services and the identification of 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content as part of a five-day effort between November 16 and 20, 2026. The sites drew over 7.3 million visits each year. More than €26 million in cryptocurrency transactions have been traced so far. "The operation targeted a criminal market worth billions of euros annually, in which illegal streaming providers sell unauthorized access to premium television channels, live sports and films, often collecting subscription payments through cryptocurrency," Europol said. "The profits generated by these services do not simply disappear. They move through payment accounts, cryptocurrency wallets and intermediaries, making it harder for investigators to identify who is ultimately benefiting." No arrests have been announced.
- 
  
  10 million exposed NGINX services at risk Censys has revealed that more than 10 million exposed NGINX services are running an affected version with HTTP/2 that are vulnerable to a set of flaws called NGINX2Root that "could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to corrupt memory in an NGINX worker process when a set of specific features are enabled – leading to code execution where ASLR is disabled or the attacker can bypass it."
- 
  
  Power management software weaponized Broadcom-owned Symantec has disclosed details of an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business (PPB), a software that manages UPS devices, as a way to execute code on a domain controller, dump Active Directory secrets and launch a persistent implant. "PPB can run a script (a .cmd file in an extcmd folder) when a power-related event such as a voltage sag or outage is detected," Symantec said. "The attacker placed their own scripts in that folder through the product's web console and had the PowerPanel service, ppbed.exe, run them. The commands in this attack chain have ppbed.exe as their ancestor and run as SYSTEM. The attacker used this channel to download tools with certutil, then loaded a .NET assembly into memory using PowerShell, and ran ntdsutil and esentutl against the Active Directory database, ntds.dit." The same channel has also been used to launch an implant ("upnpcont.exe") that uses DLL sideloading to launch a suspicious DLL ("atl.dll"). "What this attack shows is that UPS, power-management, and other infrastructure software should be treated like any other potentially dual-use RMM product; used with network restrictions, unique credentials, vigilant patching, and process-level monitoring," Symantec said.
- 
  
  Banking middleware weaponized A new campaign called BankWeaver has targeted a Temenos Quantum Fabric deployment with an exposed authentication service that was configured to accept anonymous access to obtain administrator privileges and deliver malicious Java components via the platform's extension mechanism. The attack targeted an unspecified financial services institution in early September 2026. "Attackers could generate an anonymous token by accessing a public application and then exchange it for an administrator token on another exposed application," Forescout said. "The new token obtained by the attackers granted access to administrative functions within the Temenos Fabric platform, including managing running applications and creating new services." The malicious components delivered as part of the attack include: FabricShell, which provides arbitrary command execution and database queries, and FabricShadow, which collects host information, stages output locally, and exfiltrates results to remote servers. Temenos has since released updates and guidance to configure the service as private and advised customers to restrict internet access to Spotlight and Fabric administrative and authentication services.
- 
  
  Fake updates deliver Python backdoor A new wave of Microsoft Teams social engineering activity exhibiting similarities to Edgecution was uncovered by Arctic Wolf Labs last month. "In the October wave, following a lull in observed cases from August to September, new delivery artifacts and operational patterns were observed," the cybersecurity company said. "The campaign abuses a malicious Edge extension and Chrome Native Messaging to run a Python backdoor outside the browser sandbox. The activity shares early chain tradecraft with PREY-0059, including external-tenant Teams impersonation of IT support, legitimate runtimes paired with scripts, and S3-hosted payloads disguised as legitimate software. While PREY-0059 used S3 buckets named after targeted victims and delivered a Java-based RAT alongside a Java runtime, the current activity used generic Microsoft-themed tenants and buckets, an Edge extension, and a Python backdoor paired with a Python runtime."
One thing worth taking away from this week's stories is how much damage can happen without a particularly clever attack. A forgotten server, a stolen credential, or a feature nobody thought to monitor can be enough. AI may be changing how some attacks are carried out, but many of the ways attackers get in are still surprisingly ordinary.
The harder part is knowing what deserves attention before it becomes a problem. That includes software sitting quietly in the background, services exposed for convenience, and accounts with more access than they need. Somewhere between keeping things running and adding new capabilities, it's easy to lose track of what you've already put online. This week offers several good reasons to look again.

articles.title: L’iPad pliable d’Apple pourrait coûter jusqu’à 5 000 dollars, et un choix crucial reste en suspens
articles.text:
Apple travaillerait toujours sur un iPad pliable doté d’un écran de 19 à 20 pouces une fois déployé. Mark Gurman évoque désormais un prix compris entre 3 000 et 5 000 dollars pour cette tablette dont la sortie reste incertaine.
Imaginez un iPhone Duo suffisamment grand pour occuper une bonne partie de votre bureau une fois ouvert. C’est à peu près ainsi que l’on pourrait résumer le projet J312, avec une différence visible dès qu’on referme l’appareil : il n’aurait pas d’écran à l’extérieur. Le journaliste de Bloomberg, Mark Gurman, a donné de nouvelles précisions sur ce prototype alléchant sur le papier, mais qui pourrait donner des sueurs froides à votre banquier, à en croire les tarifs supposés.
Un écran géant qui ferait grimper la facture
La précédente estimation tournait autour de 3 000 dollars, un montant déjà évoqué en octobre 2025 dans notre article sur les difficultés de l’iPad pliable. Ce chiffre se retrouve aujourd’hui tout en bas de la fourchette avancée par Gurman. À l’époque, il était question d’une dalle de 18 pouces. Le format décrit aujourd’hui dépasserait de six à sept pouces la diagonale du plus grand iPad Pro. À ce stade, Apple n’a annoncé ni produit ni tarif.
Fabriquer une dalle pliable de cette taille en quantité suffisante reste l’un des obstacles, et des difficultés de production pèseraient sur le coût, auxquelles s’ajoute une question plus terre-à-terre : celle de l’encombrement. Le format pliable permettrait de glisser dans un sac un écran qu’on aurait sans doute envie de poser sur une table pour travailler. Reste à savoir si l’ensemble serait encore assez maniable pour lire ou dessiner en le tenant à la main.
C’est aussi ce qui rend le calendrier fragile. Apple aurait d’abord envisagé de présenter l’appareil en 2027, puis en 2028. L’horizon de 2029 circule depuis l’an dernier et Gurman envisage toujours que le projet reste au stade du prototype.
Un iPad géant, ou un Mac qui se plie ?
Un écran géant soulève un autre dilemme : quid du système d’exploitation ? Apple hésiterait encore entre iPadOS, macOS et un nouveau système. Avec iPadOS, on retrouverait les applications tactiles de la tablette et ses fenêtres redimensionnables. On aurait enfin la place d’afficher côte à côte un document, ses notes et un navigateur sans passer son temps à déplacer les fenêtres. Les applications disponibles resteraient celles de l’iPad.
Avec macOS, l’intérêt serait différent. On pourrait imaginer ouvrir ses logiciels de bureau sur un écran tactile de 20 pouces, puis replier le tout en fin de journée. Encore faudrait-il adapter au doigt des menus et des commandes pensés pour le pointeur. Un système conçu spécialement pour l’appareil permettrait de repenser cette interface, avec une question de plus à régler : quelles applications pourrait-on y installer ?
Apple fait déjà tourner macOS sur certains iPad en interne, selon Gurman. Ces essais servent aujourd’hui à explorer des pistes pour iPadOS. Sur une machine qui pourrait atteindre 5 000 dollars, le choix du système finirait par répondre à une question très pratique : est-ce qu’on pourrait y faire le même travail que sur son Mac, ou faudrait-il encore emporter les deux ?
