Peace of mind on the road just got cheaper for Black Friday: save up to 44% on dash cams from Garmin, Viofo and more
From entry-level options to premium, feature-packed cameras, there’s one for any budget
Black Friday is here, and now is a fantastic time to splurge on some new tech to upgrade any old and tired gear to improve your quality of life, where you can save a bit of cash compared to buying at full price.
That’s especially true with the best dash cams in Australia, where one can save you lots of headaches and avoid insurance disputes for a small to medium cash investment. And now that it’s Black Friday, you can even save more on that upfront investment, or even spring for a nicer option that you weren’t initially considering.
From some no-frills but effective options for under AU$150 such as the Garmin Dash Cam Mini 3, to a complete front-and-rear set that’s packed with features, like the 70mai 4K A9000 Ultra, for less than AU$600, there’s a lot to choose from.
We expect these deals will only be live until Monday, November 30, so be quick if you don't want to miss out on these savings. And if you don't see something you like, then be sure to check out a wider range of dash cams at Amazon.
- Follow our live coverage of the Black Friday sales in Australia for more deals and discounts
Despite coming from a big brand like Garmin, this dash cam is the cheapest we’ve found among our best-rated options. The low price is largely because it doesn’t have a screen (which could arguably be more preferable for some) and records videos in 1080p resolution (the others here are 4K), but there’s still a lot to love, particularly the compact 52.1 x 31.6 x 20.3 mm chassis, easy mounting interface, voice control and image quality that is sharp and clear enough to read licence plates, street signs and road markings. Read our full Garmin Dash Cam Mini 3 review here.
If you like the idea of a compact dash cam like the Garmin above, but you want 4K video and an on-device screen, the Vantrue E1 Pro just costs a little bit more. It also includes voice control, fast Wi-Fi transfer rates, a supercapacitor internal battery that will be resilient against Aussie summers, and a polarising filter to reduce glare to a minimum. Read our full Vantrue E1 Pro review here.
Jumping up price points significantly from the two above, this 70mai dash cam also includes a rear camera, both of which shoot 4K footage with Sony Starvis 2 IMX678 sensors. Our 70mai 4K A900 Ultra review found it was easy to set up, has a user-friendly design and interface and an optional hardwire kit (sold separately) can provide extra features like around-the-clock surveillance monitoring.
The successor to our pick for the best overall dash cam, the Viofo A329, the new A329S adds some new features like advanced low-power impact detection and hybrid parking recording mode, a more modular design to allow for expandability, multiplexed video recording options and the use of the newer HK6 hardwire cable. This also has two cameras, though the rear only records in 2K instead of 4K resolution but is also optimised for wider viewing angles (up to 160°).

articles.title: Dyson frappe fort pour le Black Friday : il offre ce laveur de sol ultra fin avec son aspirateur robot
articles.text:
Dyson frappe fort pour le Black Friday : il offre ce laveur de sol ultra fin avec son aspirateur robot
C’est le jour J pour le Black Friday 2026, et c’est à ce vendredi de promotion que Dyson réserve son offre la plus avantageuse. Un aspirateur robot lavant à moitié prix, accompagné pour l’occasion d’un nettoyeur de sol offert : de quoi s’équiper (pour préparer les fêtes de fin d’année) à très bon prix !
On l’a vu tout au long du mois de novembre, Dyson a mis les petits plats dans les grands. Le britannique a mis en place de nombreuses promotions, et dégaine pour le jour J son arme ultime pour des sols impeccables. C’est en effet un lot ultra avantageux que Dyson propose, en offrant tout bonnement un PencilWash pour l’achat de son aspirateur robot Spot+Scrub Ai testé en tout début d’année 2026 par Les Numériques.
Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai
Entrons dans le vif du sujet. Lancé à 1199 €, le Spot+Scrub Ai se monnaie actuellement en promotion entre 589 € et 649 €. Néanmoins, sur le site de Dyson et en appliquant le code promotionnel OFFREFLASH, l’appareil s’affiche à 649 € et est livré avec un petit camarade destiné à simplifier l’entretien des surfaces dures : le PencilWash. Celui-ci se monnaie en ce moment 199 € dans le cadre de promotions. Autant dire que la combinaison représente l’offre ménagère la plus avantageuse du moment chez le fabricant. À noter : il faut être rapide, puisque ce code promotionnel n’est valide que ce 27 novembre.
Deux appareils pour du ménage sans effort
Le Spol+Scrub Ai, un peu cher à son lancement, devient un rapport qualité/prix bien plus avantageux dans le cadre de l’opération de Dyson. Le robot officie comme aspirateur et laveur, et s’avère efficace en aspiration et doué pour naviguer dans les intérieurs. Sa base de vidange a en outre le mérite de fonctionner sans sac (contrairement à celle du V10 Konical tout récemment testé dans nos colonnes !).
Dyson PencilWash
Le PencilWash, lancé début 2026, prend quant à lui la forme d’un laveur de sol au format balai. Ou plutôt crayon, compte tenu de la minceur de son manche, qui cache sa batterie. L’appareil n’est sans doute le plus redoutable face aux taches incrustées - nous testons d'ailleurs actuellement son successeur, le W1 PencilWash conçu pour améliorer sa prestation -, mais il simplifie le passage de la serpillière sur des carrelages, parquets ou linos, et ne transforme pas les séances de ménage en sessions de musculation. Nous l’avons précisé plus haut, ce dispositif, vendu à ses débuts à 349 €, s’affiche en ce moment à 199 €.

articles.title: Safari añade modo oscuro adaptativo en iOS 27.3 para oscurecer webs claras
articles.text:
Safari añade modo oscuro adaptativo en iOS 27.3 para oscurecer webs claras. La función resuelve un problema habitual entre quienes activan el tema oscuro en su iPhone: entrar en una página web sin ese modo y recibir de golpe un fondo blanco que ilumina toda la pantalla, sobre todo de noche.
Qué es el modo oscuro adaptativo de Safari y cómo funciona
El modo oscuro adaptativo —cuya versión beta probó Applesfera, detallando su funcionamiento y cómo activarlo— analiza los colores de cada página visitada para determinar si su diseño es claro u oscuro. Cuando detecta que una web muestra tonos claros y no cuenta con un modo oscuro propio, Safari la oscurece de forma automática.
El proceso consiste en invertir la luminosidad de los colores sin alterar los tonos originales. Así, los fondos claros se convierten en oscuros y el texto que antes era oscuro pasa a mostrarse en claro.
Los degradados también quedan sujetos a este ajuste automático. El sistema modifica el texto para mantener el contraste necesario y asegurar que la lectura siga siendo clara en cualquier página.
Esta solución llega después de que otros navegadores y sistemas operativos ya ofrecieran alternativas similares. Samsung, por ejemplo, incluye esta opción en el navegador propio de sus dispositivos Android, lo que había generado cierta sorpresa por la demora de Apple en sumar esta función a Safari.
Cómo activar el modo oscuro adaptativo en iPhone y iPad
Para usar esta función es necesario tener el sistema configurado en modo oscuro y contar con iOS 27.3 instalado, que por el momento se encuentra en fase beta pública.
Para activar el modo oscuro adaptativo en el iPhone o el iPad, abre Ajustes, entra en Apps, selecciona Safari y activa la opción Modo oscuro adaptativo.
Cómo activar el modo oscuro adaptativo en Mac
En equipos Mac, el proceso varía ligeramente respecto a los dispositivos móviles, aunque mantiene la misma lógica de configuración dentro del propio navegador.
Los pasos son los siguientes: Abrir Safari. Ir a Safari > Ajustes desde la barra de menú. Entrar en Sitios web, seleccionar Modo oscuro adaptativo y activarlo.
Ahora bien, quienes no quieran instalar la beta pública de iOS 27.3 podrán acceder a esta función en diciembre de 2026, cuando Apple lance la versión final del sistema junto a otras novedades previstas para esa actualización.
Cómo activar el modo oscuro en Google Chrome y en el buscador de Google
Activar el modo oscuro en el entorno de Google implica distinguir dos elementos diferentes: el navegador Google Chrome, que incluye pestañas, barra de direcciones y menús, y el buscador de Google, es decir, la página de resultados que aparece en google.com. Cada uno cuenta con su propia configuración, por lo que activar uno no implica que el otro cambie de forma automática.
En el caso del navegador Chrome instalado en una computadora, el proceso comienza al abrir una nueva pestaña. Desde allí se debe ingresar a la opción Personalizar Chrome, ubicada en la parte inferior derecha, o bien abrir el panel lateral disponible en la parte superior derecha.
Dentro del apartado de Diseño o Aspecto aparece la posibilidad de elegir el tema Oscuro, o también la alternativa Dispositivo, que ajusta Chrome según la configuración general del sistema operativo. Una vez aplicado el cambio, las pestañas, la barra de herramientas y los menús del navegador adoptan tonos oscuros de manera inmediata.
Distinto es el procedimiento para modificar el aspecto del buscador propiamente dicho. Para ello es necesario ingresar a google.com y realizar cualquier búsqueda. Luego debe presionarse la opción Configuración, visible arriba a la derecha o al pie de la página, y dentro de ese menú seleccionar Ver toda la configuración.
El siguiente paso consiste en entrar al apartado Aspecto, elegir allí la opción Tema oscuro y confirmar los cambios con el botón Guardar. Tras completar esta acción, el fondo de la página de resultados deja de ser blanco y pasa a mostrarse en tonos grises oscuros o negros.
En dispositivos móviles, el procedimiento varía según el sistema operativo. En Android, debe abrirse Chrome y acceder al menú de tres puntos ubicado en la parte superior derecha, identificado como Más.
Desde allí se ingresa a Configuración y luego a la sección Tema, donde puede seleccionarse Oscuro o la opción Predeterminado del sistema. Al aplicar el cambio, tanto la interfaz de Chrome como el buscador adoptan el tema oscuro.
En el caso de iPhone o iPad, tanto Chrome como la aplicación de Google suelen ajustarse automáticamente al tema general configurado en el sistema operativo. Por ese motivo, el cambio se realiza desde los Ajustes del iPhone, ingresando a Pantalla y brillo y seleccionando allí la opción Oscuro. Al activarla, no solo el sistema adopta ese diseño, sino también las aplicaciones compatibles con esta función, incluido el buscador de Google.

articles.title: Nvidia stops AI GPU shipments to Southeast Asia amid purported China cloud access ban, report claims — data centers in Singapore, other countries, in trouble as Commerce Department requires cloud providers to obtain export license
articles.text:
Nvidia stops AI GPU shipments to Southeast Asia amid purported China cloud access ban, report claims — data centers in Singapore, other countries, in trouble as Commerce Department requires cloud providers to obtain export license
Dell, Supermicro, and other server manufacturers have been told to suspend shipments to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia.
AI data centers in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia are facing trouble as Nvidia has reportedly ordered its manufacturing partners to stop shipping AI servers to the region. According to the Financial Times, Dell, Supermicro, and other firms that make AI servers using Nvidia AI GPUs have told their customers from the four countries that the AI chip maker has forbidden them to ship their orders. The move comes as the U.S. closed the loophole that let Chinese AI companies rent compute from data centers outside China equipped with advanced AI chips sourced from American semiconductor manufacturers like Nvidia.
The U.S. has banned the export of advanced AI chips to China since 2022 in an effort to limit its advancement. Even though President Trump eventually allowed Nvidia to export H100 AI GPUs to China in December 2025, companies that wanted to buy them needed to secure an import license from the Commerce Department. Aside from that, the White House is also collecting a 25% fee for every chip, making it more expensive for a data center in China to buy them. Because of this, many Chinese AI labs are instead renting compute from data centers located abroad. They mostly do this in Southeast Asia, which is just around a four-to-six-hour flight from major cities like Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and Shanghai, although some firms are looking in further areas like Europe.
It remains unclear if Nvidia’s order is permanent or temporary, but the new export rules give cloud providers 90 days to apply for an export license and prove that their customers do not include restricted entities. However, one cloud provider executive told the Financial Times that there are no clear instructions on how to go about this. “There’s this new rule but no guidance on execution,” they said. “No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It’s causing sheer chaos in the region.”
This sudden halt of orders is causing trouble for many data centers in Southeast Asia. Sources say that Aolani, a Singapore-based cloud company with a deal to provide compute to ByteDance, is losing financing for the project as bankers have stopped issuing credit to the tune of $500 million as Nvidia GPU shipments to the region remain in jeopardy. The Chinese social media giant could also potentially drop out of the arrangement, as it won’t be able to access the powerful Nvidia chips that many AI labs still prefer for training their models.

articles.title: À 174,99 €, le Sonos Ace séduit par son silence, malgré ses 312 g
articles.text:
Le casque Sonos Ace n'a jamais été aussi accessible. Ce 26 novembre, pour le Black Friday, Amazon l'affiche à 174,99 €, soit 61 % de moins que son prix de référence de 449 €.
Premier casque de la marque, le Sonos Ace vise directement les Sony WH-1000XM, Bose QuietComfort Ultra et Apple AirPods Max. Il y a dix jours, nous le relayions déjà à 199 €, et il était à 227 € pendant les Jours Flash Prime d'octobre.
Le voici encore moins cher : Amazon le propose à 174,99 € pour le Black Friday. L'arrivée de l'Ace Ultra, annoncé par Sonos en septembre, explique sans doute ce déstockage. Ce casque s'adresse à ceux qui veulent une excellente réduction de bruit et un son équilibré, et plus encore à ceux qui possèdent déjà une barre de son Sonos.
Black Friday : le casque Sonos Ace est à 174,99 € au lieu de 449 € chez Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le Sonos Ace ?
- Pour sa réduction de bruit : très efficace dès les basses fréquences, elle se place au niveau des meilleurs casques du marché.
- Pour son autonomie : nous avons mesuré 30 h 30 avec la réduction de bruit activée, et 3 minutes de charge offrent 3 heures d'écoute selon Sonos.
- Pour son audio spatial : relié à une barre de son Sonos, il diffuse le Dolby Atmos avec suivi des mouvements de la tête.
Une réduction de bruit parmi les meilleures
Pour un premier essai, Sonos a frappé fort. Comme l'explique notre test, la réduction de bruit active isole remarquablement bien, des basses aux médiums : en avion comme en ville, la sensation de bulle de silence est bluffante. Seules les voix, surtout masculines, passent un peu plus que sur un AirPods Max. Côté connectique, la puce Qualcomm Snapdragon Sound gère le multipoint et toute la famille AptX, et le port USB-C transmet le son sans perte. Les appels restent clairs, même en milieu bruyant.
Un son équilibré et un vrai casque home cinéma
Le Sonos Ace livre un son équilibré et naturel, plus agréable sur la durée que celui des Bose selon nous. Il lui manque un peu de détail et de dynamique pour rivaliser avec les références audiophiles, mais il ne déforme jamais un morceau. Son vrai atout, c'est le home cinéma : associé à une barre de son Sonos, il devient un casque Dolby Atmos très immersif, avec un suivi des mouvements de la tête quasiment sans latence.
Quelques concessions sur le confort
Très bien fini, le Sonos Ace pèse en revanche 312 g, contre environ 250 g pour ses concurrents de Sony et Bose. Il reste confortable grâce à ses coussinets en mousse à mémoire de forme, mais il fatigue un peu plus sur les très longues sessions. Il ne se plie pas non plus, et l'application Sonos propose assez peu de réglages, avec un simple égaliseur à trois bandes.
✅ Les points forts
- Réduction de bruit au niveau des meilleurs.
- Autonomie mesurée à 30 h 30 avec réduction de bruit.
- Audio sans perte en USB-C et Dolby Atmos avec les barres Sonos.
❌ Les limites
- Plus lourd que la concurrence (312 g).
- Structure non pliable, application peu fournie.

Sous la barre des 175 €, le Sonos Ace devient l'un des casques à réduction de bruit haut de gamme les plus intéressants du moment. Il convient parfaitement à un usage nomade, et il prend tout son sens pour les possesseurs d'une barre de son Sonos.

articles.title: SpaceX turns to Apollo and Goldman Sachs for record Nvidia GPU financing
articles.text:
SpaceX secures $44 billion funding deal to snap up a hoard of Nvidia Vera Rubin chips
Nvidia's Vera Rubin processors are heading to SpaceX
- SpaceX secures $44 billion in financing for Nvidia's next-generation processors
- Apollo and Goldman Sachs lead the record-breaking GPU financing transaction
- Nvidia's Vera Rubin processors are scheduled to reach SpaceX in 2027
SpaceX has secured $44 billion in debt financing led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs to purchase Nvidia's Vera Rubin processors for its computing infrastructure.
The transaction includes senior and subordinated notes, with BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and KKR-advised accounts providing major initial commitments.
Hardware deliveries are expected during the first half of 2027, giving the company additional computing resources for its planned artificial intelligence investments.
Apollo and Goldman Sachs lead record GPU financing
The financing attracted commitments exceeding the amount initially sought, making it the largest transaction of its kind involving GPUs.
Apollo and Goldman Sachs organized the financing deal, while participating investment institutions supplied substantial initial commitments through their respective funds and managed accounts.
The transaction follows an October disclosure by SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk that the company was seeking external financing.
Three disclosed debt tranches provide further details about the financing costs and repayment periods.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
According to Reuters, the $25.17 billion senior secured A3 notes carry an 8.259% yield and mature in April 2033.
Another $4.4 billion in senior secured A2 notes carries a 7.66% yield, with repayment scheduled for April 2031.
The package also includes $2.564 billion in subordinated secured Class B notes, carrying an 8.36% yield and maturing in April 2033.
Musk indicated that the additional capital would support investments in data centers and other artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The latest financing provides substantial borrowing capacity for the company's hardware acquisition plans.
However, the financial institutions have not disclosed the precise number of processors involved, their individual prices, or the complete repayment schedule.
Apollo partner Jamshid Ehsani described SpaceX as an ambitious participant in the computing industry.
“SpaceX is one of the most ambitious builders of compute in the world, and we are pleased to have led this financing alongside Goldman Sachs,” said Apollo partner Jamshid Ehsani.
“This transaction reflects the strength of Apollo’s integrated platform, where origination, structuring, syndication and principal investing work together to deliver flexible capital at scale.”
He added that the arrangement emphasizes asset-backed lending structures designed to protect against potential financial losses.
Nvidia Vera Rubin processors will arrive in 2027
The proceeds will finance purchases of Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, an advanced computing system developed for demanding artificial intelligence workloads.
Its capabilities are intended to support computationally intensive activities, including training large models, running inference operations, and processing substantial volumes of data.
SpaceX plans to install the hardware within its terrestrial computing infrastructure rather than deploy the processors aboard spacecraft.
Deliveries scheduled for January through June 2027 will determine when the company can begin incorporating the equipment into its facilities.
The acquisition comes as major technology companies commit substantial capital to computing infrastructure required for increasingly demanding AI applications.
Access to advanced processors has become an important consideration for organizations seeking sufficient computing capacity for development and deployment.
However, the financing announcement provides limited information about SpaceX's intended deployment scale or the specific AI projects requiring the equipment.

articles.title: The Sonos Ace Ultra are my new favourite headphones — but don't dismiss the originals
articles.text:
The Sonos Ace Ultra have replaced my all-time favourite headphones — but I'd still recommend the originals
Sonos has made a great pair of headphones even better, without changing what made me love them in the first place
As much as my colleagues and I try to remain objective when testing and recommending the best headphones, the fact ultimately remains that if you love the way a certain pair of headphones sounds, feels and fits into your life, then they're the right pair for you. And I'm a case in point.
When Sonos made its long-awaited debut in the wireless headphones market with the Sonos Ace in 2024, it's fair to say that my UK-based colleagues weren't entirely bowled over by them. You can read our Sonos Ace review for their full thoughts, and they did at least concede they were fantastic for watching movies.
I, on the other hand, very rapidly fell in love with them. So much so, in fact, that just four months after they launched, I wrote about how there hadn't been a single day I hadn't worn the Sonos Ace. And despite having had the opportunity to try numerous other pairs of premium wireless headphones from brands like Sony, Bose and Sennheiser in the intervening years, I've invariably gravitated back towards the Sonos.
Well, until now. The Aces have finally been usurped as my go-to pair of headphones... although Sonos needn't worry too much, as it's the company's own Ace Ultra that have taken their place.
When the Sonos Ace Ultra were announced, I already had an inkling I was going to love them, and my confidence only grew after my headphone-obsessed colleague Harry Padoan published our Sonos Ace Ultra review.
Having finally got my hands on a pair, I can confidently say my expectations weren't just met — they were exceeded. But that doesn't mean I've consigned the originals to the scrap heap. Far from it, in fact. While I'm smitten with the improved sound and welcome new features of the company's latest pair, there are still plenty of reasons why I'd recommend buying the originals — particularly if you can find them at a sizeable discount.
If it ain't broke...
Of all the things I loved about the original Sonos Ace, it was ultimately their comfort that kept me coming back to them. Sound quality is, of course, incredibly important when choosing a pair of headphones, but it counts for very little if you find yourself wanting to take them off after an hour or so.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I've long maintained that the Sonos Ace are the most comfortable pair of over-ear headphones I've ever worn, and I'm pleased to say the Ace Ultra can now claim that accolade.
Sonos has resisted the temptation to drastically overhaul the design of its debut headphones, and I'm all for it. The plush ear cushions, comfortable headband and understated aesthetic remain, and there's still something wonderfully premium about the way they look and feel.
There are a few minor cosmetic changes, mind you, most notably the Sonos logo on the right earcup, which now sports a shiny chrome finish. It's a small detail, but I personally prefer the more muted appearance of the logo on the original Ace, which I think is more in keeping with the otherwise understated design of the headphones. It's hardly a dealbreaker, though.
That minor cosmetic gripe aside, it's no longer uncommon for a pair of premium wireless headphones to command a price of around AU$700 — Sony, Sennheiser, Apple and Bowers & Wilkins all occupy this territory — but I'd argue not all of them look and feel as expensive as their price tags suggest. The Sonos Ace Ultra, however, absolutely do.
I'm also pleased that Sonos has retained physical controls. As much as some manufacturers seem intent on convincing us that touch-sensitive surfaces are the future of headphone interaction, give me a physical button any day of the week.
It might not make for the most exciting generational update from a visual perspective, but I'd much rather a company recognise when it's got something right than make changes purely for the sake of differentiating a new product.
More musical, more enjoyable
While the changes to the exterior of the Sonos Ace Ultra are subtle, it's a different story under the hood. Sonos has developed an entirely new 40mm driver complete with a redesigned motor structure, promising deeper bass and greater sonic detail. And the fruits of the company's labour are immediately apparent.
I never had any major complaints with the way the original Sonos Ace sounded, but having spent time with the Ace Ultra, it's become apparent there was more performance to be eked out.
The newer pair presents music in a more expansive, engaging manner. There's a greater sense of space to recordings, and music feels less confined to the immediate area around my ears. It's a presentation that does a better job of drawing me into whatever I'm listening to.
And it's not necessarily a difference that requires you to sit down and critically analyse a piece of music to appreciate, either. The Ace Ultra is simply a more enjoyable pair of headphones to listen to — it's comfortably the biggest reason I'd choose the newer model over its predecessor.
I'm also pleased to see Sonos give users greater control over the sound of their headphones with more comprehensive EQ adjustments. The limited equaliser afforded to owners of the original Ace always struck me as a bit of an oversight, particularly given the premium price of the headphones.
I'd love to see those same adjustments rolled out to the first-generation Ace via a software update, although I can equally appreciate why Sonos might want to keep them as a point of differentiation for its more premium pair.
New tricks, but it's an old favourite I still love
Perhaps the biggest addition with the Sonos Ace Ultra is the ability to hand over music playback from the headphones to compatible Sonos speakers, which is made possible with the inclusion of Wi-Fi support. It was a feature many people felt was missing from the first-generation pair, so it’s obviously good to see Sonos listened to consumer feedback.
As someone who has invested quite heavily in the Sonos ecosystem at home, I'm arguably among the target audience for such a feature. And yet, at the time of writing, I haven't actually used it. In all honesty, I'm not entirely sure I ever will.
That's not a criticism of its implementation, nor do I think it's a pointless addition. I'm sure there are plenty of Sonos owners who will relish the opportunity to seamlessly transition from personal listening when arriving at home, to music filling a room. It just doesn't necessarily fit into the way I listen to music at home.
Crucially, though, I wouldn't let that put me off buying the Ace Ultra. I don't need to make use of every feature a product offers to consider it worth my money, and there's more than enough appeal here away from its integration with the wider Sonos ecosystem.
There is, however, one ecosystem-specific feature I'm particularly glad to have carried over from the original Ace: TV Audio Swap.
It's a feature that I continue to find genuinely useful. If my partner is working and I want to watch a movie or spend a few hours playing games, being able to transfer audio from my Sonos Arc Ultra soundbar to my headphones without having to fiddle around with my TV's Bluetooth settings is wonderfully convenient.
And unlike simply connecting a regular pair of Bluetooth headphones to my TV, I can still enjoy an immersive spatial audio experience without disturbing anyone else in the room.
It's one of those features that solves an actual problem in my household, rather than one that requires me to adapt my habits in order to make use of it.
An improvement in noise cancellation, but not a dramatic one
One area where it took me a little longer to appreciate the improvements afforded by the Sonos Ace Ultra was active noise cancellation (ANC).
Our review found the noise cancellation of the Ultra to be an improvement over its predecessor, although my initial experiences had me questioning whether that was indeed the case. During my first few train journeys wearing the new headphones, for example, I could swear the voice of the onboard announcer was more noticeable than it had been when wearing the original Ace.
One possible explanation is that, while I find the Ace Ultra every bit as comfortable as their predecessors, the ear cushions on my original pair have had a couple of years to soften and mould to the contours of my head, potentially creating a more effective acoustic seal.
However, having since spent more time comparing the two pairs side by side, I'm inclined to agree with my colleague. The Ace Ultra does a slightly better job of shutting out the outside world, although I'd argue the improvement isn't anywhere near as apparent as the jump in sound quality.
That's perhaps testament to how effective the noise cancellation of the original Ace already was, so any improvement in this department was likely going to be hard to detect.
But if you're an existing Sonos Ace owner considering upgrading purely for improved noise cancellation, I wouldn't necessarily make it your primary reason for doing so. For me, at least, the improvements to sound quality are a far more compelling argument.
Don't discount the original Sonos Ace
As much as I've enjoyed my time with the Sonos Ace Ultra, I'm not about to stop recommending the original Sonos Ace.
In fact, given how frequently I've seen them discounted since their launch, I'd argue they've become an increasingly compelling proposition.
You're still getting exceptionally comfortable headphones, thoroughly enjoyable sound, a premium design and, if you're a fellow Sonos soundbar owner, the excellent TV Audio Swap feature.
And while I can certainly appreciate the sonic improvements afforded by the Ultra, the arrival of a superior pair of headphones doesn't suddenly make the original pair any worse.
Indeed, if you're already an owner of the first-generation Sonos Ace and you're perfectly happy with them, I don't think there's an immediate need to upgrade — unless you’ve been won over by the new Agave or Sand colours. If you can pick up a pair of the originals for considerably less than the Ultra, there's every chance you'll be just as enamoured with them as I was when they first launched.
But if you're in the market for a new pair of premium wireless headphones and your budget can stretch to the Sonos Ace Ultra, I have little hesitation in recommending them.
Sonos has taken a pair of headphones I already loved, left virtually everything that made me love them intact and improved upon arguably their most important attribute — the way they sound.
I suspect it'll be quite some time before another pair of headphones manages to prise them away from my ears.
Max is a senior staff writer for TechRadar who covers home entertainment and audio first, NBN second and virtually anything else that falls under the consumer electronics umbrella third. He's also a bit of an ecommerce fiend, particularly when it comes to finding the latest coupon codes for a variety of publications. He has written for TechRadar's sister publication What Hi-Fi? as well as Pocket-lint, and he's also the editor of Australian Hi-Fi and Audio Esoterica magazines. Max also dabbled in the men's lifestyle publication space, but is now firmly rooted in his first passion of technology.

articles.title: Huawei pode lançar antes uma das principais mudanças do iPhone 20
articles.text:
Huawei pode lançar antes uma das principais mudanças do iPhone 20
Osta O1 é cotado com tela curva nas quatro bordas, tecnologia esperada para o iPhone comemorativo em 2027.
A Apple deve lançar, no ano que vem, um novo iPhone com mudanças visuais para marcar os 20 anos da linha, e pode apostar pela primeira vez em uma tela curva nas quatro bordas. Mas a Huawei pode se adiantar com um celular já nos próximos meses: o Osta O1.
Segundo o leaker Digital Chat Station, conhecido por vazamentos na cadeia de fornecimento de celulares na China, o aparelho incluiria também um chip da família Kirin 9020 e já teria sido registrado para lançamento na China.
Rumores apontam que o modelo deve aproveitar parte do projeto do recém-lançado Huawei Mate 90 Air, apresentado nesta semana. A curvatura na tela, porém, deve ser uma das principais diferenças entre os dois aparelhos.
O Mate 90 Air tem uma tela OLED LTPO de 7 polegadas, com resolução de 1.320 x 2.760 pixels e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz. O processamento fica a cargo do Kirin 9020, mesmo do Huawei Pura 80 Pro, que chegou ao Brasil custando R$ 7.999.
A ficha técnica inclui 12 GB de RAM, versões com 256 GB ou 512 GB de armazenamento, e bateria de 6.500 mAh com carregamento de 66 W. Nas câmeras, traz um sensor principal de 50 MP, teleobjetiva de 12 MP e uma ultrawide de 8 MP.
Ainda não há mais detalhes sobre o Osta O1, mas, segundo o Digital Chat Station, o aparelho repetirá parte das especificações acima. O GSMArena reforça que isso já aconteceu no lançamento do Osta O1 Pro, que trouxe as mesmas características visuais e de hardware do Huawei Pura X View.
Mas é o desenho da tela, com curva nas quatro bordas, que chama atenção. Rumores iniciais sobre o iPhone comemorativo de 20 anos (até aqui, iPhone 20) apontam que a empresa pretende reformular a parte frontal do dispositivo com essas microcurvaturas em todos os cantos e bordas “invisíveis”.
Telas curvas nas quatro bordas não são novidade no mundo dos smartphones, mas, em geral, os aparelhos — com o Xiaomi 14 Ultra e o Oppo Find X8 Pro, — possuem apenas o vidro curvo, mantendo o display dobrado apenas nas laterais.
Caso o Osta O1 se confirme com um display quad-curvo, não seria a primeira vez que a gigante chinesa “furaria” a Apple com meses de antecedência. Antes, quando o iPhone Duo e seu formato “passaporte” ainda era apenas um rumores, a Huawei lançou o Pura X Max.
A Apple ainda não confirmou o aparelho ou o nome dele, mas espera-se que ela repita o feito de 2007, nos dez anos de iPhone, quando a empresa apresentou o iPhone X. Além da tela, os rumores citam botões capacitivos sem partes móveis, melhorias na bateria e nas memórias dedicadas a tarefas de IA, mas deve manter a Ilha Dinâmica.

articles.title: Easter eggs de GTA 6: Bigfoot, ovnis y un misterio al estilo Monte Chiliad
articles.text:
Los jugadores de Grand Theft Auto 6 ya encontraron decenas de easter eggs en Leonida, desde avistamientos del Skunk Ape, la criatura que ocupa el lugar de Bigfoot (Pie Grande), hasta ovnis, homenajes a Vice City y un monumento que podría esconder el nuevo gran misterio de Rockstar Games. Algunos hallazgos parecen confirmados por su aparición dentro del mapa, mientras otros todavía generan dudas.
La búsqueda importa porque Rockstar convirtió los secretos en una parte central de sus mundos abiertos. En GTA 6, los guiños no afectan la historia principal, pero invitan a recorrer pantanos, playas, carreteras y edificios en busca de escenas ocultas, personajes extraños y referencias a juegos anteriores del estudio.
Qué es un easter egg y por qué aparece en videojuegos
Un easter egg, o “huevo de Pascua”, es un mensaje, objeto, función o referencia que los creadores esconden dentro de una obra para que sea descubierto por quienes prestan atención a los detalles. Puede ser una broma interna, un homenaje a otra franquicia, una escena secreta o una actividad que desbloquea contenido.
El término se popularizó en 1980 con Adventure, un juego de Atari 2600. Su programador, Warren Robinett, escondió un mensaje con su nombre dentro del juego después de que la empresa evitara incluir a los desarrolladores en los créditos. El descubrimiento fue comparado con la búsqueda de huevos de Pascua y dio origen a una expresión que sigue vigente.
En GTA 6, los easter eggs aparecen como parte de la exploración de Leonida. Algunos son visibles durante una partida normal; otros exigen visitar lugares concretos, esperar una hora determinada o cumplir condiciones climáticas específicas.
El Skunk Ape ocupa el lugar de Bigfoot en Leonida
Uno de los secretos más comentados es el Skunk Ape, una criatura alta, peluda y cubierta de barro que aparece en los pantanos y manglares. Los avistamientos se concentran en el sur de Cottonmouth Lake, la carretera entre esa zona y Gambit Bay, el puente al sur de Grassrivers y Pelican Valley.
La figura recuerda a Bigfoot, uno de los misterios más conocidos de GTA: San Andreas y GTA V. En esta ocasión, la criatura se relaciona con un tótem y con una línea de Extraños y Lunáticos vinculada a Kirk, quien inicia una especie de búsqueda del ser en los humedales.
Los jugadores también reportaron luces extrañas en el cielo. Un ovni puede aparecer en un camino de tierra del condado de Kelly, cerca de Port Gellhorn, durante la madrugada. Según los hallazgos compartidos, el evento exige que el personaje esté solo y puede desbloquear el trofeo The Truth Is Out There.
El monumento de Manifest Canyon recuerda al Monte Chiliad
El misterio que más discusiones genera está en Manifest Canyon, en el condado de Kelly. Allí hay un monumento formado por un pilar, un globo terráqueo y cuatro caballos. Una placa afirma que los animales representan la fauna, la corrupción, la humanidad y el “yeyo”, una combinación que parece seria y satírica al mismo tiempo.
La comunidad ya lo relaciona con el Monte Chiliad de GTA V, un enigma que llevó a los jugadores a estudiar murales, símbolos, montañas y teorías durante años. Aún no existe una explicación definitiva sobre el monumento de Leonida, pero su diseño sugiere que podría tener conexiones con otros secretos.
Otro hallazgo es un nido con huevos pintados en lo alto de una torre de radio del condado de Vice-Dale. Jason o Lucía pueden tomar uno y lanzarlo al vacío, lo que activa una escena breve. El detalle funciona como un easter egg literal dentro de un mapa lleno de referencias.
Vice City, Red Dead Redemption y otras referencias
Rockstar también recuperó elementos de su propia historia. En tiendas retro aparece la camisa hawaiana azul de Tommy Vercetti, mientras guías turísticos hablan de un antiguo jefe criminal de los años ochenta. El Hotel Ocean View y el Club Malibu siguen presentes como lugares restaurados dentro de la Vice City actual.
Las referencias a Red Dead Redemption incluyen el sombrero de Arthur Morgan, libros sobre el Viejo Oeste, menciones a Flaco Hernández y matrículas de New Austin. En tiendas de coleccionables aparecen objetos vinculados con Bully y Manhunt.
También hay guiños a GTA IV y GTA V: un libro sobre un mafioso de Liberty City, una nota sobre Fabien LaRouche y una conversación sobre el Monte Chiliad. Leonida convierte así la exploración en una búsqueda constante de referencias, bromas y misterios que todavía no tienen respuesta.

articles.title: 75 millions d'euros pour les données de santé des hôpitaux, avec pas tant de souveraineté que ça, déplore la Cour des comptes
articles.text:
Les pouvoirs publics ont injecté 75 millions d'euros dans les entrepôts de données de santé des hôpitaux. Jeudi, la Cour des comptes a reconnu des avancées, mais regrette que le chantier de la souveraineté ne soit pas total.
Dans un rapport publié le jeudi 27 novembre, la Cour des comptes dresse le bilan des entrepôts de données de santé hospitaliers, les bases qui rassemblent les informations médicales produites par les hôpitaux pour la recherche et les soins. Les objectifs de déploiement sont bien atteints, avec 54 entrepôts recensés par la CNIL, le gendarme des données, mais les magistrats relèvent des systèmes qui communiquent mal, des usages peu évalués et des risques de sécurité et de souveraineté à mieux maîtriser. Ils appellent l'État à clarifier sa stratégie dès 2027.
Black Friday Roborock
Profitez du meilleur du nettoyage et bénéficiez de meilleures offres et services : plus de points Cadeau, réductions sur les packs, assurance transport gratuite, paiement en plusieurs fois sans frais, prix garantis pendant 30 jours
Quand les hôpitaux français peinent à partager leurs données de santé
Un entrepôt de données de santé fonctionne un peu comme une grande bibliothèque médicale. Il rassemble et classe les informations produites par un hôpital pour qu'elles servent à la recherche, au pilotage de l'établissement ou à l'amélioration des soins. Son intérêt vient d'abord de la nature de ces données. Ce sont des données cliniques, qui complètent celles, surtout médico-administratives, du Système national des données de santé (SNDS). Les établissements de santé, en particulier les CHU, ont lancé ces entrepôts. La première autorisation date de 2017, et en mai 2026, ils représentaient plus d'un tiers des 156 entrepôts de données de santé recensés par la CNIL. L'État et la Sécurité sociale ont accompagné le mouvement via France 2030, avec pas moins de 75 millions d'euros, étalés sur plusieurs années et répartis entre 16 projets lauréats.
Sur ce point, la Cour des comptes considère que le pari est tenu. Les objectifs chiffrés ont été atteints. Le reste a moins bien suivi en revanche. L'État n'a par exemple pas suffisamment anticipé l'organisation des entrepôts dans les territoires, la mise en commun des moyens ni les conditions de leur fonctionnement. Les systèmes informatiques hospitaliers communiquent mal entre eux, ce qui complique le partage des données et ajoute des coûts. Quant à la Plateforme des données de santé (ex-Health Data Hub), elle n'a pas réussi à fédérer les acteurs comme prévu. Elle coordonne un socle commun de données hospitalières, mais ce travail reste à poursuivre.
Les entrepôts ont pourtant déjà des résultats à montrer. L'AP-HP comptait en avril 110 publications scientifiques tirées du sien. Santé publique France mise de son côté sur le projet Orchidée pour produire, à partir des données hospitalières, des indicateurs de surveillance épidémiologique, notamment sur les infections respiratoires. Dans les hôpitaux, ces outils servent aussi aux tableaux de bord d'activité ou à mieux coder les séjours. Mais ces usages restent assez inégaux, en réalité peu suivis et insuffisamment évalués.
Les acteurs extérieurs, qu'ils soient publics ou privés, ont du mal à savoir quelles données existent, puis à y accéder dans des délais raisonnables. Ce point va compter, car le règlement européen sur l'espace des données de santé, adopté en mars 2025, va progressivement obliger les détenteurs de ces données à les ouvrir. La Cour demande donc de mieux mesurer l'utilisation réelle des entrepôts et la qualité des recherches qui en sortent, et de faciliter le partage des données.
La qualification SecNumCloud n'est toujours pas exigée pour héberger les données de santé
Les données utilisées pour la recherche sont pseudonymisées, c'est-à-dire que le nom et les identifiants directs des patients sont remplacés par un code. Mais les magistrats de la Cour des comptes relèvent que les entrepôts restent reliés aux systèmes informatiques des hôpitaux, et donc exposés à leurs failles. Or ces systèmes sont une cible régulière des pirates, comme l'a encore montré il y a quelques jours la cyberattaque contre le CHU de Guadeloupe. La Cour n'a cependant relevé aucun incident de sécurité déclaré qui concerne directement un entrepôt. Elle pointe aussi les limites du contrôle, en rappelant que la CNIL a fixé dès 2021 un référentiel exigeant. Sauf qu'aujourd'hui, ses vérifications restent trop limitées pour garantir que les entrepôts le respectent dans la durée. Les magistrats recommandent donc de renforcer les contrôles, sur dossier comme sur place.
Pour l'hébergement, les pratiques sont différentes entre les établissements. Certains gardent leurs propres serveurs, d'autres passent par un prestataire. Dans ce cas, la certification « Hébergeur de données de santé » est exigée, mais pas la qualification SecNumCloud, qui garantit un haut niveau de sécurité et de souveraineté. Le rapport présente plusieurs scénarios pour faire évoluer ces exigences, chacun avec un gain de souveraineté et un surcoût différents. Le sujet est sensible, puisqu'il a fallu des années de polémique pour que la Plateforme des données de santé choisisse en avril le Français Scaleway (groupe Iliad-Free) pour remplacer Microsoft. La migration est attendue d'ici 2027.
Alors combien coûte vraiment un entrepôt ? C'est difficile à dire, notamment faute d'un suivi comptable assez précis. Selon les estimations recueillies par la Cour, construire un entrepôt coûte de quelques millions à 40 millions d'euros, puis il faut compter de 1 à 15 millions par an pour le faire fonctionner. Les aides au démarrage ont couvert environ la moitié des investissements initiaux prévus par les projets soutenus. Le fonctionnement, la maintenance et les évolutions technologiques ont en revanche été mal anticipés. Les finances publiques étant serrées, la Cour propose un modèle mixte, avec autofinancement des établissements, prestations de services et redevances prévues par le règlement européen, dont les modalités restent à préciser.
L'argent public pourra encore compléter, à condition d'être mieux ciblé et conditionné à des résultats mesurables. La Cour demande enfin à l'État de clarifier sa stratégie dès 2027 et de mieux suivre les usages comme les coûts. Les nouveaux crédits nationaux ne devraient alors aller qu'aux entrepôts qui atteignent une taille critique, montrent des usages réels et proposent des données de qualité, standardisées.

articles.title: PC portable : Core i9 ou Ryzen 5, quel TECNO Megabook correspond à votre usage ?
articles.text:
PC portable : Core i9 ou Ryzen 5, quel TECNO Megabook correspond à votre usage ?
Deux cents euros séparent les deux TECNO Megabook K15S vendus chez Auchan pour le Black Friday. Avant de regarder le prix, demandez-vous ce que vous ferez vraiment de votre ordinateur. Voici comment choisir, et comment obtenir 100 € en échange de votre ancien ordinateur portable.
Votre ordinateur portable rame à l’ouverture du moindre tableur et vous comptez profiter du Black Friday pour le remplacer ? Prudence. Dans ces moments-là, la tentation consiste à s’orienter vers le processeur le plus puissant, au risque de payer pour une puissance que vous n’utiliserez pas. Chez Auchan, TECNO propose deux versions de son Megabook K15S. Elles ont presque tout en commun, du châssis en métal à l’écran de 15,6 pouces. Mais elles s’adressent à deux profils bien distincts.
Quel que soit votre choix, vous disposerez d’un écran Full HD de 15,6 pouces, de 16 Go de mémoire vive et une batterie de 70 Wh compatible avec la recharge rapide USB-C 65 W. La connectique est particulièrement complète : elle comprend deux ports USB-A, deux ports USB-C (dont un dédié à la recharge et un multifonction), une sortie HDMI 1.4, un lecteur de cartes microSD, une prise casque-micro et un port Ethernet RJ45 Gigabit. Le bouton d’alimentation intègre un lecteur d’empreintes et un volet occulte la webcam quand vous ne l’utilisez pas.
Core i9 ou Ryzen 5 : à chaque usage son processeur
Le vrai critère de choix repose sur vos usages. Le Megabook K15SRA se destine davantage aux utilisateurs qui sollicitent régulièrement leur processeur, notamment pour le multitâche et les applications exigeantes. Son Core i9-13900HK compte 14 cœurs et 20 threads, tandis que son SSD de 1 To offre un espace de stockage confortable. Cette capacité constitue un avantage par rapport aux 256 Go proposés sur la version Ryzen. La mémoire vive peut être étendue jusqu’à 32 Go, offrant davantage de possibilités pour accompagner vos usages au quotidien. Son écran IPS Full HD de 15,6 pouces offre une résolution de 1920 × 1080 pixels. Auchan l’affiche à 699,99 € au moment où nous écrivons ces lignes.
À l’inverse, si votre quotidien tient plutôt entre la bureautique et les visioconférences, la puissance d’un Core i9 ne vous sera pas d’une grande utilité. La bonne solution ? Le Megabook K15SDA, à 499,99 €, qui s’appuie sur un Ryzen 5 7430U, une puce à basse consommation. Associé à une batterie de 70 Wh, le Ryzen 5 7430U constitue une configuration adaptée aux usages quotidiens, de la bureautique aux visioconférences. Le K15SDA dispose en revanche d’un SSD de 256 Go, contre 1 To pour le K15SRA. Une capacité à prendre en compte si vous stockez beaucoup de fichiers localement.
Reprise : 100 € remboursés en quatre étapes
La bonne nouvelle, c’est que, quel que soit votre choix, les deux modèles ouvrent droit à un remboursement de 100 € si vous retournez un ancien ordinateur portable. Sur le principe, c’est simple. Il ne s’agit pas d’une remise au moment de l’achat. Vous payez le prix affiché, puis TECNO vous verse la somme par virement. La marche à suivre tient en quatre temps.
- Vous achetez l’un des deux Megabook chez Auchan, en magasin ou en ligne, hors vendeurs tiers de la place de marché.
- Vous vous inscrivez sur le site de l’opération dans les 15 jours.
- Une fois votre dossier accepté à titre provisoire, vous disposez de 15 jours pour renvoyer votre ancien PC portable.
- Le virement arrive dans les 25 jours qui suivent la validation.
L’ancien ordinateur portable peut être de n’importe quelle marque et dans n’importe quel état, à condition que son écran mesure au moins 12,6 pouces. Les netbooks sont exclus.
En pratique, le K15SRA convient aux usages plus exigeants, tandis que le K15SDA cible davantage la bureautique et les usages quotidiens.
Bon à savoir
L’offre est réservée aux particuliers majeurs résidant en France et titulaires d’un compte bancaire SEPA, dans la limite des 3 500 premiers produits éligibles. Elle court jusqu’au 18 janvier 2027, ce qui laisse le temps d’y penser pour un cadeau de Noël. Vérifiez le prix et la disponibilité chez Auchan avant de vous décider, puis consultez les conditions complètes sur la page de l’opération.

articles.title: 15 tech gadgets that improved my tech life are on sale for less than $50 — Black Friday pricing means some are even under $25
articles.text:
15 tech gadgets that improved my tech life are on sale for less than $50 — Black Friday pricing means some are even under $25
From SSD cloners to screwdrivers, travel-light tech accessories, these are affordable game-changers.
As much as I love high-priced tech like my RTX 4090-equipped custom gaming rig or the 65-inch LG OLED TV I use as my monitor, most of us can't afford to spend several hundred dollars or more on a tech gift, no matter how important the recipient might be in our lives. But you can still improve the tech lives of your friends and family (or yourself) while spending a comparatively small amount of money during the Black Friday deals season.
I own all of the affordable devices listed below, and they all typically sell for less than $50. Some are even under $20! All of these products have made my tech-saturated world a little lighter, brighter, or just plain nicer in their own way. If you're looking for a small tech splurge for yourself, or an affordable gift for that tech-savvy friend or family member, one of these $50-or-under options might be a good fit and a great deal while Black Friday deals keep their prices lower than normal.
My favorite $50 deals
- Rosewill M.2 SSD Cloner ($49.99)
- Hoto Electric Screwdriver Kit ($29.98)
- 8BitDo Retro R8 Mouse with Charging Dock ($49.99)
Become an IT hero with Rosewill's M.2 SSD Cloner
Last year, a family member asked for help with an older desktop PC that was struggling to run Windows 10 and several programs on a cramped 110 GB SSD. I figured I could clone the boot drive onto a more spacious drive, so the OS and programs had more space to stretch out.
But the thought of juggling multiple USB enclosures or having to take the drive home and shuffle it in and out of my desktop filled me with dread, as I pictured hours spent getting everything done and the system back up and running. So I looked into getting an M.2 SSD cloner and was surprised to see they can be found for less than $50.
With support for NVMe M.2 SSDs and offline cloning, this handy device makes it simple to move your files or OS from one drive to another. And with a 20 Gbps USB-C interface, it's also speedy in your OS of choice if you want to use software to clone or move your data between drives.
While I don't love the glossy plastic shell of Rosewill's cloner, it's one of the more affordable options. And it supports both NVMe M.2 drives and older AHCI models (Sorry, SATA). Using the cloner is pretty straightforward. You plug in the included USB-C power adapter, put your source drive in the left slot, the destination drive in the right slot, press the power button on the back, and a few logos light up, letting you know you're ready to go. Press the clone button on the top, and the drive cloning will commence (provided your destination is the same size or larger than your source).
That's assuming you want to do an offline clone. But because I needed to also resize the partition between the old 110 GB and a newer Team Group 512 GB SSD, I used the second included USB-C cable to connect the Rosewill cloner to my laptop and powered up the device. Within seconds, both drives were recognized in Windows, so I fired up the excellent free DiskGenius software, cloned the old partition to the new drive with a few clicks, and then used the software to drag the boot partition to the full size of the new drive. The whole process took just a few minutes, since the Rosewill cloner supports 20 Gbps USB, and I wasn't exactly copying a huge partition. 
When the cloning process was finished and the partition expanded, it was hard to believe it was all that easy. I had expected to be at the task for hours, but I was done in less than 30 minutes. Sure, unless you're in IT, a drive cloner might not be something you use regularly, but it's sure handy to have around when you need it. You could also use it to save some money by buying a laptop with a cramped SSD and swapping in something much roomier – provided, of course, the laptop's storage isn't soldered to the motherboard. 
The Rosewill cloner is also handy for just checking the contents of old M.2 drives you may have lying around. But if that's all you need, you can buy an NVMe enclosure or a single-drive dock. I also own a version of this model from Suitok, which costs $15.99.
This tiny, cheap, magnetic, USB-charging flashlight is great for PC building and other everyday tasks
I picked up the OLIGHT IMINI 2 mini flashlight last year on impulse because it looked well-designed and cost around $20, but it's often on sale for much less. Its simple design and built-in USB-A plug for charging make it fun to use – just pull the back off, and it turns on. The magnet at the back lets you easily mount it anywhere you need a little extra light. I've used it inside a steel PC case while fiddling with RGB wires, and under my sink while attaching a glass rinser.
At just 2.17 inches long, this flashlight is rated to 50 lumens, and it sports a magnetic back with a USB-A plug for charging. Pulling the back off turns on the flashlight, and the magnetic back makes it easy to mount the light on anything made of ferrous metal.
The OLIGHT IMINI 2 is also small enough for your keychain, is designed to live with your keys, and includes two silicone covers for the USB port and a little carabiner clip. But the flashlight portion is only held to the charging port via a magnet, and I feel like (for me, at least) it would likely fall off and get lost before too long if left on my keys.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
I've used the HOTO 3.6V Screwdriver Set to build dozens of PCs
I build a lot of PCs, though not as many lately thanks to the RAM apocalypse, and I also do regular home improvement work around my apartment. So a cordless screwdriver is a nice thing to have. I also own a much slimmer Wowstick, but have found HOTO's NEX O1 Pro to be much more useful thanks to its extra (and variable) torque. It's great for loosening those factory-installed screws on PC cases that just don't want to let go, and also good for assembling furniture.
The HOTO won't replace my DeWalt drill for bigger, tougher jobs. But for everyday tasks, it's powerful enough, easy to charge over USB-C, and even looks good on my workbench.
Hoto's wireless screwdriver has three torque settings, charges over USB-C, and looks surprisingly good. It's even proven quite durable, as I've dropped it off of ladders and my workbench at least a dozen times over the past few years, and it's still working flawlessly.
Cheap USB media control box makes PC volume and track control a more tactile, retro experience
For those of us who grew up in the 1900s, few things beat a chunky tactile volume knob and physical buttons for controlling media. And Vaydeer's USB device provides that, and then some. I own the previous version of this device, and love it for controlling and muting music at my treadmill desk while I work.
I use the buttons on it to play / pause audio and video and move forward to the next track or backward to the previous one. It's totally plug-and-play, as no drivers are needed.
Just plug this simple USB device into a USB port and you can control the volume and select tracks without fiddling with your keyboard or mouse.
Bring a retro SNES feel to modern gaming with 8Bitdo's SN30 Pro wireless Bluetooth controller
What's not to love about a SNES-inspired wireless gaming controller that's compatible with Windows, Mac, Android, and the Nintendo Switch? Not much, as far as I'm concerned. Especially considering it's not super expensive.
As you might expect, given the SN30 Pro's small size and many more buttons than the SNES controller it was based on, its Rumble motors aren't the strongest. And the layout can feel a little cramped for some modern games. But for any retro game, and especially platformers, this is my go-to controller. It feels familiar and nostalgic, which, for me at least, goes well with those occasional long game sessions.
With its SNES-inspired design, this controller will entice gamers of a certain age. But its appeal goes beyond its looks, with Hall Effect joysticks and support for the Switch 1 and 2, PC, macOS, and basically any OS that supports games and Bluetooth.
Retro looks meets modern specs in this NES-themed mouse from 8BitDo
There are so many gaming mouse options, most with specs that go well above and beyond my wrist-twitching capabilities. So I instead chose something with style that caught my eye, 8BitDo's Retro R8 Mouse with Charging Dock. This NES-inspired mouse is designed for nostalgia, with its black, gray, and red color scheme and round red side buttons. And 8BitDo went the extra mile (or two) by designing a weighted charging dock (with its own NES-like touches) and a spot for the 2.4 GHz dongle. This is the kind of extra feature that's more common in mice that cost twice as much.
The nostalgia of this mouse's design is nice. But it also sports a 26,000 DPI sensor, 4K polling, and a really nice charging dock that also houses the 2.4 GHz dongle. If you're in a pinch or not gaming, Bluetooth is also supported.
Under the hood, you get a decent 26,000 DPI sensor and 4K polling (plenty for us non-esports gamers), an ambidextrous design with two side buttons on either side, and a clicky, rubberized scroll wheel. The side buttons, which are concave, took a little getting used to for me. But they are also so distinctive that now I miss them while I game using other mice. 
If the NES theme isn't your thing, the company also sells a translucent-green XBox version, as well as a champagne-hued C64 Edition.
Never run out of USB ports with this powered 11-port hub
If you're like me, you never have access to enough USB ports. I solved this problem by picking up this Ikai hub, with 60W of power for your external drives and peripherals, and a premium metal shell. It sports three speedy 10 Gbps ports (two USB-C), along with seven 5 GBps USB-A ports. The final USB-C on the end of the hub is for charging your phone or other devices, and delivers 20W.
The other nice feature is that all the data ports have a side button, so you can toggle them on and off to save some power. I also find this handy for swapping between wireless mice and keyboards, while keeping the tiny dongles plugged in so I don't lose them.
With 11 ports and up to 10 Gbps of bandwidth, a solid aluminum shell, and buttons so you can cut power to individual ports you aren't using, this USB hub is a great addition to your desk. It has external power for better stability and even a 20W USB-C PD port on the end for charging phones or peripherals.
The sole thing to keep in mind about this (and basically any) hub, is that it has a single 10 Gbps connection to your PC. So don't expect to plug in multiple high-speed devices (like SSDs) and have them run simultaneously at full speed. If that's what you need, you should look at one of the best Thunderbolt or USB4 hubs (which cost significantly more).
Add recessed power and USB charging ports to your desk for under $20
OK, this one's only for the DIY-inclined, because it involves cutting a rectangle in your desk (or anywhere else you might want some flush-mount power ports, like a nightstand). Jgstkcity's recessed power strip lets you drop a couple of AC outlets and two USB charging ports (one 30W USB-C) anywhere you need them – again, once you've cut a hole for it.
It is, of course, smart to be cautious of no-name power accessories and strips. But I've used two variations of these strips for roughly three years now, and nothing has ever felt hot or failed. I have this model installed in the narrow stand I built that lives right behind my couch, up against the wall. It's a super-convenient place for power outlets, especially when friends or family stop by. I just warn people not to put drinks near there. Thankfully, the coffee table, in front of the couch, is an even more convenient place for those.
You'll probably need a drill and a saw to install it, but having a couple of power plugs and USB-C PD power right on the surface of your desk or nightstand is super convenient. And once you have the hole cut, this strip is dead-simple to install.
Stay charged and save space while traveling abroad with Anker's slim Nano Travel Adapter
When you're traveling to another country for more than a few days, every small bit of space you can save helps. But you also usually need a travel adapter to plug your devices into the outlets of other countries. Anker's Nano Travel Adapter serves both needs well, as it's roughly half the thickness of other adapters and is designed to work in over 200 countries. 
The Nano Travel Adapter also has four USB ports for charging, which is super convenient for keeping my phone, e-reader, and earbuds juiced up without needing a separate charger. There are two USB-A ports on the bottom and two USB-C ports on the side, with the latter delivering up to 20W. The adapter also comes in black or white/silver. I opted for the white one, which makes it easier to find after months in a drawer when I'm not traveling.
Anker's slim travel adapter is 43% smaller than many other adapters, while supporting over 200 countries with its fold-down plugs. It also has two USB-C and two USB-A ports for charging, at up to 20W.
The major downside over other travel chargers is that the Nano Travel Adapter doesn't support plugging in devices with three-prong (grounded) plugs. But I haven't found this an issue since I typically plug things like my Baseus flat laptop charger in while traveling, rather than high-power devices like a desktop PC or hair dryer.
Give your wrists (and elbows) a fresh resting space
For anyone who spends their days (and/or nights) in front of a keyboard, a good wrist rest is key for both short-term comfort and long-term limb health. And having stumbled onto these combo wrist and elbow rests earlier this year, I never want to use anything else.
Even if you have a wrist rest you've been using for years, there's a good chance it's a little funky or the fabric is worn out. Gel and fabric rests only tend to last a few years before they get funky, so even if you don't quite need a new one now, it's nice to have a replacement waiting in the wings.
These unique wrist and elbow rests are designed to hang over the edge of your desk, which makes them a great option for people who lean on their elbows or if you just have a cramped desk setup. Available in multiple colors and sizes, the 11.8-inch version is wide enough that I use one for my compact keyboard at work, and the other at home for my gaming setup.
Lithium rechargeables are great for high-drain devices, and this 8-AA set with charger is just $27
After the good experience I've had with the company's NiMH batteries, I bought Powerowl's Lithium rechargeable batteries earlier this year. And boy am I glad I did. These last months longer in my smart door locks than those older batteries, which means I only have to swap the cells on two doors a few times a year now.
Full disclosure: I have had one of these batteries refuse to recharge after its first power cycle. But out of the three sets I now own, that's not a terrible track record. I just wish the company also made AAA lithium cells for my other devices.
These 1.5V lithium batteries are designed for high-drain devices and rated at 3600 mWh. The charger plugs in over USB-C and can also charge older NiMH batteries.
TP-Link's AX1800 WiFi 6 USB Adapter delivers Wi-Fi 6 to older devices over USB
Have you upgraded your router to Wi-Fi 6 or later, but your desktop or laptop doesn't have the requisite hardware to take advantage of your recent network tech? TP-Link's AX1800 WiFi 6 USB Adapter is here to solve that problem for you. It's quite large by USB Wi-Fi dongle standards, but I've found it works quite well with my Wi-Fi 6 router.
I have the router running downstairs from my office, and it instantly fixed an issue I was having with very poor reception from the SFF PC I built in the Fractal Terra case.
Sure, it's big and bulky with two antennas, but this Wi-Fi 6 USB adapter can deliver some serious speed to your desktop or laptop when paired with a Wi-Fi 6 or later router.
Orico USB 3.0 Clamp Hub is easy to mount on many desks
This is a four-port, 5Gbps USB-A hub that's designed to clamp onto your monitor or desk and give you extra convenient connectivity.
It comes in black or silver and has a nice, sturdy metal frame. Just note that its clamp section is pretty shallow, and its adjustable screw can only open between 10 and 32 mm, so it won't fit on all monitors or desks.
An otherwise standard four-port USB 3.0 hub, this Orico model stands out for its metal frame and clamp design.
Clean up the cables under your desk with a tray
If you to get a handle on the PC cables in your home or office, some cheap cable management trays will do the job. This two-pack comes with tape, though heavier loads will ultimately require some screws.
Besides the trays, this kit also comes with cable ties and a few cable clips you can place along the bottom or sides of your desk. One of these has been holding up the PC cable clutter in my living room for the past year. But I had to screw it into my desk because it's holding an Anker power strip, plus the large external power brick from my TV / Monitor.
If there's a rat's nest of cables under your desk, attaching some trays down there can help you clean it up. This set has tape for light loads, but for longer-term cleanliness, you probably want to consider screws.
Keep a fast charging cable with your keys
You may, like me, be swimming in a world of USB cables. But that doesn't mean you always have one when you need it away from home. This short 240W USB4 charging cable from EndlesShine solves that by being small enough to attach to your keys. It's not always the most convenient option, at just over 5 inches long, but it will do in a pinch and has come in handy more than once, particularly on trips when I'm traveling light.
It's short in length, at 5.11 inches, but this keychain cable supports 240W charging and USB4 (40Gbps speeds). Clip it onto your keys, and you'll always have a fast cable when you need one.
If you're the type who is rough with your keys, the plastic cap may wear out over time, so you might want to just keep the cable in a pocket or your bag. It even comes in white and yellow if you don't like basic black.

articles.title: Cómo revisar si un celular Android viene con virus de fábrica y qué hacer
articles.text:
Un celular Android nuevo puede traer programas maliciosos instalados de fábrica, y la cantidad de equipos con esa infección que detecta cada mes la empresa Kaspersky se multiplicó por más de dos veces y media en un año.
La compañía comparó noviembre de 2025 con octubre de 2026 y contabilizó los equipos con código malicioso en el sistema o en las aplicaciones preinstaladas.
Dos familias de programas espía, llamadas Triada y Keenadu, aparecieron en el 88% de los equipos infectados entre enero y octubre de 2026. Solo Keenadu afectó a más de 220.000 dispositivos en ese período, según la empresa.
Cómo llega el software malicioso a un equipo nuevo
Según la empresa de ciberseguridad, el código malicioso puede ingresar a través de la cadena de producción. En algunos casos, puede ser instalado de forma intencional por un proveedor.
En otros, una marca legítima puede recibir software comprometido de un tercero que actúa de mala fe, o construir el sistema sobre una base previamente infectada sin que la empresa lo advierta.
Los dos programas funcionan por módulos: los atacantes pueden enviar componentes adicionales al teléfono.
La empresa enumera módulos conocidos de Triada que roban credenciales de aplicaciones de mensajería y redes sociales, interceptan llamadas y mensajes de texto, sustituyen enlaces en el navegador y sustraen criptomonedas.
Keenadu, en cambio, se utilizó principalmente para generar clics falsos en anuncios. Las versiones examinadas por la empresa recibían la orden de permanecer inactivas durante unos dos meses y medio, un plazo que, según los investigadores, probablemente busca que el dueño se acostumbre al equipo y no detecte comportamientos inusuales.
Esa demora puede dificultar la detección: un teléfono puede parecer normal durante semanas. Entre los síntomas que menciona el informe figuran una menor duración de la batería, recalentamiento, fallos en aplicaciones y anuncios que consumen datos móviles. Se registraron equipos que reproducían sonidos sin motivo aparente.
Cómo y qué revisar en un celular Android
Google indica en su página de ayuda que Play Protect, su sistema de análisis y protección, viene activado de forma predeterminada.
Para comprobarlo, hay que abrir Google Play Store, tocar el ícono de perfil e ingresar en Play Protect y luego en Ajustes. Allí debe estar activada la opción para analizar aplicaciones con Play Protect.
La misma página explica cómo verificar si el equipo está certificado: desde el perfil de Play Store se accede a Ajustes y, en la sección Información, aparece el estado de certificación del dispositivo.
Esta comprobación permite confirmar que el equipo cumple con los requisitos de compatibilidad de Google, un dato útil al evaluar un teléfono de marca desconocida.
Play Protect puede alertar sobre aplicaciones potencialmente dañinas, desactivarlas o eliminarlas, y ofrece la posibilidad de desinstalarlas desde la notificación. Cuando aparezca una alerta, conviene revisar y, si corresponde, desinstalar la aplicación señalada.
Es útil controlar la lista de aplicaciones en busca de nombres desconocidos que el usuario no instaló y que no pertenecen a la marca del teléfono.
La compañía de ciberseguirdad aclara un límite importante: cuando el código está en la partición del sistema, puede requerirse asistencia especializada para eliminarlo, y en algunos casos ni siquiera reinstalar el sistema operativo resulta suficiente.
Por eso, restablecer el teléfono a su estado de fábrica puede no bastar si la infección está incluida en el software original.
Qué hacer si hay señales de infección en el celular Android
El restablecimiento de fábrica borra todos los datos del teléfono, según la ayuda de Android, y exige recordar la cuenta de Google y su contraseña, contar con una copia de seguridad y cargar la batería al 70% como mínimo.
Es un paso razonable ante una aplicación dudosa, aunque no garantiza eliminar software malicioso preinstalado.
Si las alertas reaparecen tras el restablecimiento, la opción prudente es dejar de usar el equipo para operaciones bancarias, mensajería y cuentas importantes, y reclamar al vendedor o al fabricante. Cambiar las contraseñas desde otro dispositivo es una medida adicional de seguridad.
El informe también identificó estos programas en relojes inteligentes infantiles y en reproductores de televisión conectados a internet.

articles.title: Dyson may have just won Black Friday with a 59% discount on the V8 Cyclone — now just AU$268
articles.text:
Dyson may have just won Black Friday with a 59% discount on the V8 Cyclone — now just AU$268
Less than AU$300 for a Dyson stick vacuum? In this economy? What a bargain
I think it's fair to say that Dyson tech can err on the expensive side, yet the Dyson Black Friday sale has flipped that notion on its head entirely, with up to AU$900 off many of its most popular products.
The standout for me, however, has to be a mega 59% discount on the superb V8 Cyclone, which now sees its price plummet to AU$268. It could just be the best vacuum cleaner deal this Black Friday sales season.
And it's not just a low-cost Dyson that should have you reaching for your wallet — as you can read in our Dyson V8 Cyclone review, it's good value even without a discount. According to my colleague who tested it, the small upgrades Dyson has given it over the original V8 make it the better machine.
- Follow our live coverage of the Black Friday sales in Australia for more deals and discounts
This is the best price on the new V8 Cyclone that I've seen. With this newer model, you're getting better suction (150AW) and up to 60 minutes of runtime on a single charge (compared to 40 on the older machine). The newer model also gets 3 suction modes as opposed to only 2.
If you're still not convinced the V8 Cyclone is worth it, let me put it another way: Firstly, it's a 2025 release, so it takes advantage of the latest tech that you won't even find on the V10 Cyclone or the V11 Advanced. Secondly, the V10 and V11 models usually cost more, even when discounted.
In fact, our reviewer also tested the new V8 against the older V11 and found that they both clean just as well, but the V8 Cyclone is lighter and easier to move around. It also matches the V11's runtime and has removable batteries too (unlike the older V8). She found that even in low suction settings, the V8 Cyclone could be quite "sucky".
And, while how a vacuum cleaner looks doesn't necessarily need to be taken into consideration, I do think it helps that the darker colour scheme Dyson has used here is quite attractive.
So, if you're keen on a new Dyson vacuum, give the V8 Cyclone some serious consideration, especially at this discounted price. And do note you can pick it up for the same price from The Good Guys.

articles.title: Black Week: Galaxy S26 FE cai ainda mais e chega a 47% OFF com cupom
articles.text:
Black Week: Galaxy S26 FE cai ainda mais e chega a 47% OFF com cupom
Galaxy S26 FE (128 GB) com tela AMOLED e câmera de 50 MP atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento, com desconto de 47% no Pix com cupom exclusivo no app Magalu
O Galaxy S26 FE de 128 GB está saindo por R$ 2.899 no Pix com cupom INFLU300 apenas pelo app do Magazine Luiza. O premium acessível da Samsung, com tela de 120 Hz e melhorias de IA, atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento na Black Week 2026, com desconto de 47% sobre o original de R$ 5.499.
O menor preço que já encontramos para o Galaxy S26 FE 5G 128 GB foi R$ 2.899, na Black Friday de 2026 (Magalu). Fora de datas promocionais, o melhor foi R$ 3.249,10 (Magalu, 5/11/2026).
O novo Galaxy S26 FE possui uma tela LTPO AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,7″, com taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de 1.900 nits. Essa combinação reproduz cores vibrantes com alta fluidez, além de entregar garantia de visibilidade em qualquer situação.
Seu chip Exynos 2500 de 3 nanômetros e os 8 GB de RAM sustentam apps pesados e novas funções de IA, como a assistente Bixby melhorada, que lê infos no celular, e o recurso My FanCam, que acompanha a pessoa durante filmagens.
O kit principal de câmeras filma em 8K. Ele inclui wide de 50 MP com OIS e ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e telefoto de 8 MP com zoom óptico de 3x para aproximações. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies e filma em 4K a 60 fps.
O corpo de alumínio do S26 FE é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Gorilla Glass Victus+, resistente contra pancadas e quedas. A certificação IP68 confere proteção em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.900 mAh tem autonomia de até 29 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a Samsung. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 45 W via USB-C e de 15 W sem fio garante energia para um dia inteiro com apenas alguns minutos na tomada.
O Galaxy S26 FE de 128 GB (R$ 2.899 no Pix com cupom INFLU300 apenas pelo app Magalu) será atualizado até o Android 24 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.
A edição 2026 da Black Friday é amanhã (27), e lojas como Magalu se preparam para oferecer diversas ofertas em eletrônicos com cupons e condições especiais até a Cyber Monday, na próxima segunda-feira (30).
