articles.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
articles.text:
Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.
According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.
As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

articles.title: Google Pixel 10a vs Pixel 9a — here's why I'd choose the older model (if the price is right)
articles.text:
I've used both the Google Pixel 10a and Pixel 9a — if the price is right, I'd choose the older model this Black Friday
The Pixel 10a is newer, but its upgrades are few and far between
With their Pro-rivaling software, impressive main cameras, and affordable price tags, Google's A-series Pixel phones have always offered discerning Android fans great value for money.
If you're in the market for a new Android phone that won’t break the bank, these colorful devices should be top of your list. And historically, I would have simply recommended the latest A series model and sent you on your way.
But in 2026, it's not that simple. The latest A-series Pixel is the Google Pixel 10a, and it’s a very good phone with a refined design, great color choices, a sharp screen, excellent cameras, and decent performance with long software support.
The problem with the Pixel 10a is that the Google Pixel 9a exists, costs less, and is virtually an identical device. Though the 9a is a little harder to find now as stock levels deplete, if you can find one, it’s a better buy than the 10a this Black Friday. I’ll explain why.
I’ve used both the Pixel 9a and Pixel 10a extensively, as I reviewed both devices at their respective launches in 2025 and 2026, and the honest truth is I cannot tell the difference between the two phones in everyday use.
That’s partly because their designs are almost identical. The 10a manages to have absolutely no camera bump at all, with the camera glass sitting flush with the back of the phone. The 9a is also all but bump-less, apart from a very small lip. Otherwise, these are the plainest Pixels going — they both lack the distinctive ‘camera bar’ design of pricier Pixels like the Pixel 10 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro.
The camera on the 10a is not better than that of the 9a. That’s because the hardware specs are 100% the same, with 48MP main, 13MP ultra-wide, and 13MP selfie lenses offered on both phones. Google uses the same photo processing too, so results are indistinguishable and, thankfully, excellent. The Pixel 11 Pro XL I’ve also tested doesn’t take significantly better photos to justify the enormous extra expense.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The 6.3-inch OLED screen on the 9a and 10a is also identical, as is the not-loads-but-enough 8GB RAM under the hood. Both phones are IP68 water- and dust-resistant too, and both have the same 5,100mAh battery.
There are vanishingly few reasons to spend more on the Pixel 10a — but the real crux here is that both phones have the Google Tensor G4 chipset.
For the Pixel 6a, 7a, 8a, and 9a, Google opted to use the same Tensor chipset as the more expensive Pixel 6, 7, 8, and 9, respectively. This alone made the A series great value, as you were getting the same processor as much more expensive, current-generation Pixel phones.
Indeed, the Pixel 9a has the same Tensor G4 chipset as the Pixel 9 and Pixel 9 Pro, but for some reason, Google decided not to give the Pixel 10a the Tensor G5 from the rest of the Pixel 10 lineup. This doesn’t make the Pixel 10a a bad phone; it just amplifies how good a deal the Pixel 9a is when it's available at a discount.
The Pixel 9a cost $499 / £499 / AU$849 at launch in April 2025, but is often heavily discounted. The Pixel 10a cost the same as the 9a at launch, but Google recently raised its MSRP to $599 / £599 / AU$949.
At full price, it’s worth saving $100 / £100 / AU$100 and getting the 9a. Although the 10a has slightly faster 30W wired charging compared to the 9a’s 23W, this is not, in my opinion, enough to warrant the extra spend.
Then again, as I write this, the Pixel 10a is on sale in the UK at Argos, Currys, John Lewis and Amazon for £349, and on sale at Amazon in the US for $549. These are very good prices, and if they're the same as the 9a's current price in your region, it’s better to opt for the newer phone. But only if the price is right.
The Pixel 10a also has Gorilla Glass 7i on its display, which is supposedly more durable than the Glass 3 on the 9a, and the newer phone also benefits from receiving seven years of software updates from launch in 2026. That'll mean it remains supported until 2033, while the 9a's seven-year update commitment will take it to 2032.
Still, bought in 2026 or 2027, the Pixel 9a will continue to receive updates for five or six years, which is better than many Android phones costing the same price (or more).
The Pixel 10a is a great phone in a vacuum, but the phone market in 2026 is anything but a vacuum. Prices are on the rise, and the newest A-series Pixel is one of the smallest ever year-on-year upgrades over its predecessor.
This makes the Pixel 9a on sale a stellar and genuine bargain — if you buy one, rest easy in the knowledge that you’re not missing out by going for the previous generation. It’s one of the smartest Android moves right now, if I do say so myself.

And of course you can also follow TechRadar on TikTok for news, reviews, unboxings in video form, and get regular updates from us on WhatsApp too.
Henry is a freelance technology journalist with more than a decade of experience in the industry. Formerly Deputy Tech Editor at the Daily Express, he has also held senior positions at Tech Advisor, and has reviewed countless smartphones over the years, obsessing over screens, battery life, and camera smarts. He reviews phones, tablets, wearables and headphones, and has contributed to TechRadar, Trusted Reviews, Stuff, PC World and Macworld. articles.title: Black Friday : le TCL C89L met le Mini-LED haut de gamme à portée de salon, dès 799 €
articles.text:
Black Friday : le TCL C89L met le Mini-LED haut de gamme à portée de salon, dès 799 €
Des milliers de LED minuscules qui s'allument et s'éteignent zone par zone, pour des noirs d'encre et des couleurs qui claquent : la technologie des téléviseurs les plus ambitieux de TCL descend d'un cran dans la gamme. Pour le Black Friday, le C89L démarre à 799 €. Encore faut-il comprendre ce que le Mini-LED change devant le film du dimanche soir.
Changer de téléviseur ne suppose pas de viser le sommet d'une gamme. Avec le C89L, également référencé C8L selon les enseignes, TCL installe la huitième génération de sa technologie SQD-Mini LED sous son vaisseau amiral X11L et au-dessus du C7L. Jusqu'au 30 novembre, il s'affiche à partir de 799 € en 55 pouces, 1 199 € en 65 pouces et 1 399 € en 75 pouces chez Darty et Boulanger. La technologie du haut de gamme, donc, sans le ticket d'entrée qui va d'ordinaire avec.
Mini-LED : comment l'écran obtient des noirs vraiment noirs
Sur un téléviseur LCD classique, un même panneau lumineux éclaire tout l'écran par l'arrière. Une lune brillante dans un ciel nocturne ? Le rétroéclairage reste allumé partout, le ciel vire au gris foncé et les détails sombres se noient.
Le Mini-LED découpe cette source de lumière en milliers de diodes minuscules, regroupées en zones pilotées une à une. Chacune s'allume, faiblit ou s'éteint selon ce que montre l'image à cet endroit précis : la lune brille, le ciel autour reste noir. Plus les zones sont nombreuses, plus le contrôle gagne en finesse, avec moins de halos autour des objets lumineux sur fond sombre.
SQD-Mini LED : ce qu'apporte la huitième génération
TCL greffe à ce principe sa technologie Super Quantum Dot. Des LED bleues éclairent une couche dense de nanocristaux, qui convertissent cette lumière en un blanc très pur. Chaque zone émet ainsi la même lumière, sans déborder sur la couleur de sa voisine : un rouge vif reste net à côté d'un ciel bleu. Le constructeur annonce une couverture de 100 % de l'espace colorimétrique BT.2020, la référence des contenus HDR. TCL soigne aussi la dalle : un film à faible réflexion atténue les reflets, et un angle de vision très large préserve l'image pour toute la famille installée sur le canapé.
TCL C89L : 55, 65 ou 75 pouces
Le nombre de zones et la luminosité de pointe grimpent avec la diagonale, selon les données de TCL :
•	55 pouces : 1 008 zones, jusqu'à 3 000 nits en HDR
•	65 pouces : 2 040 zones, jusqu'à 5 000 nits
•	75 pouces : 2 584 zones, jusqu'à 5 500 nits
Cette réserve de lumière prend tout son sens dans un salon baigné de soleil, où un écran trop sage paraît vite terne en plein après-midi. Le reste de la fiche technique est commun aux trois tailles : processeur TSR AiPQ qui ajuste contraste, couleurs et netteté en temps réel, compatibilité Dolby Vision IQ et HDR10+, interface Google TV et son signé Bang & Olufsen, compatible Dolby Atmos. Côté jeu vidéo, la dalle 144 Hz grimpe jusqu'à 288 Hz avec les sources compatibles.
Quelle taille pour quel salon ?
En 4K, on conseille généralement de s'asseoir à une distance comprise entre 1,2 et 1,5 fois la diagonale. Le 55 pouces (139 cm) convient à un canapé placé entre 1,70 m et 2,10 m de l'écran, le 65 pouces (164 cm) entre 2 m et 2,50 m, le 75 pouces (189 cm) entre 2,30 m et 2,85 m. Pour une famille qui partage séries, matchs et films du week-end, le 65 pouces offre un compromis séduisant entre immersion et encombrement.
Les prix du TCL C89L pendant le Black Friday
Offres valables jusqu'au 30 novembre 2026.
*Le distributeur est seul maître de fixer ses prix de vente. Caractéristiques communiquées par TCL : le rendu perçu varie selon les contenus, les réglages et les conditions de visionnage.

articles.title: Fritzbox am Black Friday: 9 gute Fritz-Deals rund um Router und Repeater
articles.text:
Fritzbox am Black Friday: 9 gute Angebote rund um Router und Repeater
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
In vielen Bereichen sind Hardware-Produkte aktuell teuer wie selten. Der Zeitraum rund um den Black Friday ist dabei eine gute Gelegenheit, beim Einkauf ein wenig zu sparen. Neben Apple– und Samsung-Geräten sowie Homeoffice-Gadgets sind 2026 auch zahlreiche Produkte vom Router-Hersteller Fritz reduziert. Das Angebot umfasst nicht nur Fritzboxen, sondern auch entsprechende Repeater und Gadgets fürs Smarthome. Nicht immer sind die Preise aber auch gut. Wir zeigen euch Angebote, die sich wirklich lohnen.
Fritzboxen bei Amazon, Otto und Saturn
Ganz vorn stehen zwei Fritboxen, die unter anderem bei Amazon reduziert sind und auch anderswo aktuell kaum günstiger zu bekommen sind.
Fritzbox 7690 als Router und Smarthome-Zentrale
Ihr surft zu Hause via DSL, wollt aber demnächst wechseln? Bei der Fritbox 7690 spielt das keine Rolle. Sie eignet sich für den handelsüblichen DSL-Anschluss, lässt sich laut Hersteller aber auch am Kabel- oder Glasfasermodem betreiben. Der Router unterstützt den aktuellen Wi-Fi-7-Standard mit theoretisch möglichen Übertragungsgeschwindigkeiten von bis zu 7,1 Gigabit pro Sekunde. Dazu unterstützt sie die Mesh-Produkte des Herstellers und dient dank DECT und Zigbee auch als Smarthome-Zentrale. Normalerweise kostet die Box rund 280 Euro. Derzeit ist sie bei Amazon, Notebooksbilliger.de und Otto aber auf 250 Euro reduziert. Das liegt unter dem zuletzt gemessenen Durchschnittspreis von Idealo (93 Tage, 258 Euro).
Fritzbox 5690 für Glasfaser-Nutzer
Auch die Fritzbox 5690 bietet Wi-Fi 7 (bis zu 6,4 Gigabit pro Sekunde). Sie eignet sich jedoch nur für Glasfaser-Nutzer:innen. Dabei unterstützt die Box die Standards AON und GPON. Ein externes Modem ist für die Verbindung nicht notwendig. Gleichwohl könnt ihr sie aber daran anschließen, wenn ihr das bevorzugt. Wie die 7690 unterstützt die 5690 DECT und damit entsprechende Telefone, aber auch ausgewähltes Smarthome-Zubehör des Herstellers. Ein Zigbee-Hub fehlt allerdings. Die Fritzbox 5690 kostet normalerweise ebenfalls 280 Euro. Rund um den Black Friday bekommt ihr sie für rund 247 Euro bei Amazon und Otto, oder für 249 Euro bei Saturn.
Mesh-Sets und Repeater
Passend zu den Boxen sind zudem Reichweitenverstärker (Repeater) und entsprechende Mesh-Sets vergünstigt, mit denen ihr euer Netzwerk auch in entlegene Räume erweitert.
Fritz Repeater 2700 mit Wi-Fi 7
Dazu gehört der Fritz Repeater, der ebenso Wi‑Fi 7 unterstützt. Im Einsatz übernimmt er laut Hersteller direkt die Einstellungen des Routers. Zudem ist ein 2,5-Gigabit-LAN-Anschluss verbaut, falls ihr die kabelgebundene Vernetzung bevorzugt. Mit 150 Euro ist so ein Reichweitenverstärker eigentlich nicht erschwinglich. Zum Black Friday sinkt der Preis unter anderem bei Amazon und Otto aber auf rund 120 Euro.
Fritz Repeater 6000
Der Fritz Repeater 6000 unterstützt „nur“ Wi-Fi 6, unterstützt dafür aber drei statt der normalen zwei Bänder. So soll er dabei helfen, auch große Mengen schnell durchs WLAN zu befördern. Darüber hinaus bietet er dieselben Vorzüge wie der Repeater 2700. Für die Einrichtung soll ein Knopfdruck genügen. Ein LAN-Anschluss ist an Bord. Derzeit ist der Repeater bei Otto und Amazon auf rund 200 Euro reduziert und sonst nur beim Hersteller für diesen Preis zu bekommen.
Fritz Mesh Set 1600: Repeater im Doppelpack
Wer mehr als zwei Zimmer hat, profitiert von einem sogenannten Mesh-Set. Dabei handelt es sich im Prinzip um mehrere Repeater im Paket. Zum Black Friday gibt es bei Amazon ein solches Set mit zwei Repeatern für rund 153 statt 199 Euro zu kaufen. Das Fritz Mesh Set 1600 unterstützt Wi-Fi 6, die einzelnen Repeater haben allerdings keine LAN-Eingänge.
DECT-Telefon, Heizkörperthermostat und mehr Zubehör
Fritz Fon X6 als Steuerzentrale
Das Fritz Fon X6 sieht aus wie ein handelsübliches Festnetztelefon. Es bietet jedoch viele Funktionen, die man vom Smartphone kennt. So könnt ihr bei Bedarf Podcasts darüber hören oder eure Smarthome-Geräte von Fritz steuern. Grundsätzlich funktioniert das Fon X6 auch mit anderen DECT‑Basisstationen. Das volle Potenzial schöpft ihr aber in Verbindung mit kompatiblen Fritzboxen aus. Zuletzt kostete es rund 90 Euro. Bei Amazon könnt ihr derzeit zehn Euro sparen. Damit liegt es genau auf dem Schnitt der vergangenen 185 Tage.
Fritz Thermo 302: Smarte Heizungssteuerung
Gerade im Winter kann ein smartes Heizthermostat von Vorteil sein, wenn etwa das Arbeitszimmer schon vor Dienstantritt automatisch aufgeheizt wird, sich die Heizung über Nacht aber automatisch wieder abschaltet. Das Thermostat verbindet sich per DECT mit der Fritzbox, funktioniert also nicht in anderen Smarthome-Systemen. Über die Oberfläche des Routers könnt ihr unter anderem Heizpläne festlegen. Das E‑Ink-Display zeigt jeweils die aktuelle Temperatur an. Das Thermostat sollte auf gängige Heizkörper passen. Derzeit ist es bei Amazon, Saturn und Otto auf 45 Euro. Günstiger war es in den vergangenen Wochen nicht.
Fritz Smart Control 350 erkennt offene Fenster
Passend dazu ist der Tür-Fenster-Sensor Fritz Smart Control 350 bei Amazon auf rund 26 Euro reduziert. Über die richtigen Regeln lassen sich die Heizkörperthermostate dann so einstellen, dass sie sich automatisch abschalten, wenn ihr etwa das Fenster zum Lüften öffnet. Alternativ lässt es sich auch an Türen oder am Briefkasten anbringen. Wie das Thermostat ist der Sensor nur mit DECT kompatibel.
Fritz Smart Control 440: Die Universalfernbedienung
Bis zu zwölf Geräte könnt ihr über die vier Tasten am Fritz Smart Control 440 steuern. Dazu gehören smarte Thermostaten, Steckdosen oder Glühlampen. Auch hier liegt der Fokus auf der DECT‑Verbindung zur Fritzbox. Es ist laut Hersteller aber möglich, trotzdem Zigbee-Geräte über das Smart Control 440 zu steuern. Preislich liegt das Gadget normalerweise bei 69 Euro. Bei Amazon ist es derzeit für rund 46 Euro zu haben – aktuell der beste Online-Preis.

articles.title: Une chaîne russe fait parler Dostoïevski à l’écran grâce à l’IA
articles.text:
Fiodor Dostoïevski, mort en 1881, commente l'actualité sur Russia Today. Depuis un mois, la chaîne financée par l'État russe fait intervenir un double du romancier généré par intelligence artificielle, d'abord pour lire ses textes, puis pour attaquer les Russes partis à l'étranger avec des phrases écrites à sa place.
L'idée vient d'un éditorialiste britannique. Dans une chronique publiée par Bloomberg Opinion le 17 octobre, Martin Ivens, rédacteur du Times Literary Supplement, estimait que Dostoïevski, s'il vivait aujourd'hui, soutiendrait sans doute l'invasion de l'Ukraine et passerait sur Russia Today. Margarita Simonyan, la rédactrice en chef de RT, a pris la provocation au mot. Quatre jours plus tard, elle a publié sur sa chaîne Telegram une vidéo de l'écrivain et promis d'en faire un « expert politique permanent » de RT. Dans ce premier extrait, l'avatar lisait un passage authentique du Journal d'un écrivain sur les relations entre la Russie et l'Europe. Le 4 novembre, il a pris la parole depuis un studio de la chaîne avec un texte inédit.
Un Dostoïevski entièrement fabriqué par intelligence artificielle
Le visage du romancier, le décor et les objets autour de lui sont tous générés par IA, selon l'édition russe du Moscow Times. Le rendu est loin d'être parfait. De nombreux internautes russes ont relevé une mimique peu naturelle, avec le haut du visage presque immobile.
Pour le texte, RT a changé de méthode entre les deux vidéos. Après des phrases tirées de l'œuvre de Dostoïevski, la chaîne lui a fait réciter un monologue écrit à sa manière, et personne ne sait encore si ce discours sort de la plume d'un journaliste ou d'un modèle de langage.
La chaîne a de l'expérience dans ce domaine. Dès 2024, Margarita Simonyan affirmait sur la chaîne moscovite TVC qu'une « part importante » des présentateurs de RT étaient des créations de l'IA, visage et voix compris. « Au départ, nous utilisions des modèles occidentaux, mais nous développons activement les nôtres », a-t-elle expliqué cette année au Jakarta Globe. Le nom du modèle qui anime Dostoïevski est inconnu.
En France, Thierry Ardisson avait fait revivre Dalida en 2022 dans Hôtel du temps, sur France 3, avec une tout autre recette. Une comédienne jouait la chanteuse devant la caméra, puis le studio Mac Guff remplaçait son visage par celui de Dalida grâce à l'IA. Chez RT, l'image entière est synthétique, du costume au décor.
Russia Today fait attaquer les exilés russes par son Dostoïevski
Le 4 novembre, jour de la fête de l'Unité nationale en Russie, le double numérique s'en est pris aux Russes qui ont quitté le pays depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine. « Nous voyons des milliers de Russes fuir leur foyer, abandonnant leurs enfants, leurs anciens », lance l'avatar dans l'extrait diffusé par franceinfo. Plus loin, il accuse les exilés d'avoir le cœur endurci sous l'influence de doctrines étrangères et les traite de traîtres.
Dans ses autres chroniques, d'après franceinfo, le faux Dostoïevski tient des propos conservateurs, souvent hostiles à l'Europe, et soutient la guerre menée par Vladimir Poutine.
Dans l'Union européenne, la diffusion de RT est suspendue depuis le 2 mars 2022, date à laquelle le Conseil de l'UE a coupé en urgence RT France et quatre autres éditions de la chaîne, rappelle un rapport du Sénat. Les autorités françaises ont constaté dès 2022 que RT France contournait l'interdiction en passant par des plateformes installées en dehors de l'Union, telles qu'Odysee et Rumble.
Faire commenter l'actualité à un mort grâce à l'IA est une pratique connue en Russie. En juin 2023, le parti LDPR avait présenté au Forum économique de Saint-Pétersbourg un avatar en 3D de son fondateur Vladimir Jirinovski, mort l'année précédente. Le personnage commentait l'actualité avec sa voix et ses mimiques. Pour l'historienne de la littérature Maria Maïofis, auteure d'une tribune dans l'édition russe du Moscow Times, le Dostoïevski de RT sert surtout aux vivants à faire porter leurs idées par un mort.

articles.title: Hala Mobility combines EV rentals, delivery jobs, and financial services for gig workers
articles.text:
Hala Mobility combines EV rentals, delivery jobs, and financial services for gig workers
Hyderabad-based startup Hala Mobility provides electric vehicles to delivery riders, connects them with delivery companies, and offers early-salary financing and accident insurance.
Delivery riders can cover 100 to 120 km a day, often on petrol vehicles that aren’t designed for such intensive use. Rising fuel prices add to their operating costs.
Electric vehicles (EVs) can reduce these expenses, and delivery companies are encouraging riders to make the switch. However, riders who cannot afford or access an EV have little choice but to continue using petrol vehicles.
Access to a vehicle is only part of the problem. Riders also need to know how far it can travel on a charge, where to charge it, and where to get it serviced. For companies managing large EV fleets, the challenges extend to monitoring battery health, battery swaps, energy consumption, and maintenance schedules.
Hyderabad-based Hala Mobility aims to address these gaps through an EV fleet-as-a-service and multi-modal shared mobility platform that allows riders and delivery companies to use EVs without purchasing them.
Through the Hala app, riders can rent, lease or finance vehicles. Hala was founded in 2019 by Srikanth Reddy Kalakonda, Founder and CEO, and Co-founder Snehith Reddy Meda.
Kalakonda studied computer science at Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University and completed master's degrees at the University of Padua and the Polytechnic University of Madrid. He later pursued a PhD, during which he developed Chippy, a mobility aggregator app.
Meda studied electronics and communication engineering at Manipal Institute of Technology and founded the agritech company OneBasket.
Vehicles, jobs, and financial support
Hala works with riders through two models.
For delivery companies such as Zomato, Swiggy and Zepto, it provides both riders and electric vehicles and manages operations. Delivery companies pay Hala for each order completed. Hala deducts vehicle rental and related costs and passes the remaining amount, including incentives, to the rider.
“Everything is passed on. There is no commission,” Kalakonda says.
Riders who already have delivery jobs can subscribe to a vehicle for a week, 15 days or a month. Hala’s website lists rentals starting at Rs 189 a day and three-month leases from Rs 13,999.
Kalakonda describes the business as a combination of vehicle rentals, logistics, and platform services, designed to keep vehicles in use.
Hala also allows riders to work with at least three delivery companies, enabling them to switch between platforms depending on order availability. According to Kalakonda, the average rider on its platform earns close to Rs 32,000 a month.
The startup uses data such as timely rental payments, order volumes, and customer ratings to score riders. These scores help connect them with financiers offering early-salary advances.
Kalakonda says every rider also receives accident insurance, underwritten using the same data, with Rs 5 lakh in coverage in the event of death.
About 90% of Hala's customers are gig workers who have migrated from other parts of the country and lack stable housing, which Kalakonda says affects their health.
To address this, Hala is developing Blue Base, a community hub offering charging, parking, vehicle servicing, and housing for riders.
Blue Base also plans to operate vehicles in shifts of eight to nine hours, allowing another rider to use a vehicle while the first rider rests.
Managing the fleet with data
Hala uses an internal software platform called Circle OS to track vehicles throughout their lifecycle, from deployment and servicing to refurbishment or scrapping.
Kalakonda says the system uses AI to analyse nine to 10 inputs, including data related to drivers, vehicles, charging stations, service centres, inventory, and order patterns.
The software helps Hala predict and extend vehicle life, determine when a vehicle can be refurbished instead of scrapped, and compare operating costs with rental income.
Each vehicle is fitted with an Internet of Things (IoT) telematics device that transmits data every five seconds.
Riders use this information to check a vehicle’s remaining range, identify faults, and locate the nearest service station. When a battery runs low, the app directs them to a nearby charging station and shows how many drivers are waiting.
“Every data point has to be tracked, traced, monitored, and controlled,” Kalakonda says.
He puts fleet utilisation at nearly 88% and uptime at 94%.
What growth looks like
Hala's business clients include Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto, Blinkit, BigBasket, Amazon, Flipkart, and Porter. Individual riders account for the rest of its customers.
Its fleet grew from 2,484 vehicles in March 2025 to more than 8,100 in March 2026. The company now operates nearly 18,000 vehicles across nine cities.
Kalakonda says Hala has been EBITDA-positive since its inception and profit-after-tax positive for the past two financial years. The startup reported revenue of Rs 96 crore in the last financial year and is targeting Rs 262 crore to Rs 270 crore this year.
It has raised approximately Rs 21 crore in equity and Rs 70 crore in debt. Hala is also part of the 2025 cohort of the ClimaFii Alliance, a programme run in India by Upaya Social Ventures. The startup is currently raising a Rs 135-crore Series A round to fund its financing, insurance and housing initiatives.
Kalakonda expects Hala to have around 50,000 vehicles on the road within a year and aims to build a profitable listed company by 2030 or 2031.
Beyond rentals, leasing, and delivery services, he wants Hala to become a broader support system for gig workers. “This is my safety net, and this is where I belong,” Kalakonda says, describing how he wants riders to feel about the platform.

articles.title: Le Porsche 718 Boxster passe à l'électrique, mais refuse de renoncer à son flat 6
articles.text:
Porsche vient de divulguer des informations particulièrement intéressantes concernant son prochain 718 Boxster. Ce dernier se prépare à un grand changement puisqu’il passe à l’électrique. Il s’agit de la première sportive Porsche à être électrique. Pour l’instant, seulement une berline et des SUV Porsche ont été déclinés en électrique. C’est donc un modèle d’une importance capitale pour Porsche : faire passer son roadster vers l’électricité sans perdre l’intérêt du client pour le modèle. Et les premières informations sur le modèle de série sont assez réjouissantes.
Une architecture unique
Pour contextualiser un peu avant d’introduire le 718 Boxster électrique, le Boxster est depuis la fin des années 90 le modèle d’accès à la gamme Porsche. Il s’agit d’un roadster 2 places avec un moteur central arrière, un flat 6 généralement (6 cylindres à plat) et dans quelques cas un flat 4. Une voiture appréciée pour son équilibre naturel et son gabarit compact.
Porsche ne peut pas perdre ces qualités pour le Boxster électrique. Les ingénieurs ont donc travaillé sur plusieurs solutions pour garder l’esprit du Boxster. Ainsi, la batterie est positionnée en central arrière, derrière les occupants de l’habitacle. Ce qui permet de conserver un équilibre des masses 40/60 comme les autres Boxster, mais aussi de proposer une position de conduite toujours aussi basse, ce que l’on recherche dans une sportive.
Malgré le passage à l’électrique, Porsche ne multiplie pas les moteurs électriques comme ce que peuvent proposer Alpine ou encore BMW avec la M3 électrique. Le choix a été fait d’un unique moteur arrière travaillant avec le blocage de différentiel électronique PTV+ que l’on retrouve notamment sur la 911. On ne connaît pas encore sa puissance, mais Porsche annonce un 0 à 100 km/h en moins de 3 secondes et une vitesse de pointe de 250 km/h, de quoi être décoiffé.
D’autres organes de la Porsche 911 sont utilisés, comme la direction qui provient de la Carrera GTS. Le freinage et la monte de pneumatiques s’inspirent également de la Porsche 911. Enfin, Porsche annonce un poids comparable à une 911 Cabriolet équipée de la motorisation T-Hybrid, ce qui tend à rassurer sur le poids du 718 Boxster électrique, sans toutefois donner de valeur exacte. Enfin, pour la première fois, des roues arrière directrices pourront être installées.
Une simulation de boîte de vitesses et du flat 6
Le Boxster et le Cayman ont eu du succès aussi en raison de leur motorisation. Le flat 6 est une mécanique considérée comme noble avec un son enivrant. Porsche semble vouloir le faire vivre dans le 718 Boxster électrique.
En effet, la marque allemande annonce l’intégration de sa nouvelle technologie de simulation de boîte de vitesses e-shift à 7 rapports, introduite avec la Taycan millésime 2026. Cette simulation de boîte de vitesses, activable ou non, est accompagnée d’un son généré reproduisant le flat 6 du Boxster GTS type 981, une voiture moderne, mais assez prisée des collectionneurs dès à présent.
Porsche nous donne rendez-vous au premier trimestre 2027 pour tout découvrir de son 718 Boxster. On sait déjà que la voiture sera produite dans l’usine principale de Porsche à Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen.

Source : Communiqué de presse Porsche

articles.title: Intel Nova Lake-S leak reveals 28-core Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC with 144MB cache, 5.5 GHz boost clock
articles.text:
Rumor mill: A massive leak appears to have revealed the specifications of at least seven processors from Intel's upcoming Core Ultra 4000 "Nova Lake-S" desktop lineup. The leaked SKUs are based on C1 and A0 stepping qualification samples (QS), with Intel noting that their clock speeds and other specs could change by the time they reach the market.
The most powerful chip in the lineup is the Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC, which features 28 cores, including 8 P-cores, 16 E-cores, and 4 LPE-cores. Other notable specs include 144 MB of L3 cache, a 5.5 GHz boost clock, 2.7 GHz base clock, 3.1 GHz maximum GPU frequency, and a 125W base power rating. It also features an unlocked multiplier, as denoted by the "K" suffix in its name.
The other leaked CPUs include the Core Ultra 9 4950K, Core Ultra 9 4900 BFC (locked), Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC, Core Ultra 7 4850K, Core Ultra 5 4650K, and Core Ultra 5 4650KF. While the 4950K is also a 28-core product, the rest feature between 22 and 24 cores, as well as lower clock speeds and smaller L3 caches. However, all except the 4900 BFC still have a 125W base power rating
The 22-core 4650KF is the base model on the list, featuring 6 P-cores, 12 E-cores, and 4 LPE-cores. It also has 30 MB of L3 cache, a 5.1 GHz boost clock and a 2.9 GHz base clock. It's the only SKU not to have an integrated graphics chip, as denoted by the "F" suffix.
All seven processors support up to 256GB of DDR5-8000 memory, an upgrade over the current-generation Arrow Lake-S chips that only support up to DDR5-6400. The leak also reveals up to 24 CPU PCIe lanes and a 77 PTOPS integrated NPU, as well as support for DNx, XAVC, JPEG-XS, and VVC decoding, in addition to AV1 High and Professional profiles.
It's unclear when Intel will launch these processors, but another recent leak revealed that the company is planning a next-generation desktop event in Berlin between February 22 and 25, so they'll likely be officially showcased in Germany. The report adds that motherboard manufacturers will probably tease their Nova Lake-S products about six weeks earlier, at CES 2027 in January

articles.title: Kioxia Announces GP2 Super High IOPS SSD Series
articles.text:
Thursday, November 26th 2026
Kioxia Announces GP2 Super High IOPS SSD Series
Kioxia Corporation, a world leader in memory solutions, today announced the KIOXIA GP2 Series Super High IOPS SSD, the second product in its KIOXIA GP Series of SSDs optimized for direct GPU access. Building on the technology and architecture of the KIOXIA GP1 Series SSD announced in August 2026, the KIOXIA GP2 Series delivers over 18 million random read IOPS at a 512-byte block size, nearly double the performance of its predecessor. It is also expected to deliver sequential read throughput of up to 28 GB/s, enough to saturate a PCIe 6.0 x4 link.
Super High IOPS SSDs can expand the effective capacity of a GPU system's High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) by providing an additional flash-based memory tier directly accessible by the GPU, supporting industry efforts to improve AI system capability and efficiency. This approach enables AI systems to access larger datasets, including those used in large graph neural networks, at a significantly lower cost than adding more HBM or DRAM at the same capacity, while improving GPU utilization.KIOXIA GP2 Series SSDs leverage the company's XL-FLASH generation 3 low-latency, high-performance flash memory, which is uniquely positioned to deliver higher endurance and approximately 2.5 times the IOPS of typical TLC-based SSDs, to support fine-grained data access needed for memory extension usage, and consume significantly less power per I/O. Next generations of the KIOXIA GP Series will target up to 100 million random read IOPS.
KIOXIA GP2 Series Super High IOPS SSD
Key features of the KIOXIA GP2 Series include:
- Designed to PCIe 6.0 and NVMe 2.3 specifications
- Features KIOXIA XL-FLASH generation 3 low-latency flash memory
- Random read performance of more than 18 million IOPS at 512-byte block size
- Form factors under consideration include E1.S 9.5 mm and E3.S
- Direct Liquid cooling support
- Sequential read throughput performance of up to 28 GB/s
- Up to 50 DWPD endurance
As AI workloads continue to grow in scale and complexity, Kioxia remains committed to advancing flash memory technology to help address the evolving performance and capacity demands of AI and high-performance computing architectures.
Evaluation samples of the KIOXIA GP2 Series SSDs will be available to select customers by the end of 2027.

articles.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
articles.text:
Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.
A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.
Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don’t digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO2. That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane.
Many peatlands have been drained by digging ditches that let water flow out to repurpose the land for agriculture or other uses. That lowers the water level, supplying oxygen to the exposed peat and ringing the aerobic bacteria dinner bell. Methane emissions get turned down, and CO2 emissions get turned way up.
History re: peats
The researchers used recent studies that measure gas emissions from peatlands to build a global model that estimated CO2 and methane release as the water level drops. The two gases respond differently to a given drop in water level, and CO2 in particular responds differently depending on where in the world the bog is located. Using reconstructions of water-level changes due to historical peatland drainage, the team ran their model starting in 1800.

articles.title: Estados Unidos alertó por 10 fallas que hackers ya explotan en comunicaciones, redes y sistemas de refrigeración
articles.text:
La Agencia de Ciberseguridad y Seguridad de las Infraestructuras de Estados Unidos (CISA) incorporó el 25 de noviembre diez vulnerabilidades a su catálogo de fallas explotadas activamente, es decir, errores de programación que los hackers ya están utilizando para llevar a cabo ataques. Las vulnerabilidades afectan a productos de Mitel, Juniper, Vates y Danfoss.
El catálogo, conocido como KEV, es una lista pública con evidencia sobre una falla que está siendo utilizada en ataques reales. Según el aviso oficial, las diez nuevas entradas constituyen vectores de ataque frecuentes y representan riesgos significativos para las agencias federales.
De acuerdo con el catálogo KEV de CISA, ocho de las diez vulnerabilidades deberán corregirse antes del 28 de noviembre. Para las otras dos, las agencias civiles federales del Poder Ejecutivo de Estados Unidos tienen como fecha límite el 9 de diciembre.
Cinco fallas de Mitel MiCollab afectan la versión 10.3 y anteriores
Las vulnerabilidades que afectan a MiCollab, la plataforma de comunicaciones y videoconferencias de Mitel, están presentes en la versión 10.3 y anteriores.
Dos de ellas son las más graves: una recibió una puntuación de 10 sobre 10 en la escala de gravedad y otra, de 9. La primera permite ejecutar comandos en el sistema, mientras que la segunda posibilita la inyección de código mediante un archivo XML.
Las otras tres, con puntuaciones de entre 5,3 y 5,9, permiten cargar archivos, eludir controles de acceso y obtener información sensible.
Sobre estas fallas, Mitel informó en un aviso que la versión 10.3.0.18 incluye un parche que corrige las vulnerabilidades. Para quienes no puedan actualizar, la empresa recomienda restringir el acceso externo al componente de conferencias.
Cinco fallas afectan servidores virtuales, redes y sistemas de refrigeración
Otras dos vulnerabilidades obtuvieron una puntuación de 9,8 sobre 10. Una afecta a Xen Orchestra, el software de Vates para administrar servidores virtuales, y permite que un atacante sin credenciales obtenga privilegios de administrador mediante una credencial manipulada.
Vates informó que atacantes ya explotaron la falla para obtener acceso administrativo sin credenciales y ejecutar código en infraestructuras gestionadas con Xen Orchestra.
La segunda afecta a los dispositivos Session Smart Conductor y Session Smart Router de Juniper, empresa perteneciente a Hewlett Packard Enterprise. La vulnerabilidad permite que un atacante remoto ejecute comandos con el máximo nivel de privilegios.
En su portal de soporte, Juniper indicó que recibió al menos un reporte de explotación maliciosa y recomendó actualizar a una versión corregida lo antes posible.
Las tres restantes afectan a los controladores de refrigeración AK-SM 800A de Danfoss, utilizados para supervisar sistemas de frío. Una permite leer archivos internos; otra, con una puntuación de 9,9, ejecutar comandos de forma remota; y la tercera, generar un informe que expone direcciones internas, nombres de usuario y nombres de tiendas.
CISA había incorporado otras cinco vulnerabilidades esta semana
Antes de sumar las diez fallas del 25 de noviembre, CISA ya había agregado otras cinco vulnerabilidades explotadas activamente al catálogo KEV durante esa semana.
El 23 de noviembre incluyó una vulnerabilidad de recorrido de rutas en Project MONAI MONAI Label, con una puntuación de 9,8. La falla afecta a versiones anteriores a la 0.8.6 y permite que un atacante ejecute código de forma remota mediante el parámetro de imagen del punto de acceso de almacenamiento.
A su vez, añadió una vulnerabilidad de falsificación de solicitudes del lado del servidor en N-able Mail Assure, también conocido como SpamExperts, puntuada con 9,3. Un usuario autenticado de la interfaz de programación puede inducir al servidor a conectarse a sistemas internos, comprobar qué servicios están disponibles y enviarles datos manipulados.
Al día siguiente, el organismo sumó una falla de deserialización de datos no confiables en Idunno AntiCsrf, con una puntuación de 9,3, que puede permitir la ejecución de código sin autenticación.
Además, incluyó una vulnerabilidad de ejecución remota de código en Drupal Core que afecta a las versiones 10.6.22 y anteriores, 11.3.22 y anteriores, y 11.4.13 y anteriores.
La quinta entrada corresponde a Optimizely Web Experimentation. La vulnerabilidad, con una puntuación de 7,1, afecta el registro de cuentas y podría permitir que un atacante introduzca código malicioso.

articles.title: 1Password sofre invasão e alerta clientes sobre vazamento de dados
articles.text:
1Password sofre invasão e alerta clientes sobre vazamento de dados
A 1Password sofreu uma invasão após hackers comprometerem a conta corporativa de um funcionário no GitHub.
Se você tem conta na 1Password, atenção: o serviço de gerenciamento de senhas emitiu um comunicado para alertar clientes sobre uma invasão aos seus sistemas. Os hackers não tiveram acesso a cofres de senhas e chaves de recuperação de acesso, mas dados como nome e endereço de e-mail foram expostos.
De acordo com uma investigação iniciada pela própria 1Password em 19 de novembro de 2026, o problema teve origem no comprometimento da conta corporativa de um de seus funcionários no GitHub.
Ao acessar essa conta, os invasores puderam entrar nos repositórios privados da empresa e inserir um código malicioso em serviços internos que, por sua vez, foi capaz de captura dados relacionados a clientes.
Para completar, os hackers conseguiram copiar um código-fonte interno da empresa, bem como acessar o ambiente de CI/CD (Continuous Integration e Continuous Delivery/Deployment), um conjunto de ferramentas e processos que automatiza testes, compilação e distribuição de software.
Ambientes de CI/CD podem conter credenciais de acesso e dados críticos de infraestrutura, por isso, o acesso indevido a ele configura um importante problema de segurança.
Segundo a 1Password, o vazamento expôs os seguintes dados de clientes:
- nome
- endereço de e-mail
- chaves públicas
- datas e horários de criação de conta ou último login
- tokens de links enviados por e-mail relacionados a convites, provisionamento de contas e recuperação de acesso
- parâmetros do protocolo SRP (Secure Remote Password), usado para autenticação
- metadados internos
A 1Password ressaltou que os cofres que armazenam senhas e dados relacionados não foram comprometidos, o mesmo valendo para as chaves que protegem esses cofres e para os aplicativos ou extensões do serviço.
Quanto aos tokens expostos, a companhia explica que eles não são suficientes para as contas dos clientes serem acessadas, pois esse procedimento também exige um código de verificação de seis dígitos enviado por e-mail ou autenticação de login único (SSO, na sigla em inglês).
Já a exposição de chaves públicas não chega a ser um problema grave, pois esse tipo de informação foi projetada para ser compartilhada sem que isso permita decifrar informações protegidas. A exposição de chaves privadas é que seria um problema, mas isso não aconteceu.
A 1Password afirma que apenas um pequeno número de usuários foi afetado pela invasão e que eles foram notificados individualmente sobre o problema. Em todos os casos, não é preciso que os clientes alterem senhas ou chaves de acesso.
Por outro lado, os usuários devem ficar atentos para possíveis ações de phishing que usam os dados expostos para aplicar golpes em nome da 1Password.
Do seu lado, a companhia informou já ter adotado medidas para deter a invasão e evitar outros incidentes do tipo. Entre elas está a desativação da conta no GitHub comprometida, o reforço da segurança do ambiente de CI/CD e a contratação de especialistas em segurança para validação e aplicação de ajustes nos procedimentos adotados.

articles.title: TSMC’s $22.6 billion Texas plan wouldn’t make 2nm-or-better chips until 2031
articles.text:
TSMC files for $22.6 billion Texas fab campus with local tax breaks just one county over from Musk’s Terafab — proposed Brazos County plant won’t make 2nm-class chips until 2031
The filing lists an in-fab mask shop and $14 billion of tools and equipment, most budgeted for 2030.
TSMC has made an application for a new fab and campus near College Station, Brazos County, Texas. The proposed fab would be just one county over from Terafab, would likely share supply chains, and would be positioned to make 2nm-class chips by 2031, with the $22.6 billion plan detailing how the Taiwanese chipmaker is planning to expand its U.S. operations. An application under Texas’s Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation (JETI) program for a school property-tax limit shows TSMC is weighing a new fab site. The fab wouldn’t make 2nm or more advanced chips until 2031, six years after 2nm volume production began in Taiwan. It would come with a school-tax break valued at around $354 million.
This would be the company’s “second campus” for advanced chipmaking in the U.S. and the first outside Arizona. The Comptroller has recommended the tax application for approval, which the school district and the governor still have to grant. The application comes from TSMC Arizona Corporation, which is TSMC’s subsidiary located in Phoenix. Construction is projected to start in 2027, but the plan remains under evaluation, and nothing in the filing commits TSMC to buy the land or to build on it.
TSMC is looking to build out more in the U.S. because most of its large customers are based there and the government has been “very helpful” in pursuing additional fab capacity, Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei said in October. Texas is one option for expanding beyond Arizona, though the filing doesn’t say what drew TSMC there. TSMC judges each site on its tax environment, workforce availability, utility capacity and cost, and site and infrastructure readiness, as well as its “long-term scalability and expansion potential.” TSMC says Arizona offers “established operational efficiencies and lower capital risk,” and that the tax incentive would aid this further.
TSMC has “nearly 20 fabs worldwide in progress,” Wei said on the October earnings call, including 13 leading-edge and advanced packaging fabs in Taiwan and “another five to six fabs overseas.” Annual capacity for its 2nm (N2) family is expected to more than double in 2027. TSMC also expects more of its fabs to be ramping up in the U.S.
Texas wouldn’t begin commercial operations until 2031, and the economic model filed with the plan doesn’t have it at full operations until 2032. By contrast, the second fab in Arizona is expected to begin volume production in Q3 2027, but at 3nm. In Taiwan, N2 has been in high-volume production since Q4 2025. TSMC expects A14, its next full node after N2, to enter risk production in 2027 and volume in 2028. By 2031, A14 is set to have been in volume production for about three years, so a Texas fab that starts on 2nm would be at least a generation behind TSMC’s leading edge. Taiwan has also debated limits on how advanced TSMC’s overseas fabs can be.
| TSMC’s roadmap and the Texas timeline |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Milestone | Where | When | 
|---|---|---|
| 2nm (N2) volume production | Taiwan | Q4 2025 | 
| A16 (a 2nm-family node) volume production | TSMC, site not stated | 2027 (expected) | 
| 3nm volume production, second fab | Arizona | Q3 2027 | 
| A14 volume production | TSMC, site not stated | 2028 | 
| High-NA EUV adoption | TSMC, site not stated | 2030 (planned) | 
| 2nm “and/or more advanced,” commercial operations | Texas (proposed) | 2031 | 
The new site would have one or more fabs but, as it stands, Brazos County’s announcement describes one. For scale, we’ve estimated that a single 2nm-class module with about 20,000 wafer starts a month costs $25 billion to $35 billion, so this plan’s $22.6 billion budget falls below the low end of that range.
The price tag is split in multiple ways, with $8.60 billion for buildings and other real property, while 62% of the total, or $14.02 billion, is for tooling, machinery and equipment, a category that on the filing’s list also covers power, HVAC, cleanroom, water and gas systems. The building's spending would come first, in 2027, 2028, and 2029 alone. Tool spending would begin in that last year and peak at $9.05 billion in 2030, with about 65% of the tool budget landing in that year, before ending at $963.9 million in 2032 — the form’s Schedule A stops at 2031 and $21.66 billion total.
| TSMC’s proposed Texas project: spending and hiring by year |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Year | Buildings | Machinery and equipment | New hires | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 2027 | $729.0 million | — | 0 | 
| 2028 | $2.59 billion | — | 757 | 
| 2029 | $5.28 billion | $649.2 million | 1,110 | 
| 2030 | — | $9.05 billion | 232 | 
| 2031 | — | $3.36 billion | 0 | 
| 2032 | — | $963.9 million | 0 | 
| Total | $8.60 billion | $14.02 billion | 2,099 | 
The tool spending schedule lines up with a change in how TSMC prints its chips. Lithography, the step in the chipmaking process that uses light to project circuit patterns onto the wafer, requires advanced machines. The most advanced do it with extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light. High-NA EUV tools have a higher numerical aperture, gathering more light to print finer features in one pass. Wei said TSMC intends to use High-NA in 2030, which matches the 2030 peak in Texas tool spending, but that is a company-wide plan, and nothing in the Texas plan gives a delivery schedule or names High-NA tools specifically.
What the plan does spell out is its list of eligible property: fab and central utility plant buildings, cleanroom systems, ultra-pure water and wastewater treatment with water-reclaim systems, bulk and specialty gas as well as automated material handling, and gas-insulated switchgear.
Also named is mask or reticle shop equipment as well as lithography, etch, deposition, implant, chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), diffusion, and clean/wet tools, by type, although the list names no tool vendors, EUV counts, or wafer capacity. The mask shop is highlighted as “co-located within the fab and integral to the manufacturing process.” Masks are patterned plates used by a lithography tool to project their patterns onto each wafer, one per chip layer, and every new design needs its own set. Making them on site suggests the fab is meant to stand on its own. Wei also said TSMC is working with ASML on a 12-inch photomask by 2031, which is the year the Texas site would open.
The plan’s location is in Brazos County, Texas, sited across 86 parcels and almost 3,232 acres of land, which is about five square miles. This compares to TSMC’s Phoenix campus at about 1,078 acres on the county tax roll, with about 902 more purchased in January; this leaves the Texas site at about 1.6 times that total. TSMC would build and manage the site, which sets it apart from Terafab, a fab a TSMC customer is planning one county over: Wei has confirmed talks about using its capacity but said any such fab would have to be run by TSMC.
Residents in development areas for fabs and data centers tend to raise two concerns, and both are related to utility usage. The first is power: a local report says Bryan Texas Utilities provides that for the proposed area, but it’s unclear who would serve the fab. For scale, a utility filing in Arizona reportedly puts TSMC’s built-out Phoenix campus at about 1.9 gigawatts, a figure for the whole campus, not a single fab.
The second is water: Wellborn Special Utility District reportedly provides service, while the developer is said to intend to buy its water from a third party instead. As a comparison, a state document on an unnamed company’s $45 billion, two-fab project in Sherman, as reported by the Dallas Business Journal, lists 8 to 10 million gallons a day to start with a peak at 20 to 25 million after buildout, but this isn’t a 1:1. That project is targeting production in Q4 2029.
Economic impacts are a significant part of the deal: the plan projects 2,099 direct jobs by 2030, while the agreement would require only 35, the legal minimum. Pay, on the other hand, comes with a projected average salary nearly double the wage level that would need clearing.
Texas appears willing to work with TSMC on this, with a recommendation for approval signed by Deputy Comptroller Noah Betz this week. The gross tax benefit would build over 14 years, starting four years before the formal incentive period, and would cut the district’s maintenance and operations (M&O) levy on the project nearly in half. Even so, the full $354.1 million is only 1.6% of the $22.6 billion investment. In return, TSMC would have to post a performance bond equal to 10% of the benefit.
The Comptroller believes the incentive is a compelling factor — TSMC would not invest in Texas without it — but the office says it has not audited or verified the company’s projections. TSMC, for its part, calls the limit “determinative.”
| The Texas tax deal in numbers |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Measure | Figure | Source | 
|---|---|---|
| Direct jobs TSMC projects | 2,099 by 2030 | Application | 
| Jobs the agreement would require | 35 | Comptroller | 
| Average salary TSMC projects | $135,687 in 2028, rising 2% a year | Application | 
| Minimum average wage for the project’s jobs | $73,603 | Comptroller | 
| Construction workers, 2027–2029 | 9,841 a year on average; 18,134 at the 2029 peak | Consultant’s model | 
| Out-of-town visitors | 708 a year; average stay 41 days | Consultant’s model | 
| Tax benefit, total | $354.1 million | Comptroller | 
| Tax benefit during construction, 2028–2031 | $123.6 million | Comptroller | 
| Tax benefit in the incentive period, 2032–2041 | $230.6 million | Comptroller | 
| School M&O tax over 20 years, without the agreement | $759.3 million | Comptroller | 
| School M&O tax over 20 years, with the agreement | $405.2 million | Comptroller | 
| Performance bond | $35.4 million | Comptroller | 
A potentially far larger incentive is federal: a tax credit worth 35 cents back to every qualifying dollar spent, as long as construction technically begins before the end of the year. “Qualified” means the cost of the fab’s depreciable physical property that is integral to running the fab, meaning the buildings and the tools, in the year each goes into service, and “construction” means actual physical work of a significant nature or paying or incurring at least 5% of the qualifying property’s cost, with work continuing afterward. Construction here is projected to start in 2027, after that cutoff, though off-site work under a binding written contract or early spending this year could still count, and an extension has been proposed in the Senate.
The land doesn’t count in this equation, and neither does office space. This is also a credit off the tax bill, dollar for dollar, not a deduction. The rate was 25% under the 2022 CHIPS Act and rose to 35% for property placed in service after 2025. If the full $22.6 billion qualified, that would be about $7.9 billion back, but not every dollar qualifies.
If Texas doesn’t work out, TSMC is also considering “a new land parcel in Arizona,” which would be closer to the existing North Phoenix site. TSMC says that may make many things easier, such as handling a workforce and the logistics, with the ability to use existing suppliers and relationships on known infrastructure. This is an incentive for the state of Texas to give the tax break.
The tax agreement needs approval from both the College Station ISD board and the governor. The district also owns one of the parcels on TSMC’s list for the site: almost 91 acres, with a 24,496-square-foot building from 2024. The board has set a public hearing for Dec. 10, with public comment, and could approve the project’s reinvestment zone that day.
The district has 30 days from the day it receives the application, which puts its deadline in late December. As for Brazos County, town halls could reportedly begin as early as the first week of December, though the county has promised only one, “in the near future.”
Assuming things move forward, the real measure begins with the first phase on land. Even if production arrives a generation late, it would be a positive development for U.S.-based chipmaking.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Big Vancouver gaming expo happening next week
articles.text:
A major gaming convention is happening in Vancouver next week.
From Dec. 5-6, the Vancouver Game Expo (VGX) will take place in the Vancouver Convention Centre’s East Building and feature a variety of programming, including game demos, indie studios, vendors, and special guests.
The first VGX was held last year and attracted 2,200 fans. Vancouver Game Connect Association (VGCA) and Folks At Play Inc., the show’s organizers, hope to double attendance this year. To help with that, VGX 2026 has assembled a solid lineup of over 50 developers featuring playable game demos and several notable voice actor guests.
Some of the featured studios include:
- Am I Nima (HO! Games/Outersloth)
- Beastieball (Wishes Unlimited)
- Boreal Tenebrae Act 0 (Snot Bubbles Productions)
- Fresh Tracks (Buffalo Buffalo)
- Gridhack (Threshold Anomaly Games)
- Nocturne (Pracy Studios)
- Over the Hill (Funskeletor)
- Peglin (Red Nexus Games)
- Rebounder (ThirtyThree/Aggro Crab)
- World of Anterra (81monkeys)
Meanwhile, some of the guests include:
- Caitlyn Bairstow (Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora, Rift of the Necrodancer)
- Justine Huxley (Apex Legends, Sword Art Online)
- Frankie Kevich (Control Resonant, Apex Legends)
- Victor Lucas (Electric Playground creator and host)
- David Sobolov (League of Legends, The Flash)
- Nicholas Wolfhard (Fire Emblem Engage, Monster Hunter Wilds)
Other programming highlights include VGM Next (a curated showcase of student games), various artists and other vendors, a free-play gaming lounge, cosplay catwalks and more.
An adult weekend pass is $45.61, while Saturday and Sunday day passes are $29 each. Discounted rates are available for teens and children.
All in all, it’s great to see the show returning to Vancouver. In general, Canada doesn’t have many consumer gaming shows, especially in B.C. That’s not a reflection on the talent, though.
Canada as a whole has one of the biggest pools of game developers in the world, with B.C., in particular, being home to many acclaimed studios. Some popular games made in the province include:
- Celeste (Vancouver’s Extremely OK Games)
- Don’t Starve (Vancouver’s Klei Entertainment)
- EA Sports FC (EA Vancouver)
- Gears of War: E-Day (Vancouver’s The Coalition)
- Inscryption (Vancouver’s Daniel Mullins)
- The Long Dark (Vancouver’s Hinterland)
- Luigi’s Mansion 3 (Vancouver’s Next Level Games)
- 1000xResist (Vancouver’s Sunset Visitor)
It’s also worth noting that the highly-anticipated Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, BioWare legend Casey Hudson’s spiritual successor to Knights of the Old Republic, is being made at Arcanaut Studios, which has offices in Edmonton and Kelowna.
Alongside VGX 2026, the show’s organizers are also putting on an accompanying Vancouver Game Celebration Sale on Steam. The sale will run from Dec. 4-13 and feature discounts on a variety of games made in and around Vancouver. We’ll update this story once that goes live.

articles.title: Is Alice Huang a spy or not?
articles.text:
The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, a former executive at the data-center company Megaspeed, is a Chinese spy. She had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging it and was just as abruptly reinstated on Monday of this week.
What’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest. U.S. intelligence has reportedly tracked Alice Huang’s contact with an officer of China’s spy agency, but officials haven’t offered public evidence that she was commissioned to target Nvidia’s chief. In the past week, after President Trump successfully pushed to bring Jensen Huang back, the administration has played down the allegations it once circulated internally. Whether that reflects new intelligence or political pressure is the big question.
Undisputed reporting shows the claim emerged from the White House itself. It first appeared in a highly classified memo written in March under the oversight of Secretary of State Marco Rubio and circulated to White House officials ahead of Trump’s trip to China in May. The memo formed the partial basis for the New York Times’ initial reporting on the scandal, published Oct. 29 and its existence was first reported on Nov. 8.
The memo did not definitively say, according to the Wall Street Journal, that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. CNN, by contrast, has reported that the memo concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
What’s better established is that Alice Huang was in touch with Chinese intelligence. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) is Beijing’s civilian spy agency, responsible for both foreign intelligence and domestic counterintelligence. Last weekend, the Times, citing people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports, reported that Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from the spring of 2025 until this fall, a period that overlaps her relationship with Jensen Huang. (The Chinese government has called the spy claims a “smear,” and Megaspeed says Huang left the company in August 2025 and that its business is legitimate.)
Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was Trump’s personal defense lawyer before taking over the Justice Department, told journalists on Tuesday: “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.” On the same day, Trump said a pardon was an option for Jensen Huang but that he did not think one would be needed. Senior intelligence officials reportedly told Congress that the government apparently has no actual evidence that the MSS directed Alice Huang to pursue an affair with Jensen Huang.
None of those statements necessarily exonerates Alice Huang as an intelligence agent. Instead, they support the alternate theory that the Chinese government didn’t tell her to begin the affair and that Jensen Huang broke no law by having it.
From a certain angle, the circumstantial evidence surrounding Alice Huang looks quite suspicious. She was a top executive at a company investigated for illicitly channeling Nvidia chips to China, and her husband, Kang Wei, is said to have even closer ties to the MSS, with some sources saying he worked for the agency.
The timing of the government’s reversal is at the heart of the matter. Trump has said he lobbied the board “directly and indirectly” to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, so it wouldn’t be surprising if officials who serve at his pleasure were recasting the case in terms that satisfy his agenda. That wouldn’t necessarily make their assessments wrong. But unless new intelligence has actually resolved the question, and none has been publicly identified as yet, that backdrop is critical to keep in mind. CBS has also reported that Rubio has privately voiced concerns about aspects of Jensen Huang’s return.
Earlier this month, CNN reported that the intelligence community was still working to understand Alice Huang’s relationship with Jensen Huang and that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove she was acting as a spy for Beijing. After a briefing by top intelligence officials earlier this month, Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.), the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, said he was unsure whether she was a spy or a “useful idiot.” And this week, the Wall Street Journal pointed out that under Chinese leader Xi Jinping, top corporate executives routinely maintain ties to the country’s intelligence service without being formally deputized as assets.
The crush of conflicting claims, most from anonymous government sources, obviously leaves large questions unanswered as to what actually transpired. Some of those questions that naturally spring to mind:
- Alice Huang is said to have been under U.S. surveillance for over a year. If the government suspected her of espionage, why wasn’t Jensen Huang warned earlier (and privately, so as not to cause the stock-market-destabilizing maelstrom that followed the more recent disclosure)? One explanation that has been given is that alerting the Nvidia chief might have tipped off Huang that her cover had been blown.
- If Alice Huang was a spy, what information did she pass to the Chinese government, and what influence did she actually have?
- Most critically, how did the allegation reach the public at all? The likeliest answer is a leak. A source told CNN that Rubio briefed Trump on the intelligence in May, yet Trump has since said he only recently learned of the concerns, and in October he presented Jensen Huang with the National Medal of Science. Officials who felt they could not get through to the president may have turned to reporters instead, which would explain how the contents of a memo whose existence has never been disputed found their way into print. What remains unclear is who leaked it, and whether they anticipated the fallout.
There are answers to all of these questions, of course, but when the public will get them is anybody’s guess. Jensen Huang is due to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next week, and by the look from the statements of some of its members, he’s likely in for a rough ride. Unfortunately, congressional hearings, particularly public ones, rarely unearth secrets that haven’t already been disclosed.

articles.title: Japan is packing chipmaking labs into trucks — mobileFab set to travel the country, drumming up interest in hardware careers
articles.text:
Japan is packing chipmaking labs into trucks — mobileFab set to travel the country, drumming up interest in hardware careers
Japan's answer to a 43,000-worker chip talent gap
- Japan's Minimal Fab Promotion Organization debuts mobileFab, a truck-mounted container with three photolithography tools
- The tools are about 30 cm wide, process 12.5 mm wafers without a cleanroom, and add wiring to wafers AIST has already taken to the transistor stage
- No fleet size, route, cost, or funding has been disclosed, and similar mobile fabs are emerging at Purdue and US startup InchFab
Japan has been trying to rebuild its chip industry since 2022, with about ¥10 trillion in public funding now secured, according to the 2026 policy proposal from the Japan Electronics and Information Technology Industries Association (JEITA).
One of the least glamorous yet overbearing obstacles is people: Japan does not have enough engineers who have actually run a fab tool, and an industry group in Tsukuba now thinks part of the answer is to put the tools on the back of a truck.
The Minimal Fab Promotion Organization is due to unveil mobileFab, a shipping container fitted with three ultra-compact chipmaking machines, at SEMICON Japan 2026.
Bringing the fab to students: what actually in the box?
The group's press release pitches it as an inversion of the usual training model: instead of sending students to a semiconductor plant, the plant comes to them. This can be seen as a delayed response to a decade-long engineer shortage, a framing that the organizers are also embracing.
The organization is not a government body, however; It is a general incorporated association of equipment, materials and parts makers and device users, formed in 2017 by merging research programs that began at the state-backed National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) in 2010, according to MONOist.
The container holds a resist coater, a maskless exposure tool, and a developer, the three machines needed for photolithography, the step that prints circuit patterns onto silicon. Each is about 30 cm wide. Each is about 30 cm wide. AIST researchers specified the standard tool footprint as 294 mm wide, 450 mm deep, and 1,440 mm tall, so these probably resemble vending machines rather than desktop gadgets in terms of actual volume.
Minimal Fab wafers are half-inch disks, 12.5 mm across, processed one at a time; A standard 300 mm wafer has roughly 576 times the surface area for context. The tiny format lets the system skip the cleanroom: wafers move between tools in sealed shuttles, and each machine maintains its own local clean environment rather than relying on a building-scale one.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The tech itself isn't new, but that is the point: Yokogawa, a core member of the organization and its first certified operator, claims the approach cuts capital investment to about 1/1000 of a conventional fab, and it has built a small integrated circuit of roughly 1,000 transistors on Minimal Fab tools under contract with JAXA.
The container handles lithography only. Under the program the organization describes, AIST's Tokyo Waterfront center first processes wafers through transistor formation, then ships them to schools. There, students use mobileFab to pattern wiring before etching and testing the results on site. The upshot is that a student can design, build, and measure a working circuit without the school owning a front-end line.
The model is borrowed from schools already doing this with fixed installations: The release points to Kumamoto Prefectural Technical Junior College, where students design integrated circuits that AIST takes to the transistor stage before returning them for wiring and electrical testing.
Sasebo National College of Technology in Nagasaki runs four Minimal Fab tools and a year-long, cross-departmental curriculum, and in March 2026it formally opened S-PORT, a semiconductor training center meant to serve as the hub for all 51 of Japan's national technical colleges. AIST's Toru Hayakawa told MONOist in 2024 that educational adoption, including Sasebo, was growing.
The organizers justify the project with a familiar number. Citing JEITA, the release says Japan's nine largest chipmakers alone will need about 43,000 semiconductor workers over the next ten years, a figure JEITA's policy proposal calls a shortfall.
That number has crept upward. In 2022, JEITA put the need at roughly 35,000 engineers across eight companies, when Hideki Wakabayashi, who led its policy task force, told the Financial Times that "the biggest shortage is engineers," as reported by E&T. A year later, it was 40,000 across eight firms, including Kioxia, Renesas, Sony and Toshiba, per EE Times Japan.
Not the only mobile fab play globally
The drivable fab has arrived in several places at once: Purdue University's electrical engineering school unveiled its own Mobile Fab in October 2026, a roughly 100 sq ft truck-based lab with LED lithography and a sputter coater that the school estimates could be reproduced for about $500,000, against roughly $2 million for a comparable cleanroom.
"Lithography can seem very abstract until you see the process happen," said PhD student Yusuf Adebakin. US startup InchFab is building container-sized fabs costing $5 million to $15 million and selling workforce training alongside them, while Carnegie Mellon's Hacker Fab has published an open source DLP stepper that resolves features under 2 microns.
The pressure behind all of them is similar. A SEMI Foundation analysis suggests the US could be short as many as 157,000 semiconductor and microelectronics workers by 2030, and TSMC previously pushed back its first Arizona fab over a lack of skilled installation workers. The cleanroom remains the big barrier to teaching any of this, so much so that one YouTuber converted a backyard shed into one just to make memory cells.
What sets Japan's effort apart is maturity. Minimal Fab has a standardized tool format, a certification scheme, and more than a decade of process work behind it, and AIST spin-off Hundred Semiconductors is already trying to take the same tools into small-volume production. By contrast, most of the alternatives being discussed or explored are still prototypes at best.
One container running single half-inch wafers through a lithography cycle of 15 to 20 minutes is a teaching instrument, not a pipeline, however. The organization has not published a resolution figure for its exposure tool, but comparable DLP systems work at around the micron scale, orders of magnitude away from the 2nm-class process Rapidus is bringing up in Hokkaido. Students will learn process fundamentals, not how a leading-edge line runs.
The harder problem may be motivation rather than access here: Toshiba's Takashi Miyamori told Nikkei in 2022 that "most Japanese studying science subjects are more interested in IT," as relayed by EIS. A truck that lets a technical college student print a circuit pattern and test it the same afternoon is a reasonable bet against that preference, and a cheap one by industry standards.
Whether it shifts career choices at any meaningful scale depends on details the organization has yet to share: how many trucks, how often they visit, and who pays for the whole process.
