Source : Power On Podcast

articles.title: Crearon una mano robótica que se imprime en 3D y cuesta menos de USD 650
articles.text:
Investigadores del Instituto de Tecnología de Nueva Jersey (NJIT) diseñaron una mano robótica de cinco dedos que se imprime en una impresora 3D doméstica y cuesta menos de USD 650 en piezas. El prototipo, llamado PHD-Hand, tiene 15 articulaciones motorizadas y logró sostener los 33 tipos de agarre de una clasificación estándar de la mano humana.
El diseño es de Neel Adwani, doctorando en ingeniería eléctrica y computación, junto con Muhaiminul Islam Akash, Saffia Ouali y Ethan Liu, bajo la dirección del profesor Cong Wang. El trabajo fue aceptado en la conferencia internacional de robots humanoides de IEEE-RAS, que se celebrará del 6 al 9 de diciembre en Santa Clara, según informó Humanoids Daily.
Adwani dijo que la cifra de menos de USD 650 incluye los servomotores (pequeños motores que mueven cada articulación), la placa de control, el filamento de impresión y las varillas de acero. El estudio, publicado en el repositorio arXiv, sostiene que el diseño reduce la barrera de entrada para quienes desarrollan manos robóticas.
Cómo es el diseño de la mano robótica
La mayoría de las manos robóticas económicas mueven los dedos con cables, similares a tendones. Según Adwani, esos cables se estiran, se resbalan y necesitan ajustes constantes. PHD-Hand los reemplaza por varillas y articulaciones rígidas, un sistema que evita ese mantenimiento.
Cada dedo tiene tres motores ubicados debajo de él. Dos mueven el nudillo, que se imprime en un material flexible y permite doblar el dedo y abrirlo hacia los lados. El tercero acciona juntas las dos articulaciones superiores mediante una varilla de acero de 0,6 milímetros. Una sola placa controla los 15 motores.
La mano mide 200 milímetros de la muñeca a la punta de los dedos y pesa 570 gramos. Eso la deja cerca del tamaño de una mano adulta y algo más pequeña que la Linkerbot L20, una mano comercial de unos 225 milímetros que los autores usan como comparación. Se imprime con plásticos TPU y PETG, sin estructuras de soporte.
Cada dedo se arma con 18 piezas, impresas o compradas. Los autores comparan esa cifra con las más de 27 piezas por dedo de una mano anterior accionada también por articulaciones, publicada en 2021 en Nature Communications, que requería mecanizado industrial.
Qué puede hacer y qué le falta
El equipo probó la mano con la clasificación de agarres de Feix, un conjunto de 33 posturas humanas, y la mostró sosteniendo objetos como una taza y un taladro. También hizo tareas con los objetos ya en la palma: quitar la tapa de un frasco, girar un destornillador de precisión y rotar un cubo de 55 milímetros.
Los autores admiten limitaciones. Algunos agarres, como sostener un palo o usar palillos chinos, salieron imperfectos porque los dedos no se flexionan tanto como los humanos y la mano no tiene la membrana de piel entre el pulgar y el índice.
El prototipo acumuló unas 200 horas de pruebas y tuvo dos fallas, en ambos casos la rotura de la varilla de acero que acopla las articulaciones superiores. El artículo aclara que aún no se hizo un estudio formal de fatiga. Tampoco tiene sensores de tacto, y la fuerza de agarre no se midió: el equipo planea informarla en un trabajo posterior.
Adwani afirmó que el equipo publicará los archivos de diseño y el software de control como código abierto en aproximadamente un mes. El hardware usará la licencia CERN-OHL-P v2 y el software, la licencia MIT, según Humanoids Daily.
“Las manos robóticas no deberían ser un lujo que solo pueden pagar unos pocos laboratorios”, dijo Adwani. Su argumento es que estudiantes, aficionados, empresas emergentes y laboratorios podrán construir una y mejorarla.
Los próximos pasos que enumeran los autores son pasar la varilla de acoplamiento por la falange media, rediseñar la base del pulgar, añadir la membrana que falta y imprimir cada dedo en una sola pieza, algo que todavía no logran de forma fiable.

articles.title: Unamuno, escritor y filósofo: “El que uno es, el que se cree ser y el que le cree otro”
articles.text:
“El que uno es, el que se cree ser y el que le cree otro”, escribió Miguel de Unamuno. Se trata de un problema que tenemos todos los que subimos una foto a algún sitio. La diferencia entre lo que somos y lo que creemos que los demás van a pensar de nosotros. Antes de Instagram, Unamuno resumía así la teoría de Holmes:
En el prólogo del libro “Tres novelas ejemplares y un prólogo” (1920) cita a Oliver Wendell Holmes en relación con una teoría sobre varias versiones de nosotros mismos. Holmes habla de una teoría de las diversas personas que somos.
Unamuno fue novelista, ensayista y rector de la Universidad de Salamanca. Pertenece a la generación del 98. Sus dudas y el conflicto entre razón y fe están presentes en su pensamiento. En el prólogo de su libro habla de esta cuestión de quiénes somos y también de qué es lo que hace que una persona sea real. Se pregunta por ello tanto en el caso de los personajes que existen fuera de un libro como en el de los personajes ficticios.
Versiones que no coinciden
Para ilustrar el problema, Unamuno introduce dos personajes. Los llama Juan y Tomás. Cuando Juan y Tomás hablan, intervienen seis personajes. Ahí está el Juan real, el Juan que Juan cree que es y además está el Juan que cree Tomás.
De esta manera separamos a la persona de sus versiones. En la primera versión, solo su Hacedor conoce al Juan real. El Juan que Juan piensa que es puede ser muy distinto. Por otro lado, también está el que Tomás supone que es y que puede ser diferente.
Por esto tampoco solucionamos el problema desde el punto de vista del otro. En el esquema de Holmes que recoge Unamuno, Tomás tiene su propio Juan. Pero este sigue siendo diferente. Saber lo que opina el otro de nosotros es conocer una de las imágenes.
Podríamos hablar de la imagen que creamos en las redes sociales. Nosotros elegimos qué foto poner. Qué queremos mostrar y qué dejamos fuera. Es un perfil que recoge una parte de lo que queremos mostrar. Está expuesto a la interpretación de quien visita nuestro perfil. También hay una presión por crear una imagen perfecta.
El que uno quisiera ser
Pero Unamuno va más allá de estas tres versiones. Después de resumir la teoría de Holmes, añade otro elemento. Habla de quien uno quisiera ser. Considera que es un creador. Está relacionado con la realidad interior del individuo. En este punto se pierde algo de la argumentación de Unamuno si nos quedamos solo en estas tres imágenes.
Unamuno plantea el problema de la identidad en clave de voluntad. Cuando habla del que es real, está interesado en el que quiere ser. Este es el contexto de este prólogo. En él se pregunta por la realidad de sus personajes. También por la realidad de las personas de carne y hueso hablando de cómo es nuestra imagen frente a la de los demás.
Dice así: “Y digo que, además del que uno es para Dios (si para Dios es uno alguien), y del que es para los otros y del que se cree ser, hay el que quisiera ser”.

articles.title: NITES seeks policy framework to ringfence IT workers from AI job displacement
articles.text:
NITES seeks policy framework to ringfence IT workers from AI job displacement
The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) is for technology moving forward the industry but not with leaving workforce behind.
The IT-union body NITES has called for a comprehensive policy framework to safeguard tech sector employees from job displacement arising from the uptake of Artificial Intelligence (AI), automation and other emerging technologies.
The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has urged the government to initiate consultations with industry stakeholders and employee representatives to formulate such a forward-looking policy on responsible AI adoption and workforce protection, as it advocated that "technology should move the industry forward without leaving its workforce behind".
NITES acknowledged that technological advancement is important to the industry's growth, but added, in the same breath, that adoption of AI and automation must not leave employees without adequate notice, financial security or opportunities to move on to alternative employment.
It said that tech companies must be transparent when undertaking workforce reductions, particularly where such decisions are attributed to AI or automation.
Employees and government authorities must know how many people are affected, the reason behind their positions being eliminated and just how many jobs are directly being replaced by technology, it said in a release.
NITES has, in the past, raised its voice against mass layoffs, forced resignations and unfair employment practices in the IT sector.
While those earlier representations were not specifically focused on AI-related job losses, NITES believes the changing employment landscape now requires a dedicated policy framework to address this emerging challenge.
It has, accordingly, pitched for mandatory safeguards for affected employees.
"Employees should not be left to bear the entire burden of technological change. Companies adopting AI and automation should be required to provide reasonable advance notice, fair severance compensation and payment of all outstanding statutory and contractual dues," NITES said.
Further, employers should make all-out efforts to re-skill and redeploy existing employees within their organisations before eliminating their positions on account of technological advancements.
While existing labour laws provide certain retrenchment protection to eligible workers, NITES is of the view that stronger and more specific safeguards are necessary to address the challenges arising from AI-driven job displacement.
"Re-skilling must be meaningful and outcome-oriented. Merely providing access to online courses or training material cannot be considered adequate support," it said, exhorting employers to make genuine efforts to equip affected employees for alternative roles and future employment opportunities.
"The increasing impact of AI on employment now requires a dedicated policy-level discussion involving the government, Nasscom, IT companies and employee representatives," it said.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ tablet review - slim and powerful with laptop performance
articles.text:
- RATING
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ is an excellent pro-level tablet which offers the power, performance, and portability of a laptop. It give users more flexibility and allows them to be in control to power through their tasks wherever and whenever they want.
Samsung don’t sell laptops in Australia but the closest you can come is with the Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ tablet.
It has the power, design and features that can match a laptop for nearly all your tasks on the move.
And when paired with the excellent Pro Keyboard accessory made from premium aluminium and featuring a dedicated Galaxy AI key, the Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ tablet turns into a powerhouse.
On its own, the Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ has a slick design and is only 5.3mm thick and weighs just 555g.
It also has an IP68 rating so it’s built for everyday use anywhere.
We used it most of the time attached to the Pro Keyboard but it was still an impressive experience just to kick back with the tablet on its own.
And with those svelte measurements it was absolutely no effort to use and carry it around.
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ has a 12.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display which is simply stunning.
It has 120Hz refresh rate and up to 1,600-nit peak brightness so you can use it anywhere even outside in the sun.
Not only does it have a stunning screen but it also has impressive audio as well with four-channel spatial audio, that’s twice as many as the previous model.
If you’re watching movies and streaming your favourite TV shows, it’s going to look and sound amazing.
Samsung also has the Tab S12 Ultra, which offers the same chip and a 14.6-inch display. One other difference is the Ultra has Wi-Fi 7, and the S12+ has Wi-Fi 6E.
The Tab S12+ is powered by 3nm MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, which is a step up from the previous model, which means it can run multiple apps at the same time, power through tasks with the on-board AI.
And the other benefit is excellent power efficiency which gets users more than 20 hours of use on a single charge.
What adds to the power efficiency is the new 3D vapour chamber, which keeps things cool to maintain the performance of the CPU, GPU and NPU.
Even when you’re multitasking or rendering and editing large files, the enhanced thermal system can help dissipate the heat to maintain performance and your battery.
This is a pro-level tablet with the power, performance and display quality to match and would be in the same ballpark as Apple’s iPad Pro.
For our review we were provided with the Galaxy Tab S12+ 5G which has a SIM card slot for a 5G SIM card. And on that same tray was room for a microSD card.
This is ideal for the user who needs to stay connected on the move, even when there is no Wi-Fi.
This is a feature we loved and we’re surprised 5G connectivity isn’t offered as an option on more laptops.
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ comes with a 6-month trial of Google AI Pro and access to Gemini Notebook which can help users get even more organised, more efficiency and more productive.
What we liked was the ability to upload content we had created, whether it was a document, a recording, or a presentation and have Google AI Pro provide feedback and answers to our questions.
For a student this feature would allow them to upload whatever they’re studying and have Google AI Pro provide tests and quizzes about the material.
On top of this you also have Galaxy AI at your fingertips which includes features like Now Nudge and Multi Window so it’s possible to finish your tasks and receive intuitive follow-up actions.
Now Nudge can see what’s on your screen and provide suggestions to complete tasks do things like adding events to your calendar and anticipating what you need to do next.
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ also comes with the S Pen and gives users an excellent tactile way of interacting with the device.
If you’re a note-taker like we are this was a great way to get down our thoughts and take notes.
You can hop into the Creative Studio to create and generate images and turning drawings into images using the S Pen.
Adobe Photoshop is now on the Galaxy Tab S12+ and it also has been optimised for the device’s amazing display.
It also works well with S Pen so you can easily access things like quick tools and adjust settings in seconds.
Another favourite use of the S Pen was being able to annotate documents.
Also on board is another beloved feature – Samsung’s DeX. It makes the tablet feel more like a PC than ever with a Windows-like desktop.
It’s also easy to connect wirelessly to another screen or even a TV to spread out your work.
If you’re fully embedded in the Samsung ecosystem there’s also Multi-Control, which allows users to use the keyboard and mouse from the Galaxy tablet or attached keyboard to control your other Galaxy devices.
Each device remains independent but you can still drag and drop items between them.
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ is available now and is priced from $1,999.
VERDICT
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ is an excellent pro-level tablet which offers the power, performance, and portability of a laptop. It give users more flexibility and allows them to be in control to power through their tasks wherever and whenever they want.

articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le téléviseur TCL 65C89K à 879,00 €
Actuellement noté 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, le téléviseur TCL 65C89K délivre une colorimétrie précise en SDR comme en HDR avec un contraste très efficace. Le Black Friday fait descendre son prix à 879,00 € chez Cdiscount, soit une baisse d'environ 2 % et 20,00 € d'économie.
Le TCL 65C89K succède au C89B avec l'objectif de proposer un affichage Mini-Led 4K très lumineux et contrasté. Équipé d'une dalle HVA de 65 pouces compatible avec les principaux formats HDR, ce modèle s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo par la maîtrise de son rétroéclairage et sa grande fidélité visuelle.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le téléviseur descend à 879,00 € chez Cdiscount, contre un prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours de 899,00 €, soit environ 2 % de remise. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 20,00 €.
Une luminosité impressionnante et une image fidèle
Ce téléviseur Mini-Led délivre des images très dynamiques grâce à un pic lumineux mesuré à 3283 cd/m² par notre laboratoire, ce qui permet de profiter pleinement des contenus HDR en pleine journée. Sa dalle 144 Hz assure une excellente fluidité dans les scènes d'action rapides. Actuellement noté 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, l'appareil restitue les couleurs avec une grande précision, comme le détaille notre test complet.
TCL 65C89K
Points forts
- Pic lumineux record pour un Mini-Led (3280 cd/m²).
- Colorimétrie précise en SDR et HDR.
- Contraste et local dimming très efficaces.
- Compatible HDR10+ et Dolby Vision.
- Bon système audio.
- Consommation maîtrisée.
Points faibles
- Reflets encore bien visibles.
- Angles de vision imparfaits.
- Toujours un peu de blooming.
- Dérives colorimétriques en mode jeu.
- Seulement deux HDMI 2.1.
Une connectique ciblée et quelques limites optiques
Sur le plan de l'équipement, l'écran intègre seulement deux ports HDMI 2.1, ce qui oblige à alterner les branchements si vous possédez plusieurs consoles de dernière génération. Les reflets restent visibles dans les pièces baignées de soleil direct et les angles de vision étroits dégradent le contraste pour les spectateurs assis sur les côtés. Malgré ces concessions sur le placement dans la pièce, le modèle comblera les amateurs de cinéma installés bien en face de l'écran.

- Bonne spatialisation sonore en mode Cinéma.
Points faibles

- Télécommande sans rétroéclairage.

articles.title: Nvidia reportedly blocks AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia
articles.text:
What we know so far: Server makers have been told they can't ship machines built around Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. Dell and Supermicro, which assemble the chips into finished servers, have told buyers in those countries that Nvidia will not let their orders go out, according to FT sources. No one yet knows whether the stoppage is a pause or a lasting change.
Nvidia and its partners are still working out how to comply with Washington's new export controls, sources have told the Financial Times, and that process will decide how long the freeze lasts. Nvidia declined to comment. Dell, Supermicro, ByteDance and Aolani did not respond to requests for comment.
The four countries matter because Chinese AI developers have favored them as places to reach Nvidia hardware that Washington restricts from export. They matter to Nvidia, too: the company booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up 72% in 12 months, according to its accounts. That unit also carries some of Nvidia's Taiwan and China revenue.
Many Chinese companies have skirted the export rules by renting the chips instead of buying them. Cloud providers buy servers loaded with Nvidia processors and lease the computing time to customers, including Chinese ones. The US Commerce Department introduced new rules last week meant to end that practice.
Under the rules, cloud providers that already serve Chinese customers have 90 days to obtain a license or face export restrictions. Providers say the process is unclear. "There's this new rule but no guidance on execution," an executive at a cloud provider told the Financial Times. "No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It's causing sheer chaos in the region."
The rules followed an upheaval at the top of Nvidia. Chief executive Jensen Huang was briefly ousted after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman tied to a cloud provider that leased access to Chinese companies. That provider is being investigated for alleged involvement in smuggling.
The reports complicated Huang's stance that the US should keep selling Nvidia chips to Chinese companies to deepen their dependence on American technology. Huang returned to the helm this week, and many had hoped that would open a path to less strict enforcement. The sources said there is little indication Nvidia will hold back from carrying out the new rules.
The stakes are high for Chinese AI labs. Beijing has pushed to develop domestic alternatives, but the country's leading labs remain heavily reliant on Nvidia processors to develop their flagship models. That reliance is greatest during early-stage training, which demands the most computing power.
Demand from Chinese tech companies has fueled Southeast Asia's data center boom, particularly in Malaysia and Indonesia, where billions of dollars have gone into AI infrastructure. The new US restrictions have put much of that investment in jeopardy.
Aolani, a Singapore-based cloud company, is one example. It planned to provide advanced computing power to ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese parent, through leasing agreements, two of the sources said. The two said the disruption has led some bankers who had agreed to finance the project to stop issuing credit worth about $500 million, and ByteDance may now drop the deal.
Cloud operators now face a 90-day deadline with no clear licensing path. Server makers are holding orders at Nvidia's direction. Developers who built facilities around Chinese tenants are waiting to learn whether those tenants can still use them.

articles.title: Trop de bips dans votre voiture neuve ? Euro NCAP s’apprête enfin à sévir
articles.text:
Si vous avez conduit une voiture neuve récemment, vous connaissez la bande-son : un bip quand on dépasse la limite lue par la caméra, un autre quand on frôle une ligne blanche, un rappel à l’ordre si le regard quitte la route. Euro NCAP, l’organisme européen qui attribue les étoiles de sécurité aux voitures neuves, admet maintenant que ces alertes poussent les conducteurs à couper leurs aides, ce qui est contreproductif.
Dans un entretien accordé à Auto Express publié le 21 novembre, Matthew Avery, son directeur du développement stratégique, annonce que les voitures seront bientôt notées sur leur « facteur d’agacement ». L’organisme trouve aujourd’hui pénibles, voire dangereuses, des alertes qu’il a lui-même encouragées. À partir de 2029, une voiture trop bavarde pourra perdre des points dans sa note finale.
Une prise de conscience tardive
« Notre mission est de bannir les bips et les bongs », résume Matthew Avery. Pour lui, un conducteur qui désactive ses aides fait à peu près la même chose que s’il coupait son airbag ou détachait sa ceinture. Une surveillance du conducteur trop sensible ou une aide au maintien dans la voie trop autoritaire coûteront donc des points, et il prévient les constructeurs qu’Euro NCAP « arrive ».
Pour mesurer tout ça, l’organisme fait rouler depuis cette année chaque voiture testée sur 2 000 kilomètres de routes ouvertes, et relève au passage les fausses alertes. Il lui faut néanmoins des dizaines de milliers de kilomètres de données avant de noter quoi que ce soit, d’où l’échéance de 2029.
Euro NCAP a lui-même récompensé ces alertes
Soyons justes, l’obligation vient de l’Union européenne. Son règlement sur la sécurité générale des véhicules impose ces aides sur toutes les voitures neuves immatriculées depuis juillet 2024, de l’alerte de survitesse à la détection de somnolence.
Pourtant, le barème d’Euro NCAP donnait déjà des points aux voitures équipées de ces systèmes, et une cinquième étoile pèse lourd dans une brochure commerciale. Matthew Avery le reconnaît à demi-mot quand il prévient que les constructeurs qui montent des équipements grossiers ne pourront plus compter sur de bonnes notes. Jusqu’ici, ils le pouvaient donc.
Personne ne demande pour autant de jeter les aides à la conduite. Matthew Avery affirme que les assistances sur autoroute, comme le régulateur de vitesse adaptatif qui garde tout seul la distance avec la voiture de devant, réduisent de 30 à 40 % le taux d’accidents.
Le problème vient surtout du réglage de ces alertes, et personnellement, j’ajouterais le son et volume même de ces bips à l’équation. Matthew Avery cite en exemple le dernier système de BMW, qui vérifie si le conducteur franchit une ligne volontairement et s’il y a un vrai danger avant de toucher au volant. Et c’est un constat que l’on partage avec le représentant d’Euro NCAP : les derniers systèmes BMW ou Volkswagen ne bipent que quand c’est nécessaire selon nos tests. L’organisme aurait dû exiger dès le départ ce genre d’aide, qui ne se manifeste qu’au moment où l’on va vraiment percuter quelqu’un.
Euro NCAP a déjà corrigé le tir sur une autre source de distraction : le tout-tactile. Ses protocoles 2026 réclament des commandes physiques pour les fonctions les plus urgentes, comme les clignotants ou les feux de détresse, avant d’accorder les cinq étoiles. On verra si les constructeurs suivent aussi vite sur les bips. En attendant 2029, la loi européenne oblige toujours la voiture à réactiver l’alerte de survitesse à chaque démarrage.
Enfin, comme nos confrères d’Automobile Magazine, qui ont attiré notre attention sur le sujet, on attend avec une certaine impatience que l’Euro NCAP se penche sur la Citroën ë-C3 (ou l’une de ses cousines). Elle a pour le moment échappé au test.

And with sound tuned by Bose — and not a three-figure Bose price in sight — there's a lot to sharpen your claws about when it comes to Skullcandy.
Today's best Skullcandy Method 360 ANC deals

articles.title: A month with the iPhone Duo has changed how I use my phone
articles.text:
For years, the definition of a premium smartphone depended on its cameras, processors, and how light it felt when you stowed it in your pocket. The iPhone Duo challenges that concept by asking consumers to pay more for a fundamentally different smartphone experience, even if it means sacrificing what they’ve long thought of as high-end features.
In a little under a month of using the Duo, I’ve found that the trade-offs I was initially concerned about matter far less to me than I had expected. What’s been more interesting is how the Duo’s foldable form factor has changed my everyday habits, including how I interact with apps, which apps I use, and how I organize and personalize the phone itself.
I also easily forgot a number of my initial concerns about switching to the Duo. The apps, for the most part, are now optimized for the Duo; I’ve reacquainted myself with Touch ID; and I don’t miss the Pro Max camera on most days.
That’s not to say the Duo doesn’t have its shortcomings. I still miss that telephoto lens sometimes, and I’m still longing for Face ID — though not as much since Apple shipped a face unlock feature in the latest update. But after a month of using the Duo, I’ve found these compromises have had less of an impact on my day-to-day experience compared with the benefits that the new form factor brings.
Multitasking feels more natural
I was surprised by how much I’ve grown to appreciate the Duo’s multitasking capabilities. Initially, I didn’t think I’d regularly use it to view two apps side by side, given the still fairly limited screen space even while the phone is unfolded, especially compared with an iPad. But I’ve found myself snapping apps to both halves of the screen more often than I had imagined.
For starters, Apple has made this side-by-side mode incredibly intuitive and easy to use — you simply drag the app over to the left or right side of the screen and drop it into the target box that appears.
I have regularly taken advantage of this feature to do all sorts of things.
I really enjoy keeping X open as I read through the news, which allows me to switch back and forth between the article I’m reading and real-time reactions to it. Sometimes I’ll keep email or Slack open on the side while I’m working on something else so I don’t miss an important message or notification.
And much like the overstimulated members of Gen Z (which I am not), I sometimes like scrolling social media while engaging with some other media off to the side.
Case in point: I passively watched Netflix’s “Love is Blind” reunion while reading the gossipy tweets and Reddit posts about the main characters on the other side of the screen. This sort of TV watching behavior used to be called second-screen viewing, but now it’s morphing into something new. Everything is happening on one screen, so should we call it “Duo screen viewing,” perhaps? It makes me long for even more interactive TV experiences where commentary and content are combined.
It really is like having two phones
I’ve noticed another shift in my behavior since adopting the Duo as my main device. When I’m out and about, the Duo feels more like an (arguably heavier) iPhone mini. For those who still miss smaller iPhones, the Duo is the next best thing. Despite its weight, the phone feels small. You can cover it with one hand; you can type with a thumb; you can reach the top and bottom easily; and you can even fit it into your front and back pockets. The Pro Max now feels unbelievably strange in my hand — how was I ever comfortable wrangling this giant rectangle?
The Duo’s small screen works well when you’re on the go, especially for short interactions like responding to a quick text or pulling up directions to a destination. It’s not as great for mindless scrolling, which I appreciate, as it forces me to engage with the real world instead of killing every moment of boredom or unease by opening up apps.
But when you’re home or somewhere with time to kill, you can unfold the screen and enjoy your apps super-sized. It’s the best of both worlds.
I find that I instinctively unfold the phone when I’m preparing to watch videos, because the larger screen is best for that. It’s also unfolded if I’m shopping, as it’s more convenient for looking at products, zooming in to examine the details, or complete checkout forms.
Generally, I also unfold the Duo when I’m actively using apps. This setup has also allowed me to rethink my Home Screen layout: With the Duo closed, I prefer to see just widgets on the small screen with key information like weather, time, battery life, and so on. Meanwhile, the only app icons on the Home Screen are those in the dock.
The Duo apps are ready now
In the weeks since its launch, most of the apps that weren’t yet optimized for the Duo have been upgraded to support its foldable form factor. In mid-November, Apple said there were over 200,000 Duo-ready apps, and in my experience, that certainly feels true. A majority of my so-called “daily drivers” — with the glaring exception of key Google apps like Gmail and Drive — have dropped the black band on the side of the screen that was frustrating early testers of the phone.
Most apps now take advantage of the available space, whether that’s on the Duo’s small front screen or the wider, unfolded one.
I’ve also found it interesting to see the different interpretations developers have had for how to best optimize their app for Duo.
Some have used the form factor as a way to bring in some sort of novelty: there’s a note-taking app that opens and closes like a notebook, with pages you can write on with the Apple Pencil; a retro Walkman-like music player; a tiny typewriter; a gaming handheld; a game where you close the phone to make grilled cheese.
As much as I love the whimsy of this group of apps, I appreciate how my everyday apps feel better to use on the unfolded screen. Spotify, at last, feels less cluttered when it has more screen real estate. A number of note-taking, list-making, and calendar apps also feel somehow more usable when spread out.
The Netflix app is actually fantastic with its support for multiple viewing modes, which include playing video on the closed outer display, the “laptop” orientation with its big player controls, and the “tent” mode.
Other developers have similarly reimagined how their app would work if it had originally been designed for the Duo’s small and larger screens.
One good example of this is Sofa, a handy utility for organizing the books, movies, TV shows, podcasts, albums, and games you want to check out. When the Duo is closed, its navigation is tucked off to the right side in a vertical bar, while the main screen focuses on the items you’ve saved. But when the Duo is unfolded, the number of items displayed on the screen also expands into a two-column layout, with more of your items featured on the screen and your lists on the left side. It doesn’t feel like two different apps, but like you’ve opened up the app itself and given it more space to spread out.
In terms of your daily social media scroll, apps like TikTok and Instagram have been updated to be perfectly usable on the Duo, whether the phone is open or closed. When closed, TikTok now stretches the video to cover the screen, instead of showing the ugly black bar. Scrolling short-form videos on the Duo, while unfolded like a slightly smaller iPad mini, has become my preferred way to watch.
I’m reading more books
Here’s another surprise: I’ve spent less time with my Kindle, and am instead reading books on my Duo. Unfolded, the Duo is a decent enough replacement for an e-book reader, albeit it can be a bit more stimulating as it’s not an e-ink device. However, the matte inner screen isn’t quite as bright and distracting as your typical glossy OLED display. There’s less glare and softer reflections, but there’s also something about the display that just feels calmer than a smartphone, allowing you to more fully engage with a book’s text.
Unfolded and held vertically, reading on the Duo feels a lot like reading on the standard Kindle, at least in terms of hand-feel. And putting your phone into the “Do Not Disturb” focus mode can help you not be distracted by incoming notifications and messages while you read.
You can also unfold the device while keeping it in landscape orientation, with the screens bent slightly inward like a real book. For even more fun, you can turn on Kindle’s page-turn animation, which makes it seem as if you’re turning the page in a physical book. And I love how you can “performatively read” using an app like Book2Life or Actually Read — they display the book’s cover on the Duo’s outer screen as you read the text on the inner screen.
E-book readers will likely find they can carry one less device when they’re out and about, because the Duo can stand in for whatever Kindle or other reader you typically keep in your purse or bag. You can save the Kindle for other times, whether that’s at home, on long travel days, or when you don’t want to worry about sand getting into your $2,000 phone.
I don’t need a PopSocket
On the big-screened iPhone 17 Pro Max I used to carry, I tended to keep a PopSocket of some sort on the back because the phone was both heavy and large, which made it hard to hold for longer periods of time. The Duo is similarly heavy, but its shape makes it far easier to hold in one hand without the extra help.
Folded, you can do the usual one-handed hold where the bottom edge of the phone rests on your pinky, your other three fingers cradle the back, and your thumb is free to navigate the screen.
Unfolded, the Duo’s like using a small Kindle or iPad mini, where two hands are required. You also don’t need a PopSocket for balancing the phone on the side, because it can be propped up like a tent or opened like a tiny laptop. Or, if you prefer, Apple and others offer Duo cases with a built-in stand. (Apple’s case comes in navy and taupe, though, so if you’re not boring, you’ll probably want to shop from third-party vendors).
If you think you still might need a PopSocket at times, or you just aren’t ready to give it up, the brand now makes a slimmer version: its Low-Pro Grip. There are other competitors, like the OhSnap grips, which aren’t a bad alternative either.
It’s inspiring personalization
There’s something about the Duo that seems to have kicked off a new iPhone personalization trend, at least judging by what I’ve been seeing on social media.
Unlike a regular iPhone, where every phone case is simply a shell that offers a degree of protection based on the materials used, the Duo case lineup provides far more variety.
You can buy cases with and without built-in screen protectors, and some use adhesive to better stick to the outer screen, while others don’t. Some cases let you customize the band around the outer screen with a different color than the case that protects the rest of the phone.
Then you have cases that cover the hinge, while others leave it exposed. There are cases that offer holes where you can attach straps, wristlets, and charms. Some of those have attachment points at the bottom and others on the side.
Essentially, there are a lot of options for customizing how you want to carry the Duo and how you want to express your own style.
I’m also now starting to see whimsical cases that come with attached pens. (Thank goodness — most of the pen cases so far have been kind of plain!)
I also believe there’s something about the Duo that particularly appeals to women. Maybe because it’s small, or maybe it’s because you can attach a strap to its side and carry it like a little purse. Or maybe because, like a purse, you can deck it out with chains and charms — a choice that’s grown increasingly popular as young people have embraced whimsical, retro tech as a way to express their individuality and sense of fashion.
The Duo easily lends itself to this trend, perhaps even more than a regular iPhone. It becomes an accessory you want on display, not one buried in a bag.
Before switching to the Duo, I spent a lot of time thinking about what I’d be giving up by moving away from the Pro Max.
I’m surprised to find that, a month later, I only think about what I’d have to give up if I switched back to a traditional iPhone. It’s not just the extra space of the unfolded screen I’d miss — it’s all the little habits I’ve developed around having different screen sizes for different purposes.
The Duo makes me pause and think about how I want to use an app. That small moment of deliberation, before I even open the phone, has helped me break some of my more mindless smartphone habits, particularly around social media.
That’s not a benefit I could have anticipated if I’d judged the device by its specifications alone.

articles.title: Are there hidden gems in Dollarama’s tech section? [Part 3]
articles.text:
All the way back in 2022, I took it upon myself to find out whether the tech section at Dollarama carries hidden gems — you know, to alleviate some of the financial burden that comes with being a tech enthusiast.
Armed with a few dollars and VERY low expectations, I bought a bunch of products from the Canadian value retailer, including Bluetooth speakers, headphones, wireless chargers, gaming mice, and more. Although some of the purchases turned out to be complete duds, I actually managed to find some decent products that punched well above their weight class.
That one-off experiment turned into a two-part series, and now, four years later, I’m back with a third edition.
First things first, Dollarama’s tech section has definitely gotten more interesting in the last four years, even though it’s still dominated by the Tech1 brand.
My new haul includes not only a wireless mouse and a MagSafe-compatible accessory, but also wireless earbuds and even a gadget designed to give other drivers the middle finger — literally.
Here’s what I found at my local Dollarama:
Audio on a budget
Acellories GemstonePro wireless earbuds ($5.03)
We’re starting strong with this one. After selling wired audio products for years now, Dollarama now carries wireless earbuds, and they’re surprisingly good considering they cost just about the same as two large double-doubles from Timmies.
The first thing I noticed when I was picking up the earbuds was their packaging. For something that costs $5, Accellories has spent a lot of resources ensuring a somewhat positive first impression. The other big thing is that they’re available in two colorways: White and Black.
I picked up the Black ones and was surprised to see extra silicone tips and a charging cable included in the box.
It makes you wonder what the company’s margin is if it includes all that in a $5 package. Also makes you wonder whether all the bigger brands are charging us a premium for things that don’t cost all that much. Of course, there’s a lot more that goes into the price of wireless earbuds than what all is included in the package, and the GemstonePro shines in that department too.
The earbuds don’t boast the most premium build out there, but they don’t feel flimsy either. The buds and the case feature a Nothing-like translucent design, with an RGB LED battery indicator on the latter. The buds themselves feature a mic and capacitive touch buttons on each stem to play/pause music, which I REALLY wasn’t expecting on a $5 device.
The case charges via USB-C, and I’ve found that the buds are good for roughly 1.5 hours of playback on a full charge. Acellories claims 20 hours of playback with the case, though that claim is definitely incorrect. I was able to get roughly 5 hours of playback. Just one full charge of the buds knocked the case’s battery indicator from 100% down to 52%.
Lastly, and most importantly, the buds don’t sound tinny, as we’ve come to expect from cheap earbuds. In fact, they’re surprisingly decent for something that costs $5, as long as you’re not expecting audiophile-grade sound here. Normally, I’d say that earbuds this cheap are best reserved for listening to podcasts and audiobooks, but the GemstonePro are good enough for music too.
They’re also a great option for kids who just can’t be trusted with expensive options just yet.
Tech1 wired gaming headset ($4.78)
Remember when I said the GemstonePro doesn’t feel flimsy? Well, these are the opposite. One wrong move, and I feel like I could snap these with ease. That, however, is the only real complaint I have with the headset.
Audio-wise, they sound decent enough, with loud and clear audio. Bass is practically non-existent, but I was still able to make out which direction enemy footsteps were coming from in games like Valorant. That, in itself, justifies the $5 price tag.
The microphone works great too, so your teammates shouldn’t have any trouble understanding your comms.
Similar to the GemstonePro, I’d recommend picking these up for a kid who’s just getting into gaming. Considering the build quality, they won’t last long, but they’ll get the job done.
Tech1 USB-C to 3.5mm audio adapter ($4.50)
Nothing much to see here. If you own 3.5mm wired headphones or earbuds and would like to use them with your modern USB-C phone, this $4.50 adapter works as intended.
Note that Tech1 hasn’t mentioned any audio specs on the packaging, so we don’t know the adapter’s bit depth. What I was able to confirm, however, is that the adapter works seamlessly with both Android and iOS phones and supports mic use too.
Phone accessories without the premium
Tech1 USB-C charging cable ($4.53)
Again, this isn’t a particularly exciting find, but a functional one nonetheless. Tech1’s USB-C to USB-C charging cable is 3ft long. More impressively, it’s braided and doesn’t feel cheap.
The packaging advertises 5V/2.1Amps, making these cables more suited to slow overnight charging, instead of quick refills during the day.
XO Poppy MagSafe-compatible case and wallet ($5)
This one actually comes as a case plus MagSafe wallet combo, though for this experiment, I was only interested in the latter.
The case fits the iPhone 12 Pro Max and the iPhone 13 Pro Max. I couldn’t find a combo for other phones, so if you happen to own either of those models, great for you. If not, getting a MagSafe-compatible wallet for $5 is still a pretty sweet deal on its own.
The wallet can hold 3 cards comfortably. You can squeeze in a fourth, but that’s also where things start getting a little tight. More importantly, the wallet’s magnets are surprisingly strong. I gave my phone a vigorous shake with the wallet attached, and it did not detach.
Tech1 touchscreen stylus and ballpoint pen ($3)
The Tech1 stylus is the first real bust of the haul. It’s a pathetic excuse of a stylus that’s basically a ballpoint pen with a soft silicone tip slapped onto the other end. There’s no tech here — the silicone tip’s job is to mimic your finger, and it doesn’t do a great job at that.
It works just fine for regular tapping and scrolling, but that’s about it. It doesn’t track properly enough to be used for sketching or for handwritten notes. In my use, I found it easier to just use my finger for tasks that required even a little accuracy.
For $3, I can see the stylus being useful for people with limited hand mobility, but for all others, I’d recommend saving your money.
Nathan Vista handheld phone carrier ($4)
This goes for over $45 on most online stores, so it being available for just $4 at Dollarama is already a big win.
Runners need to carry their phone not just for navigation, tracking, and music, but also for communication in emergency scenarios, and this phone carrier makes that easier without hurting the wallet.
The strap feels gentle on the skin and is stretchy, allowing you to wrap it around your wrist, arm, and even bicep. The phone itself sits inside a transparent compartment that registers touch, which means you can continue using your phone through the carrier while running. The case is one-size-fits-all, and I was able to squeeze an iPhone 17 Pro Max in with ease, so most slab phones should fit just fine.
For just $4, this is an absolute steal for runners.
Budget desk setup
Tech1 wireless optical mouse ($4.78) and N Squared multicoloured desk pad ($4.50)
After the wireless GemstonePro earbuds, the Tech1 wireless mouse might just be the biggest standout of the haul.
Looks-wise, the mouse isn’t all that special. It has an ordinary look to it, but don’t let that fool you. The mouse sports a small footprint, and it’s extremely light too. It runs on a single AA battery, which does add to the mouse’s overall weight, but nothing substantial.
It communicates over a 2.4Ghz connection with a USB-A dongle that you plug into your device of choice. When not in use, the dongle can conveniently sit inside the mouse body, making the $4.78 gadget a solid addition to your portable setup.
The N Squared multicoloured desk pad, on the other hand, seems to have confused itself with a mousepad. A traditional mousepad only needs to accommodate your mouse, while a desk pad is supposed to cover a big portion of your desk, if not all of it.
At 14×14 inches, the $4.50 N Squared multicoloured desk pad is so small that it can’t really be called a desk pad. I don’t see the point of getting this, unless you’re looking to cover your bedside table with it.
And even if you do try to use it as a mousepad, the leather-like finish will ensure that there’s just enough friction that your mouse can’t glide across as intended. This was another miss for me.
Wonderfully unnecessary
Tech1 electronic hand gesture for cars ($5)
That subhead is exactly how I felt when I first saw the hand-gesture light at Dollarama. It’s literally a hand with Orange LEDs across it that alternate to display three different hand gestures: rock on/devil horns, an open palm, and the middle finger.
The sign is meant to go on the rear glass of your car, attached with the included sticky Velcro pads. The sign itself takes three AA batteries, while its remote takes one AAA cell.
Although not exactly my thing — I’d rather focus on the road than flipping other drivers off — the device works surprisingly well. The LEDs themselves are bright, and I was easily able to make out the gestures through my car’s tinted rear windshield — even during the day.
And if you’re like me and don’t want to gesture to other drivers on the road, no one’s stopping you from using it in your room instead. Think of it like that reversible octopus mood plushie, but with a remote control.
HomeDeco colour-changing moon light ($5)
I’m leaving this haul’s biggest dud for the end. I’m actually a big night light guy. I’m not scared of the dark, but I like having a faint light glowing somewhere in the room if and when I need to get up in the middle of the night.
The light requires three AA batteries, and even after popping in a fresh set, the light just didn’t turn on.
I found others online with working units, so I likely got a defective one. This happened with a few products in earlier editions, so I’m not all that surprised. That’s $5 lost on a moon that never shines.

articles.title: How often should you do maintenance on a Mac?
articles.text:
Every Mac user knows that the operating system runs very well, and it can give you impressive performance for quite some time. But this is a machine and eventually there can be some problems which arise. Hence the reason why it makes sense to perform some maintenance. Now the question is, how often do you need to perform that maintenance? Here’s what you need to consider.
Does Mac OS maintain itself?
Yes, it does a lot of things in the background, on its own. The idea here is that it automates many tasks like clearing out expired temporary files, rebuilding internal databases or rotating system logs. All of that is made automatically in the background, which makes it incredibly rewarding and exciting as well, something to take into account.
Another thing that Mac OS does is it performs SSD Optimization. It trims the device in order to keep any file fragments close to one another. Doing so improves the overall speed of the device, and it leads to a way better and more consistent experience. Silicon Macs also have better RAM management and a system called unified memory. That’s excellent, and it truly helps enhance the experience in better ways than you might expect.
Things to do on a weekly basis
- A good idea is to wipe down the screen, keyboard and trackpad. It’s very easy for these to get dirty, so cleaning everything up is a very good idea.
- Some people leave their Mac open, and that can lead to all kinds of problems. The best approach is to try and restart your Mac often, as it will help reset processes and just improve performance as a whole.
- Do a better triage on your desktop and downloads folder. Basically, the idea is to try and better optimize your desktop’s files and not leave unused stuff. Removing things is easier, and it can eliminate many of the possible issues that sometimes arise.
Monthly maintenance tasks
- Use a cleanup tool like CleanMyMac. That can help optimize your Mac, perform maintenance and ensure everything runs smoothly. It’s something that, thanks to the app, you can do automatically. In doing so, you streamline the process, and it can help convey a much better overall result. It’s excellent and totally worth considering, especially in this situation.
- Try to leave at least 15% of your drive capacity free. That’s used by the operating system to ensure everything runs smoothly. Otherwise, you can end up with problems, and it’s certainly one of those things you want to avoid.
- Empty the trash, if you didn’t do so for quite some time. It allows you to recoup a lot of space, and it’s well-worth the effort.
- While there, also try to do a checkup to see if there are any app or Mac OS updates you can install. The idea here is simple, you want to install updates, because they might help tackle vulnerabilities, security problems and other stuff of that nature. Keep that in mind, as it can help you quite a bit.
- Another thing you can do is to audit login items and background extensions. Those things start with your Mac every time you login, and they consume system resources. Only allow stuff that you need to start off with your Mac, as it can help quite a lot.
- It’s also a good idea to clean up ports and cooling vents once every 1-2 months as well. Clean hardware will help make the experience smoother, and that’s exactly what you need to pursue.
Other maintenance tasks
2 times a year, you can go into heavier maintenance. For example, you will need to uninstall unused applications properly, declutter the web browsers, verify your backup strategy and reclaim any system data space. It’s imperative to try and do that at least 1-2 times a year, because it helps you streamline the SSD storage and it will make things easier.
Annually, you can also assess the battery health and charging habits for your device, evaluate the internal dust, conduct a privacy and security checkup, and just ensure everything is running smoothly. It’s important to make sure that these maintenance tasks are performed often, so you don’t need to worry about anything here, and that’s what will help the most.
Conclusion
We recommend taking your time when it comes to performing maintenance on a Mac. And that’s the thing, the primary focus is on ensuring it all works correctly, and that it gives you the ROI that you are looking for. Ensuring that you optimize your approach and that you always perform some maintenance tasks will help you more than expected. It’s never the easiest thing to achieve, but if it’s done right, it can give you an exceptional value, so keep that in mind.

articles.title: Cuál temperatura debe tener el aire acondicionado en invierno
articles.text:
En países como España, la llegada del invierno no implica dejar de lado el aire acondicionado. Los electrodomésticos con bomba de calor permiten elevar la temperatura de las habitaciones durante los días fríos y pueden complementar otros sistemas de calefacción presentes en la vivienda.
La clave está en evitar ajustes extremos. La temperatura ideal del aire acondicionado en invierno se sitúa entre 20°C y 22°C, según Repsol, un rango que ayuda a compensar el frío exterior sin crear un ambiente excesivamente seco ni una diferencia térmica incómoda al salir o entrar del hogar.
Una diferencia moderada respecto de la temperatura de la calle evita que el ambiente sea sofocante. Al abrir una puerta o una ventana, el contraste entre el interior y el exterior puede aumentar la sensación de frío. Por eso, conviene sostener una regulación constante antes que encender y apagar el aparato de forma reiterada.
Cómo puede un aire acondicionado funcionar como calefacción
Muchos modelos cuentan con bomba de calor, una tecnología reversible que permite utilizar el mismo aparato en modo frío durante el verano y en modo calor en invierno. Esta función capta energía térmica del exterior y la traslada al interior para elevar la temperatura de las habitaciones.
Según Midea, este sistema puede generar hasta 4 kW de calor por cada 1 kW de energía eléctrica consumida, aunque el rendimiento concreto depende del modelo, el aislamiento de la vivienda y las condiciones meteorológicas.
Hacia dónde debe dirigirse el aire caliente del aire acondicionado
La orientación de las regillas de ventilación modifica la forma en que el calor se reparte por el ambiente. En invierno, la salida del aire debe apuntar hacia abajo, porque el aire caliente tiende a subir. De esta manera, el flujo puede alcanzar antes las zonas bajas de la habitación y distribuirse de manera más uniforme.
Si las rejillas quedan orientadas hacia el techo, el calor puede concentrarse en la parte alta y tardar más tiempo en llegar a las personas que están en la estancia. A la par, es útil despejar el espacio frente a la unidad interior para que muebles, cortinas u otros objetos no bloqueen la circulación del aire.
Qué temperatura debe tener el aire acondicionado en la jornada nocturna
El dormitorio suele requerir una configuración distinta de la sala o el comedor. Para dormir, Repsol sugiere programar el aire acondicionado aproximadamente una hora antes de acostarse y mantener la habitación entre 15’C y 17°C.
Esa temperatura busca evitar tanto el frío como el exceso de calor durante el descanso. Una habitación muy caliente puede ser incómoda, sobre todo si se utilizan mantas o ropa de cama de invierno.
Cómo reducir el consumo del aire acondicionado al usar el modo calor
El uso eficiente comienza por cerrar puertas y ventanas mientras el aparato está encendido. Las filtraciones de aire y un aislamiento insuficiente obligan al sistema a trabajar durante más tiempo para mantener el nivel programado. Revisar burletes, persianas y cortinas puede ayudar a conservar el calor acumulado en el interior.
Asimismo, es clave elegir la función de programación o temporizador cuando el electrodoméstico la incluya. Mantener una temperatura estable y moderada suele requerir menos energía que alternar períodos de apagado con ajustes muy elevados.
El ventilador en modo automático puede colaborar con esa regulación, al adaptar la intensidad del flujo a las necesidades de la estancia.
Qué mantenimiento necesita el aire acondicionado
La limpieza de los filtros forma parte de las tareas básicas para conservar el funcionamiento del aire acondicionado. El polvo acumulado dificulta el paso del aire, disminuir el rendimiento y afectar la calidad del ambiente interior.
Midea señala que, frente a una caldera tradicional, este tipo de sistema suele requerir menos revisiones periódicas. La ventaja adicional es que el aparato no genera humos, gases ni cenizas dentro de la vivienda, porque no funciona a través de combustión.
Aun así, una revisión técnica cuando el electrodoméstico presenta ruidos inusuales, pérdida de potencia o fallas en el modo calor permite detectar problemas antes de que afecten su capacidad para climatizar el hogar.

articles.title: Votre IA du quotidien a un coût humain : sa pollution a fait 650 morts en un an, souvent loin des data centers
articles.text:
Votre IA du quotidien a un coût humain : sa pollution a fait 650 morts en un an, souvent loin des data centers
Une question à ChatGPT, une vidéo en streaming, une photo envoyée dans le cloud : chacun de ces gestes fait tourner des data centers, et leur électricité a un prix. Aux États-Unis, une étude du MIT attribue environ 650 morts prématurées en 2023 à la pollution des centrales qui les alimentent. Les régions les plus touchées se trouvent souvent loin de la Virginie et du Texas, qui consomment pourtant l'essentiel de ce courant.
Des chercheurs du MIT, de l'université de Californie à Irvine et de Yale ont publié le 19 novembre dans Environmental Research Letters une estimation inédite. En 2023, la pollution de l'air due à l'électricité produite pour les centres de données américains aurait causé environ 650 décès prématurés : 513 attribués aux particules fines, 137 à l'ozone. C'est près de 5,3 % de la mortalité imputable à toute la production électrique du pays.
Quand on parle des nuisances des data centers, on pense d'abord aux riverains, comme ceux qui ont porté plainte contre le vacarme du centre de données d'Elon Musk. Noelle Selin, professeure au MIT qui a supervisé l'étude, invite à regarder plus loin : "Même si vous pensez ne pas être concerné parce qu'aucun data center ne se trouve près de chez vous, détrompez-vous."
L'échelle donne le vertige. Les data centers ont consommé 176 TWh en 2023, soit 4,4 % de l'électricité américaine, selon le Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. Le laboratoire prévoit qu'ils en absorberont entre 6,7 et 12 % d'ici 2028.
Une pollution qui ignore les frontières des États
Le nord de la Virginie et le Texas concentrent l'essentiel de la demande. Leurs taux de mortalité sont pourtant environ deux fois plus faibles que ceux de la plupart des États du Midwest. Les taux par habitant les plus élevés touchent l'Iowa, le Nevada, le Dakota du Sud et le Kansas. Le Nebraska, le Missouri et l'Arkansas, qui accueillent peu de data centers, paient eux aussi un lourd tribut.
Plusieurs mécanismes se combinent. Le réseau est interconnecté : un serveur en Virginie tire souvent son courant de vieilles centrales au charbon et au gaz de la vallée de l'Ohio. "Si vous raccordez un data center au réseau, vous devrez peut-être allumer votre centrale vraiment sale pour répondre à cette nouvelle demande", résume Noelle Selin. Les vents portent ensuite les polluants vers les États voisins. Dans les plaines agricoles du Midwest, où le charbon répond souvent à la demande supplémentaire, l'ammoniac des engrais se combine aux rejets des centrales et multiplie les particules fines.
Albert Chen, doctorant au MIT et coauteur, souligne que les zones rurales sont nettement plus exposées que les villes.
Plus de 10 000 générateurs suivis heure par heure
L'équipe a simulé heure par heure la production de plus de 10 000 générateurs américains, avec puis sans la demande des data centers, en supposant que ceux-ci tournent en continu. Un modèle de chimie atmosphérique a ensuite suivi la formation et le trajet des polluants. Résultat : entre 0,02 et 0,08 µg/m³ de particules fines en plus en moyenne annuelle, avec des pics locaux proches de 0,2. C'est peu, mais à l'échelle de tout un pays, cela suffit à peser sur la mortalité.
Pour Albert Chen, choisir où implanter un site demande de regarder "plus que le prix du foncier et de l'énergie". Les chercheurs vont maintenant étudier la production d'électricité sur site, que certains acteurs poussent très loin, à l'image des moteurs de Boeing 747 qu'Elon Musk a fait modifier pour alimenter son centre de données.
	
Même si vous pensez ne pas être concerné parce qu'aucun data center ne se trouve près de chez vous, détrompez-vous.
En France, où l'électricité vient surtout du nucléaire et de l'hydraulique, la question se pose autrement. Pourtant, l'Arcep chiffrait déjà la facture : 2,7 TWh d'électricité et 575 000 m³ d'eau potable engloutis en 2024 par 160 data centers français. Et l'Europe connaît la soif de ses centres de données sans en publier les chiffres.
L'étude du MIT rappelle que l'empreinte d'un serveur se mesure sur toute la chaîne qui l'alimente, bien au-delà de ce que voudrait afficher un Nutri-Score de l'IA.

articles.title: En los pantanos de Florida hay conejos de peluche con paneles solares montando guardia: su presa son serpientes invasoras
articles.text:
En los Everglades de Florida hay cocodrilos, serpientes y también conejos de peluche dentro de pequeñas jaulas. Aunque la escena suene bastante absurda, en realidad tiene todo el sentido porque forma parte de un experimento llevado a cabo por la South Florida Water Management District. Su objetivo es atraer a las serpientes invasoras que infestan los Everglades para que puedan ser capturadas y retiradas de la zona.
La tecnología entra en juego. En 2025, investigadores de la Universidad de Florida y el organismo de gestión del agua de la región probaron estos señuelos mecánicos para atraer a las serpientes invasoras, concretamente la pitón birmana. Un ejemplar adulto puede medir hasta 6 metros de longitud, pero más que por su tamaño, el problema para capturarlas es que se camuflan demasiado bien y encontrarlas a simple vista es una tarea casi imposible. Aquí es donde entran en juego los conejitos robóticos que hacen que sea la serpiente la que salga de su escondite.
El esfuerzo de las autoridades da una idea de la dimensión del problema. Según la Comisión de Conservación de Pesca y Vida Silvestre de Florida, desde 2017 los equipos contratados por el estado y el organismo gestor del agua han retirado más de 19.000 pitones.
Un caballo de Troya térmico. Para diseñar la trampa, los científicos usaron conejos de peluche y los equiparon con motores, resistencias y otros componentes, todo alimentado con energía solar. El objetivo es intentar reproducir las señales que una pitón asociaría con una presa viva: el aspecto de un conejo de los pantanos, su temperatura corporal, el movimiento y también el olor, porque sí, los conejitos robóticos también tienen un emisor de fragancia. Cuando una serpiente se acerca, las cámaras que rodean la jaula la detectan y un agente especializado es enviado para capturarla y retirarla de la zona.
Usar conejos vivos no salía a cuenta. Antes de llegar a esta solución probaron con conejos vivos protegidos en jaulas. La trampa funcionaba y atraía a los reptiles, pero requería una atención diaria y resultaba inviable para cubrir miles de hectáreas. Con los señuelos robóticos consiguen el mismo efecto, sin tener que dedicar tiempo a vigilarlos, alimentarlos y atenderlos a diario
Cómo llegaron ahí. Durante décadas, EEUU importó estas serpientes para venderlas como mascotas. Se cree que muchas de ellas fueron abandonadas en la zona a principios de los años 80 porque habían crecido demasiado y resultaban difíciles de mantener. El clima cálido y húmedo del sur de Florida, unido a la presencia de abundantes presas y pocos depredadores naturales permitió que la población de pitón birmana aumentara. Las autoridades estiman que las pitones han acabado con el 95% de los pequeños mamíferos y han alterado la cadena trófica de los Everglades.

articles.title: Tous les fabricants de smartphones revoient leurs ambitions à la baisse pour 2027, sauf un
articles.text:
Autant dire que la crise mondiale de la mémoire frappe durement les constructeurs de smartphones. Les principaux modèles touchés sont ceux d’entrée de gamme et de moyen de gamme, les fabricants n’étant plus capables d’absorber l’explosion des prix des composants sur ces appareils. Ceux haut de gamme étaient en revanche plus épargnés, en raison de leur prix plus élevé. Du moins, jusqu’à maintenant. La crise semble désormais toucher quasiment tous les acteurs du secteur et toutes les gammes. C’est simple, quasiment tous les constructeurs de smartphones auraient revus leurs objectifs de livraison à la baisse pour 2027.
Des objectifs de livraison revus à la baisse pour 2027
Selon les informations exclusives du média chinois Jiemian News, quasiment tous les fabricants de smartphones auraient revu à la baisse leurs objectifs de livraison pour 2027. Apple et Samsung font partie des constructeurs les moins touchés par la crise de la RAM. Pourtant, Apple aurait prévu de produire environ 220 millions d’unités en 2027, soit une baisse de 5,6 % par rapport à l’année précédente. De son côté, Samsung aurait prévu de produire 210 millions d’unités en 2027, soit une diminution de 9,5 % par rapport à l’année précédente.
D’autres constructeurs prévoiraient de réduire encore plus drastiquement leurs livraisons, à l’image de Xiaomi (- 25 %), Oppo (- 14 %), Huawei (- 16 %) ou encore Vivo (- 29 %). Seul un fabricant n’aurait pas prévu une réduction de ses livraisons pour 2027, à savoir Honor. Le constructeur chinois prévoirait de mettre sur le marché 50 millions d’unités en 2027, soit autant qu’en 2026. Ceci s’explique par ses bons résultats financiers ces derniers mois.
Les fabricants de smartphones n’ont pas fini de souffrir
Même en revoyant leurs objectifs de livraison à la baisse pour 2027, les fabricants de smartphones parviendront-ils à faire face à la crise ? Pour l’instant, rien n’est moins sûr. Les principaux acteurs du marché pourraient continuer à augmenter les prix de leurs appareils, tout en effectuant des compromis, avec par exemple des caractéristiques techniques revues à la baisse. Ces limitations ne se limiteraient d’ailleurs pas aux fiches techniques des smartphones, étant donné que même les applications sont dorénavant bridées afin de limiter la consommation de mémoire.
Par ailleurs, une baisse des prix de la mémoire ne serait pas attendue avant 2030. Les fabricants de smartphones vont probablement devoir faire face à cette crise durant encore plusieurs années. Une crise qui déborde d’ailleurs sur les PC et l’industrie automobile. Un conseil : si vous avez besoin d’un nouveau téléphone, n’attendez pas trop longtemps.

articles.title: Paula, 23 años: "He durado un día en el trabajo. Tanto tiempo buscando, por fin consigo empleo y al final no me gusta"
articles.text:
Paula tiene 23 años y llevaba bastante tiempo buscando trabajo hasta que, por fin, consiguió que la contrataran. El problema llegó cuando empezó a conocer el puesto y se dio cuenta de que no era lo que esperaba. Solo necesitó un día para decidir que no quería volver, una experiencia que ha compartido en su cuenta de TikTok (@paula.lap) y que comenzó aclarando algo: "Hermanas, he durado un día en el trabajo. He durado un día en el trabajo por voluntad propia. A mí nadie me ha echado de ningún lado".
La joven reconoce que le resultó complicado tomar esa decisión después de todo lo que le había costado encontrar empleo. "Os prometo que sentí una mezcla de emociones", explica, porque llevaba tiempo esperando aquella oportunidad y, cuando finalmente llegó, no le gustó. Mientras le explicaban las tareas que tendría que realizar, Paula ya estaba pensando en marcharse.
Un horario de lunes a sábado que terminó de convencerla
Una de las cosas que menos le gustaron fueron las condiciones del horario: 40 horas semanales repartidas de lunes a sábado. Paula empezó a preguntarse si realmente merecía la pena quedarse en un lugar donde no se encontraba a gusto, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que acababa de empezar y todavía podía buscar otras oportunidades.
Y es que, aunque reconoce que tiene poca experiencia laboral, tampoco ve necesario aguantar en un puesto que no le convence. "Tengo 23 años, de trabajo bien poquito todavía", comenta antes de plantearse si es mejor quedarse pasándolo mal o empezar otra vez de cero. Su respuesta es clara: prefiere volver a buscar empleo las veces que haga falta.
La situación llegó a afectarle hasta el punto de levantarse llorando al día siguiente solo de pensar que tenía que regresar al trabajo. Finalmente decidió no continuar y retomar la búsqueda de otro puesto, pese a que encontrar el anterior le había llevado bastante tiempo.

articles.title: Vardhaman Jain: Who is the industrialist behind Tirumala’s gold donation?
articles.text:
Vardhaman Jain: Who is the industrialist behind Tirumala’s gold donation?
Vardhaman Jain, a Chennai-based entrepreneur linked to Access Healthcare and Asia Engineering, has donated 121 kg of gold ornaments worth Rs 206 crore to Tirumala.
A donation of 121 kg of gold is difficult to overlook. But behind the Rs 206 crore offering made to Venkateswara at Tirumala is a businessman whose career has largely unfolded in healthcare services and Asia engineering and technology.
Chennai-based industrialist and philanthropist Vardhaman Jain, along with his wife Radhika Jain, made the offering on Thursday, November 26, 2026. The donation comprises 46 gold ornaments and is among the largest contributions received by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD).
The ornaments were presented in the presence of Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and senior TTD officials. They were first displayed at Ranganayakula Mandapam before being ceremonially taken to the sanctum sanctorum.
From building healthcare services businesses to taking up leadership roles in large technology companies, Vardhaman Jain's professional journey has covered several areas. Here's a look at the entrepreneur behind the offering.
From Vision HealthSource to Access Healthcare
Before Access Healthcare became a part of his business journey, Vardhaman had already worked in the healthcare services industry. He co-founded Vision HealthSource, a healthcare services company that was acquired by Perot Systems in 2003.
Following the acquisition, he held senior positions at Perot Systems and Dell Services. His responsibilities included managing director of Dell Services' BPO operations, giving him experience in managing large-scale business process services.
In 2011, he went on to establish Access Healthcare with Shaji Ravi and others. The company provides technology-enabled revenue cycle management services to healthcare providers, primarily in the US. Its offerings cover medical billing, coding, accounts receivable management, analytics and automation-led services. The company has also had Anurag Jain as its chairman and CEO, while Shaji Ravi has served as founder, president and managing director.
Healthcare services are not the only area in which Vardhaman has worked. His professional interests also include business process automation and technology development. Public company profiles credit him with patents related to medical image processing and the use of data extracted from electronic images.
Vardhaman studied statistics at Loyola College in Chennai before pursuing computer science at the University of Texas at Austin.
A career that extends beyond business
Alongside his business interests, Vardhaman has been associated with initiatives in healthcare, education and skill development.
His philanthropic work includes the Shree Sarita Jain Foundation Trust and Aavishkaar, a skill-development initiative for underprivileged youth. He is also listed as the managing trustee of Kanchi Kamakoti CHILDS Trust Hospital.
His association with Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams is not limited to the latest offering. Earlier contributions include electric buses for pilgrim transport and financial support for the Sri Venkateswara Bhakti Channel, besides other temple-related initiatives.
What went into the 121-kg offering?
According to TTD, the couple's donation used 121 kg of 24-carat gold to prepare ornaments for two temples. Of this, 106 kg was used for jewellery intended for Venkateswara at Tirumala, while the remaining 15 kg will go towards a vastram for Sri Padmavathi Ammavari at the Tiruchanoor temple.
The collection includes a crown, necklaces, anklets, armlets, waist ornaments, hand ornaments and pada kavachams, along with covers for the conch and chakra. Diamonds, blue and yellow sapphires, rubies, emeralds and saligrama stones also feature in the ornaments.
The Rs 206 crore offering has brought Vardhaman's philanthropic contributions into the spotlight. Yet, his work across healthcare, technology, education and temple initiatives shows that his interests extend well beyond a single business or industry.

articles.title: « À garder strictement au sein de SAP » : un message interne trahit une cyberattaque contre le géant allemand du logiciel
articles.text:
Quelle est l’ampleur exacte de cette affaire ?
Le 26 novembre 2026, l’hebdomadaire Der Spiegel révélait que SAP, le géant des logiciels de gestion, faisait face à une cyberattaque. Selon le magazine, l’incident avait causé une vive agitation en interne ces derniers jours.
Interrogé par le média puis, le lendemain, par Reuters, SAP a reconnu avoir « identifié une activité suspecte » sans répondre dans le détail.
L’entreprise, dont les logiciels permettent à de grandes organisations de gérer leur comptabilité, leurs ressources humaines ou leurs achats, a avant tout cherché à rassurer, précisant avoir immédiatement pris les mesures nécessaires pour protéger ses clients et garantir la sécurité de ses services. « D’après notre enquête à ce jour, nous n’avons trouvé aucune preuve d’un accès non autorisé aux données métier de nos clients », a précisé l’éditeur à Reuters.
Le code source de SAP dans le viseur des pirates ?
Selon l’article du Spiegel, l’affaire avait en interne un nom de code, « Project Granite ». L’information vient d’un message adressé aux salariés, que s’est procuré le magazine. Le document ne détaille pas en quoi consistaient les « activités suspectes » repérées. Il demande en revanche aux équipes de ne pas en parler, en précisant que toute information sur ce projet est interne et « à garder strictement au sein de SAP ».
Le message affirmait par ailleurs que rien n’indiquait à ce stade que des données clients étaient touchées, et SAP en concluait qu’il n’était « pas nécessaire » de prévenir ses clients.
Des sources internes ont donné plus de détails au média allemand. Selon elles, les attaquants auraient ciblé les espaces de SAP sur GitHub, la plateforme où l’entreprise publie le code de nombreux produits et projets open source.
D’après une personne au fait du dossier, les pirates auraient volé des jetons d’authentification d’employés, qui leur auraient servi à modifier et à copier du code source de SAP. Toujours selon ces sources, ils se seraient peut-être aidés d’agents IA.
Pour l’heure, SAP n’a confirmé ni le vol de jetons, ni la modification du code, ni le recours à l’IA. Depuis, l’entreprise a tout de même restreint l’accès à GitHub, suspendu ses processus de développement automatisés et remplacé ses clés de signature, selon le quotidien économique Handelsblatt, qui cite une nouvelle fois des sources internes.
