articles.title: Black Friday : 17 PC portables à prix CASSÉS chez Amazon, du Dell 15 au MacBook Air M5
articles.text:
Le Black Friday, c'est demain, et Amazon a déjà baissé le prix de nombreux PC portables, de l'ordinateur de cours au PC gamer. Nous en avons retenu 17, en commençant par le MacBook Air M5 et le Dell XPS 13 testés par notre rédaction, puis le Dell 15 que nos lecteurs ont le plus acheté ce mois-ci.
À la veille du Black Friday, nous ouvrons avec les deux PC portables testés par notre rédaction, le MacBook Air M5 et le Dell XPS 13, puis le Dell 15 que nos lecteurs ont le plus acheté ce mois-ci, avant les quatorze autres, du moins cher au plus cher, que nous n'avons pas testés.
La sélection va de l'ordinateur de cours à 449 € au PC gamer en RTX 5070, avec des remises de 12 % à 47 % sur les prix de référence affichés par Amazon au relevé du 26 novembre. Les plus fortes économies en euros, 470 €, reviennent au Dell 15 Core i5 16 Go et au Dell 15 Core i7, et la plus forte en pourcentage, 47 %, aux deux Dell 15 Core i5.
- Apple MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 (16 Go, 512 Go) à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 399 € (-14 %)
- Dell XPS 13 à 1 349 € au lieu de 1 799 € (-25 %)
- Dell 15 (Core i5-1334U, 16 Go, 512 Go) à 529 € au lieu de 999 € (-47 %)
- Dell 15 (Core i5-1334U, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 449 € au lieu de 849 € (-47 %)
- HP OmniBook 3 17,3 pouces (Ryzen 5 130, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 449 € au lieu de 549,99 € (-18 %)
- ASUS Vivobook S14 (Snapdragon X, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 449,99 € au lieu de 699,99 € (-36 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 (Ryzen 5, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 449,99 € au lieu de 599,99 € (-25 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces (Core 3, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 479,99 € au lieu de 549,99 € (-13 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 (Ryzen 5, 16 Go, 512 Go) à 569 € au lieu de 649,99 € (-12 %)
- Samsung Galaxy Book6 (Core 5, 8 Go) à 599 € au lieu de 899 € (-33 %)
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces OLED (Core 5 320, 8 Go, 512 Go) à 629,99 € au lieu de 899,99 € (-30 %)
- Dell 15 (Core i7-1355U, 16 Go, 1 To) à 829 € au lieu de 1 299 € (-36 %)
- Samsung Galaxy Book6 (Core Ultra 5, 16 Go) à 899 € au lieu de 1 299 € (-31 %)
- Lenovo Yoga Slim 7 OLED 14 pouces (Ryzen 7 AI 345, 16 Go, 512 Go) à 899,99 € au lieu de 1 049,99 € (-14 %)
- Acer Nitro V 15 (Ryzen 7 170, RTX 5050, 16 Go, 512 Go) à 999 € au lieu de 1 399 € (-29 %)
- MSI Cyborg 15 (Core 7 240H, RTX 5060, 16 Go, 512 Go) à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 499 € (-20 %)
- ASUS TUF Gaming F16 (Core i7-14650HX, RTX 5070) à 1 499,99 € au lieu de 1 799,99 € (-17 %)
MacBook Air M5 : l'ultraportable d'Apple noté 8/10, à 1 199 € pour le Black Friday
Notre test du MacBook Air M5 lui attribue 8/10. Sans ventilateur, il travaille en silence, son SSD lit et écrit deux fois plus vite qu'il y a un an et nous avons mesuré environ 12 heures d'autonomie. Nous avions testé la version 1 To ; celle-ci a 16 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de stockage.
✅ Points forts
- Silence total : aucun ventilateur, et des performances solides au quotidien selon notre test.
- Stockage rapide : des vitesses de lecture et d'écriture doublées en un an, d'après nos mesures.
- À savoir : 1 199 € était déjà son prix affiché lors de notre test, et l'écran reste limité à 60 Hz.
Dell XPS 13 : 450 € de moins sur l'ultraportable de 1 kg noté 7/10, à 1 349 €
Notre test du Dell XPS 13 (2026) lui donne 7/10 pour son châssis en aluminium usiné, son écran tactile mat de 13,4 pouces et ses 8 à 10 heures d'autonomie. Nous l'avions en main en Core 5 320 avec 16 Go ; cette version, annoncée par Amazon en Core Ultra 7 355 avec 1 To de SSD, n'est pas celle que nous avons testée.
✅ Points forts
- Très compact : 1 kg et 12,7 mm d'épaisseur sur notre modèle de test.
- Écran 2,5K de 30 à 120 Hz : avec un traitement antireflet très efficace, selon notre test.
- À savoir : seulement deux ports USB-C, pas de prise casque, et le chargeur est vendu à part.
Dell 15 Core i5 16 Go : le PC portable préféré de nos lecteurs, à 529 €
C'est le PC portable le plus acheté via Clubic ce mois-ci : un 15,6 pouces Full HD à 120 Hz, dalle IPS antireflet, avec un Intel Core i5-1334U, 16 Go de DDR5 et un SSD NVMe de 512 Go. Son clavier est en AZERTY et il prend en charge le Wi-Fi 6, selon Amazon. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 16 Go de mémoire : de la marge pour le multitâche, là où Windows 11 occupe déjà 5 à 6 Go d'une machine à 8 Go selon notre test du Dell XPS 13.
- Connectique complète : USB-C Power Delivery, USB-A, HDMI et lecteur microSD.
- À savoir : il coûte 80 € de plus que la version 8 Go de cette sélection, pour le double de mémoire.
Dell 15 Core i5 8 Go : la même base à 449 €, avec 2 ans d'intervention à domicile
Même processeur Core i5-1334U et même écran 15,6 pouces Full HD à 120 Hz que la version 16 Go, mais avec 8 Go de mémoire. Dell y inclut 2 ans de service sur site après un diagnostic à distance, selon la fiche Amazon. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Le prix le plus bas de la sélection : 449 €, à égalité avec le HP OmniBook 3.
- Service à domicile : Dell se déplace pendant 2 ans, chez vous ou au bureau.
- À savoir : la fiche Amazon se contredit sur le clavier, AZERTY dans les caractéristiques et QWERTY dans le résumé, et le chargeur est vendu séparément.
HP OmniBook 3 : un grand 17,3 pouces passé sous les 450 €, à 449 €
Ce 17,3 pouces à dalle HD+ antireflet réunit un AMD Ryzen 5 130 à six cœurs, 8 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de SSD, dans un châssis de 16,4 mm. Son prix a encore baissé : il était affiché à 474 € le 25 novembre. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Grand écran : 17,3 pouces pour les films et le travail sur deux fenêtres.
- Connectique généreuse : deux USB-C, deux USB-A, HDMI 2.1 et une webcam 1080p.
- À savoir : la définition est HD+ et non Full HD, et le chargeur n'est pas fourni.
ASUS Vivobook S14 : 250 € de remise sur ce 14 pouces à Snapdragon X, à 449,99 €
Ce 14 pouces 16:10 de 1 920 x 1 200 pixels repose sur une puce Snapdragon X à huit cœurs, avec 8 Go de LPDDR5X et 256 Go de SSD, et ASUS le dit conforme à la norme militaire américaine MIL-STD 810H. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Robustesse annoncée : norme MIL-STD 810H, selon ASUS.
- Plus de hauteur d'écran : le format 16:10 affiche davantage de lignes qu'un Full HD classique.
- À savoir : la puce ARM oblige à vérifier la compatibilité de vos logiciels, et le SSD s'arrête à 256 Go.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 Ryzen 5 : 512 Go de SSD pour moins de 450 €, à 449,99 €
Ce 15,6 pouces Full HD mat associe un AMD Ryzen 5, 8 Go de LPDDR5 et un SSD de 512 Go, avec un clavier AZERTY. C'est une base simple pour les cours et la bureautique. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Stockage confortable : 512 Go de SSD à ce prix.
- Dalle mate : moins de reflets près d'une fenêtre.
- À savoir : l'écran est une dalle TN de 250 nits, et le chargeur n'est pas fourni.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces : un clavier rétroéclairé pour moins de 500 €, à 479,99 €
Ce 14 pouces WUXGA (1 920 x 1 200) associe un Intel Core 3, 8 Go de mémoire et 256 Go de SSD, avec un clavier AZERTY rétroéclairé, selon Amazon. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Clavier rétroéclairé : pratique pour taper le soir.
- Format 14 pouces 16:10 : plus facile à glisser dans un sac qu'un 15,6 pouces.
- À savoir : 256 Go de SSD seulement, et pas de chargeur dans la boîte (Lenovo conseille un modèle de 65 W).
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 16 Go : deux fois plus de mémoire, à 569 €
Ce 15,6 pouces Full HD reprend la base Ryzen 5 de série 40 avec 16 Go de mémoire, 512 Go de SSD et une puce graphique Radeon 610M. Son clavier AZERTY n'est pas rétroéclairé. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 16 Go de mémoire : le double de la version à 449,99 € de cette sélection.
- 512 Go de SSD : de la place pour les documents et les photos.
- À savoir : c'est la remise la plus faible de la sélection, -12 % sur un ancien prix de 649,99 €.
Samsung Galaxy Book6 : 300 € de moins sur ce 14 pouces avec Galaxy AI, à 599 €
Ce 14 pouces 16:10 antireflet de 350 nits associe un Intel Core 5 série 3, 8 Go de mémoire et 256 Go de stockage, avec un lecteur d'empreinte digitale et les fonctions Galaxy AI. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Lisible en pleine lumière : dalle de 350 nits avec traitement antireflet.
- Déverrouillage rapide : lecteur d'empreinte digitale intégré.
- À savoir : 8 Go de mémoire, c'est juste pour un usage intensif ; la version 16 Go est aussi dans cette sélection, à 899 €.
Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces OLED : Core 5 320 et 30 % de remise, à 629,99 €
Ce 14 pouces de 1 920 x 1 200 pixels associe un Intel Core 5 320, 8 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de SSD, avec un clavier AZERTY rétroéclairé. Notre test du Dell XPS 13, qui utilisait la même puce, la destine à la bureautique, au web et au multimédia léger. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Deux fois plus de stockage : 512 Go contre 256 Go pour le 14 pouces à 479,99 €.
- Clavier rétroéclairé : en AZERTY, pour travailler le soir.
- À savoir : la remise se calcule sur le prix barré de 899,99 € affiché par Amazon, et le chargeur n'est pas fourni.
Dell 15 Core i7 : 1 To de SSD et 470 € de remise, à 829 €
Ce 15,6 pouces Full HD monte en gamme avec un Intel Core i7-1355U, 16 Go de DDR5 et 1 To de SSD, un clavier rétroéclairé et un lecteur d'empreinte digitale, pour 1,94 kg. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- 1 To de stockage : de quoi garder photos et vidéos en local.
- Confort au quotidien : clavier rétroéclairé et lecteur d'empreinte digitale.
- À savoir : pas de carte graphique dédiée, et 1,94 kg sur la balance.
Samsung Galaxy Book6 Copilot+ : Core Ultra 5 et 16 Go, 400 € de moins, à 899 €
Cette version Copilot+ du Galaxy Book6 passe à un Intel Core Ultra 5, 16 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de SSD, sur un écran 14 pouces 16:10 de 350 nits. Samsung annonce jusqu'à 24 heures d'autonomie en lecture vidéo. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Fonctions IA : label Copilot+ et outils Galaxy AI, comme le détourage instantané des arrière-plans.
- Plus à l'aise : 16 Go et 512 Go, le double du modèle à 599 €.
- À savoir : les 24 heures d'autonomie sont un chiffre de Samsung en lecture vidéo, pas une mesure de Clubic.
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7 OLED : l'écran OLED et le Ryzen 7 AI pour 899,99 €
Ce 14 pouces OLED de 1 920 x 1 200 pixels pèse 1,19 kg et embarque un AMD Ryzen 7 AI 345, 16 Go de DDR5 et 512 Go de SSD, avec une batterie de 70 Wh. Sa webcam Full HD a un obturateur physique. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Léger : 1,19 kg pour une batterie de 70 Wh, selon la fiche Amazon.
- Webcam avec obturateur : pour couper la caméra d'un geste.
- À savoir : le chargeur n'est pas inclus (Lenovo conseille un modèle GaN de 65 W), et la remise de 14 % reste modeste.
Acer Nitro V 15 : un PC gamer RTX 5050 sous les 1 000 €, à 999 €
Ce 15,6 pouces Full HD à 165 Hz associe un AMD Ryzen 7 170, une GeForce RTX 5050, 16 Go de DDR5 et 512 Go de SSD NVMe, avec un double ventilateur piloté par l'application NitroSense. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Ray tracing : pris en charge par la RTX 5050, selon Amazon.
- Écran 165 Hz : le plus rapide des PC gamers de cette sélection.
- À savoir : 512 Go de SSD, c'est vite rempli avec quelques jeux récents.
MSI Cyborg 15 : la RTX 5060 à 1 199 €, 300 € sous son prix conseillé
Ce 15,6 pouces Full HD IPS à 144 Hz associe un Intel Core 7 240H à dix cœurs, une GeForce RTX 5060 de 8 Go, 16 Go de DDR5-5600 et 512 Go de SSD NVMe PCIe Gen4. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- RTX 5060 de 8 Go : un cran au-dessus de la RTX 5050 du Nitro V 15.
- Clavier de joueur : rétroéclairage RGB sur 4 zones et pavé numérique.
- À savoir : 1,95 kg, et un SSD de 512 Go à étendre vite.
ASUS TUF Gaming F16 RTX 5070 : le PC gamer le plus puissant de la sélection, à 1 499,99 €
Ce 16 pouces FHD+ à 144 Hz associe un Intel Core i7-14650HX à 16 cœurs, une GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop de 8 Go en GDDR7, 16 Go de DDR5 et 512 Go de SSD NVMe. Il perd 300 € sur son prix conseillé de 1 799,99 €. Nous ne l'avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- RTX 5070 : la carte graphique la plus haut de gamme de cette sélection.
- Évolutif : deux emplacements M.2 pour ajouter un SSD, G-Sync et webcam Windows Hello.
- À savoir : 2,20 kg, et 512 Go de stockage d'origine.
Black Friday 2026 : demain, le 27 novembre, et jusqu'au Cyber Monday
Le Black Friday 2026 tombe demain, vendredi 27 novembre, et le Cyber Monday le lundi 30. Au relevé du 26 novembre, 12 des 17 PC portables de cette sélection portaient déjà le badge « Top Offre Black Friday » chez Amazon, et le HP OmniBook 3 a encore perdu 25 € depuis la veille. Les prix peuvent changer d'ici vendredi, dans un sens comme dans l'autre : vérifiez-les avant de commander, et suivez notre direct Black Friday 2026 et notre page Black Friday.
Black Friday : quel PC portable acheter selon votre budget ?
Sous 500 €, visez au moins 512 Go de SSD et, si possible, 16 Go de mémoire : c'est ce qui sépare le Dell 15 à 529 € des modèles 8 Go. Entre 600 et 900 €, le poids et l'écran font la différence, du Galaxy Book6 au Yoga Slim 7 OLED. Pour jouer, la carte graphique décide de tout : RTX 5050 sur le Nitro V 15, RTX 5060 sur le MSI Cyborg 15, RTX 5070 sur le TUF Gaming F16. Vérifiez aussi si un chargeur est fourni : plusieurs fiches Amazon de cette sélection l'annoncent vendu à part.

articles.title: How PCB Design Affects Battery Life in Smart Home Devices
articles.text:
Smart home devices are becoming part of everyday life. From wireless door sensors and smart locks to temperature monitors and security systems, many connected devices promise months or even years of operation without needing a battery replacement.
Yet battery life can vary significantly between products that appear to perform similar functions.
While battery capacity is an obvious factor, the electronics inside a device play an equally important role. Power management, wireless communication, component selection, and printed circuit board (PCB) design all influence how efficiently a smart device uses energy.
Understanding these factors helps explain why some devices last longer than others.
1. The Hidden Power Consumption Inside Smart Devices
A smart home sensor may appear inactive for most of the day, but its internal electronics are rarely completely switched off.
Even when the device is not actively collecting or transmitting data, certain components may continue drawing small amounts of current.
Typical power consumers include:
- Microcontrollers responsible for processing sensor information
- Wireless communication chips
- Voltage regulators and power management circuits
- Sensors and monitoring components
- Status indicators and supporting circuitry
The total energy consumption depends on both how much current these components draw and how long they remain active.
For battery-powered devices, reducing unnecessary power consumption is often just as important as selecting a larger battery.
2. Why Standby Power Matters More Than You Think
Many smart home devices spend most of their operating life in standby or sleep mode.
A wireless door sensor, for example, may wake only when a door opens, while a temperature sensor might take measurements periodically.
This makes standby current particularly important.
Consider a simplified example using a 1,000 mAh battery.
If a device consumes an average current of 0.1 mA, its theoretical operating time is approximately 10,000 hours. Increasing average consumption to 0.2 mA reduces that theoretical figure to 5,000 hours.
These calculations illustrate the importance of small current differences. Actual battery life will be lower or otherwise affected by temperature, battery chemistry, usable capacity, ageing, and operating conditions.
Low-power electronic design therefore focuses on minimizing unnecessary current during the long periods between active operations.
Selecting voltage regulators with low quiescent current, disabling unused peripherals, and managing sensor power can make a meaningful difference.
3. Wireless Connectivity Can Affect Battery Efficiency
Wireless communication is another important factor in smart home battery performance.
Common technologies include Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Zigbee, Thread, and Wi-Fi. Each provides different capabilities, communication characteristics, and power requirements.
However, choosing a low-power wireless technology does not automatically guarantee long battery life.
Energy consumption also depends on how frequently the device communicates, the amount of data transmitted, signal strength, and whether messages must be retransmitted.
For example, a wireless sensor operating with poor signal quality may require additional transmission attempts to deliver information successfully.
PCB antenna placement, nearby metal components, and enclosure materials can influence wireless performance.
A properly designed antenna region, appropriate grounding, and sufficient clearance from interfering components can help maintain reliable wireless connectivity.
By reducing avoidable communication problems, good hardware design can also help limit unnecessary energy consumption.
4. How PCB Design Influences Battery Efficiency
The PCB connects and supports the electronic components that control a smart device.
Although PCB layout alone cannot determine battery life, its design can influence electrical efficiency, signal integrity, and overall system reliability.
Several considerations are particularly important.
Power distribution: PCB traces must be appropriately sized for their expected currents. Excessive resistance in power paths can create voltage drops and energy losses, particularly during high-current operating periods.
Component placement: Positioning power management components and their supporting capacitors correctly helps maintain stable supply voltages. Poor placement can increase electrical noise and reduce circuit performance.
Wireless layout: RF traces, antenna clearance, and ground-plane design influence wireless communication quality. The layout should follow the wireless chipset and antenna manufacturers’ recommendations.
Low-leakage design: Suitable components, clean manufacturing processes, and careful handling of sensitive high-impedance circuits help reduce unwanted leakage currents.
Power management integration: The PCB must support effective control of regulators, sensors, and other peripherals so that unused circuits can enter low-power states.
For device manufacturers, reviewing power distribution, component placement, and wireless layout during the PCB design stage can help identify potential efficiency problems before prototypes move into production.
The most effective approach considers hardware, firmware, and PCB layout together rather than treating them as separate design tasks.
5. Testing Battery Life Before Mass Production
Calculating expected battery life is useful, but real-world testing remains essential.
A device may perform efficiently during sleep yet consume significantly more energy when transmitting data, driving a motor, activating an alarm, or communicating with a network.
Engineers should therefore measure current consumption across different operating conditions, including:
- Deep sleep and standby
- Sensor measurement and processing
- Wireless transmission and reception
- Startup and wake-up events
- Low-battery operation
Average current consumption can then be estimated from the current drawn in each state and the time spent in that state.
Testing should also consider battery voltage changes, temperature variations, and communication reliability.
For smart locks and other motor-driven products, short periods of high current deserve particular attention because they can cause temporary battery voltage drops and affect device operation.
These measurements help engineers refine their designs before large-scale manufacturing begins.
Better PCB Design Supports Longer Battery Life
Battery life is one of the most important practical features of a smart home device, but it is influenced by much more than the battery itself.
Efficient power management, reliable wireless communication, thoughtful PCB layout, and well-designed firmware all contribute to energy performance.
For consumers, these improvements may mean fewer battery replacements and more dependable operation.
For manufacturers, addressing power efficiency early in development can reduce design revisions and improve product reliability.
Ultimately, longer-lasting smart home devices begin with smarter electronic design—not simply bigger batteries.

articles.title: GTA 6 abandonne une fonction que les joueurs adoraient : Rockstar s’explique
articles.text:
Avec GTA 6, Rockstar Games a décidé de ne pas donner la possibilité de rejouer les missions narratives de l’histoire principale. En abandonnant ce système qui permettait de réessayer une séquence marquante, le studio a surpris les fans. Les développeurs expliquent qu’il s’agit d’un choix artistique assumé dès les premières étapes du développement.
Une rupture avec le système des anciens épisodes de GTA
Introduite avec l’extension « The Ballad of Gay Tony » dans GTA 4, la possibilité de rejouer des missions était encore là dans GTA 5 grâce à son système de médailles qui récompensait les missions secondaires. Pendant des années, les joueurs ont donc pris l’habitude de passer par le menu pour retenter leur chance sur certaines missions afin d’améliorer leurs scores. Dans GTA 6, chaque mission principale s’effectue une seule fois, sans possibilité de rattrapage.
À lire : GTA 6 tourne-t-il mieux sur PS5 ou Xbox Series X ? On connait enfin la réponse
Avant la sortie du jeu, Scott Butchard, directeur du design senior chez Rockstar Games, a expliqué que l’équipe avait étudié cette option au début de la production avant de l’écarter. Selon lui, sélectionner une quête depuis un menu cassait l’immersion et dévalorisait les décisions prises au fil de la partie. Le studio a ainsi décidé de ne pas intégrer une fonctionnalité qui déconnecterait le joueur des conséquences de ces choix dans la trame principale.
L’immersion avant tout
GTA 6 s’inspire également de la philosophie de Red Dead Redemption 2 en proposant une narration immersive et une expérience proche de la simulation dans un monde ouvert. Les missions s’apparentent ainsi davantage aux quêtes d’un jeu de rôle, où le résultat obtenu importe moins que la manière dont elles alimentent l’histoire du joueur. Ainsi, les développeurs ont voulu mettre l’accent sur l’impact des décisions prises durant l’aventure.
À lire : GTA 6 pousse le réalisme des voitures électriques très loin, mais oublie un détail essentiel
Aucune mise à jour officielle ne semble prévue par Rockstar pour réintégrer cette option dans le futur. Les joueurs de GTA 6 sur PC devront probablement attendre l’arrivée de mods conçus par la communauté pour retrouver la possibilité de relancer des séquences spécifiques.

articles.title: Netflix anuncia el proyecto más ambicioso de Las Guerreras K-pop antes de la llegada de su esperada secuela
articles.text:
Además de una segunda parte, las Guerreras K-pop también tienen gira. Las protagonistas de la película irán a actuar en directo. Netflix y AEG Presents han anunciado que el universo de HUNTR/X llega a los escenarios en junio de 2027 con KPop Demon Hunters Golden World Tour.
Los personajes animados (Rumi, Mira y Zoey) van a compartir escenario con los “vivientes”. Además de todo esto, también habrá acrobacias y coreografías. En la web oficial de la gira explican que los asistentes también son parte activa de la experiencia.
La dirección creativa es de Amy Tinkham. Tiene experiencia en giras y producciones escénicas. También se ha anunciado que van a contar con tecnologías que permitan interacción entre los personajes animados y las personas que estén presentes.
Una gira europea sin España en el calendario
El calendario que ha anunciado Netflix arranca el 5 de junio de 2027 en Baltimore. A partir de ahí, seguirá girando por EE. UU. y Canadá durante el verano, para el día 1 de septiembre empezar su parte europea en Zúrich.
A continuación pasarán por Milán, Ámsterdam, Viena, Berlín, Hamburgo, Copenhague y Oslo. También irán a Colonia, Bruselas, París, Dublín, Glasgow, Birmingham y Mánchester. Y terminan este primer calendario europeo en Londres los días 22 y 23 de octubre de 2027.
Falta España en el listado de ciudades. Aunque sí están previstos más destinos internacionales que se anunciarán, por ahora no hay confirmación de que vengan a nuestro país.
Han pasado las fechas de apertura de las primeras fases de venta. Ya hubo preventa para clientes Mastercard. Esta comenzó el 18 de noviembre y también hubo preventa para fans registrados. El día 20 de noviembre a las 10:00 (hora local) arrancó la venta general. También se han anunciado unos paquetes VIP limitados. Estos pueden tener ventajas como asientos reservados, fotos en el escenario o productos exclusivos.
Por otro lado, Netflix trabaja en la secuela. Ted Sarandos (codirector ejecutivo de la empresa de streaming) ha anunciado que la secuela tendrá un amplio estreno en cines. En las informaciones sobre el proyecto se habla de 2029. Sin embargo, en el anuncio de la plataforma no está confirmado.

articles.title: Vegapay raises $10M in Series A round co-led by Vertex Ventures, Prosus
articles.text:
Vegapay raises $10M in Series A round co-led by Vertex Ventures, Prosus
Vegapay raises $10 million in a Series A round co-led by Vertex Ventures and Prosus to expand its Credit Line on UPI offerings, launch secured credit products and strengthen its banking technology platform.
Fintech infrastructure startup Vegapay has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and Prosus, as it looks to expand its credit infrastructure offerings for banks and financial institutions.
The round also saw participation from existing investors Elevation Capital and Eximius Ventures. It comprised primary and secondary components, with more than 40 employees getting an opportunity to sell a portion of their vested employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs).
Founded in 2022 by Gaurav Mittal, Himanshu Agrawal and Puneet Sharma, Vegapay provides an issuer processing and credit lifecycle management platform for Credit Line on UPI (CLOU) and credit cards.
The company will use the fresh capital to onboard more banks onto its Credit Line on UPI platform, introduce secured credit lines backed by fixed deposits, gold and mutual funds, and expand its credit card, prepaid card and forex card programmes. It also plans to strengthen its engineering and risk teams.
As of November 2026, Vegapay claims to command a majority share of India's Credit Line on UPI market. Its platform is live with YES BANK, Unity Small Finance Bank, Suryoday Small Finance Bank and BOBCARD, and powers programmes for Paytm, BharatPe, Kiwi UPI, Scapia and EbixCash World Money, among others.
Vegapay's platform covers the entire credit lifecycle, including customer onboarding, underwriting, real-time authorisation, billing, repayments and reconciliation. It allows banks to operate multiple co-branded credit programmes on a single platform, with individual credit limits, pricing structures and rules. Banks can deploy the platform on their own cloud infrastructure or on-premises.
“UPI was India’s payments revolution. Credit Line on UPI is the UPI moment for credit, and banks should lead it. At Vegapay, we are building the infrastructure layer that banks need. It runs the full credit line lifecycle for the bank, the bank keeps the customer and the credit book, and one platform can run many co-brand programmes, each with its own limits, pricing and rules,” said Gaurav Mittal, Co-founder and CEO of Vegapay.
Nikhil Marwaha, Partner at Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India, said the adoption of credit on UPI could reshape India's lending landscape, adding that Vegapay's platform enables banks to move from product development to launch within weeks.
Credit Line on UPI allows banks to offer customers pre-sanctioned credit lines that can be used at UPI QR codes through existing payment applications, without requiring a separate card or app. The model is expected to expand access to formal credit by leveraging India's existing digital payments infrastructure.

articles.title: Moloi: The Soweto founder taking African take to the world
articles.text:
From teaching himself to code in Soweto to taking his technology business global, Seati Moloi is determined to challenge perceptions of where innovation comes from. The founder and CEO of Khoi Tech spoke to PHATHISANI MOYO about his journey from a curious township boy fascinated by video games to building an African-owned technology company and why he believes Africa must stop being a consumer of technology and start owning it.
When Seati Moloi and his siblings asked their mother for money as children, she had an unusual response. Rather than reaching into her purse, she would buy them a packet of lollipops and send them into the streets to sell.
The exercise had a small business lesson. If the sweets cost 50 cents, the children were expected to return with 80 cents. They would then share the proceeds.
His mother was teaching them how to work, make money and create something for themselves.
“She was effectively saying, ‘I’m not going to simply give you money; I’m going to teach you how to work, create something and generate revenue,’” Moloi recalled in an interview with TechCabal on Wednesday.
That lesson has stayed with Moloi, the founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Khoi Tech, a Soweto-born wearable technology company that has grown from selling wireless earphones and smartwatches into digital health, employee wellness and workplace safety solutions. Having represented South Africa at London Tech Week twice, Moloi is now pushing the bigger idea that African companies should not only use technology built elsewhere, but create and own it.
But entrepreneurship was only one part of the education Moloi received at home. His parents also recognised their son’s insatiable curiosity about how gadgets worked.
Growing up in Soweto, a township rich in liberation history, during apartheid, he was fascinated by computers and video games. While other children were content playing them, Moloi says he wanted to understand how they were made. He wanted to create his own.
The boy who wanted to make video games
His fascination with technology began long before the internet made information and programming tutorials readily accessible. Moloi recalls being drawn to video games, but playing them was never enough. He wanted to understand what went into making them.
“I was fascinated by video games and wanted to create my own. I remember making a game based on The A-Team (the popular action-packed 1980s television series) using paper and pen. I even tried to contact the publishers,” he recalled.
His mother recognised that this was more than a passing childhood interest. Instead of getting him another game, she bought him a computer to explore the technology behind them.
Moloi says he taught himself BASIC programming using old Commodore computers. His father encouraged him to pursue mathematics and science at school, and by his final years of high school, he already knew he wanted to work with computers.
“I credit my parents for having the foresight to recognise the passion their child had and invest in it,” he said.
It was not a childhood without its difficulties. Moloi grew up in a tough environment during the final years of apartheid, a system of racial segregation and oppression, but he was also an ordinary township boy who played soccer and did the things children do.
What distinguished him, he says, was his curiosity and the encouragement he received at home.
“I was a township child with a keen interest in understanding how things were made,” he said. “I wanted to challenge the status quo and create things for myself.”
Building computers after work
After studying computer science at Pentech College in Cape Town and being groomed at Zakheni Computing, an enterprise technology solutions provider, Moloi and a few friends began assembling computers from individual components.
They would travel to suppliers in town, buy motherboards and other parts, assemble the machines, install software, and put together complete personal computers (PCs). The computers belonged to an era when hard drives were bulky, and storage was measured in megabytes rather than the gigabytes and terabytes familiar today.
Moloi remembers installing programmes such as WordPerfect and Lotus 1-2-3, as well as MS-DOS, before putting the machines to use or selling them to people who wanted computers in their homes.
“We could create something from individual components and sell it to people,” he said.
His parents, however, wanted him to gain corporate experience before committing himself to entrepreneurship. He eventually joined First National Bank, one of Africa’s oldest lenders, as a software developer, working on systems for automated teller machines and speed point terminals.
It was not quite the career he had imagined for himself.
Moloi entered a profession that was still largely white-dominated in the years following apartheid. Although he found the technical work relatively straightforward, the corporate environment’s inequalities made the experience uncomfortable at times.
“I didn’t particularly want to go into employment, but my parents insisted,” he said. “They wanted me to gain experience and understand how things worked in a corporate environment before venturing out on my own.”
He lasted about two years.
During the day, he worked as a software developer. In the evenings, he returned to assembling machines with his friends. They were beginning to attract customers, some of whom needed help using their new computers.
His first ventures included SMN Computers, a hardware business that assembled and sold PCs and eventually secured corporate clients, including the City of Johannesburg and Rand Water. They also worked with International Business Machines (IBM), a global technology and consulting company, that trained them in software development, especially websites.
But selling computers eventually became limiting. The company risked becoming what Moloi describes as a “box dropper,” competing with much larger players on the supply of hardware.
The team moved into software development through another business, Biza Telecoms, working on mobile applications and short message service (SMS) applications. Those experiences laid the groundwork for Khoi Tech, which was established around 2020.
From gadgets to data
Moloi founded Khoi Tech after identifying an opportunity in consumer electronics. He had always enjoyed exploring new devices and understanding how they worked. The company began developing wireless earphones and smartwatches under an African brand.
The name Khoi is derived from the word Khoisan, Southern Africa’s earliest known inhabitants. Its products included the Khoi Afripods wireless earphones and Khoi Afriwatch smartwatches.
The ambition was straightforward: create devices that people used every day, but sell them under an African brand. “Why isn’t Africa creating its own products?” Moloi said, describing the thinking behind the business.
The company received an important early boost through Telkom FutureMakers, the telecommunications group’s enterprise and supplier development programme, which supports black-owned businesses and entrepreneurs from disadvantaged backgrounds by helping them develop business ideas, access markets, sharpen their skills and scale their operations.
According to Telkom’s 2023 Integrated Report, the programme approved a R500,000 grant ($27,000) for Khoi Tech to develop its smartwatch prototype, which was launched in September 2022. The funding also helped the company build the backend systems needed to support the device.
The smartwatches generated health-related information that could help doctors, employers and other organisations. Khoi Tech began developing artificial intelligence (AI)-powered health monitoring systems that could use this data to support remote patient monitoring and provide insights into people’s health over time.
Moloi says he and his team engaged medical professionals to understand the challenges of monitoring patients outside traditional healthcare settings and accessing historical health information.
“We realised very early that we were not necessarily in the device business. We were in the data business,” he said. The idea was to sell devices, collect and store the information they generated, process it through Khoi Tech’s systems and make useful insights available to individuals and corporate customers.
The company began developing remote patient monitoring and employee wellness solutions, alongside applications for driver safety and the mining industry.
For underground miners, wearable devices can help companies monitor employees and identify their locations. In transport, the technology can support driver wellness and fatigue-risk management.
The move also changed how Khoi Tech approached manufacturing. It works with contract manufacturers in China to produce devices according to its specifications, while developing its software and backend systems in South Africa.
“We realised that we were not necessarily in the device business. We were in the data business. We use the devices to extract data and store it in our databases. Our solution is mainly focused on the backend system,” Moloi said.
Getting the devices approved was not a simple process. Khoi Tech had to submit them for testing and certification by the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA), South Africa’s telecommunications regulator, to address component defects and repeat parts of the process.
It took about two years to secure certification and approval.
Moloi would have preferred to manufacture everything locally, but says the cost was prohibitive given the company’s resources. The experience reinforced the importance of developing the software and intellectual property that sit behind the products, rather than relying on hardware sales alone.
A moment to pinch himself
For a founder who began his journey in Soweto, taking Khoi Tech to London Tech Week was a particularly meaningful milestone.
The company was selected as part of a South African startup cohort supported by the United Kingdom-South Africa Tech Hub, Telkom and Disraptor, a South African technology venture builder. Khoi Tech’s 2026 participation marked its second consecutive appearance at the event.
Moloi remembers the first experience on the tech world stage as almost surreal.
“It was one of those moments when you wanted to pinch yourself several times to see whether you were still alive!” he said.
There was pride in standing before international organisations and presenting technology developed by a company from Soweto. Some people he met, he says, were surprised by what the team had built, particularly its solutions for corporate customers and the mining sector.
Dinner with the Mayor of London and explaining how the company developed its technology was another highlight. Moloi found the experience challenged a familiar belief that innovation of this calibre must come from established technology hubs or wealthy countries.
“There is sometimes an assumption that because we come from this part of the world, we cannot be innovative or think at that level,” he said.
The ambition to own the technology
Moloi speaks passionately about technology sovereignty. He believes African countries cannot remain dependent on foreign companies for the platforms and systems that underpin everyday life.
He points to reliance on global technology companies such as Microsoft, Google and WhatsApp, arguing that local talent can develop alternatives that serve African markets.
“It’s everything, my brother,” he said when asked why ownership matters.
For him, sovereignty begins with controlling the technology stack that supports a country’s economy and security. South Africa’s broader digital economy accounts for an estimated 10% to 15% of gross domestic product (GDP), according to the GSMA’s 2024 report on digital transformation in South Africa. Retaining more of that economic value through locally developed technology, intellectual property and platforms is central to his argument.
He makes the point with a familiar example: if WhatsApp were switched off, South Africans might have to return to SMS because they have not built a comparable platform of their own.
His argument is not that the continent should isolate itself from international companies. Rather, it should develop the capability to build its own systems, collaborate from a position of strength and retain more of the value created by its innovations.
Moloi believes countries such as China and Singapore offer lessons in developing technological independence. He was also invited to join a group of entrepreneurs who recently travelled to Silicon Valley with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, but declined, saying he was more interested in learning from the East.
“If you go to Shenzhen, for example, you will see that it is living in 2050,” he said.
His frustration reflects a concern echoed across Africa’s technology industry for years. The continent continues to struggle to create the conditions needed to turn that potential into globally competitive, locally owned technology businesses.
TechCabal previously reported that even companies such as Khoi Tech face challenges accessing investors and networks outside established technology hubs. Much of Africa’s talent still builds on technology developed elsewhere rather than owning the products and platforms shaping the digital economy.
For young people growing up in townships, Moloi wants his journey to offer hope and a different picture of what is possible.
“Being born in Soweto or any other township should not be seen as a limitation,” he believes.
The Soweto-born founder hopes young people will use the tools available to them, including artificial intelligence, to build solutions that address the needs of their communities and the wider continent.
“They need to take the baton and continue the race,” he noted.
Moloi believes that the future begins with recognising that a child from Soweto can do more than use technology built elsewhere. That child can help create it.

articles.title: GTA VI unofficial PC ports are already rendering in-game graphics despite Take-Two's takedowns
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Grand Theft Auto VI has been available on consoles for less than a week, and the cat-and-mouse game between Rockstar and users trying to play it on PC is in full swing. The game isn't playable on PC yet, but progress toward that goal continues steadily despite Take-Two's aggressive moves against unofficial ports.
Social media videos demonstrated early progress on vibe-coded PC ports of Grand Theft Auto VI just two days after the game's console launch. Other users also claim to have taken a crucial step toward running the game on emulators and uncovered the exact graphics settings for each console.
Although clips from this week reveal modders have successfully rendered GTA VI's in-game graphics on PC, framerates remain in the single digits, and glitches are clearly visible. Further development will likely have to happen underground, as a Take-Two DMCA notice struck down a port called Leonida and more than 3,000 GitHub forks. Leonida was the first project known to have booted the game on PC.
 – __cxc__ (@ChenXuchuan) November 24, 2026
 – Brackz (@Brackzmeta) November 25, 2026
The website PortWatch VI is tracking the race between several porting attempts. None have achieved a playable frame rate, but several have at least reached GTA VI's first chapter. In the lead is AvatarManz, who forked a port called Victory and achieved frame rates of between 6 and 20fps on an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX. However, his project currently uses up to 46GB of RAM.
Meanwhile, unconfirmed reports claim some users have dumped the files from the PS5 version and run it on jailbroken consoles. Playing GTA VI on PS5 normally requires firmware version 26.07-14.23.00 or newer, which hasn't been jailbroken so far. If reports of the dump are genuine, the game might become playable on PS5 emulators, which have made significant progress in recent weeks.
Data mining might also have revealed a list of graphics settings Rockstar used for each console. The original posts listing the settings on X and gtaforums.com were deleted, but not before several outlets copied them. If the list represents a potential graphics menu for an official PC version, then the wait might be shorter than for Grand Theft Auto V and Red Dead Redemption II, both of which took over a year to reach PC.
Unsurprisingly, the standard PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X use identical settings, which vary between medium and high for effects like global illumination and shadows. The PlayStation 5 Pro engages ray-traced shadows and sets them to high, while the Xbox Series S lowers many settings to medium or low and adjusts motion blur.
Since experts have described GTA VI as CPU-heavy, settings related to pedestrians are likely crucial to predictions about what kind of CPU a PC version would need to hit 60fps. The settings menu reveals three such options: AI behavior & motion, pedestrian and vehicle density, and physics quality, with all set to medium on Series S and high on all other consoles. GTA VI is locked to 30fps on all consoles, so reaching 60fps on many CPUs might require turning these settings down.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.text:
AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  University of Plymouth
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
- Share:
Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.
AI Finds Hidden Bladder Cancer Clues in Medical Records
Under current medical referral guidelines, one of the main warning signs of bladder cancer is visible blood in the urine (hematuria). However, blood in the urine can also result from noncancerous problems, including kidney stones and prostate conditions. This overlap makes it difficult to determine which patients need further investigation and contributes to missed cases.
Confirming bladder cancer currently requires a procedure called cystoscopy (where a long, thin tube with a small camera inside is moved up the urethra and into the bladder). Although effective, the examination is invasive, highlighting the need for better ways to identify patients who are most likely to have the disease.
To explore a possible solution, a team led by Professor Shang-Ming Zhou at the University of Plymouth's Centre for Health Technology studied electronic medical records from nearly 70,000 patients. The records covered a 25-year period, from 1995 through 2020.
The researchers created an AI model called PRECISE-AGZ and used it to investigate 48,261 possible health indicators (from smoking and exercise habits to medication use). From this enormous collection of information, the system narrowed the list to 38 features that were especially useful for predicting bladder cancer risk.
AI Identifies 85% of Bladder Cancer Cases
The results suggest that AI could substantially improve the way patients are assessed for bladder cancer.
The model correctly identified 85% of patients who had bladder cancer and accurately classified 91% of those who did not have the disease. It also performed better at detecting bladder cancer than existing NHS referral guidelines.
Importantly, the system demonstrated effective detection as early as 12 months before a patient's official diagnosis. Some of the warning signals it recognized could be traced back up to five years, suggesting that valuable clues may exist in medical records long before cancer is discovered.
The AI confirmed the importance of established risk factors, including smoking and blood in the urine. However, it also uncovered unexpected associations that conventional screening approaches would be unlikely to detect.
For example, patients diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or dementia appeared to have a lower risk of bladder cancer. Meanwhile, long-term use of tamoxifen (a breast cancer medication) was associated with a higher risk.
These findings do not establish that Parkinson's disease or dementia protects against bladder cancer, or that tamoxifen causes it. Instead, they raise questions about possible shared biological mechanisms that researchers believe deserve closer examination.
Another surprising finding involved blood in the urine. Although this symptom is often considered a major warning sign, its significance appears to depend partly on a patient's other medical conditions. Among men with benign prostate enlargement, for instance, blood in the urine was associated with a lower bladder cancer risk.
Understanding these relationships more fully could eventually help doctors distinguish patients who need urgent investigation from those who may not require invasive testing.
A New Approach to Early Cancer Screening
Beyond identifying warning signs, the AI system could also divide patients into three groups according to their estimated likelihood of having bladder cancer: low-risk (below 7% probability), uncertain (grey zone: 7-55%), and high-risk (above 55%).
This approach could help healthcare providers decide which patients need immediate attention and which may benefit from additional monitoring.
For example, patients in the uncertain category might be monitored before undergoing procedures such as cystoscopy. If further research confirms the system's reliability, this could reduce unnecessary examinations while allowing doctors to concentrate resources on people at greatest risk.
PhD student Xu Wang, who led the data analysis, said: "Bladder cancer ranks as the ninth most common cancer worldwide, with 614,000 new cases diagnosed in 2022."
"Despite its prevalence, no routine screening program exists for the general population, and - following symptoms - detection relies heavily on invasive cystoscopy procedures. Our system goes far beyond traditional symptoms, and it's great to have uncovered the results that we have. The research shows that the combination of multiple factors - from medication histories to seemingly unrelated conditions - can reveal patterns invisible to conventional screening methods."
Could AI Help Doctors Catch Bladder Cancer Earlier?
The potential benefits extend beyond improving diagnostic accuracy. Detecting bladder cancer earlier could mean more treatment options, better survival outcomes, and fewer patients undergoing invasive procedures unnecessarily.
Dr. Helen Winter, Clinical Director for the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance, emphasized the importance of developing better screening methods.
"Bladder cancer has a major unmet need in early detection and the prospect of a screening tool is hugely exciting for patients and their families.
"It could identify those most at risk more accurately, reduce harm from invasive procedures, and catch cancer earlier, when survival outcomes and quality of life can be dramatically improved."
Professor Shang-Ming Zhou believes the findings point toward a more individualized approach to cancer screening, in which AI helps doctors interpret a patient's broader medical history rather than relying primarily on individual symptoms.
"This work represents a paradigm shift towards precision screening for bladder cancer.
"By harnessing the power of interpretable machine learning and comprehensive health records, we're moving closer to detecting this disease at its earliest, most treatable stages."
More Research Needed Before Clinical Use
Despite the promising results, the researchers caution that the technology is not yet ready for widespread clinical use.
All the patient information used in the study came from the SAIL database in Wales. Before the model can be introduced into other healthcare settings, researchers will need to determine whether it performs equally well with different patient populations and medical record systems.
Professor Zhou explained why broader testing is essential.
"It's important to emphasize that further validation across different healthcare systems is essential before anything is rolled out more widely - for example, all of the data analyzed came from the SAIL database in Wales, so we'd want to investigate other datasets too.
"But it's a very exciting early study. Additional studies would also be needed to confirm the causal relationships suggested by the model's predictions."
The findings offer an encouraging glimpse of how artificial intelligence might improve cancer screening by uncovering patterns hidden within years of routine medical information. With further validation, such tools could help doctors recognize bladder cancer sooner, prioritize patients who need testing, and potentially improve outcomes.
The study, "Early Detection of Bladder Cancer Using Advanced Feature Engineering and Swarm Intelligence Optimization on EHRs," was published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering.
The research also involved collaborators from North Bristol NHS Trust and University Hospitals Bristol NHS Foundation Trust.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Plymouth. Original written by Mrs. Amy King. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Xu Wang, Andrea Preston, Jonathan Aning, Michael Loizou, Shang-Ming Zhou. Early Detection of Bladder Cancer Using Advanced Feature Engineering and Swarm Intelligence Optimization on EHRs. IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, 2026; 73 (11): 3680 DOI: 10.1109/TBME.2026.3658230

articles.title: Building a Production-Ready Culture and Skills Through SRE-based Training
articles.text:
Training can act as a confidence engine, turning repeated behaviors into habits and culture. In her talk, Engineer Confidence with Reliable Training Programs at GOTO Copenhagen, Jennifer Petoff showed how we can tailor training programs that equip developers and operators with the skills to run their services in line with the organization’s maturity and growth, and apply SRE principles to the training itself.
Software ownership is a human challenge as much as it is a technical one. Most formal education programs are geared towards the first 10% of the software development life cycle, the build phase, Petoff said. Engineers and operators are tasked with maintaining, debugging, securing, and evolving systems they may not even have written:
There’s this implicit assumption that coding proficiency translates seamlessly to operational confidence, but it doesn’t. Without systematic training, this may create imposter syndrome, stress, and maybe even attrition in your organization.
AI has magnified the relative cost and complexity of post-build operations. Petoff suggested thinking about how to equip developers and operators with skills to run their services scalably in production.
Culture is not some grand mindset you need to shift. It’s much more tactical. You can change your culture by changing what people do every day, Petoff said. Training people acts as a confidence engine, giving engineers the self-efficacy to adopt new operational behaviors. When behaviors are repeated over time and across teams, they become habits, and those habits comprise your organizational culture. Petoff suggests avoiding a sink-or-swim mentality (letting people fend for themselves rather than training them), as it can breed stress or frustration.
Training needs depend on the maturity of your organization in adopting key principles and practices, the familiarity of engineers with the organization and infrastructure, and the experience of individuals. For organizations starting their DevOps or SRE journey, she suggested addressing skill gaps and tailoring the message to who is on your team. Organizations that already have well-developed production best practices should aim at reinforcing their culture and building upon their practices to foster confidence.
Your training program should take into account the size of your organization and how fast it’s growing to get the most from your investment. If your organization is small and growing slowly, focus on one-on-one knowledge transfer through mentoring and shadowing, Petoff suggested. For a large and slowly growing organization, invest in ongoing education. When it’s small but growing rapidly, invest in onboarding. If you’re both large and growing rapidly, invest in a full life cycle training program, onboarding, all the way through ongoing education and beyond, she said.
The foundational principles of SRE and elements of the service reliability hierarchy can be applied to the training program itself, Petoff explained:
Monitor through attendance tracking and survey feedback. Address issues that surface via the monitoring. Write postmortems when something goes wrong to learn from that failure. Observe concrete job-related behaviors to more effectively tie the training to business impact.
To scale production safety training to tens of thousands of developers, they created a self-paced training and piloted it with a 1% cohort, making changes based on audience feedback before scaling it up. Petoff said they automated the distribution, enrollment, and escalation notifications up the management chain.
A production-ready workforce and organizational culture is non-negotiable in the generative AI era, Petoff stated. Learning drives confidence, confidence drives behavior, and behavior repeated over time drives culture. You need to look at the training costs and benefits to make the right level of investment based on the specific organizational situation. Applying SRE principles to the training program itself led to a more consistent, reliable, and scalable experience, she concluded.
InfoQ interviewed Jennifer Petoff after her talk.
InfoQ: How can we tailor the training message to individual team members?
Jennifer Petoff: In the Generative AI era, we are all moving faster than ever, and it’s easy for training to get sacrificed as something important, but not urgent. Developers and operators may also look upon training with skepticism: Is this training tied to some fleeting corporate hype that will quickly be forgotten?
You need to convince them "what’s in it for me?" (WIIFM). The answer ties directly to what motivates people and varies among team members.
- For the practically-minded: Tie the training to reductions in toil or on-call load.
- For the growth-minded: Connect it to higher-value skills that can unlock career opportunities.
- For people motivated by self-preservation: Explain how the training will build future-proof skills.
These "WIIFM" elements can be conveyed in written communications, through talking points to managers, or peer-to-peer discussions incorporated into the program.
InfoQ: How did you observe job-related behaviors?
Petoff: We built a hands-on training environment using real production infrastructure, but without real-world users and associated stakes. We could "break" our training infrastructure on demand, and students would work in groups of three to troubleshoot realistic production issues.
By structuring the training in this way, instructors could directly observe how participants used system diagrams, diagnosed production issues, and mitigated an outage. We looked at how people engaged with production during the exercises instead of quizzing them or asking for a simple nod of understanding.
InfoQ: What have you learned from applying SRE principles to training programs?
Petoff: Reliability is about mastering the operational "how" of any complex initiative. Training programs are just the tip of the iceberg. I believe that you can "SRE" anything in work, life, and for your well-being. Building is time-bound, but operations are forever. Planning a project beyond launch to include mechanisms to streamline operations and drive continuous improvement will pay you back tenfold and free up time to work on more impactful initiatives without getting buried under a mountain of toil.

articles.title: Justiça condena oito pessoas à prisão por piratearem a Sky
articles.text:
Justiça condena oito pessoas à prisão por piratearem a Sky
Maior pena passou dos 15 anos de prisão. Grupo vendia receptores e chaves para liberar canais via satélite.
A Justiça Federal condenou oito pessoas envolvidas em um esquema que vendia receptores de TV via satélite e chaves para liberar canais pagos sem autorização. O grupo atuou entre 2013 e 2017, com fornecedores no Paraguai e revendedores em Porto Alegre. A Sky participou do processo como assistente de acusação.
A sentença foi assinada em 10 de novembro pelo juiz federal Lademiro Dors Filho, da 7ª Vara Federal de Porto Alegre. Todos os condenados poderão recorrer em liberdade. O chefe do núcleo fornecedor no Paraguai recebeu a maior pena: 15 anos, três meses e 20 dias de prisão, em regime inicial fechado.
O esquema utilizava o card sharing, ou compartilhamento de chaves. Segundo explicações da Sky anexadas ao processo, os decodificadores oficiais usam cartões criptográficos para liberar a programação transmitida via satélite. Na modalidade de pirataria, dados de cartões legítimos são copiados e distribuídos pela internet a vários usuários. Além dos aparelhos, o grupo oferecia suporte para renovar o acesso à programação.
As defesas sustentaram que os aparelhos eram receptores de canais abertos e questionaram sua capacidade de captar programação paga. O juiz considerou que o contrabando estava demonstrado pela entrada clandestina dos equipamentos sem homologação da Anatel. Já a venda de acesso aos canais foi comprovada por diálogos interceptados, códigos comercializados e depoimentos.
Os fornecedores mantinham uma empresa no Paraguai e abasteciam dois núcleos de revenda em Porto Alegre. Os receptores também entravam no Brasil sem documentação fiscal em remessas semanais ou quinzenais.
A sentença reconheceu 117 entradas clandestinas de mercadorias: 59 destinadas à Aztime e 58 à Azmegashop. Em um dos depósitos, a Polícia Federal apreendeu 446 receptores, além de planilhas de estoque, códigos de acesso e registros de vendas.
Os oito réus foram condenados por organização criminosa e contrabando. Os líderes dos núcleos também receberam penas por violação de direito autoral e estelionato. Três integrantes também foram punidos por lavagem de dinheiro: dois do núcleo fornecedor no Paraguai e o responsável pela Azmegashop.
As defesas negaram a existência de uma organização estruturada e sustentaram que os acusados mantinham relações comerciais ou profissionais. Os pedidos de absolvição dos oito condenados foram rejeitados e outros dois acusados foram absolvidos por falta de provas.
A decisão também determinou multas e a perda de bens e valores ligados aos crimes em favor da União. O juiz não fixou indenização mínima e os prejuízos das operadoras não foram estimados durante o processo. As empresas ainda poderão buscar compensação na Justiça cível.
A condenação ainda pode ser revista em segunda instância. A consulta ao processo registra apelações apresentadas em 23 de novembro. Esses recursos permitem pedir ao Tribunal Regional Federal da 4ª Região (TRF4) a revisão da sentença.
Em outro caso, divulgado em junho, dois irmãos receberam penas de nove anos e dois meses por operarem um serviço de IPTV pirata em Goiás.

articles.title: ‘GTA 6’ rompe el récord de estreno en físico en España... con una caja sin disco
articles.text:
Cada día que pasa nos encontramos con nuevos logros de GTA 6. Lo nuevo de Rockstar Games ha tenido un debut formidable tanto en críticas como en ventas, generando varios miles de millones de dólares en ingresos cuando recién ha pasado una semana desde su lanzamiento. Si bien la mayoría de las compras de Grand Theft Auto VI fueron en formato digital, la versión en "físico" también rompió récords en varios países; y lo hizo pese a no incluir un disco en la caja.
Como ya todos saben, las versiones físicas de GTA 6 son un tanto mentirosas, pues en su interior traen solamente un código de descarga. Esto le ha valido a Rockstar y Take-Two Interactive críticas bastante fuertes, en consonancia con las que le cayeron a PlayStation por sus planes de matar el formato físico a partir de 2028. Aun así, a la hora de las ventas a una gran cantidad de personas no les ha importado la ausencia del disco Blu-ray dentro del empaque.
Según reporta The Game Business, GTA 6 se ha coronado como el mayor lanzamiento físico que se ha dado en el comercio minorista de España desde que NielsenIQ recopila esta información. Desafortunadamente, la publicación no menciona cifras concretas sobre el desempeño comercial del juego en el mercado español. No obstante, sí ofrece un panorama un poco más específico sobre lo que ocurre en la región.
En Francia, por ejemplo, GTA 6 habría vendido más de un millón de copias físicas en sus primeros tres días. En Reino Unido, en tanto, lo nuevo de Rockstar Games sería el juego más vendido en físico desde 2019, consiguiendo unos 32 millones de libras esterlinas en solamente tres días.
GTA 6 también disfruta de las buenas ventas en formato "físico"
Las ventas de GTA 6 en formato físico se iniciaron mucho después en comparación con las versiones digitales para PS5 y Xbox Series X|S. Las cajas del nuevo juego de Rockstar salieron a la venta en las tiendas minoristas el pasado 12 de noviembre; es decir, una semana antes de su lanzamiento.
Al no incluir un disco en la caja, quienes eligieron esta posibilidad quedaron limitados a descargar el juego de los servidores de Xbox y PlayStation. Pero es evidente que un número de personas mayor al esperado ha optado por esta vía para, al menos, tener el empaque en sus manos como recuerdo de que formaron parte del lanzamiento más grande de la historia de los videojuegos.
Lo de GTA 6 hasta aquí ha sido alucinante. Al cierre de su primer día a disposición, el juego ya había generado casi 4.000 millones de dólares en ingresos. Además, el título se convirtió en el lanzamiento más exitoso en la historia de PlayStation, con más de 39 millones de jugadores únicos. La propuesta de Rockstar logró el mayor número de usuarios en simultáneo de la plataforma, superando todos los registros previos, incluso aquellos pertenecientes a títulos gratuitos y con multijugador.

articles.title: GTA 6 a failli avoir un parc d’attractions inspiré de Disney World
articles.text:
Leonida, l’État fictif dans lequel se déroule GTA 6, s’inspire de la Floride, et sa ville principale, Vice City, de Miami. Sorti le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, le jeu de Rockstar Games aurait donc pu permettre de visiter un immense parc d’attractions inspiré de Disney World, situé près d’Orlando dans la vraie vie.
L’idée d’un parc à Leonida a bien été sur la table, mais elle a dû être abandonnée par Rockstar Games, comme l’a confié Rob Nelson, producteur de GTA 6 et codirecteur du studio Rockstar North, dans une interview accordée à Video Games Chronicle et publiée ce jeudi 26 novembre. Comme les fléchettes ou le bowling, le parc d’attractions fait partie des idées écartées en cours de développement, faute de temps ou de justification narrative.
Intégrer un parc Disney dans GTA 6 aurait été trop ambitieux
« Un parc d’attractions aurait représenté énormément de travail, un travail que nous n’avions pas les moyens de fournir, et nous n’avions pas de raison narrative suffisamment solide pour y envoyer [Jason et Lucia] », explique Rob Nelson. C’est donc autant une question de ressources qu’une logique de récit. Il précise à ce sujet : « Il s’agit de savoir s’il existe une raison narrative qui justifie de consacrer ce temps à la création d’un parc d’attractions entièrement fonctionnel. Nous déterminons simplement ce dont nous avons réellement besoin pour servir l’histoire et renforcer le sentiment d’être à Leonida. »
La même logique a été appliquée à toutes les activités envisagées par les développeurs, comme le confie un Rob Nelson amusé : « On veut tout faire, on veut pouvoir prendre chaque guitare, s’asseoir derrière la batterie. Avions-nous besoin de faire un jeu de golf complet ? Ce n’est pas vraiment le truc de ces personnages. » On rappelle que Jason et Lucia cherchent à joindre les deux bouts dans GTA 6. Par conséquent, ils ont logiquement moins le temps pour se consacrer à des moments de pur plaisir. Quant à la perspective de visiter un parc, ce n’est pas vraiment en adéquation avec leur obligation de faire profil bas.
Il ajoute : « C’est tout le défi : où s’arrêter ? À quel moment estime-t-on que c’est suffisant ? Nous avons poussé les intérieurs aussi loin que possible, mais il faut ensuite les remplir — ils doivent paraître naturels. » D’après le décompte d’un joueur publié sur Reddit, 1 563 des 5 588 bâtiments de Leonida peuvent être visités, soit près de 28 %. Ce chiffre n’a pas été vérifié de façon indépendante, mais il fait plus que doubler les quelque 700 intérieurs évoqués par une fuite en 2025. Sur les intérieurs, Rockstar Games n’a pas eu la main légère.

articles.title: Black Friday Fnac : jusqu'à -50 % sur les produits Dyson et 50 € offerts dès 400 € d'achat
articles.text:
Black Friday Fnac : jusqu'à -50 % sur les produits Dyson et 50 € offerts dès 400 € d'achat
C'est l'une des seules occasions de l'année de s'offrir du Dyson à prix cassé. Pour ce Black Friday, la Fnac cumule des remises allant jusqu'à 40 % et plus sur les aspirateurs et appareils de coiffure de la marque, avec un bonus de taille : 50 € crédités sur votre compte fidélité dès 400 € d'achat. Une aubaine à saisir jusqu'au 30 novembre.
Aspirateurs : l'hygiène haut de gamme à prix réduit
C'est le cœur de métier de Dyson. Que vous cherchiez à remplacer un vieil aspirateur ou à automatiser le ménage, les remises actuelles permettent d'accéder à la technologie de pointe de la marque tout en validant le palier des 400 €.
Aspirateur sans-fil Dyson V15 Detect Absolute
C'est la référence absolue pour l'entretien des sols. Le V15 Detect embarque un laser vert qui révèle la poussière invisible à l'œil nu, et un capteur piézoélectrique qui compte et mesure les particules aspirées en temps réel. Avec ses 240 Air Watts et ses 60 minutes d'autonomie, il nettoie en profondeur. Affiché à 469 € au lieu de 799 € (-41 %), c'est le produit parfait pour déclencher les 50 € de cagnotte à lui seul.
Aspirateur robot Dyson Spot + Scrub AI
Pour ceux qui veulent que le ménage se fasse tout seul. Ce robot laveur utilise une intelligence artificielle et une caméra pour détecter les taches et les zones les plus sales, afin d'adapter sa puissance et son débit d'eau. Il nettoie en profondeur les tapis et les sols durs sans intervention. Son prix chute à 649 € au lieu de 1 199 € (-46 %), soit une économie immédiate de 550 €. En plus de cette remise record, il vous rapporte les 50 € de cagnotte fidélité.
Aspirateur à main Dyson Car+Boat
Conçu pour la voiture, le bateau ou les petits espaces, cet aspirateur à main compact combine puissance d'aspiration et légèreté. Il est livré avec des accessoires spécifiques pour nettoyer les recoins étroits et les tissus. Son prix baisse à 199 € au lieu de 279 € (-29 %). C'est l'allié parfait pour compléter un panier déjà bien rempli et franchir la barre des 400 €.
Beauté : le coiffage professionnel à la maison
Dyson a révolutionné le soin des cheveux avec des appareils qui rivalisent avec le matériel des salons de coiffure. Pour ce Black Friday, les outils phares de la marque bénéficient de remises immédiates, rendant l'accès à cette technologie plus abordable.
Fer à boucler Dyson Airwrap i.d.
Outil de coiffure star, l'Airwrap i.d. est la version connectée du célèbre multi-styler de Dyson. Grâce à l'application mobile, il analyse votre profil capillaire pour créer et mémoriser les programmes de coiffage parfaits (boucles, ondulations, lissage). Il s'équipe de barres d'enroulement, de brosses et d'un séchoir pré-coiffant. Il est proposé à 399 € au lieu de 549 € (-27 %). En l'associant à un petit produit Dyson ou du panier Fnac, vous dépassez les 400 € et empochez la cagnotte.
Sèche-cheveux Dyson Supersonic Nural
Le dernier-né des sèche-cheveux Dyson. Le Supersonic Nural est équipé de la technologie de contrôle de la température, qui empêche la chaleur excessive et protège la barrière cutanée du cuir chevelu. Il est également doté d'un capteur d'accessoires qui ajuste automatiquement les réglages de chaleur. Il passe à 299 € au lieu de 399 € (-25 %). Un achat malin à combiner pour déclencher les 50 €.
Une occasion en or de passer chez Dyson
Dyson est une marque dont les prix sont rarement cassés à ce point. Avec des remises allant jusqu'à -50 %, et la possibilité de récupérer 50 € sur votre compte fidélité, ce Black Friday est sans doute le meilleur moment de l'année pour vous équiper en hygiène et beauté.
L'offre se termine le lundi 30 novembre à 23h59. Ne laissez pas passer cette occasion de cumuler les économies et de vous faire plaisir, tout en préparant vos cadeaux de fin d'année.

articles.title: Amazon Autos : le comparateur de voitures d’Amazon arrive près de chez nous
articles.text:
Le service de comparateur et d’achat de voitures d’Amazon, baptisé Amazon Autos, s’apprête à franchir l’Atlantique. Il ne sera bientôt plus limité aux États-Unis puisqu’il va arriver au Royaume-Uni début 2027, soit dans quelques semaines, comme l’a annoncé Amazon dans un communiqué ce 24 novembre.
Amazon Autos : un comparateur de voitures intégré à Amazon
Sur Amazon, on peut tout acheter (ou presque) : tout ce qui est imaginable par votre esprit est en vente sur Amazon. Y compris des voitures : Amazon Autos est un service qui permet de rechercher, comparer et réserver des voitures directement depuis Amazon. Le site ne vend en réalité pas de véhicules en propre ; Amazon s’occupe simplement de mettre en relation les acheteurs avec des concessionnaires partenaires. Ce sont ces derniers qui décident du prix, annoncent leur stock et finalisent les ventes.
Amazon Autos couvre les voitures neuves, d’occasion ou encore celles certifiées d’occasion. Sur ce service, les acheteurs peuvent voir les stocks, regarder les prix, avoir une estimation de la reprise de leur véhicule, consulter les options de financement, réserver un modèle ou encore prendre contact avec un concessionnaire.
Avec Autos, Amazon semble vouloir devenir le portail principal d’information et d’achat de voitures. L’intérêt d’un tel service est surtout d’éviter de multiplier les sites de concessionnaires qu’on consulte ; sur Amazon Autos on peut comparer directement plusieurs annonces, avec les équipements et les prix. Le tout via l’interface d’Amazon, qu’on connaît déjà. De quoi aussi palier aux chatbots qui permettent de faire de chercher des véhicules et de comparer nombre d’annonces en une requête.
Ce service d’Amazon ne sera plus limité qu’aux États-Unis
Amazon Autos avait été lancé aux États-Unis en décembre 2024. Le service était disponible au départ dans 48 villes seulement, puis avait été étendu à 150 villes américaines, avec des véhicules issus de 35 marques. Aujourd’hui, Amazon veut aller beaucoup plus loin.
Début 2027 donc, Amazon Autos sera enfin disponible au Royaume-Uni. Outre-Manche, Hyundai sera le premier constructeur dont les véhicules neufs seront disponibles. La gamme devrait comprendre des modèles électriques, hybrides et essence, dont les Ioniq 3 et Ioniq 5, ainsi que les i20 et Kona. Au lancement, on pourra aussi voir les voitures d’occasion du groupe britannique Vertu Motors.
Pour le moment, Amazon n’a annoncé aucun pays supplémentaire dans lequel Amazon Autos sera disponible, ni de calendrier. On sait seulement qu’au Royaume-Uni, d’autres constructeurs et concessionnaires britanniques seront disponibles au lancement. Mais si c’est un succès, Amazon pourrait envisager d’étendre Autos à d’autres marchés européens, notamment ceux de l’Union européenne.
