articles.title: 1Password confirms data breach after hacker compromises employee's GitHub account
articles.text:
What we know so far: 1Password has confirmed that a hacker stole customer names and email addresses from its backend systems. The attacker compromised a single employee's GitHub account and was able to push malicious code into those services and pull customer records. The stolen data does not include passwords or anything stored in customer vaults, but it still leaves users open to convincing phishing attempts, and 1Password has not said how many people are affected.
1Password began its investigation earlier this month. By then, the intruder had used the hijacked account to browse the company's source code and insert malicious instructions designed to collect customer data.
The change was a subtle one. Code written to look like part of the normal system doesn't need to break anything, and one compromised developer login was enough to put it into production. Attacks on source repositories and build pipelines have become a common route into software companies, and this one fits that pattern.
Beyond names and email addresses, the haul included public keys and the account and user identifiers that 1Password uses internally. Public keys are designed to be shared, so exposing them doesn't hand over access to anything. The identifiers could still help someone build a more believable lure or match records to a particular customer.
The leaked data also included tokens from certain emailed invitation links and account recovery links. Those tokens are key to the account enrollment and recovery process and could, in principle, be used to start taking over an account.
But according to the company, an attacker would also need to pair a token with a single sign-on method or with a six-digit numeric code sent to the user's email. Six digits is a small space for guessing, so the company has lengthened those codes to 10 alphanumeric characters. That raises the number of possible combinations from a million to more than a trillion, which makes guessing impractical.
The company has disabled the affected GitHub account and rotated the internal credentials that the breach compromised. Rotation is standard after an intrusion like this, because any secret the attacker could have seen must be treated as compromised. It has also added a new detection system to spot similar attacks.
1Password hasn't said how the attacker got into the GitHub account in the first place. It also hasn't said how long the malicious code ran before it was found or how many customers' records were pulled. Those answers will be important to security teams deciding how much to trust the fix.
For people who use the product, the more immediate problem is social engineering. A criminal who knows a person's name and email address and knows they use 1Password, can write a message that looks routine.
1Password warns that fake emails, texts, or phone calls may reference invitations or account recovery attempts, the same events the stolen tokens relate to. A message about a recovery request that the recipient never made would be easy to take seriously.
The company has set out what it won't do. It says it will never ask customers for their account password or Secret Key, and that those should be entered only into the official 1Password app or website. That guidance is useful because a password manager's value rests on a few secrets that never leave the user's hands. A fake page that captures a master password or Secret Key would be far more damaging than the data already taken.
The incident shows how the security of a product with strong encryption can still depend on ordinary systems around it. 1Password's vault design appears to have held, since the company says vault data wasn't exposed. The attack didn't try to break that design. It went through a developer account that could change code running on the servers.
Companies that handle sensitive data have long been urged to tighten controls around code repositories, including strong authentication on developer accounts, limits on who can push to production, and review of changes before they ship. The company's new detection system points toward the last of those. Whether that is enough will depend on the details 1Password hasn't yet shared.
For now, customers should treat any unexpected message mentioning 1Password with suspicion and go straight to the official app or site rather than following a link.

articles.title: Fizz Black Friday: save $10/mo for 18 months with promo code
articles.text:
Videotron’s Fizz Mobile added to its Black Friday offers with a new promo code discount.
Customers can use code “FIZZ180” to get a $10/mo discount for 18 months, quite a bit of savings on top of Fizz’s already decently priced plans. However, the fine print notes the promo code can only be applied to plans that cost $40 or more.
Still, you can get quite a lot out of a $40 plan from Fizz. For example, in Ontario, Fizz offers a $45/mo 150GB 5G plan with Canada-wide calling and texting. With the discount code, that’s just $35/mo.
But if that doesn’t suit you, the neat thing about Fizz is that it lets you customize various options of your plan, so you can trade out some data for international calls or Canada/U.S. calling and essentially build your perfect plan.
Fizz has other Black Friday offers beyond the $10 discount code as well. The wireless provider has had a string of special offers all month, but the next one is $100 off a new iPhone as long as you activate a Fizz phone plan before Nov. 26 at 11:59 p.m. PT.
Further, anyone who activates a Fizz phone plan before Dec. 8 at 11:59 p.m. PT will get 60GB of free data as well. Even better, existing customers will get these bonuses too.
Check out the Fizz website to learn more about its Black Friday deals.

articles.title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
articles.text:
Microsoft released .NET 11 on 10 November, and .NET MAUI in .NET 11 changes the default runtime from Mono to CoreCLR on all supported platforms. It also adds incremental XAML hot reload, implicit XAML namespaces and new test project templates. The work spanned seven previews and a release candidate, and the documentation describes product quality as the release's focus. Overall, this release consolidates more than it expands.
.NET MAUI (Multi-platform App UI) is Microsoft's cross-platform UI framework for Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows apps built from one C# and XAML codebase. .NET 11 is a Standard Term Support release with two years of support. Microsoft notes that MAUI follows its own support policy, separate from the runtime's STS and LTS lifecycle.
The runtime switch is the most significant change. According to Microsoft, CoreCLR puts mobile and desktop apps on the same runtime as the other .NET workloads. Release builds use composite partial ReadyToRun by default. On Apple platforms, which disallow JIT compilation, code that isn't precompiled runs in the CoreCLR interpreter. Native AOT is an opt-in publishing option, and its Android support is still experimental. Microsoft recommends developers to test app libraries before choosing their deployment model.
XAML gets four main improvements. First, incremental hot reload, still in preview, patches live instances of pages and controls without recreating them. It is on by default in Debug builds, works with dotnet watch, and can be disabled with EnableMauiIncrementalHotReload. Second, implicit namespace declarations are now on by default, so the root xmlns and xmlns:x are optional. Third, lazy ResourceDictionary loading makes large dictionaries initialise up to roughly eight times faster when XAML source generation is used. Finally, RelativeSource bindings with a resolvable AncestorType now compile to trim-safe code.
Handlers keep replacing the legacy renderers with newer implementations. Windows uses the new CollectionView2 handler by default, Android Shell is now handler-based, and iOS and Mac Catalyst now use handlers for NavigationPage, TabbedPage and FlyoutPage. The old renderers remain available as a manual fallback. On iOS, Appearing now fires before a page is pushed rather than after it becomes visible, and secondary toolbar items move into an overflow menu. Developers who depend on the old timing should switch to NavigatedTo.
Controls get smaller additions. Maps gain clustering and custom pin icons, plus an Azure Maps-backed implementation on Windows. TabbedPage gains badges, BoxView a Fill brush, and LongPressGestureRecognizer becomes configurable. Shell also supports route templates such as trip/{tripId}.
Animation methods now accept a CancellationToken, and their non-Async variants are obsolete. On the platform side, a new Passkeys class in Microsoft.Maui.Authentication wraps WebAuthn creation and assertion, while the server still has to validate challenges and attestation. Permissions.PostNotifications now works on iOS, and splash screens can have dark-mode variants.
For Android, the minimum API level rises from 21 to 24, and x86 architecture is no longer supported. The release notes report shorter builds: an incremental build after a managed source change dropped from 68.3 to 52.3 seconds. They also report startup gains of 2.4 to 4.5 per cent from partial ReadyToRun, at the cost of a slightly larger package. Apple targets now require iOS, tvOS and Mac Catalyst 18.2 and macOS 15.2, with Xcode 26.4.
Several changes break existing code. The Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package no longer ships, the Color record is now sealed, Java.Lang.Object.JavaFinalize() is obsolete, and non-font SwipeItem icons are no longer tinted automatically. When upgrading, Microsoft advises to focus on throughly testing navigation, custom handlers and trimmed publishing.
The full list of changes, including per-preview release notes, is in the .NET MAUI documentation. .NET MAUI ships as a workload with NuGet packages, so a project can pin specific versions.

articles.title: El truco de GTA 6 para ganar 100.000 dólares en solo 10 minutos
articles.text:
Los jugadores de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) descubrieron un método que permite conseguir hasta 100.000 dólares en menos de diez minutos gracias a un error en una de las actividades del videojuego. El truco consiste en aprovechar un almacén utilizado por narcotraficantes para esconder cocaína dentro de ositos de peluche, cuya mercancía vuelve a aparecer cada vez que los usuarios se alejan del lugar y regresan.
La estrategia se ha popularizado entre la comunidad de jugadores porque permite acumular grandes cantidades de dinero sin necesidad de completar misiones principales, participar en enfrentamientos o realizar actividades demasiado complejas. Además, algunos usuarios encontraron una manera de acelerar el procedimiento utilizando a los dos protagonistas de la historia: Jason y Lucia.
El método fue compartido y perfeccionado por jugadores en Reddit. Uno de ellos aseguró que, mediante una combinación de vehículos, cambios de personaje y encargos a los compañeros, es posible obtener entre 88.000 y 100.000 dólares en aproximadamente diez minutos.
El descubrimiento llega una semana después del lanzamiento del videojuego, que debutó el 19 de noviembre para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X/S. Desde entonces, los usuarios han encontrado diferentes secretos, actividades ocultas y errores que permiten aprovechar algunas de las mecánicas diseñadas por Rockstar Games.
Dónde encontrar el almacén que permite ganar dinero en GTA 6
El truco comienza en un almacén ubicado cerca de Hamlet, al sur de Vice City. En estas instalaciones, los jugadores encuentran mercancía perteneciente a narcotraficantes que utilizan ositos de peluche para esconder cocaína.
Al llegar al lugar, es posible encontrar los restos de un enfrentamiento entre bandas y varias furgonetas con droga en su interior. Lo llamativo es que los usuarios pueden recoger la mercancía sin tener que enfrentarse a enemigos ni superar una misión específica.
Una vez que consiguen la droga, pueden transportarla y venderla para obtener dinero dentro del juego. Sin embargo, el verdadero beneficio aparece cuando descubren que la mercancía vuelve a generarse después de abandonar la zona y regresar.
Este comportamiento permite repetir la operación varias veces. En condiciones normales, los jugadores tendrían que desplazarse constantemente entre el almacén y el punto de venta, lo que consume tiempo y reduce las ganancias por minuto.
Cómo conseguir hasta 100.000 dólares en diez minutos
La comunidad encontró una forma de optimizar el procedimiento mediante el uso de varias furgonetas. En lugar de depender de un único vehículo, los jugadores pueden organizar diferentes transportes para acumular más mercancía y reducir los desplazamientos.
Otro elemento importante es la posibilidad de alternar entre Jason y Lucia. GTA 6 permite cambiar entre ambos protagonistas durante la aventura, una característica que los usuarios están aprovechando para gestionar mejor las actividades y acelerar la recolección de la droga.
Además, el personaje puede encargar a su compañero que venda la mercancía. De esta manera, no es necesario realizar personalmente todos los viajes hasta el punto de venta.
La combinación de estas mecánicas permite aprovechar el error del almacén con mayor eficiencia. Uno de los jugadores que compartió el procedimiento aseguró haber conseguido entre 88.000 y 100.000 dólares en menos de diez minutos.
No obstante, estas cifras corresponden a experiencias compartidas por usuarios y pueden variar dependiendo de cómo se realice el procedimiento y de las condiciones de la partida.
Rockstar todavía no habría corregido este error de GTA 6
Uno de los aspectos que más llama la atención es que el truco continúa funcionando después de la primera actualización de GTA 6, publicada el lunes posterior al lanzamiento.
Esto significa que, al menos según los reportes de los jugadores, Rockstar todavía no habría solucionado el comportamiento que permite recuperar la mercancía del almacén repetidamente.
La compañía podría corregirlo mediante una futura actualización si considera que afecta al equilibrio de la economía del modo historia. Sin embargo, hasta el momento no se ha confirmado cuándo llegará un parche específico para solucionar este problema.
Mientras tanto, los jugadores continúan explorando el mapa de Leonida para encontrar nuevas actividades, secretos y formas de conseguir dinero. El descubrimiento demuestra cómo la comunidad puede identificar rápidamente comportamientos inesperados dentro de un videojuego y convertirlos en estrategias para avanzar con mayor facilidad.

articles.title: Mistério no espaço: sistema estelar triplo encontrado por astrônomos “não deveria existir”
articles.text:
Pesquisadores do Instituto Trottier de Pesquisa sobre Exoplanetas (IREx) da Universidade de Montreal, no Canadá, identificaram um sistema estelar a 28 anos-luz da Terra, com uma estrela anã-vermelha e duas anãs-brancas, do qual astrônomos não conseguiram explicar a origem.
Batizado de Welopōʻai, o sistema não segue as regras convencionais de surgimento e evolução estelar: “Este sistema não deveria existir”, comentou o professor Patrick Dufour da UdeM, especialista em anãs brancas e coautor do estudo. “Não temos uma explicação clara de como ele surgiu.”
A pesquisa foi publicada na revista Astronomy & Astrophysics.
Para quem tem pressa:
- Astrônomos da Universidade de Montreal identificaram um sistema estelar a 28 anos-luz da Terra, chamado Welopōʻai, formado por uma anã-vermelha e duas anãs-brancas;
- A configuração surpreendeu os pesquisadores porque, pelas teorias convencionais de evolução estelar, a interação entre as estrelas deveria ter provocado uma fusão. Mesmo assim, o sistema permaneceu estável;
- Os cientistas ainda não sabem explicar como o sistema se formou nem como conseguiu se manter. Novas observações devem ajudar a investigar essa configuração incomum.
Uma interação que não deveria existir
**Para maior compreensão: uma anã-branca representa o núcleo de uma estrela que já morreu, ou seja, que chegou ao fim de sua evolução e não produz mais energia, mas continua emitindo luz e calor enquanto esfria lentamente. Já uma estrela anã-vermelha é uma estrela pequena, relativamente fria e de baixa luminosidade, que ainda produz energia e pode viver centenas de bilhões ou até trilhões de anos.
A descoberta começou durante uma busca por exoplanetas. Os pesquisadores procuravam pequenas variações na velocidade de estrelas, provocadas pela atração gravitacional de planetas em órbita, que poderiam mostrar novos exoplanetas.
No entanto, encontraram uma variação mil vezes maior do que o esperado em uma anã-vermelha já conhecida, e foi aqui que o foco mudou.
Os pesquisadores também já conheciam a primeira anã-branca que orbita longe da anã-vermelha, mas ela não poderia explicar essa variação.
Assim, investigando o sistema mais profundamente, eles identificaram uma nova companheira, que inicialmente foi considerada um “parceiro invisível”. Somente após outras observações ficou claro que se tratava de uma segunda anã-branca, com massa próxima à metade da massa do Sol.
Um sistema estelar desse tipo já é uma peculiaridade e tanto. Imagine que o nosso Sistema Solar tivesse duas estrelas parecidas com o Sol e que a Terra estivesse próxima demais de uma delas. À medida que essa estrela envelhecesse e se expandisse, nosso planeta poderia ser engolido, certo? Errado… pelo menos no sistema Welopōʻai.
Antes de morrer, a estrela mais próxima da anã-vermelha tinha uma massa 40% maior do que a do Sol. Em teoria, a dupla poderia ter se fundido, mas a companheira de baixa luminosidade continuou em órbita de maneira estável.
Esse tipo de sistema estelar não pode ser comparado com nenhum outro sistema conhecido em um raio de até 100 anos-luz da Terra, o que dificulta a compreensão de como ele pode existir e de como foi sua evolução.
Leia mais:
- Sistema planetário incomum tem evolução orbital observada em tempo real
- Planeta com até o dobro da massa da Terra pode estar escondido após Netuno
- Via Láctea é mais pesada do que se imaginava
Para os pesquisadores, portanto, os próximos passos são compreender como e por que essa interação aconteceu, já que ela não deveria ter se mantido estável por tanto tempo.
“Descobertas como esta nos lembram que nossa própria vizinhança cósmica ainda guarda surpresas notáveis”, afirmou Étienne Artigau, pesquisador do IREx e principal autor do estudo.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: El Black Friday más allá de teléfonos y ordenadores: areneros autolimpiables, proyectores y cámaras dashcams
articles.text:
Muchas personas aprovechan el Black Friday para comprar teléfonos, televisores, portátiles y otros productos bastante caros. Sin embargo, el Black Friday afecta a todo y puedes encontrar novedades en sectores muy interesantes, por ejemplo el del cuidado de mascotas con areneros o impresoras 3D.
En PowerPlanet van a lanzar una ambiciosa campaña de ofertas, que ya está disponible y que durará hasta el 7 de diciembre, alargando casi una semana el CyberMonday. Hemos dejado aquí dividido por categorías las mejores ofertas que puedes encontrar.
Areneros autolimpiables
A la hora de tener una mascota en casa, sobre todo gatos, el principal incoveniente es la limpieza del arenero. En Power Planet puedes encontrar dos modelos en oferta, los dos con una capacidad de 76 litros y que se pueden controlar desde el teléfono móvil. Son estos dos:
PETKIT Pura Max 2 de 309 euros: es el más silencioso, con hasta 35 dB, y su depósito sellado aguanta hasta 15 días. Admite gatos de hasta 8 kg y mayores de 6 meses. Baja casi a la mitad.
PETKIT Pura Max 3 de 439 euros: admite gatos de 1,5 a 10 kg y hasta 3 o 4 gatos, e incluye el desodorizador N50.
Para nosotros, compensa más el Pura Max 2; pero si tienes varios gatos o gatos grandes, entonces el Pura Max 3. Más modelos en los areneros y productos para mascotas en oferta.
Proyectores de calidad
No hay nada como sentarse en el sofá a ver una película un viernes por la noche. Mucho más si lo hacemos en un buen proyector con una gran calidad de imagen. Hemos encontrado dos modelos que tienen una resolución FHD e incluyen Netflix de manera preinstalada.
Wanbo X5S de 259,90 euros: 1.100 lúmenes ANSI, HDR10 e imagen de hasta 140 pulgadas. Trae Netflix, YouTube, Disney+ y Prime Video preinstalados, y tiene HDMI 2.1 con eARC para conectar una barra de sonido.
Wanbo Mozart 1 Pro de 359,90 euros: 1.200 lúmenes ANSI, Android TV 11, autoenfoque y corrección trapezoidal automática. Su sonido es más completo, con dos altavoces de 10 W y subwoofer.
Si dudas entre ambos, el X5S es la opción más económica y con más plataformas mientras que el Mozart 1 Pro es el que mejor suena y el más fácil de colocar. Tienes más modelos en los proyectores en oferta.
Dos dashcam: una compra barata que seguro que valoras
Cada vez más coches y motos llevan cámaras integradas para grabar el entorno, especialmente útil en caso de accidente o de atropello y que ayuda a esclarecer el motivo de cara a las aseguradoras. Si tu coche no la trae de serie, te dejamos dos modelos de dashcams con una increíble calidad de imagen y que no se va mucho de precio.
DDPAI N5 Pro de 119,95 euros: cámara delantera 4K con sensor Sony Starvis 2 y 143° de visión, trasera en 2K, visión nocturna NightVIS 2.0, 64 GB internos y asistente de conducción ADAS. No tiene pantalla: se maneja desde la app por Wi-Fi 6.
DDPAI Z60 2026 de 109 euros: pantalla IPS de 3 pulgadas, cámara delantera 4K, trasera 1080p por cable y GPS integrado sin suscripción.
Si quieres ver la imagen en la propia cámara, entonces la elección es la Z60 2026. Pero si prefieres más resolución atrás y asistente de conducción, la N5 Pro. Más modelos en las cámaras y accesorios para coche en oferta.
Empieza a imprimir en 3D
La impresión en 3D está de moda. Si tienes espacio para poner una en tu casa, aprovecha este Black Friday con ofertas muy interesantes y ponte a imprimir desde ya. No necesitas conocimientos demasiado técnicos. Tienes dos modelos en oferta:
Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo  de 399,99 euros, con unas dimensiones de 256 × 256 × 256 mm, hasta 500 mm/s y sistema CANVAS de cuatro colores. Su boquilla de acero endurecido permite imprimir PLA con fibra de carbono, y nivela sola en 121 puntos. 
Creality K2 Combo de 529 euros: 260 × 260 × 260 mm y hasta 600 mm/s. Su sistema CFS se amplía hasta 16 colores, y la cámara con IA pausa la impresión si falla una capa.
Si quieres empezar pero no gastarte mucho dinero, elige entonces la Elegoo. Si quieres algo más pro, para crecer hasta 16 colores, entonces tu elección debería ser la Creality. Más modelos en las impresoras 3D en oferta.
Bonus: dos monitores gaming de Xiaomi, de 24 y 27 pulgadas
Una magnífica compra teniendo en cuenta los precios que suele tener Xiaomi en su día a día para todo lo que ofrece, que es mucho en el caso de los monitores gaming.
Xiaomi G24i 2026 de 105 euros: 23,8 pulgadas Full HD, panel Fast IPS a 200 Hz, 1 ms y FreeSync Premium. Baja un 47 %.
Xiaomi G Pro 27Qi 2026 de 309 euros: 27 pulgadas 2K a 180 Hz con Mini LED de 1.152 zonas, hasta 2.000 nits y HDR1000. Su soporte se ajusta en altura, gira y pivota.
Para elegir el correcto tienes que tener en cuenta a qué vas a jugar. Para jugar a shooters con poco presupuesto, el G24i; pero si quieres la mejor imagen HDR en juegos y series, el G Pro 27Qi. Más pantallas en las ofertas de informática.

articles.title: The Download: Better bionic hands and AI’s natural-gas boom
articles.text:
The Download: Better bionic hands and AI’s natural-gas boom
Plus: SpaceX has won approval to launch 1 million data center satellites.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he's cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it's wired up to nerves in his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, or a loved one's hand.
Davidson is the ninth person to have this experimental device implanted, but he's the first to take it home and use it independently. Researchers hope his experiences will reveal how useful the technology really is in day-to-day life, and how it might affect his brain and nervous system.
Find out how a new generation of prosthetics is learning to feel.
—Jessica Hamzelou
How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
— Casey Crownhart
In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote about how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I've lost count of how many times he's been proven right.
Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on have expanded, and the local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. Meanwhile, Meta's emissions are up 45% over last year's.
Across the US, natural gas has become the default to meet exploding power demand. Here’s what that means for the future of the grid.
This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 SpaceX has won approval to launch 1 million data center satellites
The FCC says they'll help meet AI computing demand. (Reuters $)
+ But they could overcrowd the orbit and obscure the stars. (Bloomberg $)
+ SpaceX must start deploying them by 2033 under its license. (BBC)
+ Europe has opened a megafactory to build a Starlink rival. (CNBC)
+ Can data centers really work in orbit? (MIT Technology Review)
2 The US Army just blew up nearly five tons of unstable explosives
The EPA reports ‘zero’ airborne lead following the detonation. (Verge)
+ Scientists are now testing soil and water for contamination. (Wired $)
+ Officials were criticized for poor communication beforehand. (Axios)
3 Earth just had its first six-day streak above 2°C
Scientists say it’s an early warning of what's to come. (Guardian)
4 Ukraine has claimed the first-ever laser takedown of a jet drone
Its Blysk laser downed a Russian kamikaze drone. (Bloomberg $)
5 Neuralink has won approval for a brain-implant trial in ALS patients
It's the final stage of testing before seeking market clearance. (Gizmodo)
+ China is racing to catch up in brain-computer interfaces. (SCMP)
+ A BCI gave a man with ALS his voice back. (MIT Technology Review)
6 Hackers have breached the US Treasury's financial crime watchdog
It's taken systems used to report money laundering offline. (FT $)
7 Bankrupt startup Character.ai wants to sell millions of user chats
42 attorneys general are trying to block the sale. (TechCrunch)
8 The hunt for dark matter is getting weirder
Scientists are using levitating magnets and nuclear clocks. (Quanta)
+ Dark matter's hiding places keep growing. (MIT Technology Review)
9 Scientists used seabird spies to track ships that had gone dark
Recorders on the birds detected ships with trackers off. (404 Media)
10 This Thanksgiving, AI is becoming a popular sous-chef
But food bloggers say its recipes are often "total nonsense." (Axios)
Quote of the day
“Hey, by the way, this might be the last time we see each other—potentially, probably not, but maybe—because of AI.”
—Daniel Kokotajlo, former OpenAI researcher and author of the "AI 2027" forecast, tells The New York Times how he plans to bring up AI extinction risks with his wife’s family this Thanksgiving.
One more thing
AI models flub these intelligence tests. Can you fare any better?
Judged purely on its puzzling skills, AI is improving a lot—and quickly. In late 2024, even the best models could figure out only 18% of the infamous New York Times Connections puzzles; by early 2025, some could solve them nearly perfectly.
But puzzles do more than highlight AI's progress. Seeing where models succeed and fail, and where humans still beat them, offers a window into the technology's strengths and weaknesses.
We've gathered seven puzzles that have stumped models. Try them yourself to find out whether you can outsmart AI.
—Grace Huckins
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)
+ Fly across the universe in this interactive map of space.
+ A film industry analyst has produced a fascinating, data-driven look at movie shots and cuts.
+ They say F1 cars corner like they're on rails, so Red Bull Racing put one on an actual railway line.
+ Travel like 007 with License to Locate, which maps every James Bond filming location, from Jamaica to Venice.
Deep Dive
The Download
The Download: the agentic web arrives and the drive for safer roads
Plus: A $1 trillion tech selloff has deepened fears of an AI bubble.
The Download: dead startups fueling AI and interspecies communication
Plus: Hackers have disrupted the US Federal Election Commission’s website.
The Download: testing tech promises and searching for cognitive immortality
Plus: Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia CEO.
The Download: AI agent tracking and climate feedback loops
Plus: Hackers exposed 41,000 Homeland Security workers.
Stay connected
Get the latest updates from
MIT Technology Review
Discover special offers, top stories, upcoming events, and more.

articles.title: The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
articles.text:
This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend.
The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
Many of our favorite gadgets and gizmos are cheaper than they’ve been all year, making now the perfect time to shop.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge. With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. We’ll provide context when possible and keep this post updated throughout the day.
AirPods Pro 3
Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.
Disney Plus, Hulu Bundle
You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.
Anker Universal Charger (100W)
Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.
Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle
The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.
HBO Max
An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly, ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.
Kindle Paperwhite (2024)
Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches)
SwitchBot Bot Rechargeable
Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.
Sony WH-1000XM4C
Sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.
Sonos Play
The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.
Apple AirTag (second-gen)
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus
Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.
Zepath USB-C Li-ion AA Batteries
Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.
Samsung P9 microSD Express Card
The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.
Apple iPad (11th generation)
Apple’s 11th-gen iPad is the successor to the previous 10-gen model. It has a new A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.
Peacock
Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.
Xteink X4 Classic pocket e-reader
With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.
Oura Ring 5
The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.
007 First Light
007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.
Apple Watch Series 12
The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.
Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver
Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.
Anker Laptop Power Bank
Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.
Nothing Ear 3A earbuds
You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.
Lego Project Hail Mary set
Outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary. And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.
Hoto 3.6V Electric Screwdriver Kit Pro
Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.
Sony DualSense Wireless Controller
Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.
MacBook Neo
Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.
Ember Mug 3 (14-ounce)
Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.
LG B6E OLED TV
Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.
JBL Tour One M3
JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.
Iniu P55-E2 Power Bank (10,000mAh)
Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.
Hisense CanvasTV (2026)
Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.
Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo
The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.
Moft Trackable Tripod Wallet
Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.
Govee Table Lamp 2
Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.
Eufy Omni C28
The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.
Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K
Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.
Sharge Icemag 3 Power Bank
The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.
Saros
Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.
Bose QuietComfort Headphones Gen 2
Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”
Dreame X60 Ultra
The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.
Garmin Forerunner 265S
Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.
Samsung The Frame (2025)
Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.
TP-Link Tapo Matter-Certified Smart Plug Mini
TP-Link’s smart smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms, and lets you set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.
Pixel Buds 2a
Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.
Roku Pro Series 4K OLED TV
Roku now makes some of the most affordable, yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.
Alienware AW2726DM QD-OLED monitor
If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.
Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro
Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.
Beats Powerbeats Pro 2
The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.
Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike
The big difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.
Yoto Mini (2024) speaker
A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.
Nex Playground
The Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.
Apple AirPods Max (second-gen)
Nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some new features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.
Govee Uplighter Floor Lamp
It’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.
Meta Quest 3S
The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.
Ghost of Yōtei
Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.
Beats 360 headphones
The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.
Donkey Kong Bananza
Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.
Lego Mandalorian N-1 Starfighter
Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.
Amazon Alexa Photo Frame
A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.
Aqara Smart Lock U400
This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It will also work with the new Aliro standard and be compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking.
Twelve South AirFly SE
Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.
Catan (6th Edition)
In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.
Control Resonant
Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.
Kodak Charmera Keychain Digital Camera
The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.
Birdbuddy Pro (solar)
Birdbuddy’s charming, camera-equipped feeder identifies and snaps shots of each bird that stops by, supplementing its 5-megapixel stills with insightful facts via an app. The solar roof helps keep the camera’s battery topped up even when it’s cloudy outside.
Azul
Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.
Magna-Tile Classic 32 Piece Set
Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge, especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.
Lego Botanicals Mini Bonsai Trees set
Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.
Sonos Beam (Gen 2)
The Beam isn’t as powerful as the Sonos Arc, nor can it match the flagship soundbar’s Dolby Atmos immersion bubble. But you still get room-filling surround sound for less money — and the Beam ties into the Sonos ecosystem for added convenience. Read our review.
Google Pixel 11 Pro
Google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging. Read our review.
Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow
Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.
Insta360 Link 2
The Insta360 Link 2 offers the same auto-swiveling design as its excellent predecessor, only in a smaller form factor. It also offers a slate of new features, including group tracking and no-follow zones.
CMF Buds 2A
With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.
Fanttik X9 Pro Portable Tire Inflator
The Fanttik X9 Pro can inflate a car tire in under a minute, making routine maintenance fast and easy. There are four one-click presets for cars, motorcycles, bikes, and balls, along with a manual mode that reaches a maximum pressure of 150 PSI.
Philips Hue Festavia string lights
These smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible.
Wuben G5 rechargeable flashlight
The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.
Anker 140W 2-in-1 USB-C to USB-C Cable
No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.
Echo Dot Max
The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.
Glocusent Bookmark Style Reading Light
Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.
Vantage
Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan, but it is far more interesting.
LIFX Everyday Smart Light Bulbs (two-pack)
LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they fit seamlessly into any major smart home platform. Best of all, the smart features come at a price that makes buying multipacks more affordable than other brands.
SwitchBot Standing Circulator Fan
A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.
JBL Go 4
The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.
Fairphone 6 Plus
Fairphone’s latest is a very light update to the 6, adding a newer processor and carrying forward its repairability and ethical values. Tradeoffs compared to a traditional smartphone are few, and the benefits are real.
Ugreen Nexode 240W USB-C Cable with Digital Display
The proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.
Apple Watch SE 3
The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Omata AI turns WhatsApp into a business operating system for SMEs
articles.text:
Nigerian startup Omata AI has built a WhatsApp-native business operating system that helps small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) manage their day-to-day operations through simple conversations.
The flagship product of Autonomous Data Enterprise, a company founded in 2026 by Stanley Okafor, Omata AI lets merchants record sales, manage inventory, track customer balances and monitor business performance by sending WhatsApp messages. A connected dashboard gives them more oversight.
“Our vision is to make business management as easy as sending a WhatsApp message,” Okafor told Disrupt Africa. “For example, a trader can send a message such as, “I sold two bags of rice for NGN50,000”, and Omata AI can interpret the information, prepare a structured transaction and request the merchant’s approval before confirmation.”
Okafor said that many small businesses across Africa still rely on notebooks, memory and scattered WhatsApp chats to manage their records. Existing accounting, POS and inventory tools are often too complex or too costly for them.
“Rather than asking merchants to adapt to complicated software, we want business software to adapt to the way they already operate,” he said.
The startup’s main differentiator is what Okafor calls a “human-approval-first” architecture. Under this design, AI cannot change financial records without the business owner’s sign-off.
“Unlike a general-purpose chatbot, a business-management system cannot afford to misinterpret figures or process the same transaction repeatedly,” he said.
Omata AI is founder-funded and pre-revenue. It is currently working with 10 merchants in early-stage pilots, and it is entered in the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026. The startup plans to adopt a subscription model with affordable entry-level plans for individual traders.
“We are prioritising product validation, merchant feedback and operational reliability rather than aggressively scaling user numbers,” Okafor said.
The startup is focused on Nigeria for now but plans a gradual expansion into other African markets where WhatsApp is widely used for business.

articles.title: 6 Best Affordable WordPress Hosts for Small WooCommerce Stores
articles.text:
A store with only a few orders a day can still lose an afternoon of work when a plugin update goes wrong. Restoring yesterday’s backup may bring the site back, while leaving today’s orders out of the restored database. Low traffic does not make that recovery problem disappear.
Small stores can find affordable hosting with useful recovery tools, but the costs and restore controls vary. Prices are in United States dollars. Taxes, optional extras and later domain renewals cost more.
Check checkout separately from product pages
Low-cost WooCommerce hosting needs to cover both shopping and the work of putting a store back together. Product pages can often use cached copies [1]. Carts, customer accounts and checkout [2] need fresh data as people shop. A fast catalog page alone says little about how checkout will behave. A useful test follows a customer through adding an item to the cart. It should include changing the amount, using a discount and paying for the order. That work should use the store’s actual plugins and a test payment method. Any plan can look right in a feature list while the store’s mix of plugins still needs work.
1. SiteGround GrowBig for staging and planned changes
SiteGround [3] GrowBig suits a small store whose owner expects to change plugins, layouts or payment settings often. Its staging tool gives the owner a place to test those changes before they reach the live site. On-demand backups also let the owner save a copy before a planned update. The store can keep that copy as well as its scheduled backups.
GrowBig costs $4.99 a month for the first 12 months, paid in advance, or $59.88 for that term. It renews at $29.99 a month, or $359.88 for a year at that rate. The owner needs to budget for that later bill from the start. A low first-year price does not make the plan cheap in later years.
The plan includes 50 gigabytes of storage, managed WordPress updates, caching, email and migration. StartUp costs less and can host a single small store, but GrowBig is the more useful comparison when staging and on-demand backups matter. The buyer should not assume StartUp has those tools just because both plans run WordPress.
Staging needs a careful store workflow. A test copy can fall out of date as live orders arrive. Replacing the live database with an older staging database can erase changes made by customers. The owner should decide which files or settings to move before making the changes live.
GrowBig still needs a checkout test with the store’s theme, payment method and plugins. Before upgrading, check whether the account can handle those requests well. The number of product pages alone will not answer that question.
2. GreenGeeks Premium for a small store with restore controls
GreenGeeks [4] offers Premium for busy websites and small stores. It includes 100 gigabytes of storage, LiteSpeed optimization and caching, automatic WordPress updates, daily backups and migration, subject to the migration terms. Live chat and ticket support are open around the clock.
The first-term rate is $8.95 a month with 12 months paid in advance. That makes the first hosting term $107.40. The plan then renews at $30.95 a month, or $371.40 for a year at that rate. A store looking at Premium needs to budget for that later bill as well as the first year.
Premium and Pro include on-demand backup and restore features. Lite uses a different restore process. The cheapest plan does not offer the same way to get a site back. For a store, the choice affects who can start a restore and how the work gets done.
Daily backups can still leave recent orders outside the available recovery point. Before opening the store, its owner should check how to restore an older site and keep newer order records. Caching also needs to respect carts and checkout. Premium is aimed at small stores, but that does not prove how fast checkout will be or how many sales it can handle.
3. Hostinger Unlimited when a long commitment fits the budget
Hostinger Unlimited offers daily backups and 50 gigabytes of storage, while the cheaper Premium plan has weekly backups. Unlimited is the more useful plan to compare for a store that changes throughout the week. With a weekly backup, the saved site can be much further out of date than the store’s records.
The advertised rate works out to $3.49 a month. To get it, the buyer must pay $167.52 up front for 48 months. That pays for the first four years of hosting, rather than just one year at a low price. The renewal rate shown is $16.99 a month for the same term. An owner should weigh that payment against how long the store may last and how much it may grow.
The low rate can suit a new shop that expects to use WordPress for several years. It is less useful when the owner is still testing the sales model or may need to move the store soon. A low rate does not remove the cost of paying early for years the store may never use.
Daily backups still need a restore plan. The buyer should check how to restore Unlimited before relying on its backups. That means knowing which saved copies are kept and what happens to recent orders. A saved copy helps only when the person in charge of the store knows how to use it. The hosting mailboxes are also free for only the first year. A store that uses them to email customers needs to budget for that later cost.
4. Bluehost eCommerce Essentials for included store tools
Bluehost’s eCommerce Essentials plan installs WooCommerce for the owner and includes store tools. It may be worth the cost when those tools replace extensions the store would have to buy on their own. A store that needs only a basic catalog and checkout should compare the package with the lower WordPress tiers before paying for the larger bundle.
The current offer is $14.99 a month for 36 months. The service costs $539.64 for that term. Renewal is listed at $21.99 a month. That is more to pay up front than the plans with a one-year term here, even if the monthly rate seems within budget. The value depends on which tools the shop will use.
The plan includes 100 gigabytes of storage, managed WordPress updates, a website security certificate, a content delivery network and a migration tool. These features help run the site, but its scheduled backups are weekly. A store with daily orders needs to decide whether to pay for an extra backup service. That cost needs to be part of the plan comparison.
The first upgrade may therefore be a recovery service rather than a larger hosting plan. Buying more storage would not close a gap between backup points. Before choosing the plan, the owner should price the extensions it replaces. Then add the cost of any backup or order-recovery service the store still needs. The business email offer is a trial, so staff mail may cost more once it ends.
5. DreamHost Launch for a low-cost starting account
A small WooCommerce store with modest needs can use DreamHost’s Web Hosting Launch plan, which supports WordPress. The annual offer costs $2.89 a month, with $34.68 paid for the first year. It renews at $10.99 a month. The first-year cost is easy to compare with other one-year offers. There is no need to divide a four-year payment to work out a price for one year.
Launch includes 25 gigabytes of storage, daily automated backups, a website security certificate and a first-year domain offer. Its limit of 25 websites does not mean it can host 25 equally busy stores. The account still has to do the work those sites need.
DreamHost also gives an estimate of how many visits a month the plan can serve. For a store, that estimate cannot replace a checkout test. Customers who search products, log in and place orders create a different workload from visitors reading cached pages. A store can need more resources before it reaches that broad visit estimate.
Launch is most useful here as a modest initial hosting purchase. Before changing a live store, the owner should check how long backups are kept and how to restore them. They should also check whether they need a separate staging tool. Included email lasts only for a 3-month trial, so the owner needs to budget for customer-service mail after that.
6. HostArmada Start Dock for a single-store account
HostArmada [5] Start Dock offers a single website with 15 gigabytes of storage and 7 daily backup copies, with free restores. An owner can use that history to judge how far back a restore could go. A fault discovered several days after an update may require an older copy, even when the website appeared to work immediately afterward.
The first 12 months cost $2.15 a month, for a first-year service total of $25.80. It renews at $11.95 a month, or $143.40 for a year at that rate. The account also includes cPanel and one website migration, with phone, chat and ticket support available around the clock.
The higher Web Warp and Speed Reaper tiers retain 14 and 21 daily backup copies respectively. Those older copies may matter more than extra storage when the store needs to fix a fault found days later. They still do not provide a fresh copy after every order.
Start Dock offers a low-cost account for one store with a set backup history. Before paying, the owner should check how to request a restore and how long it may take. They also need to know how to keep order records created after the chosen backup.
Choose the recovery window before choosing the plan
The store owner should decide how much missing order history the business could piece back together. A shop with a few manual orders may accept a daily backup and written steps for matching up its records. A shop with orders throughout the day may need database backups more often, or a service that records each change as it happens.
That requirement should become a test before launch. On a test copy, the person responsible for the store can create a sample order, take a backup, create another order and then rehearse the recovery. The exercise should show which records return, which disappear and what evidence remains with the payment provider. A successful page restore alone does not answer those questions.
The owner should also write down who can access backups, who contacts support and who decides when checkout can reopen. Once those steps are clear, the owner can compare plans with those needs in mind. The affordable plan is the one that fits the store’s workload and recovery needs at its ongoing cost, including any extra service needed to protect recent orders.

articles.title: Cuisinart Tri Zone : un airfryer prometteur qui cuit aussi la pizza, mais un détail en plastique peut tout bloquer
articles.text:
| Commodité d'emploi |  | 
| Dimensions (L x H x P) | 380 x 390 x 400 | 
| Capacité | 8.6 L | 
| Programmes de cuisson | Oui | 
| Cuisson |  | 
| Puissance | 2000 W | 
| Température min | 80 °C | 
| Température max | 210 °C | 
Deux paniers pour cuire le poulet et les frites et, juste en dessous, un petit four assez large pour une pizza. Avec le Tri Zone, Cuisinart réserve aussi une place aux amateurs de feuilletés. Nous avons mis les trois tiroirs à contribution.
Une pizza de 30 cm de diamètre dans un airfryer à double panier ? Las, il faut généralement se résoudre à la couper en parts, mais Cuisinart a trouvé où la loger entière. Sous les deux cuves de 4,3 l du Tri Zone, une large poignée ouvre effectivement un troisième tiroir qui occupe toute la largeur de l'appareil. Il abrite un petit four de 5 l capable de monter à 230 °C. La pizza a ainsi son étage et les frites peuvent garder le leur.
Proposé lors de sa sortie à 199 €, le Cuisinart Tri Zone (AFT13XSSE) totalise donc 13,6 l. Pour un poulet et son accompagnement, on dispose de 8,6 l répartis dans deux paniers que l'on peut régler séparément. Les 5 l restants se prêtent aux préparations que l'on étale sur une plaque, comme une tarte ou une fournée de biscuits. De quoi envisager ce Cuisinart en guise de petit four dans un logement qui en serait dépourvu, à condition de lui trouver une place à demeure.
Avec 38 cm de large, 39 cm de haut et 40 cm de profondeur, le Tri Zone prend ses aises dans la cuisine. C'est surtout au moment de le soulever qu'on mesure ce à quoi l'on s'engage. Avec ses 10,9 kg, autant dire qu'on réfléchira à deux fois avant de lui attribuer une étagère en hauteur.
Cuisinart demande de laisser 5 à 10 cm entre l'appareil et le mur pour que l'air chaud puisse s'évacuer. On aurait bien posé le plat de service sur le dessus pendant qu'on sort les paniers, mais la notice interdit d'y déposer quoi que ce soit. Il faut donc lui garder une place à côté.
Derrière la façade noire et inox, la cavité est entièrement métallique. Une fois les tiroirs retirés, on distingue bien les deux résistances supérieures, chacune au-dessus de son panier, et la résistance qui court sous le plateau du four.
Dans les cuves du haut, une plaque perforée surélève les aliments et laisse les jus s'écouler au fond. Ces paniers offrent chacun un volume de cuisson utile de 330 cm² pour 10 cm de hauteur intérieure. À vide, un tiroir pèse 910 g et se saisit d'une main par sa poignée pour remuer les frites.
Cuisinart annonce des revêtements antiadhésifs sans PFAS. Les plaques perforées se soulèvent par le centre pour libérer l'accès au fond des cuves. Les paniers et leurs plaques passent au lave-vaisselle, même si le fabricant conseille de les laver à la main pour en prolonger la durée de vie. Pour les parois métalliques, la notice préconise un chiffon humide.
Sur le bandeau tactile, on touche L à gauche ou R à droite pour régler le panier correspondant, et B un peu plus bas pour le four. Les deux paniers donnent accès aux mêmes six modes. Air Fry, Roast, Grill et Bake couvrent les usages les plus courants, auxquels s'ajoutent la déshydratation et Re Crisp pour redonner du croustillant à un reste. Dans le tiroir du bas, le choix se resserre autour des modes Pizza, Toast et Manuel. On sélectionne ensuite le thermomètre ou l'horloge pour ajuster son réglage.
Les habitués des airfryers retrouveront assez vite leurs marques. Pour les autres, un coup d'œil au manuel en français est bienvenu, car le panneau est intégralement en anglais. Entre Match Settings et Sync Cooking, notamment, le choix dépend de ce qu'on met dans les cuves. Des frites dans les deux ? La première touche copie le mode, la température et la durée d'un panier sur l'autre. Du poulet d'un côté et des pommes de terre de l'autre ? La seconde coordonne la fin des deux cuissons en conservant les réglages propres à chaque plat. Le four a sa propre minuterie.
En mode Air Fry, un signal invite à secouer le panier à mi-cuisson. La touche Shake Reminder permet de le désactiver. Pour savoir si le poulet commence à dorer, il suffit d'appuyer sur la petite ampoule du côté concerné. Les deux fenêtres éclairées permettent de surveiller chaque préparation en laissant les tiroirs fermés. On aurait volontiers retrouvé la même fenêtre un étage plus bas, où il faut tirer le plateau pour constater l'avancée de la cuisson.
Une fois les commandes assimilées, reste à savoir combien de temps donner aux frites. Pas de livret de recettes, d'application ni de tableau de cuisson pour se repérer selon le poids de pommes de terre. La notice conseille de bien répartir les morceaux dans le panier. Pour la minuterie, il faut tâtonner.
En manipulant l'un des paniers, nous avons cassé le petit ergot en plastique qui signale sa fermeture à l'appareil. Même en sélectionnant le panier intact, impossible de lancer la cuisson. Nous avons heureusement retrouvé le morceau et pu poursuivre le test après l'avoir recollé. Vu les conséquences de la casse sur notre exemplaire, ce contact de fermeture mériterait d'être plus robuste.
À 160 °C, il faut compter 3 min 24 s de montée en température pour le premier panier et 3 min 38 s pour le second. Dans le premier tiroir, nos trois sondes suivent des cycles assez proches. On relève en moyenne 156 °C au centre, 159 °C dans le coin inférieur gauche et 154 °C dans le coin supérieur droit. Le second panier reste lui aussi un peu en retrait de la consigne, avec des moyennes comprises entre 153 et 158 °C. Cette fois, c'est au centre que la moyenne est la plus basse.
En poussant le réglage à 200 °C, l'écart de vitesse se creuse. Le premier tiroir demande 4 min 50 s, le second 6 min 2 s, soit plus d'une minute de différence pour deux paniers pourtant identiques. Dans le premier, les trois sondes enregistrent des moyennes comprises entre 192 et 196 °C. Dans le second, les deux coins se tiennent autour de 195 °C, tandis que le centre plafonne à 198,9 °C et affiche tout juste 190 °C en moyenne.
Faute d'indications pour nos frites, nous sommes partis sur les 20 min proposées par défaut en mode Air Fry. Nous les avons remuées au signal de mi-cuisson. À la sonnerie, quelques bâtonnets commençaient à brunir aux extrémités, d'autres étaient encore pâles. Même les plus dorées étaient tout juste cuites. Nous avons donc ajouté 5 min. Après 25 min au total, il restait encore des morceaux insuffisamment cuits et l'ensemble manquait de croustillant.
Les cuisses de poulet nous ont donné davantage satisfaction. Elles sont ressorties bien cuites avec une peau dorée, et leur jus est resté sous la grille de leur panier.
Pour un apéritif dînatoire, nous avons garni une pâte feuilletée de pesto rouge, détaillé nos roulés puis réparti le tout sur la plaque du bas. À la dégustation, les feuilletés étaient aussi réussis que ceux que nous préparons au four traditionnel.
À 1 m de l'appareil réglé sur 200 °C sur les deux paniers, notre sonomètre indique 52 dB et 50 dB quand un seul panier est en fonction. Le souffle de ventilation s'entend dans une cuisine ouverte. Il se situe au niveau d'autres appareils de ce gabarit passés par notre labo, entre les 51 dB du Panasonic NF-BC1000 et les 53 dB du Ninja Combi SFP700 mesurés dans les mêmes conditions.
Le Cuisinart Tri Zone demande de la place, mais ses trois tiroirs ont chacun leur utilité. En haut, on peut régler séparément la cuisson de la viande et de son accompagnement, en coordonner la fin et surveiller le dorage à travers les fenêtres. Les paniers prennent toutefois leur temps pour chauffer et on aurait apprécié un tableau de cuisson pour mieux choisir les réglages dès la première fournée. C'est finalement la présence du tiroir du bas qui nous a le plus convaincus : une bonne alternative pour remplacer un petit four traditionnel dans une cuisine modeste.
Le Ninja Combi SFP700 associe air chaud et vapeur pour cuire sur deux niveaux, tandis que le Panasonic NF-BC1000 mise sur une cuve de 9,6 l, dont on retire la cloison pour faire place à un grand plat. Pour les amateurs de pizzas et de tartes qui manquent de place sur leur plan de travail, le Moulinex Easy Fry XL Surface 4L offre un format plus compact avec un tiroir assez large pour cuire une pizza entière.

articles.title: Votre Chromecast avec Google TV s’offre une seconde jeunesse grâce à cette mise à jour
articles.text:
On pensait le Chromecast avec Google TV relégué aux oubliettes par le nouveau Google TV Streamer, mais Google ne semble pas encore avoir coupé le cordon. Onze mois après le dernier patch, le géant de Mountain View vient de déployer un nouveau firmware pour sa clé TV lancée il y a six ans déjà. Cette mise à jour vient prolonger la durée de l’appareil, toujours très populaire chez les amateurs de streaming.
Un correctif ciblé pour le streaming et la sécurité
La mise à jour déploie le patch de sécurité Android d’août 2026, remplaçant la version d’octobre 2025 installée l’an dernier. Google ne se contente pas de boucher les failles puisque la page officielle mentionne des améliorations sur la connectivité Wi-Fi, la stabilité du flux vidéo et le rendu de l’affichage. De nombreux bugs sont également balayés au passage, venant ainsi rendre la navigation plus fluide.
D’abord repéré sur le Chromecast avec Google TV (4K), le Chromecast avec Google TV (HD) reçoit aussi une mise à jour (voir ci-dessus). Si vous ne voulez pas attendre la notification de mise à jour, vous pouvez la lancer manuellement en vous rendant dans les paramètres du système, puis dans « À propos > Mise à jour du système ».
Le Chromecast avec Google TV toujours debout
Pour les plus bidouilleurs, ce correctif pourrait corriger la faille sabrina-unlock-v2 qui est utilisée par la communauté pour déverrouiller le bootloader et installer des systèmes alternatifs comme LineageOS. Cette vulnérabilité serait donc bloquée, même si Google n’a pas confirmé l’information officiellement. Les utilisateurs de ROMs personnalisées devront donc vérifier à deux fois avant de valider l’installation.
À lire : Le Chromecast avec Google TV gagne une des meilleures fonctionnalités de son successeur
Commercialisé en 2020 puis retiré du catalogue il y a deux ans, le Chromecast avec Google TV continue donc son chemin. Face à la hausse globale du prix des lecteurs multimédias, pouvoir conserver ce petit dongle reste donc une bonne affaire. Même si Google pousse désormais son nouveau TV Streamer, on ne refusera pas des mises à jour pour les anciens modèles.
