articles.title: Nvidia prepara un recorte de hasta el 30 % en el suministro de GPU para jugadores
articles.text:
Nvidia podría reducir entre un 20 % y un 30 % el suministro de chips destinados a las tarjetas gráficas para videojuegos durante el trimestre comprendido entre noviembre de 2026 y enero de 2027. La medida, que todavía no ha sido confirmada por la compañía, genera preocupación entre los fabricantes y los usuarios de PC, debido a sus posibles efectos en la disponibilidad de estos componentes y en sus precios.
La información fue difundida por el medio especializado VideoCardz, donde se señala que Nvidia habría comunicado a sus socios una nueva reducción en la asignación de chips para tarjetas gráficas. De concretarse, sería un segundo recorte consecutivo en ese mercado, después de una disminución registrada durante el trimestre anterior.
Por ahora, no existen detalles que permitan determinar si la medida afectará a todos los mercados o si se centrará unicamente en Asia. Nvidia tampoco ha emitido un comunicado oficial sobre estos reportes.
Por qué Nvidia reduciría el suministro de tarjetas gráficas
Uno de los factores que explicaría este posible recorte es la creciente demanda de componentes para inteligencia artificial. Nvidia se ha convertido en uno de los principales proveedores de procesadores utilizados en centros de datos, donde las empresas tecnológicas necesitan cada vez más capacidad de cálculo para entrenar y ejecutar modelos de inteligencia artificial.
Estos centros de datos requieren chips especializados y otros componentes de alto rendimiento. Ante la fuerte demanda de este sector, los fabricantes deben distribuir sus recursos entre diferentes líneas de productos, incluidas las tarjetas gráficas destinadas a videojuegos.
Los reportes apuntan a que Nvidia estaría priorizando los componentes relacionados con la inteligencia artificial frente a las GPU para el mercado de consumo. Sin embargo, esta explicación todavía no ha sido confirmada por la empresa.
La situación refleja un cambio en el negocio de Nvidia. Aunque sus tarjetas GeForce siguen siendo importantes para los jugadores y creadores de contenido, el crecimiento de los centros de datos ha convertido al negocio de inteligencia artificial en uno de sus principales motores económicos.
Las tarjetas gráficas podrían subir de precio
Una reducción en el suministro de GPU podría generar dificultades para los fabricantes que dependen de los chips de Nvidia para producir sus tarjetas gráficas. Si reciben menos unidades, tendrán menos productos disponibles para distribuir entre tiendas y consumidores.
El efecto también podría trasladarse a los precios. Cuando la oferta de un producto disminuye y la demanda se mantiene elevada, los distribuidores pueden incrementar sus tarifas, especialmente si existen pocas alternativas disponibles.
En diferentes mercados ya se han reportado movimientos en los precios de distribución de algunos modelos. Entre los ejemplos mencionados figuran la GeForce RTX 5090 D V2, cuyo precio habría aumentado hasta cerca de 500 dólares, y la RTX 5080, que habría alcanzado aproximadamente los 420 dólares en determinados canales de distribución.
Estas cifras corresponden a reportes sobre precios mayoristas y no representan necesariamente los valores que pagan los consumidores en las tiendas. Tampoco permiten anticipar cuánto podrían costar estas tarjetas gráficas en otros países.
Fabricantes como Colorful y GALAX también aparecen mencionados en los reportes relacionados con posibles ajustes de precios. No obstante, todavía no hay información suficiente para establecer el alcance de estos cambios.
Qué pasará con las tarjetas gráficas para PC
Si el recorte se concreta, los jugadores podrían encontrar menos unidades disponibles de determinados modelos de Nvidia durante los próximos meses. El impacto dependerá de la cantidad de chips que reciban los fabricantes y de la capacidad del mercado para compensar la reducción con otros productos.
Una de las alternativas mencionadas en los reportes sería recurrir a modelos anteriores, como las RTX 3050 y RTX 3060, para cubrir parte de la demanda de quienes buscan una tarjeta gráfica más económica.
Estas GPU pertenecen a generaciones anteriores, pero todavía pueden resultar útiles para equipos de entrada y configuraciones que no necesitan ejecutar videojuegos con las opciones gráficas más exigentes.
Por otro lado, la posible reducción del suministro también genera dudas sobre el futuro de los precios de las tarjetas de gama alta, especialmente si la demanda de los jugadores se mantiene elevada.

articles.title: Los expertos lo tienen claro: el tipo de calefacción que tienes en casa determina cuánto ahorrarás este invierno
articles.text:
La bajada en el mercurio ya se ha hecho notar y muchos hogares ya han tenido que encender la calefacción en algún momento. Con el invierno a la vuelta de la esquina, este gesto se repetirá cada vez más en las próximas semanas, con el consecuente aumento de la factura. Y este año, parece que calentar la casa saldrá más caro.
Es lo que apuntan los expertos después de constatar los efectos de las tensiones en Oriente Medio y el encarecimiento de los precios de la energía: concretamente, según un estudio del comparador energético Hello Watt del que se hace eco El Español, el gasto estimado en calefacción aumentará un 48% respecto al invierno del año pasado.
El tipo de calor resulta fundamental. En declaraciones a ese medio, el director general de Hello Watt Danny Salazar ha explicado que la diferencia entre utilizar una forma de calefacción u otra puede ser abismal en términos económicos. Según este experto, los radiadores eléctricos, los calefactores y las estufas serán los que más hagan notar la subida en términos absolutos.
Con los radiadores eléctricos, de hecho, el estudio señala que un hogar que consuma 4.000 kWh de calor útil pagaría unos 1.017 euros entre octubre y marzo. El año pasado, ese mismo hogar, con el mismo consumo, habría pagado unos 688 euros. Eso supone pagar unos 329 euros más, que se traducen a su vez en un incremento del 48%, siguiendo el precio medio estimado del PVPC de 25,4 céntimos por KWh con impuestos.
La bomba de calor, una de las mejores opciones. Sin embargo, no todo está perdido y parece haber opciones más baratas. Un split de aire acondicionado con bomba de calor, en esas mismas condiciones, tendría un gasto estimado de unos 339 euros en la época de frío. Es decir, 678 euros menos que con los radiadores eléctricos. La bomba de calor permitiría reducir el gasto en calefacción en torno a un 67%. Tanto es así que la OCU considera las bombas de calor como uno de los sistemas de calefacción más eficientes y rentables para los próximos años.
Sin embargo, otros expertos no se dejan llevar ciegamente por el entusiasmo y avisan de que para que este método caliente de verdad un hogar se necesita cumplir de antemano algunas condiciones. Jordi Martí es arquitecto y, según recoge El Confidencial, existen razones por las que muchas personas que se pasan a las bombas de calor no consiguen notar luego el confort o el ahorro previstos. El problema suele estar en el tipo de vivienda y en el aislamiento del edificio. Si la bomba de calor tiene que trabajar a temperaturas muy altas para mantener una estancia confortable, puede perder eficiencia. «Lo que quiere la bomba de calor es ir tranquila, es cuando brilla, no le pidas mucha potencia», explica este profesional.
La aerotermia, muy eficiente a la larga. Otro de los sistemas de calefacción más novedosos e interesantes es la aerotermia, un método de climatización que, como cuenta la OCU, ha ganado mucho protagonismo en los últimos meses, sobre todo con el encarecimiento de los combustibles fósiles. Es hasta cuatro veces más eficiente que una caldera de gasóleo y, por ello, resulta especialmente interesante para hogares donde no llega la red de gas natural o que tengan una caldera antigua que necesite una reforma integral.
El Español también coincide en que es la alternativa más económica en consumo, aunque también destaca que precisa de una mayor inversión inicial.
¿Y qué hay del gas? Según el estudio de Hello Watt, calentar la vivienda con gas tendría un coste estimado de unos 315 euros, algo menos que los 339 de la bomba de calor. Pero ojo, porque hay truco: esta estimación se debe al tope que hay actualmente vigente de la tarifa regulada (TUR), que mantiene el precio del gas en 5,04 céntimos por kWh sin impuestos, hasta el 31 de diciembre. En enero, se mantiene este tope, aunque se contempla la posibilidad de una subida del 15% y el precio por kWh pasaría a ser de unos 5,58 céntimos.
Sin embargo, esto no cuenta toda la historia: ese ahorro responde al mecanismo de ajuste de la tarifa regulada, que podría trasladar costes a las facturas posteriores, a partir de 2027. Según Hello Watt, esa deuda ascendería a unos 97 euros en total por toda la temporada de invierno, de modo que el coste energético del gas este invierno sería de unos 412 euros. De nuevo, más que la bomba de calor.

articles.title: GIVA raises Rs 90 Cr from alternative credit platform BlackSoil
articles.text:
GIVA raises Rs 90 Cr from alternative credit platform BlackSoil
GIVA said it will use the capital to fund store expansion and working capital requirements as it strengthens its omnichannel presence across India.
Jewellery brand GIVA has raised Rs 90 crore from alternative credit platform BlackSoil. This comes less than a month after the company announced a funding round of over $100 million led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management, alongside existing investors Epiq Capital and Edelweiss Discovery Fund.
The capital will support GIVA's store-related capital expenditure and working capital requirements as the company expands its retail network and strengthens its omnichannel presence, it said in a statement.
Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Bengaluru, GIVA focuses on everyday jewellery, catering primarily to Indian consumers. The brand is backed by several prominent celebrities, including Kriti Sanon and Anushka Sharma. Its portfolio spans 92.5 silver, gold, gold-plated, rose gold-plated, and lab-grown diamond jewellery.
GIVA follows an omnichannel distribution model through its own retail stores, D2C website and third-party ecommerce and quick-commerce marketplaces. The company has also been expanding its manufacturing capabilities and offline presence.
“As we continue to grow GIVA's retail presence, building the right financial and operational capabilities is important to supporting our expansion. Our partnership with BlackSoil will support our store expansion plans and working capital requirements as we scale our omnichannel business. We continue to focus on making design-led jewellery more accessible to consumers while building a wider and stronger retail network across India,” said Ishendra Agarwal, Founder & CEO, GIVA.
"GIVA has established a strong brand presence in India's D2C jewellery space, supported by its product range, growth and omnichannel presence. Its strong brand recognition, performance as well as association with reputed investors made it a compelling prospect to support. The funding from us will enable GIVA to meet its expansion and working capital requirements," said Ankur Bansal, Managing Director, BlackSoil.
The company currently retails through more than 400 stores across India and Sri Lanka.

articles.title: After a decade in Nigeria, Bolt is looking beyond rides
articles.text:
When Bolt, the Estonian mobility company, launched as Taxify in Lagos in November 2016, it entered a market where Uber, the American ride-hailing giant, had already established a lead after arriving two years earlier.
By July 2016, Uber had completed more than one million trips across Lagos and Abuja. Taxify was not only competing with an established rival; it also had to win commuters over from yellow taxis and public transportation by offering another way to get around.
A decade later, Nigeria’s ride-hailing market looks very different. Yellow taxis have lost most of their prominence, while the market has attracted other international players like inDrive, and local operators such as LagRide and Rida. In September, Uber announced it was winding down its Nigerian operations, marking the exit of the company that had once led the market.
Meanwhile, Bolt has expanded its footprint to 31 cities and says it has reached more than 14 million riders in Nigeria since it entered the market. The company also says it has invested more than ₦140 billion ($102.4 million) in the country. Beyond ride-hailing, it has expanded into other ride categories, vehicle financing, food delivery and electric mobility.
Early beginnings and price wars
Weyinmi Aghadiuno, Bolt’s Head of Regulatory and Policy, Africa, said Bolt entered into Nigeria at a time when getting around the country’s cities was often unpredictable.
“When we launched as Taxify in 2016, getting around Nigerian cities was unpredictable. People mixed traditional taxis, private arrangements, and public transport, and finding a reliable ride, knowing the fare upfront or trusting the service, was hard,” she said in an email response to TechCabal on Friday. “At the same time, smartphone adoption was rising, and Nigerians were getting comfortable using their phones for everyday services. We saw those two trends meeting.”
Nigeria’s smartphone penetration stood at 30% in 2016, proving a market for app-based services to grow. However, the competitive landscape meant Taxify needed to persuade passengers to try another app while convincing drivers to switch from a familiar platform. It approached the problem with a penetration-pricing strategy at launch.
Taxify went live in Lagos, promising rides at 30% less than its closest competitors and charging drivers a 15% commission, compared with Uber’s 25%. Drivers dissatisfied with Uber’s commission structure began migrating to the new platform, allowing Taxify to build its vehicle supply.
After Taxify lowered its prices in Lagos, Uber followed with a 40% fare reduction. The move aimed to stimulate demand, and Uber said it had introduced temporary payment guarantees to protect drivers’ earnings while the new fares took effect. However, drivers were unconvinced and argued that lower fares, combined with Uber’s 25% commission, left them with less money after operating costs.
The Los Angeles Times later reported that drivers organised on WhatsApp and moved to Taxify in numbers. Bolt describes those years as building two sides of a market at once.
“Ride-hailing wasn’t unfamiliar by then, so we had to give people a reason to download Bolt and try it,” the company said. “That took awareness campaigns, onboarding support and promotions that encouraged riders to experience the service for themselves. Word of mouth did a lot of the heavy lifting. One good ride usually became a recommendation to a friend, colleague or family member.”
Taxify maintained the same pricing strategy when it launched in Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, in November 2017, offering passengers a 40% discount for the month and retaining its 15% commission on drivers’ earnings. Uche Okafor, the company’s operations manager in Nigeria at the time, said the expansion aimed to introduce more competition in the capital and lower transportation costs for commuters.
In 2018, after entering Owerri and Ibadan, Taxify launched in Benin City in December, making it the company’s fifth Nigerian city. The company said it wanted to reach markets beyond the country’s obvious commercial centres, where ride-hailing could offer passengers another transportation option and create earning opportunities for drivers.
In 2019, Taxify changed its name to Bolt, a name that the company’s founder and chief executive said was meant to evoke speed.
New ways to keep moving
As Bolt expanded its operations across Nigerian cities, it faced a market where commuters still relied on cheaper or locally established transport options. In Uyo, Akwa Ibom State in Southeastern Nigeria, tricycles had become an important part of everyday transportation after the state banned commercial motorcycles, popularly known as okada, in 2011.
Bolt said it wanted to reflect how people already moved around different cities, and in January 2020, introduced tricycle-hailing in Uyo.
“For us, mobility solutions have to be locally relevant,” Aghadiuno told TechCabal in March. “That’s why we began by integrating a transport mode that already exists and plays a significant role in local economies.”
The COVID-19 pandemic tested the resilience of Bolt’s Nigerian business. In March 2020, movement restrictions introduced to contain the spread of the disease brought economic activity in Lagos and other cities to a near standstill. This left ride-hailing companies with fewer passengers and fewer trips.
“COVID-19 was among the hardest for transport,” Aghadiuno said. “Movement restrictions and reduced economic activity hit demand directly.”
The company tried to adapt by introducing Bolt Business Delivery in April in Lagos and Abuja, connecting businesses with couriers on its platform to deliver essential goods to customers. The company also faced tougher regulatory restrictions, as Lagos State moved to enforce new licencing rules for ride-hailing platforms. Under the regulations, third-party operators with more than 1,000 drivers faced a ₦10 million ($7,138) licence fee and a ₦5 million ($3,659) annual renewal fee, raising operational costs.
Despite these setbacks, Bolt continued to expand as demand for ride-hailing services grew beyond Lagos. In September 2020, it launched in Jos, taking its Nigerian footprint to 12 cities. Femi Akin-Laguda, the company’s country manager at the time, said more Nigerians were seeking flexible ways to move around, and rising car ownership costs made access to vehicles difficult. Against the constraint of vehicle ownership, Bolt expanded into 10 more cities in December 2020, including Akure, Asaba, Warri, Kaduna, and Uyo, taking its Nigerian footprint to 21 cities.
To address the barrier of vehicle acquisition for drivers, in June 2021, Bolt partnered with Sterling Bank’s Alternative Finance to launch a vehicle financing programme to help eligible drivers buy new or used cars. It expanded the programme in November through a partnership with Metro Africa Xpress (MAX), using the mobility company’s alternative credit-scoring technology alongside Bolt’s driver activity data to assess drivers for financing.
With pandemic-era demand for delivery still strong, Bolt launched Bolt Food, its food delivery business, in Nigeria in October 2021, entering a market that already included Jumia Food and Gokada. The market opportunity was clear: In 2019, Lagos residents spent ₦827 billion ($605.3 million) eating out, according to National Bureau of Statistics data.
During the COVID-19 lockdowns, Jumia Food also recorded 30% month-on-month growth in orders. At Bolt Food’s launch, customers were offered access to over 100 restaurants on Lagos Island. The company also pitched the service as an opportunity for restaurants to reach more customers and for couriers to earn through its platform.
Tough market
As Bolt expanded its operations in Nigeria, ride-hailing’s economics became harder to manage. In February 2023, the company laid off 17 of its 70 employees in Nigeria, as part of a strategy to improve its operational processes. After the removal of the petrol subsidy in May 2023, Bolt raised its base fare from ₦650 ($0.48) to ₦800 ($0.59). However, drivers and their unions argued that the adjustment did not reflect the jump in operating costs. Disputes over fares and the commission deducted from each trip led to repeated driver protests and strikes.
Later that year, Bolt announced that it would shut down Bolt Food in Nigeria, saying it wanted to streamline resources and maximise efficiency. By then, the service said it had partnered with more than 10,000 restaurants, delivered more than a million meals and onboarded 12,000 merchants.
According to Aghadiuno, Bolt responded to these pressures by continually adjusting its services and operating model.
“Our job is to keep both sides of that equation workable: fares passengers can manage and earnings that make driving sustainable,” she said. “That means listening to both groups and regularly reassessing our services and operating model. It has also made efficiency and innovation essential. We can’t run the business the way we did in 2016 and expect it to work in today’s economy.”
She also pointed to its expanded range of services, including Bolt Comfort, the lower-cost Bolt Lite category, tricycle rides, Bolt Send and Bolt Business, as ways of serving different mobility needs. In April 2025, Bolt launched electric tricycles in Lagos, in partnership with local electric mobility company SGX Mobility. The company said its ₦140 billion ($102.4 million) investment in Nigeria covers technology, local operations, safety initiatives and engagement with drivers and passengers.
“What got us through was staying close to the market,” Bolt said, reflecting on the difficult periods it had faced. “We kept engaging with drivers, responded to changing consumer needs, worked with relevant stakeholders and kept evolving our services, without losing sight of the long-term opportunity.”
A decade after entering Nigeria, Bolt says it is operating in a market that looks different from the one it encountered in 2016. Ride-hailing has become part of everyday urban transportation, and passengers have become more discerning about what they expect from the service. The company says growth now transcends bringing more riders and drivers onto the platform, and instead is about making the platform useful across a wide range of mobility needs.
“The next decade is about depth: more value for Nigerians and a broader idea of what mobility can mean for the communities we serve,” Aghadiuno said. “That means continuing to improve the ride experience, strengthening safety, expanding relevant services and exploring opportunities across the wider mobility ecosystem.”

articles.title: Windows 11 distribue des pilotes Intel obsolètes et vulnérables via Windows update
articles.text:
Les outils de Microsoft ont visiblement un gros problème de communication. Le site allemand Deskmodder rapporte en effet que le système d’exploitation a distribué, par l’intermédiaire de Windows Update, un pilote obsolète et vulnérable déclenchant une alerte de sécurité de Microsoft Defender.
Un pilote vulnérable, mais légitime, distribué par Windows Update
C’est après avoir mis à jour un système Intel NUC de 11e génération que Deskmodder a vu s’afficher une alerte de sécurité émise par Microsoft Defender. Celle-ci a mis en lumière un problème provenant du paquet Intel Performance Driver Extension dans sa version 1.0.0.38. Ce module lié au service Intel NUC Software Studio Service et qui a pour objectif de fournir une surveillance matérielle de bas niveau, comporte une importante faille de sécurité. Une brèche qui touche plus particulièrement le composant WinRing0 de ce pilote et dont la vulnérabilité est connue depuis 2020.
Cette faille, identifiée sous la référence CVE-2020-14979 permet une élévation locale des privilèges. Cela signifie concrètement que des attaquants disposant déjà d’un accès à la machine pourraient exploiter ce pilote légitime pour mener des attaques de type Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver et ainsi contourner les protections du noyau de Windows.
Windows Update réinstalle automatiquement le pilote après suppression
Mais le plus gros problème avec ce pilote, c’est que bien qu’il soit clairement identifié comme étant vulnérable par Microsoft Defender, Windows Update continue de le distribuer. Et cela, même après l’avoir supprimé.
Le module de mise à jour de Windows ne communique pas avec l’antivirus natif et continue de le délivrer en boucle ce pilote vulnérable lors des recherches de mises à jour. Un problème de taille alors que Microsoft a dévoilé il y a quelques mois son Driver Quality Initiative, censée corriger toute seule les pilotes problématiques.

articles.title: AI wrote the code. Can your test data tell you if it works?
articles.text:
AI wrote the code. Can your test data tell you if it works?
As organizations invest in AI, many are discovering a new bottleneck: obtaining data that is both protected and useful. Engineering teams need realistic, production-like data to validate AI-generated changes, train models, test applications, and generate business insights.
Yet, privacy initiatives can sometimes make that data harder to access, less representative of real-world conditions, or unable to preserve critical relationships between records.
The Perforce Delphix “2026 State of AI and Data Privacy Report” highlights this challenge. Among surveyed organizations, 26% say privacy controls make production-quality data harder to obtain, 25% struggle to preserve relationships across data entities, and 51% cite data quality challenges.
“Protecting data isn’t enough if it can no longer support the systems that depend on it.”
Protecting data isn’t enough if it can no longer support the systems that depend on it. For engineering teams, the question is whether their data protection strategies can preserve the qualities that make data valuable in the first place. You need a well-rounded data strategy with tools that maintain referential integrity and relationships across your environments.
What these statistics mean for practitioners
At first glance, statistics from the report, like “51% of enterprises cite data quality challenges,” may sound like a purely governance issue.
In practice, they represent engineering problems. Low-quality datasets can produce:
- Inaccurate analytics.
- Poorly trained AI models.
- Incomplete test coverage.
- Increased rework.
- Delayed releases.
- Reduced confidence in data automation.
“When an AI model is trained on incomplete or distorted data, its outputs become less reliable.”
When an AI model is trained on incomplete or distorted data, its outputs become less reliable. When test environments contain unrealistic data, defects can escape into production. When analytics datasets lack consistency, teams spend more time validating results than acting on them.
Data protection and utility are not opposing goals
A common misconception is that organizations must choose between privacy and innovation, but the most successful organizations know that compliance, quality, and speed can and need to work together.
Protected data still needs to be:
- Realistic enough for testing and validation.
- Representative enough for analytics.
- Accessible enough for engineering teams.
- Governed enough for regulatory requirements.
- Connected enough to preserve referential integrity.
There’s a two-fold goal in the AI era: reduce sensitive data exposure while also creating trusted data that remains valuable after protection. All too often, enterprises sacrifice compliance for innovation or speed. That’s a big reason 84% of respondents in our report have a data privacy exception in their non-production environments.
“There’s a two-fold goal in the AI era: reduce sensitive data exposure while also creating trusted data that remains valuable after protection.”
Organizations can only move at AI speed when they have access to trustworthy data that accurately represents production conditions. When privacy controls degrade quality, limit realism, or restrict access to representative datasets, the data layer becomes the new bottleneck.
Why referential integrity matters more than ever
Many discussions about data privacy focus on masking sensitive fields. However, masked data that loses referential integrity between entities can create a different kind of risk.
A customer, order, or payment record may still exist, but if the relationships connecting those records break during protection processes, the data no longer resembles reality. Take billing validation, for example. It needs referential integrity when a customer has multiple products, charges, and invoices across several database tables to produce the correct products or make accurate charges.
Broken relationships are especially problematic for modern AI and analytics systems. Analytics pipelines depend on consistent identifiers to join information across sources. AI and machine learning workflows depend on complete business context to identify patterns and make predictions. Software testing depends on realistic relationships between records to validate application behavior accurately.
When referential integrity is lost:
- Analytics can produce incomplete or misleading results.
- AI models can learn from flawed datasets.
- Testing environments can fail to expose production issues.
- Teams lose trust in protected datasets.
Importantly, these failures are often difficult to detect. Pipelines may continue running successfully while quietly producing degraded outcomes, which can be a very costly mistake.
This helps explain why 25% of surveyed organizations cited preserving relationships across data entities as a significant challenge. For practitioners, that statistic is a warning that privacy controls can unintentionally undermine the quality of AI and analytics initiatives if they fail to preserve business context.
Keep in mind that not all data protection solutions are created equal — enterprise-grade masking algorithms are key to preserving relationships. When applied consistently and at scale, these algorithms ensure the same input produces the same masked output across your systems and environments. Other masking approaches might be done piecemeal, resulting in broken relationships.
What engineering teams should measure
Many organizations measure privacy success through compliance metrics alone. However, AI-driven environments require a broader definition of success. Engineering leaders should evaluate privacy initiatives against several dimensions:
- Data quality: Does the protected dataset accurately reflect production conditions?
- Realism: Can developers, data scientists, and analysts use the data confidently for their intended purpose?
- Referential integrity: Do relationships remain consistent across applications, tables, environments, and data sources?
- Accessibility: Can teams obtain compliant data without introducing delays?
- Provisioning speed: How quickly can trusted datasets be delivered when needed?
These measurements help organizations determine whether privacy efforts enable AI outcomes or create new obstacles.
Designing for governance by default
As AI adoption grows, privacy cannot remain a separate process that occurs after development begins. Organizations should instead map the entire data lifecycle, from data request and discovery to reuse and retirement.
This approach helps ensure governance is built into workflows rather than applied as a late-stage checkpoint. It also provides stronger auditability, reduces compliance exceptions, and gives teams greater confidence that protected datasets remain fit for purpose.
Most importantly, it aligns privacy objectives with business outcomes instead of treating them as competing priorities.
Trusted data will become a competitive differentiator
The need for test data — in volume, coverage, and scale — is booming as agentic development continues to rise. AI has also increased the volume of change enterprises can generate, but the challenge of validating that change remains unsolved.
That responsibility still belongs to data. The organizations that gain the most value from AI will not necessarily be the ones with the most advanced models. They will be the ones with the most trustworthy data foundations — using a portfolio approach that combines data virtualization for speed, masking for security, and synthetic data for coverage as needed.
“In the AI era, trusted data, not fast model output, may be the ultimate competitive advantage.”
The research points to a clear lesson: If privacy controls uphold realism, quality, relationships between records, or access to representative datasets, they can enable AI success.
As enterprises continue investing in AI and data privacy, the real objective should be ensuring protection and utility coexist. Because in the AI era, trusted data, not fast model output, may be the ultimate competitive advantage.

articles.title: Stromversorgung von KI-Rechenzentren: „Dass die Gaskraftwerke viel länger genutzt werden, ist ein echtes Risiko“
articles.text:
Über 100 Gaskraftwerke geplant: Warum US-Rechenzentren auf diese Strategie setzen
Wer ein großes Rechenzentrum aufzuziehen will, muss geduldig sein: Der Knackpunkt ist vor allem, der Anschluss ans Stromnetz. Auf diese Genehmigung müssen Entwickler der Großanlagen in den Vereinigten Staaten eine lange Wartezeit einplanen. Bis zur Inbetriebnahme kann da, ähnlich wie in Europa, bis zu ein Jahrzehnt vergehen. Einige Entwickler von KI-Rechenzentren sind nicht bereit, solange zu warten. Sie setzen stattdessen auf eigene netzunabhängige Gaskraftwerke (also Energieerzeuger hinter dem Stromzähler), um am noch immer anhaltenden KI-Boom teilzuhaben.
Dieses Vorgehen hat Konsequenzen für die Anwohner:innen und die Umwelt. Der Campus von SpacexAI in Memphis setzt etwa bereits seit 2024 Dutzende Erdgasturbinen ein, einige davon sogar ohne Genehmigung. Zum Zeitpunkt der Einrichtung war diese Anlage eine Seltenheit und wurde noch von den Aufsichtsbehörden genau unter die Lupe genommen. Und sie ist auch jetzt noch Gegenstand laufender Rechtsstreitigkeiten. Abgeschreckt hat das die Entwickler von Rechenzentren nicht: im Gegenteil.

articles.title: Disney confirma el regreso de la animación 2D y explica cómo usará la IA en sus películas: «Puede aportar algo interesante»
articles.text:
Disney ya está lista para estrenar su nueva película, Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe. De nuevo, se trata de un filme realizado con la animación 3D que desde principios de siglo la compañía trata de implementar y mejorar cada año que pasa. Sin embargo, el estudio se encuentra a las puertas de un nuevo cambio en su forma de hacer cine. Y es que Disney comenzará a utilizar Inteligencia Artificial en sus películas.
Sin ir más lejos, hace unas semanas se confirmó que Disney llegaba a un acuerdo con Adobe como su socio oficial en innovación en IA. Entre otras cosas, el gigante del software proporcionará a La Casa del Ratón acceso anticipado a sus últimas tecnologías de Inteligencia Artificial, como Adobe Firefly y Adobe Firefly Foundry.
Y precisamente en Hipertextual hemos podido hablar sobre Inteligencia Artificial en Disney con uno de los máximos responsables de Disney Animation, el productor Roy Conli (El planeta del tesoro, Enredados, Big Hero 6). "Creo que la Inteligencia Artificial es una herramienta que, a medida que evoluciona, tiene que estar en manos de un artista. Siempre tiene que estar en manos de un artista", confirma en su paso por Madrid para presentar la película Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe.
"La idea de que algo se cree de la nada simplemente no me interesa", promete a su vez, desterrando la idea de que el estudio pueda prescindir de sus creativos en favor de crear películas solo con IA. "Pero si está en manos del artista, quizá pueda aportar algo interesante", sugiere en cualquier caso Conli. Es decir, en Disney están totalmente abiertos a usar la Inteligencia Artificial en sus películas, pero solo si esta está sujeta a las directrices humanas de sus trabajadores.
Vuelve la animación 2D a Disney
Al margen de la Inteligencia Artificial, Disney también se plantea otro paso en su dirección creativa en la animación. Y es que la compañía quiere recuperar la animación 2D tradicional. "Siempre formará parte de Disney Animation", nos promete Conli. De hecho, ya pueden verse algunos detalles de este cambio en Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe.
"Una de las cosas que más me entusiasma de esta película es que contamos con ese prólogo realizado por Tyler Pacana, un joven animador 2D increíble. Y también va a haber un cortometraje de animación de Lilo & Stitch, titulado Lilo & Scratch, que se proyectará junto con Hechizo. Y, en cierto modo, también rinde homenaje a aquella época de la animación dibujada a mano", revela a su vez.
En realidad, el corto de Lilo & Scratch es precisamente el experimento que Disney va a usar para recuperar la animación 2D desde un enfoque más moderno. El proyecto, tal y como se confirmó hace unos días, usará una técnica híbrida que combinará un sistema de animación 3D con cel-shading integrando elementos 2D. El objetivo es poder recuperar la estética clásica de Disney sin ralentizar los procesos actuales (trabajar en 3D es más rápido y eficiente que en 2D).
"Creo que la animación en sí misma es magia", apunta por otro lado Conli sobre el propio formato de animación. Y es que «magia», es una de las palabras clave en Disney. "Una de mis definiciones de «magia» es que es algo que aparece de la nada. Y eso es lo que es la animación. Literalmente, empezamos con una página en blanco y, de repente, cuatro años después, tienes esta magnífica historia en la pantalla", celebra.
"Además, creo que la animación es realmente un medio fantástico para representar la magia, porque en ella puedes hacer cualquier cosa. Por eso, la magia siempre ha desempeñado un papel muy importante en todas las películas de Disney", sentencia. La mejor prueba de ello es Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe, cuya premisa parte de que su protagonista descubre que es una bruja y tiene poderes mágicos.
Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe se estrena en cines el 27 de noviembre.

If you don't enjoy flossing the traditional way, use the power of water instead. Removing plaque using three different water pressure settings, this handy flosser will clean out those hard-to-reach gaps that your toothbrush can't. Plus, it's cordless, meaning you can take it on your travels too. Admittedly these were a lot cheaper in July (just over AU$48), but it was bestseller then, so it would be remiss of me to not include it here again.
The Lavazza Jolie machines are excellent and affordable alternatives to Nespresso. This Evo model just has a single button for extracting coffee (compared to the Jolie Plus that has programmable buttons), making it oh so simple to use.
This food processor's biggest drawcard is its small footprint (30cm tall and 16cm wide), making it great for those with smaller kitchens, but it also has a powerful 650W motor to help blitz foods to slice, grate, chop and knead in seconds. This is the lowest price we've seen for the MultiPro Go, and you can read the full review here.
We might be in the middle of winter, but there's no denying some parts of Australia need a good fan year round. This Vornado model creates tornado-like air flow that circulates around the room. Note that this is the smallest model in the range, ideal for bedrooms.
While often discounted to around this same price, we haven't seen the Nebula Mars 3 go lower, and it's a great deal. It serves up great brightness levels for a portable model, although you'll benefit most from watching at night.
Amazon devices
Amazon's current midrange 7-inch Kindle has dropped to cost less than its newer 6-inch sibling in this Black Friday deal, making it the best choice if you want to pick up one of Amazon's e-readers on the cheap. That said, with more storage than the standard model, a brighter screen and wireless charging, the Paperwhite Signature Edition is arguably better value than the base model above if you think you'll make full use of the storage and its wireless charging capabilities. It's currently down to AU$259, or 35% off, but only in the Metallic Jade colourway.
The Kindle Colorsoft is one of the best ereaders with a colour display, even offering a feature to make the hues more vivid. While I wouldn't recommend at full price, this discount makes it a little easier on the pocket for the 32GB version that also has wireless charging.
Kindles are known for their reading capabilities, but with the Kindle Scribe, you get that and a whole lot more. With a wide range of writing features, you can take notes, create sketches and brainstorm like a pro. I love its 10.2-inch glare-free screen with an ambient light sensor, and it's battery life is excellent too. It's now the previous-gen model, but arguably better value than the 2025 3rd-gen release.
Amazon's Echo Dot it's a great smart speaker with decent sound and Alexa built-in. It also has motion detection and can measure temperature, which is handy if you have a connected thermostat. It is a little long in the tooth now, having released in 2022, but it's a bargain at this price.
The Echo Dot Max features almost 3x the bass of the Echo Dot (5th gen), and its sound can automatically adapt to your space, making it the perfect addition to any smart home or party setup. We gave it a nice 4 stars in our review, namely for its great smart home capabilities and stellar sound. Now at its lowest-ever price.
Launched in October, the latest Echo home display devices have gotten a much-needed glow-up Echo Show 8 and the Echo Show 11. Aside from the updated in-cell touch and negative liquid crystal screens, both devices include new front-facing stereo speakers and a custom woofer for room-filling spatial audio. The key difference between the two? The Echo Show 8 has a smaller 8.7-inch display.
With all the same great features as the new Echo Show 8 above, if you're after a larger home display screen to connect to your Ring devices, check recipes while cooking or control your smart devices using Alexa, then the 11-inch Echo Show could be the move for you. Also discounted by 35%.
Headphones & Audio
We gave these earbuds a very impressive 4.5-stars in our Sony WF-C510 review, and slapped them with the 'TechRadar Recommends' award. We were so impressed, we'd actually pick these over the Apple AirPods 4. While we didn't love the 11 hours of charge provided by the case, the earbuds themselves will last 11 hours before needing to return to the case – making them equally excellent sounding, feeling and long-lasting.
These affordable earbuds with ANC are brimming with features, including a range of ANC modes, EQ presets and other audio adjustments. They sound good (but you'll want to tweak it from the default) and they'll last up to 7.5 hours with ANC on before they need a recharge. Check out our Earfun Air Pro 4 review for more info and take advantage of this offer.
The JBL Grip plugs the gap between the smaller Clip and formidable Flip. It's a compact speaker that delivers a big sound, offers impressive protection against dust and water and has some nifty LED lighting on its rear.
If you're looking for a great set of noise-cancelling over-ears but don't want to pay a lot of cash, this deal on the excellent WH-CH730N headphones is worth a look. As we said in our WH-CH730N review, they offer great value-for-money option with an excellent set of features, solid sound quality, and a nifty, foldable design,
The Beats Pill is a sturdy, classy portable speaker that you can use anywhere from the living room to the poolside, thanks to its IP67 waterproof and dustproof rating. It also has a substantial 24-hour battery life, so you can listen for a long time without worrying about recharging. This matches the last all-time low from February 2026.
Offering “incredible sound” according to our review, the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds have all the power and quality you’d expect from a Bose-branded item while providing the benefits of an open-ear form factor. The Immersive sound is excellent, and they give up to 7 hours of music. While they have been slightly cheaper, this is the not far off the best price we have seen since lately.
If you're finding yourself a bit baffled by Bose's huge range of QuietComfort headphones, we don't blame you. This SC variant gets you the audio brand's current mainstream (and well-regarded) noise-cancelling over-ears with a soft carry case – thus the 'SC' – rather than the hard case the regular version comes with. The cans themselves are identical. We haven't reviewed this pair but they are a modest update on the four-star QuietComfort 45, which we praised for superb noise-cancelling and, OK battery life and decent sound.
We gave these stunning earbuds 4.5 stars in our review as they have class-leading audio handling and impeccable sound quality that rivals the best wireless earbuds. With balanced sound, effective ANC and a great battery life, these Sennheiser buds will make any audiophile smile.
Arriving with a fresh aesthetic, upgraded speaker drivers for improved sound quality and a wealth of in-app customisation options, the Galaxy Buds4 Pro are a must-consider for any Samsung phone owner. Order before March 11 to secure the discounted price. Also available in white for about the same price.
Dropping to the the lowest price we've seen, this is a fine chance to snap up Apple's flagship earbuds. The ANC is best-in-class, and the sound and fit have been improved over the Pro 2. Check out our review for the full story.
The original QC Ultra was already an excellent set of ANC cans, and now these Gen2 Bose QC Ultras reassert the brand's true mastery of sound and noise cancellation. Check out our review for the full scoop.
Now down to AU$797 in all colours, there's never been a better time to secure Apple's ridiculously good noise cancelling over ears. While the design hasn't changed much, the internals have been upgraded to deliver even better ANC performance, Lossless audio over USB-C and a wealth of useful features made possible by the new H2 chip.
There's much to be said still of wired headphones, as they offer a more reliable and stronger connection to your source devices. You will likely need a 3.5mm-to-USB or -Lightning adapter (or one of the best headphone DACs) to get them connected to your phone, but do so and you’ll be rewarded with a gorgeous, high-fidelity sound. And, being Sennheiser, they’re impeccably built and are super comfortable to wear for longer sessions.
The JBL Charge 5 can bring the party, and quite loudly I might add. I use this Bluetooth speaker at home myself and love it, with up to 20 hours of playback. It's also dust and waterproof (IP67 rating), so you can take anywhere, plus it will double as a phone charger in a pinch if you need some extra juice on your handset.
The JBL Flip 7 outperforms its predecessor, getting a full five stars in our review. The sound is a lot punchier than before and that's without compromising details across the range. It even gets a bigger battery to last you up to 16 hours and makes a case for itself at a very good price indeed.
Coffee machines
This do-it-all machine from Ninja really can make pretty much any coffee you could want, whether it be hot or iced. It will select the right grind size, has user profiles to store settings, and even two bean hoppers so you can swap out for different beans.
Also available in stainless steel for the same AU$948 price.
The best entry-level bean-to-cup coffee maker has received a good discount for Black Friday, although not quite as good as the AU$359 we saw during Prime Day. It's simple to use, taking care of the grinding, tamping and pouring for you. The porta filter will even automatically slide into position for you. Do note there's no milk frothing here, but a matching milk frother is available.
This compact manual coffee machine can pour up to two espresso shots at once and features a steam wand for cafe-quality milk foaming. There's no built-in grinder, but you either use ground coffee beans or invest in a separate grinder using the cash you save with this deal.
If you've already got a decent coffee maker but one without a grinder, just add this Breville machine to get fresh ground coffee. It has over 60 settings for precise control over your beans, meaning you should be able to extract the most delicious shot from the grind catering to your taste.
A welcome saving on Breville's answer to the SodaStream. Not only can you use the InFizz Fusion to carbonate water, but you can fizz any liquid you can think of — other than hot beverages of course. This nifty machine is sure to be a hit during at-home cocktail nights.
The Breville Bambino Plus is incredibly simple to use, and can take care of most of the coffee making process for you. Grind some beans into the porta filter, insert it into the group head and use the one-touch controls to brew. It also has a hands-free milk texturing system for expertly frothed milk, while ThermoJet technology means the machine is ready to use in seconds. There's very little you need to do to simply enjoy the results — now AU$20 more than what it cost at the start of the sale.
With a nice saving, it's hard to dismiss this Breville coffee machine deal. The Barista Express has a built-in grinder, tamper, and bean hopper, so there's no need to buy a separate grinder or hand tamp. Available in a few colourways under the same listing, only the Charcoal model gets the full discount.
If you’re after a coffee that makes itself, then it’s hard to go past the Breville Creatista Plus. A great compact pod machine that uses the Original Nespresso pods, and one that can also do milk frothing without requiring a whole other appliance.
We've only reviewed the more expensive Touch model, but if you take your coffee seriously – and want a barista-level cup of joe easily, this is the deal for you. Offering automatic grinding, dosing, tamping and milk texturing, this machine lets you go from beans to latte in seconds.
Vacuum cleaners
The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal uses light to pick up hidden stains on your floors, has a heated mop pad and anti-tangle brush roller, and is equipped with LiDAR navigation. Now discounted for Amazon's Black Friday sale, this new Shark robovac is hard to pass up. Also available in Café Noir Mocha for AU$1,070.
This affordable Dreame stick vac can handle regular everyday cleaning tasks — it may not be the most powerful tool in the shed, but it sure will keep it clean. Even handy for the boat, the car or your home for not a lot of cash.
Now down by a huge AU$660, Dyson's Detect Submarine houses a powerful suction and a superb runtime of up to 60 minutes. It can handle all floor types, including wet and dry messes.
We haven't tested this cordless vacuum ourselves but user reviews are glowing and I think that says something. For quick and daily vacuuming. This one always proves popular during major sales, and I reckon it will be once more, as this is a new all-time low price in Australia.
In our Ecovacs Deebot X8 Pro Omni review, in which it scored an impressive 4.5-star score, we called it a "chatty all-in-one robot vacuum that cleans better than most others". Its biggest drawback is its regular price, but this deal takes care of that — letting you enjoy its strong suction, efficient edge cleaning, effective mopping and smart navigation.
A huge discount on what is a relatively new flagship model from Ecovacs. We haven't tested this version out yet, but if it works as well as the previous X8 Pro Omni did, then I think this is a good premium robovac to consider without the hefty price tag.
Kitchen Appliances
The Nutribullet is great value if you need a powerful blender for your liquid breakfast needs. In fact, it will even come in handy if you want to use it as a regular blender to make sauces, dips and small batches of soup. This model has a 900W motor and comes with a single 700ml cup.
The Ninja Slushi lets you skip the ice and still enjoy perfectly smooth icy drinks with very little effort. Whether you're craving a frappe, smoothie, or even a cheeky spiked slushi, its multiple drink modes have you covered. Even better, the current deal price is near to the lowest we have seen on Amazon. Check out our Ninja Slushi review for the full rundown.
This compact air fryer packs 1700W of power into a portable design, with two borosilicate glass containers that serve as both frying baskets and serving dishes. The borosilicate glass can withstand extreme temperatures, making it easy to take your favourite foods from frozen to crispy, and it's safer to use than any non-stick basket. The Crispi also comes with two removable crisping grates and two snap-on container lids for easy storage.
It's got a cult-like following and two members of our own staff are massive fans. If you love your chilled desserts — ice creams, gelatos, smoothies — but want to control your calorie intake, you really should consider getting the Ninja Creami. This Deluxe edition gets you three containers, which is great value at this price.
Not a big discount and even I balk at recommending a toaster that costs more then AU$50, but I have the Black Truffle model of this 2-slice toaster and trust me when I say it's one of the best toasters I've used. Sure, it's overkill for the average person but if you can get the perfect toast every morning (or arvo or evening), I think it's worth considering.
This Ninja kitchen appliance combines a grill and an air fryer in one machine. We liked it so much that we gave it 4.5 stars in our Ninja Smart XL Grill and Air Fryer review. The latest model comes with the same presets as the DG551, but boasts a sleeker, more slimline design. Customer reviews on the listing praise its impressive features, meat-turning reminders and that it's easy to clean.
This Shark fan has twisting ends that allow it to shoot air out in any direction. The blades can be positioned horizontally or vertically too, and while the ends need manual intervention, all other controls can be adjusted via a remote control.
PC & Gaming
This lovely little vertical mouse has dropped as low as AU$67, but I think this is still an excellent price to pay for the pointer I use every day myself. It's perfect for small mitts and encourages better posture, helping ease wrist, shoulder, and shoulder blade discomfort. And, for once, all three colour variants are around the same price.
A 100Hz-refresh-rate monitor for just AU$100? Sign me up! This display from Lenovo may be a bit small at under 24 inches with a 1080p resolution, but it uses IPS technology for sharp image quality. This is price is the lowest we've seen this monitor go on Amazon.
This handheld gaming PC has been cheaper before, dropping to the AU$899 mark but, then again, nothing really comes cheap these days. Importantly, though, this is a great performer, with a vivid 8-inch display and 144Hz refresh rate for smooth gameplay. It's also rather nice looking and comfortable in the hand.
This 32-inch affair is one of our fave gaming monitors, and if you don't trust me, check out the 92 / 100 review from PC Gamer. The display uses Samsung's QD-OLED tech and pumps out a sharp 4K resolution with an uber-smooth 240Hz refresh rate, with AMD FreeSync and G-Sync support.
The CM14 is an affordable Chromebook with a pretty good for the price 14-inch, 1920 x 1080 display. The Kompanio 540 CPU and 4GB of RAM are fine for light browsing and streaming, and the 64GB of storage is enough if you mostly use web apps and keep your files online.
The Core Ultra 5 322 and 16GB of RAM make this a well-equipped everyday laptop for the money. Its roomy 15.3-inch, 1920 x 1200 IPS display is rated at 400 nits, brighter than many screens on machines in this price range.
This is the cheapest option going if you want the M5 Air and with the 512GB SSD. Want to know more? Check out our MacBook Air M5 review.
The Cyborg 15 is an affordable option for 1080p gaming, with an RTX 5060 and a 15.6-inch, 144Hz display that suits fast-paced multiplayer games. The 16GB of RAM is a decent starting point, though be aware the GPU is limited to 55W so the 5060 will give slower frame rates than models with higher graphics power levels.
This Snapdragon-powered laptop has an impressive spec for the price, with an X Elite X1E78100 CPU, 32GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD. It also has a very nice 2944 x 1840 OLED touchscreen display that outputs 100% of the sRGB gamut. We have seen this machine slightly cheaper, but it's still a good deal if its Windows on Arm compatibility suits the apps you use.
TP-Link’s Deco X55 combines an AX3000 speed rating (aka 3,000Mbps of bandwidth to share in total) and Wi-Fi 6 connectivity to make a great all-rounder that’ll deliver fast speeds to suit an NBN 500 plan.
From Amazon’s own Eero brand, the Eero Pro 6E provides a sweet spot for busy households — it provides tri-band Wi-Fi 6E with the newer 6GHz band to help ease congestion across the network.
Netgear’s Orbi range is brilliant for a big home, with the 770 being competitively affordable when compared to other Wi-Fi 7 mesh options. Read our 4.5-star Netgear Orbi 770 review for the full story, but essentially, it offers Wi-Fi 7 and a total throughput of up to 10,800Mbps.
Phones, tablets & wearables
It looks like an iPhone and can rival Apple's performance too, thanks to a powerful chipset under the hood. In fact, our tester was quite impressed with this phone in our Xiaomi 17T review, with the biggest issue being bloatware. If that doesn't bother you, we gave this one four stars.
The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2 Wayfarer Smart Glasses are a great choice for anyone who likes wearing sunglasses but wants the perks of an AI-powered wearable. Just like wireless earbuds, you can listen to music and talk on the phone, but you can also take POV photos and videos in 3K.
A small but welcome discount on the Google Pixel Watch 5. This competent wearable delivers accurate GPS, all the essential health and fitness tracking features you need, and an attractive design. If you're upgrading from a Pixel Watch 3 or 4, you won't notice a huge leap, but for everyone else, it's easily the best Android smartwatch right now.
The Vivoactive 5 contains a lot of the premium Garmin features found in its more expensive offerings, while also priced closer to conventional smartwatches. These features include on-board GPS, on-device storage for offline music via Spotify, and fitness metrics like Body Battery and VO2 Max.
We called this the best smart ring for battery life (rated up to 12 days + a further 150 days with the charging case) while also being a more affordable option than Oura and Samsung at full price. The Gen 2 added a sleep apnoea tracker to make up for the price hike over its predecessor. Again, be sure to source the sizing kit first as not all smart rings are made the same.
Samsung's answer to the AirTag, the SmartTag 2 works with select Samsung phones to help you find mislaid items. It has a built-in hole for easier attachments, up to 700 days of battery life and it's water-resistant.
This camera has gone viral in other countries, so much so that's it's hard to find stock. In Australia, however, there's plenty, and it offers fabulous value, especially since this is single-lens kit that's cheaper than the RRP of the body alone. It's one of the tiniest cameras available today and still comes packed with features for entry-level hybrid shooters. So go on, you won't regret it.
Beauty & grooming
If you didn't know what a 'sonic' brush is, it's quieter and gentler than an oscillating electric toothbrush (like Oral-B). The DiamondClean 9000 has 4 cleaning modes, and one of them gets you 3 intensities. This value pack gets you a his-and-hers version, plus the glass is actually the charger.
Offering one of the most fuss-free shaves, the Philips OneBlade 360 is a nigh-on essential tool for any man's grooming routine. The cutting blade itself can move in any direction, ensuring constant, comfortable contact with your face to remove your beard entirely, while an included guard comb allows you to trim your facial fuzz to a desired length.
The Lawn Mower 5.0 Ultra is a solid choice if you want one device for general trimming and getting a closer shave. It includes interchangeable SkinSafe trimmer and foil heads, a built-in LED light and a waterproof design for wet or dry use, while USB-C charging and the included travel case make it easier to take on the road.
We're huge fans of the Shark CryoGlow here at TechRadar. The brand's advanced face mask combines LED facial care with a clever InstaChill cooling system to help reduce under-eye puffiness. During testing, we found this unique model to be very comfortable and capable of surprisingly good results. While a little pricey, the CyroGlow could be worth it if you're already spending a lot of cash on your skincare routine.
Gaming
Enter the wizarding world of Harry Potter, in Lego form on the Switch 2, with this collection of two games, covering Lego Harry Potter: Years 1-4 and Years 5-7.
It's fair to say Wolverine received a mixed reaction from gamers when it launched. If you were initially hesitant to play as the clawed mutant, then perhaps this 45% discount at Amazon could be enough to persuade you.
"It isn’t cheap, but the audio quality is near perfect". That was us reviewing the Inzone H9 II, and while it's still a premium price, this is a big discount on a superb gaming headset.
This deal offers you a decent saving on Meta's best 'affordable' headset, and a close second to its best ever headset according to our resident VR headset tester. In fact, he thinks it's the second-best headset anyone can buy from any brand, and it's only a more tempting offer thanks to this limited-time deal, which includes a free copy of GOLF+ to get you started.
Picture perfect
A dedicated camera might take impressive pictures, and smartphones make taking snaps easier than ever, but can we take a moment to spread some love for instant photography?
I took a Fujifilm Instax camera on holiday earlier this year, and while the quality doesn't compare to my iPhone, I absolutely love having a physical copy. I also found using the camera encouraged me to think more about framing a shot, and I'm certainly happy with the results.
Fujifilm offers a wide range of instant cameras, and the mini LiPlay 2+ bundle is currently on sale at Amazon with a 31% discount. Now, the mini LiPlay 2+ is slightly different to the Instax range, in that it's a digital camera with a photo printer built in. This means it's easier to frame shots, as you have an LCD screen on the rear. It also gets a dedicated selfie camera for fuss-free shots.
Once you've taken a picture, you can print it out to keep forever. What's more, you can print photos from your smartphone too, giving it extra functionality.
The Fujifilm mini LiPlay 2+ is available in Sand Beige and Midnight Blue colours, complete with a carry case and a pack of photo paper to get you started.
• Fujifilm mini LiPlay 2+ bundle: was AU$329 now AU$247 at Amazon
This Lego set will be the death of me
The Death Star is arguably the most iconic superweapon in all of sci-fi and the Disney+ show (and Rogue One prequel) Andor has made it a lot more menacing than ever before, with the series depicting some of the work that went into building the planet-killing space station.
And that intimidating feel translates well in Lego's current iteration of the Death Star, the 9,023-piece Ultimate Collection Series set that stands about 70cm high and 79cm wide. It also has 38 minifigures, including iconic characters like Darth Vader, Luke Skywalker and Emperor Palpatine, as well as working lifts and a miniature Imperial shuttle.
It's not a perfect set — it's a diorama that's shaped like a flat disc rather than a spherical model like the older models, and the back isn't completely flush either for easy display. It's also one of the most expensive Lego Star Wars sets to date at a staggering AU$1,499 RRP.
Still, this massive set is a great showcase of several iconic scenes from the classic movie franchise, and is a must-have for any Lego Star Wars UCS collector. It also helps that Amazon is selling it for a low price of AU$1,148.98, which should make the Lego UCS Death Star more palatable.
Lego Star Wars Death Star 75619: AU$1,499 now AU$1,148.98
A premium robovac for mid-range price
For just AU$599 (or a whopping 77% off), I think this is a reliable and capable robot vacuum that's a newer sibling to the now-discontinued X8 Pro Omni that we highly recommend after testing it ourselves. Admittedly I haven't tested this Max sibling, but I have high expectations it will live up to its the previous model's reputation.
It will vacuum, it will mop, then it will clean itself (mop included) and dry itself. All you need to do is ensure the dirty water is cleaned out regularly and you have a supply of replacement dust bags handy.
Ecovacs Deebot X8 Max Pro Omni: AU$2,599 now AU$599
The AirTag alternative for Samsung users — just AU$17.25
While the Apple AirTags might be more popular on the interwebs, Samsung users can't exactly make do with those Bluetooth trackers. Enter the Samsung SmartTags. The second generation is still going strong in Australia, and they're actually cheaper to buy than AirTags.
For example, the white single-unit Samsung Galaxy SmartTag 2 is just AU$27.50 now, which is better than a single Apple AirTag at AU$36.99 However, opt for the four-pack of the Samsung tags and the price of each unit drops even further to just AU$17.75 apiece! And that's the lowest price I've seen on either of the two brands' popular Bluetooth tracker.
So if you're a Samsung phone user, all you'll need is the SmartThings app and away you'll go.
Samsung Galaxy SmartTags 2 (4-pack): AU$169 now AU$71
The best Kindle deal right now
I review ereaders for a living and while I wouldn't recommend a colour ereader to most readers, those who read more comics or graphic novels would actually put it to good use. If you're one of them, the Kindle Colorsoft is cheaper than what it was during Black Friday and Boxing Day last year, and cheaper than July's Prime Day price of AU$279.
Now at an all-time low of AU$237 for Black Friday, the Kindle Colorsoft is a colour e-reader to consider.
The best thing about the Colorsoft is that it's the only colour ereader I've seen that has a separate Vivid mode that enhances the colours displayed (albeit ever so slightly) and, unlike other E Ink Kaleido 3 devices like the Kobo Libra Colour and Boox Go Color 7 Gen II, you get what it promises – marginally better saturation. Again, keep in mind this is an E Ink display, so don't expect it to match an iPad or your phone, but it sure displays nice colours, which is great for comic fans.
Kindle Colorsoft (16GB): AU$399 now AU$237
Don't forget to court the coupon code
If you're a regular shopper on Amazon, you probably already know that there are some deals that have coupons associated with them that save you some extra cash. It's hard to find these, though, but there's one way you can filter all deals on Amazon that have an associated coupon.
Well, we've done the filtering for you and you just need to head to this Amazon deals page with coupons for all the current listings.
You'll find all sorts of discounts here, from vacuum cleaners to the little microSD card. Like all of Amazon's deals, you can filter the coupon landing page as well to whittle down to categories to make finding items easier. If you can't find an offer you're after in the standard Amazon deals landing page, you can always try the coupons.
Are Amazon's lightning deals good?
For the most part, yes they are. There are, however, certain things you need to know about lightning deals on Amazon.
Firstly, they're usually available only for a limited time — this could be just a couple to a few hours, or maybe a couple of days. Sometimes the offer is available till stocks run out.
And that brings us to the second thing: stock is typically very limited. To put that into perspective, here's an analogy that might help — if there are 100 pieces of the item in the Amazon warehouse, perhaps only 10 of those would be available at the discounted price in a lightning deal.
The good thing is that the discounted price is typically far better than a regular Amazon deal would be. For example, if something costs AU$100 RRP and it is discounted typically to AU$60, then a lightning deal on limited stock could drop to as low as AU$30-AU$40.
During Black Friday, most of these lightning deals will likely be Prime exclusive, so not only will you need to be quick to secure your purchase, but you'll also need to be a Prime member. So be sure to sign up if you aren't already.
- Lightning deals: hurry — just hours to buy limited stocks
Are you a Prime member yet?
If there's one thing you need to do to take full advantage of any major Amazon sale is to become a Prime member. While I think many Aussies already are, some of you might still be wondering what it means to be a Prime member, what you're actually paying for and if shelling out a monthly or annual sum is actually worth it.
In short, if you're a regular Amazon shopper, I think it's worth signing up for it. Your AU$12.99 monthly fee gets you free and expedited shipping on thousands of eligible products without needing to fulfil a minimum spend.
That fee also gets you free access to Prime Video (which does have some excellent shows and movies), along with Prime Reading and Prime Gaming. Just the first one more than makes up for the investment you're making in my opinion.
While there are generally no Prime-exclusive deals right now, there are the occasional coupons or lightning deals that won't explicitly say it's for Prime members, but will only appear if you're signed in with a paid account. You can find out more about the subscription service in my dedicated guide to what is Amazon Prime in Australia.
It's also worth noting that if you've never tried this service before, signing up now will get you a 30-day free trial that more than covers the sale. If you don't want to pay at all, you can cancel as soon as the sale finishes. Keep in mind that if you use the same email later to sign up again, you will not get that free trial later even if you didn't use all 30 days.
If you're interested in getting your delivery from Amazon expedited this sale season, you can hit one of the buttons below to sign up.
It's officially Black Friday!
We're now on day 11 of Amazon's sale, and I'll be spending the day hunting down the biggest discounts and checking which deals offer the best value for money. Keep this page handy and check back regularly, as I'll be adding the best new bargains as they drop.

articles.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
articles.text:
The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it.
The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
Older Garmins still make for a great buy if you’re hunting for bargains during Black Friday.
Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm)
Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists.
The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds.
There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend:
- The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon, Best Buy, and REI, which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight.
- Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon, Best Buy, and REI, an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know.
- Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon, Best Buy, and REI. This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

articles.title: Civilization en vrai : c'est fascinant, Claude a transformé la France en carte de jeu avec des données publiques
articles.text:
Il a fallu sept heures à Claude pour transformer les États-Unis en plateau de Civilization, et une demi-heure pour refaire le coup avec la France. Entre les deux, aucune percée technologique, seulement une licence libre et un développeur qui a eu le bon goût de ne pas tout recommencer. On obtient une carte en hexagones où le PIB devient de l’or, où les universités deviennent des merveilles et où chaque ville affiche ses vraies spécialités économiques.
Tout part d’Andrej Karpathy, cofondateur d’OpenAI passé chez Anthropic en mai, qui a dévoilé usaciv dans un post publié sur X le 26 novembre. Claude Opus 5.5, piloté via Claude Code (l’outil d’Anthropic qui écrit et exécute du code en autonomie), y a mobilisé selon lui 31 sources publiques (recensement, PIB, emploi, catastrophes…) et produit environ 45 000 lignes de code, le tout ramené sur une grille hexagonale de 25 km.
San Jose y hérite ainsi d’un « Campus », puisqu’un actif sur quatre y est ingénieur, programmeur ou scientifique, contre un sur quatorze à l’échelle du pays.
Dans la foulée, Mathieu Astruc a publié franceciv, nourrie à l’INSEE, à l’IGN et à Météo-France, puis une version européenne couvrant 37 pays et 646 villes.
Un moteur américain, des données européennes
Les « 30 minutes avec Claude » revendiquées pour la France s’expliquent facilement. Le dépôt GitHub de la version européenne l’écrit noir sur blanc : il s’agit d’un portage d’usaciv, c’est-à-dire une adaptation du même code à un autre territoire. Sa licence MIT autorise n’importe qui à copier et modifier le code en créditant l’auteur, si bien que le moteur, le rendu et l’interface viennent des États-Unis.
Seule la chaîne de scripts qui télécharge et digère les statistiques a été reconstruite. Rien de honteux, puisque c’est le principe même du logiciel libre, et un fork chinois baptisé Jiuzhou (une copie du code qui vit désormais sa propre vie) a suivi le même chemin.
Mathieu Astruc en tire une leçon flatteuse pour le Vieux Continent : « L’atout le plus sous-estimé de l’Europe, ce sont ses données publiques ». Eurostat, l’IGN ou Copernicus fournissent l’essentiel de la matière. Petite ironie, le relief de franceciv comme d’europeciv provient de la NOAA, l’agence océanique et atmosphérique américaine. L’Europe ouvre ses données, mais elle emprunte encore beaucoup de données à Washington.
Voici ce que la carte contient
Dans la version européenne, le PIB et l’emploi d’une ville sont ceux de sa région NUTS 3 (le découpage statistique européen, proche de l’échelle d’un département), répartis selon la part de la population vivant dans l’agglomération. Autrement dit, une ville affiche une estimation calculée à partir de sa région, sans mesure propre.
Les « 98 000 communes » annoncées sont en fait des unités administratives locales, une catégorie Eurostat qui ne recouvre pas la même réalité d’un pays à l’autre. La documentation se contredit sur la taille des hexagones (10 km de rayon à un endroit, 17 km ailleurs).
Côté américain, Claude a carrément choisi de sauter quelques États et territoires, reconnaît Andrej Karpathy, sans dire lesquels.
Il s’agit surtout d’une visualisation de données déguisée en jeu de stratégie, sans aucune mécanique de jeu. On ne joue aucun tour et on n’envahit pas la Belgique. Andrej Karpathy l’admet d’ailleurs sans détour : « Je ne sais pas trop où je voulais en venir avec ça. »
Comment l’essayer, ou la bricoler soi-même
Les trois cartes s’ouvrent directement dans un navigateur : la carte des États-Unis, celle de la France et celle de l’Europe. Cette dernière ajoute un défi géographique quotidien : cinq lieux par jour, les mêmes pour tout le monde, et trente secondes pour cliquer au bon endroit.
Pour la faire tourner chez soi, il suffit de l’outil Python uv et de trois commandes, puisque les données déjà calculées sont incluses dans le dépôt. La carte s’affiche ensuite à l’adresse locale 127.0.0.1:8765, et seul le défi quotidien exige de reconstruire toute la chaîne de données.
- git clone https://github.com/lmveprog/Europe-Civilization.git
- cd Europe-Civilization
- uv run python -m pipeline serve
Avis aux volontaires qui voudraient en faire un vrai jeu : il va prévoir un abonnement costaud.
Tous nos articles sont aussi sur notre profil Google : suivez-nous pour ne rien manquer !
Et le second meilleur moyen de nous donner un coup de pouce, c’est d’ajouter Frandroid à vos sources préférées sur Google.
