articles.title: Recap of Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot as the Work OS and Agent Governance
articles.text:
Microsoft Ignite 2026, held in San Francisco and online from November 17 to 20, centered on running AI agents in production, with Microsoft positioning Copilot as the operating system for work and extending agent identity, governance, and cost controls across Azure, Foundry, Entra, and Defender.
CEO Satya Nadella opened the keynote by acknowledging the November 12 Microsoft 365 outage, then positioned Copilot as the operating system for work, combining chat, coding, and autonomous agents in one experience. In his edited keynote remarks, Nadella argued that customers must be able to examine and independently verify what AI does, announced an AI Transparency Initiative aligned with NIST's Agent Standards Initiative, and rejected setups where models audit other models:
These nested black boxes are simply unacceptable.
The Book of News groups the announcements by product area, and many of them ship as previews rather than in general availability.
Compute and Infrastructure
Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines are now generally available, a year after InfoQ reported on Microsoft introducing the chip at Ignite 2025 and two and a half years after the preview of Cobalt 100 VMs. According to the Azure announcement, the processor combines 132 Arm Neoverse V3 cores on TSMC's 3nm process, and the VMs run in 14 regions today, with 23 planned by the end of 2026. Microsoft claims up to 50% better CPU performance than Cobalt 100, plus up to 15% higher network bandwidth and 20% higher remote storage IOPS through Azure Boost. Customers can run cores at a fixed 3.2 GHz in Deterministic Mode or let them boost up to 3.6 GHz in Opportunistic Mode, and the lineup adds Mpsv4 VMs for high-memory workloads and storage-optimized Lpsv5 VMs. Amadeus reported more than 30% higher flight-search throughput than on Cobalt 100, and OpenAI's Vadim Filanovsky described a similar result:
We saw higher throughput and lower latency on Cobalt 200.
Confidential computing gains three previews: multi-GPU confidential computing on VR72 for models larger than a single GPU, Azure Confidential Enclaves with AKS Kata CoCo containers, and Azure Confidential Clean Room for multiparty analytics without exposing raw data.
Customers can now deploy Foundry open-weight models and agents to their own AKS clusters. At the same time, an Agent Sandbox extension provides VM-level isolation for agent-written code, and Agent Grid applies central policy to agent, model, tool, and service interactions. Flex nodes extend AKS clusters to servers outside Azure. According to the AKS team's Ignite post, managed GPU node pools, which handle GPU drivers, device plugins, and Azure Monitor metrics, are generally available, with NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 support and mixed multi-instance GPU in preview. Confidential VM node pools on Azure Container Linux are also generally available on both Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP VM sizes.
On the operations side, Azure Monitor health models are generally available and build a real-time health graph from telemetry, ranking incidents by business impact. The Azure Copilot deployment agent, also generally available, turns natural-language requirements into deployed workloads, and Azure SRE Agent picks up previews for customer-managed keys, Entra Agent ID integration, cross-agent communication, and multicloud investigations. For migration projects, Azure Catalyst is now generally available, with its agent (formerly the Azure Copilot migration agent) handling discovery, assessment, and planning. Separately, GitHub Copilot modernization adds a preview of BizTalk-to-Logic Apps migration.
Hybrid, Sovereign Cloud, and Windows Server
Microsoft now pitches Sovereign Private Cloud as a full stack on Azure Local, with VMs and AKS at the base, followed by data services, Foundry Local, GitHub Enterprise Local, and Microsoft 365 Local. Darryl van der Peijl, a Microsoft MVP for Azure Local, Hyper-V, and Azure Arc, listed what shipped in his Azure Local Insider newsletter: Foundry Local on Azure Local and GitHub Enterprise Local are generally available, while a Sovereign control panel, Blob Storage and DocumentDB on Azure Local, multi-tenancy, and rehoming are in preview. The control panel assesses data residency, encryption, network exposure, and business continuity for Azure resources without enforcing any controls, and during the preview it runs in European regions only, with the service hosted in Sweden.
Van der Peijl singled out rehoming, which moves an Azure Local instance from Azure management to local management while VMs, AKS clusters, and data stay in place:
Until now, going from connected to disconnected meant a migration project. Microsoft showed a script that does the rehoming in one run.
Azure Local also runs on arm64 for the first time, in public preview on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Development Kit, which hosts containers on bare metal without a hypervisor. Windows Server 2028 entered preview through the Windows Server Insider Program, bringing a hardened Server Core, post-quantum cryptography, native NVMe enabled by default, NVMe over Fabrics, and boot from ReFS. According to van der Peijl, Microsoft added inference as a new pillar for the release, calling on-premises inference servers token factories, and is moving network drivers from kernel mode to user mode as part of its Windows resiliency work. Windows Admin Center vMode is now generally available at no extra cost and manages up to 1,000 Hyper-V hosts and 25,000 VMs, which Microsoft described on stage as "kind of a replacement for SCVMM."
AI, Models, and Microsoft Foundry
Foundry's main theme was continuous improvement. Multi-turn evaluation and production insights that group recurring failures and rank fixes are now generally available, while the agent optimizer, human annotation, rubric evaluators, Managed Training, and Programmed Training for custom SFT and reinforcement learning loops on open-weight models are in preview. The optimizer adjusts an agent's instructions, skills, and model choice, with a human approving each change before it ships.
(Source: Microsoft blog)
In a separate engineering post, the Microsoft team behind the optimizer described how the loop works. They reported that the reflector, a separate model that reads failing traces and diagnoses why an agent scored poorly, influenced results more than switching the agent's own model, for example between gpt-4o and gpt-4.1-mini. Developers drive the loop from the Azure Developer CLI:
azd ai agent eval init                         # generate dataset & evaluator from a one-paragraph description
azd ai agent eval run                          # score the current version (baseline)
azd ai agent optimize                          # search over candidates
azd ai agent optimize apply --candidate <id>   # apply the winner locally
azd deploy                                     # ship as the next version
Writing on DEV Community, Hector Flores advised readers to treat Microsoft's claim that the model router saves up to 65% compared with a frontier model as a ceiling rather than a forecast, and he welcomed the human approval step in the optimizer loop:
Self-modifying agents with no review gate are an incident waiting to happen.
On the model front, Microsoft-Decision-1.1 is generally available in Foundry, OpenRouter, and Vercel. Built on Gemma 4 26B A4B with added image input, it scores 68 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 and runs more than twice as fast as its predecessor, and Copilot uses it to route requests. MAI-Code-2 and MAI-Code-2-Flash are generally available on GitHub, MAI-Image-2.7 is in preview, and the model router now covers the top 50 models in a catalog of more than 11,000. OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol became generally available in Foundry, with Global Standard deployments covering 28 regions. On Standard deployments with short context, Sol costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, while Astra costs $8 and $40. Foundry IQ added knowledge graphs and an iterative retrieval model, Microsoft-Retriever-1, both in preview.
Microsoft also made Azure AI Gateway generally available as a standalone product, split out of the API Management AI tier, to govern, route, and monitor access to AI models and MCP tools across providers. It includes 10,000 free requests per gateway per month, with paid billing starting January 1, 2027, across 17 regions.
Microsoft IQ, which Nadella described as an externalization of the context system behind Copilot, is now generally available without a new SKU. It exposes Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, and Web IQ context to Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Foundry, and MCP-compatible harnesses, and Web IQ is now available to all Azure customers at a lower price. Business plugins, which package reusable context, skills, and tools with hierarchical inheritance and governance, are available through the Frontier program.
Data
PostgreSQL got most of the attention on the data side. Azure HorizonDB is now generally available as a managed, PostgreSQL-compatible database with built-in vector indexing, and teams can lock it down with Entra ID, private endpoints, and their own encryption keys. Calling models from SQL through AI Functions and AI Pipelines is still in preview. The same holds for Fabric HorizonDB, a serverless variant inside Fabric that provisions in seconds and pauses when nobody uses it, and for a DMS path that moves existing Azure Database for PostgreSQL servers onto HorizonDB.
Teams moving off Oracle can test a new Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration in Azure DMS, also in preview. Cosmos DB developers now have a generally available Rust SDK and semantic reranker, and Cosmos DB Shell lets them query from VS Code or the portal with MCP support built in. On Azure Managed Redis, the Redis 8 preview folds JSON, search, time-series, and vector search into a single version. Anyone who wants to develop against Azure SQL Database on a laptop can pull a preview container that needs no Azure subscription.
Developer Tools
The Microsoft Copilot SDK 2.0 is generally available, built on a native Rust runtime, supported in six languages, and using the same agent harness Microsoft and GitHub run internally. The GitHub Copilot app now takes Azure DevOps repositories from clone to merge and runs tests in a real, signed-in browser. Copilot code review adds local reviews in the CLI and app, secret detection, adaptive review effort, and cross-repository context. Copilot Code, a natural-language app builder with cloud and local sandboxes, is in the Frontier program, with general availability planned for December and a macOS local sandbox still to come.
Copilot and Business Applications
The Copilot app now brings Chat, Cowork, Code, and Autopilot into one experience, and Office in Copilot puts Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside it as a generally available feature. Autopilot, a long-running personal agent with its own identity, memory, and tool access, is rolling out to Frontier customers. Salesforce in Copilot entered preview with more than 38 prebuilt sales skills, and zero-copy data federation between Salesforce Data 360 and Fabric OneLake is generally available. For spend control, Agent 365 FinOps previews cost visibility, policies, alerts, and Fabric-based chargeback.
Cost tracking also featured in practitioner reactions. In his newsletter, Microsoft principal AI apps architect Anurag Karuparti wrote that tokenomics is among the top challenges his customers raise, and he proposed a different unit for agent ROI:
The metric that matters isn't just tokens consumed. It's cost per successful business outcome. That's how I think enterprises should start measuring agent ROI.
Writing for business leaders, Aaron Reich, CTO of the Accenture and Microsoft joint venture Avanade, built his Ignite analysis around trust rather than speed:
Speed isn't the bottleneck anymore, trust is. As AI drives the cost of knowledge toward zero with apps being easier to build, agents doing more work, and abundant intelligence, the scarce things are hard and need more attention: institutional knowledge, judgment, accountability and trust.
Security, Identity, and Governance
At the Microsoft Hub, where he spent the week answering customer questions, Microsoft MVP Muhammad Atif noticed a change in what customers wanted to know:
How do we actually put this into production? How do we scale AI and agents across the organisation? How do we govern and secure them? How do we control the cost as adoption grows?
Entra now assigns Agent IDs automatically to discovered local agents, starting with GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code, and previews an MCP Firewall that controls access to MCP servers, tools, prompts, and transports. The Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise, which gives agents permission-controlled access to Entra data, is generally available. Defender's runtime protection for local AI agents on Windows is generally available to Defender for Endpoint P2 customers, while Intune previews local agent governance that marks devices with unapproved agents as noncompliant. Agent 365 now has a generally available tools registry that lists the plugins, skills, MCP servers, and connectors agents use; MCP governance is in preview through Azure AI Gateway and LiteLLM; and Dynamic Agent Risk combines runtime, posture, and blast-radius signals into risk levels for each agent. Microsoft Perception, formerly Project Perception, is now generally available, with its Triage Agent covering about 80% of alerts in a typical Defender queue.
(Source: Microsoft Tech Community, Agent 365 blog)
In her Ignite recap, cloud and identity consultant Shannon Kuehn warned against handling agents as ordinary applications:
Treat agents like apps and you'll spend 2027 cleaning up after them.
Conclusion
The complete list of announcements is available in the Microsoft Ignite 2026 Book of News, and Microsoft has made keynote and breakout session recordings available on demand on the Ignite website.

articles.title: Confira o Olhar Digital News na íntegra (26/11/2026)
articles.text:
Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta quinta-feira (26/11).
Nvidia proíbe envio de servidores para quatro países asiáticos
A Nvidia proibiu o envio de servidores equipados com chips de inteligência artificial para Malásia, Singapura, Tailândia e Indonésia, atingindo parceiras como Dell e Supermicro. O anúncio ocorre após um escândalo de espionagem que abalou a fabricante e levou à renúncia de seu CEO, Jensen Huang, que foi reconduzido ao cargo nesta semana.
Terra quebra novo recorde de calor e acende sinal de alerta
A temperatura média global permaneceu acima de 2°C em relação aos níveis pré-industriais durante sete dias consecutivos em novembro de 2026. Na última segunda-feira (23), a anomalia chegou a 2,25°C, o maior valor diário já registrado, segundo o Serviço de Mudanças Climáticas Copernicus, da União Europeia.
FIFA confirma ataque cibernético com acesso a dados pessoais
A FIFA informou nesta quinta-feira (26) que foi vítima de um ataque cibernético que permitiu o acesso não autorizado a um conjunto limitado de dados pessoais e comerciais. O órgão máximo do futebol internacional não informou quantas pessoas ou empresas foram afetadas, quando ocorreu a invasão e nem que tipos de dados foram acessados.
NASA procura empresas parceiras para desenvolver reator nucelar lunar
A NASA abriu uma chamada para empresas interessadas em desenvolver e testar o primeiro reator nuclear destinado à geração de eletricidade na Lua. Batizado de Lunar Reactor-1, o sistema deverá produzir 20 quilowatts de energia elétrica. A agência espacial dos Estados Unidos pretende deixar o equipamento pronto para lançamento em 2030.
Alessandro Di Lorenzo é editor do Olhar Digital e formado em jornalismo pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS).
André Milhomem integra a equipe de redes sociais do Olhar Digital e do programa Olhar Digital News.

articles.title: Comprar una GPU de NVIDIA está a punto de volverse más difícil (y aún más caro)
articles.text:
Si planeas armar un PC gaming, conseguir una GPU de NVIDIA tal vez se vuelva todavía más difícil y caro que ahora. Según reporta VideoCardz, el gigante verde implementaría un fuerte recorte a la asignación de chips para los fabricantes de sus tarjetas gráficas. Esto impactaría de forma directa en la disponibilidad del hardware en el mercado minorista y ya se teme por nuevas subidas de precio.
Todavía no hay anuncios oficiales en tal sentido, pero rumores que circulan en foros chinos sostienen que NVIDIA planea reducir la distribución de chips para GPU destinadas a uso comercial gaming entre un 20 y un 30 por ciento. Este cambio se implementaría en el trimestre fiscal que se inició en noviembre y que se extiende hasta enero de 2027, inclusive.
Si esto se confirma, será el segundo recorte a la asignación de chips para GPU que implementa NVIDIA, al menos en China. De acuerdo con la información disponible, algo similar ya sucedió en el trimestre previo. Todavía no hay detalles sobre si el presunto recorte que implementaría el gigante verde podría impactar solo en el gigante asiático, o si también se verá en el resto del mundo.
La citada publicación menciona que reportes anteriores apuntaban a que los principales socios fabricantes de GPU de NVIDIA se estaban quedando sin stock de modelos de la línea RTX 50. Asimismo, se indica que algunas marcas estarían tratando de cubrir huecos de demanda con modelos de entrada y de gama media con algunos años de antigüedad, tales los casos de las RTX 3050 y 3060.
NVIDIA recortaría la asignación de chips para sus GPU de uso comercial y gaming
Como ya indicamos, NVIDIA no ha confirmado la veracidad del rumor sobre un nuevo recorte en la asignación de chips para sus GPU de uso comercial y gaming. Las principales especulaciones apuntan a que la presunta reducción busca liberar chips para los productos destinados puntualmente a la inteligencia artificial. Y no es descabellado pensar que algo de esto hay, si la historia realmente es así, considerando que la firma californiana es la principal empresa de hardware de IA del mundo.
Pero la disponibilidad más acotada de chips gráficos podría no impactar únicamente a quienes quieren una GPU de NVIDIA para su PC gaming. Otros dispositivos de la industria, incluyendo consolas como la Nintendo Switch 2, también dependen de los componentes de la firma. Ya veremos qué sucede con todo esto.
Por lo pronto, NVIDIA tiene varios temas de resolver más allá del aparente recorte de sus GPU para usuarios finales. La compañía viene de semanas bastante convulsionadas tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang por el escándalo de sus relaciones extramatrimoniales y su posterior regreso a la conducción.

articles.title: Feds will now pay 80 percent of costs under AI Compute Access Fund if purchased from a sovereign provider
articles.text:
Small and medium-sized businesses will only have to pay 20 cents on the dollar for AI compute costs under the latest updates to the federal government’s compute access fund, if that compute is purchased from a “sovereign provider.”
AI Minister Evan Solomon announced the next phase of the AI Compute Access Fund in Toronto on Thursday. The government is now seeking proposals from health and life sciences projects looking to access the fund. The re-opening of submissions follows the AI Compute Access Fund’s $700-million top-up under the refreshed AI strategy earlier this year, bringing its total available funds to $1 billion.
The AI Compute Access Fund aims to help Canadian SMBs with compute costs between $100,000 and $5 million by covering up to 50 percent of eligible costs for cloud-based AI compute services, or up to 80 percent of eligible costs for the same services from a sovereign, Canadian-owned compute provider. Previously, the program only covered 67 cents on the dollar if applicants used Canadian compute providers.
The AI Compute Access Fund originally launched in March 2025, with $300 million allocated for applicants, but the government quickly discovered that demand vastly exceeded that earmark
“Canadian companies are developing AI that can help detect disease earlier, improve access to home care, and keep critical networks running,” Solomon said in a statement. “By encouraging more companies to use Canadian computing providers, we are also helping create the demand that supports investment in infrastructure owned, operated, and governed in Canada.”
The AI Compute Access Fund is open to Canadian-incorporated companies with fewer than 500 employees that are generating revenue or have raised Series A financing. Applicants must be developing AI products or services and have a commercialization plan with an existing AI compute service agreement in place.
Solomon also announced on Thursday an additional 45 companies being supported by more than $52 million in funding under the program. Recipients include Ottawa-based surveillance tech company Solink, Kitchener-based virtual healthcare platform myStoria, and Calgary-based regulatory AI company Ultimarii. This follows the $66 million sent to 44 SMBs this past May, bringing the fund’s total commitments to more than $118 million for 89 Canadian companies.
The program’s previous call for proposals ended in July 2025. According to its website, the AI Compute Access Fund is now accepting proposals for the health and life sciences sector until Jan. 4, 2027.
The AI Compute Access Fund originally launched in March 2025, with $300 million allocated for applicants, but the government quickly discovered that demand vastly exceeded that earmark, Solomon recounted on a recent episode of The BetaKit Podcast.
RELATED: Canada’s AI strategy contains $2.3 billion in spending but few details on new privacy regulations
“We thought … we’ll get a couple hundred people who need compute; [we got] 1,500 asks,” Solomon said, explaining why the program was topped up with $700 million earlier this year.
The program forwards the goals of the federal government’s AI strategy announced by Prime Minister Mark Carney alongside Solomon this past June. The strategy is built on six pillars, including increasing AI adoption and building Canada’s sovereignty. Thursday’s announcement follows the government pledging 500 megawatts of sovereign AI compute for Canadian AI companies as part of the 2026 federal budget earlier this month.
“What we’re making sure is that, if there’s this race to get compute, it’s not just the big hyperscalers that can take the compute and grab it,” Solomon said on The BetaKit Podcast.
Feature image courtesy Evan Solomon via LinkedIn.

articles.title: Kenyan, Nigerian, Ugandan startups named as Latitude59 Kenya finalists
articles.text:
Ten startups from Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda have been selected as finalists for the Latitude59 Kenya Pitch Competition, and will now pitch on the main stage at the event in Nairobi on December 4.
Disrupt Africa reported last month startup and technology event Latitude59 was returning to Kenya for the fourth year, with startups invited to compete for non-equity funding, partner prizes, and the opportunity to pitch on the main stage.
Ten finalists have now been chosen from a record 509 applications from 25 countries – seven from Kenya, two from Nigeria and one from Uganda.
The Kenyan ventures include Inner Circle, which runs a marketplace where African creators earn money from their audiences through mobile money, paid sessions, subscriptions and direct messages in six markets; Farmsky, which builds AI-powered infrastructure for farmers and agricultural SMEs; Sustainable Africa, which builds data infrastructure designed to make African businesses and value chains verifiable and financeable; and ElementPay, which gives businesses in emerging markets bank accounts in their own names in more than 27 countries.
The other Kenyan startups are MasomoGPT, which helps users learn by drawing on things they already enjoy; Chargebyte, which makes solar-powered charging and Wi-Fi stations to widen access to energy and connectivity; and Bahari Mezani, which provides solar-powered cold storage and logistics to reduce fish spoilage and post-harvest losses along the Kenyan coast.
The Nigerian finalists are Ruralpass, which provides identity verification and risk assessment tools that help banks and insurers serve smallholder farmers, and BetaLife, which connects hospitals, blood banks and donors to improve the delivery of blood and medical supplies.
Uganda’s Kyuka Ventures, the remaining finalist, converts plastic waste into clean LPG cooking fuel.
“What stands out about this year’s TOP10 is the range of founders and ideas,” said Krista Meinarde, head of investor-startup relations at Latitude59. “Put them on one stage, and you get a real picture of where African tech is heading, and these are the teams to watch.”
Before the final, the startups will get pitch training and mentoring from pitch coach Gleb Maltsev.
The winner will receive a “golden ticket” to Tallinn, Estonia. The prize fast-tracks them into the top 30 of the Latitude59 2027 Pitch Competition and covers their return trip. It also gives them the chance to meet investors and potential partners in Estonia’s startup ecosystem.

articles.title: Samsung pourrait laisser Gemini fouiller dans vos SMS pour y répondre à votre place
articles.text:
L’arrêt de Samsung Messages sur le marché américain n’empêche pas le constructeur sud-coréen de développer de nouvelles fonctionnalités pour sa messagerie. En Corée du Sud, la version 16.3.27.7 de l’application, en cours de déploiement, intègre dix nouvelles fonctions pensées pour l’intelligence artificielle. Elles pourraient donner davantage de place aux assistants IA, comme Gemini. L’assistant de Google pourrait ainsi interagir directement avec l’application. Il pourrait rechercher des conversations, rédiger, envoyer, transférer ou supprimer des messages, y répondre et retrouver un contact, rapporte ce 27 novembre Android Authority.
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
Une messagerie pilotée à la voix
Plutôt que d’ouvrir Samsung Messages et de parcourir ses différentes conversations, les utilisateurs pourraient simplement faire appel vocalement à Gemini. L’assistant serait ainsi capable de retrouver un élément précis dans leurs échanges. Il serait aussi possible de lui demander, en langage naturel, de rechercher un message particulier et de le transférer à un autre contact, sans avoir à ouvrir l’application de messagerie.
Côté disponibilité, la mise à jour est pour l’instant proposée à certains Galaxy sous One UI 9.0 en Corée du Sud, dont les modèles Ultra jusqu’au Galaxy S23 Ultra. Samsung n’a annoncé aucune date de lancement, ni en Corée du Sud ni ailleurs. Pour l’instant, ces fonctions n’existent que dans le code de l’application.

articles.title: How Much Does Coram AI Cost? Pricing, Licences and What's Included
articles.text:
If you’ve been looking at AI security camera platforms, you’ve probably noticed Coram AI doesn’t put a price on its website. So how much does it actually cost?
Here’s the short answer. Coram AI doesn’t publish a price list. Its pricing is quote-based and depends on three things: how many locations you have, the type of cameras you’re using, and how many days of video you want to keep. Every order includes an on-site appliance called Coram Point, which you buy upfront and own, plus a per-camera software licence on a one, three, five or 10-year term.
That might sound vague, but the way the price is built is actually quite clear. Here’s what goes into a Coram quote, what you get for it and what costs extra.
Why Coram doesn’t publish a price
Coram is an AI physical security platform used by schools, healthcare groups, warehouses and multi-site businesses. Because no two sites are the same, Coram prices each deployment based on its real requirements rather than a one-size-fits-all plan.
The three inputs are simple. The number of locations decides how many Coram Point appliances you need. The type of camera affects how many video feeds each appliance has to handle. And the days of storage you need decides how much recording capacity goes on site. Coram says that once its sales team has those three details, it can come back with a price quickly.
Quotes are in US dollars, so Australian buyers should factor in the exchange rate on the day.
What you’re actually paying for
A Coram quote has two main parts.
The Coram Point appliance. This is the on-site box that records your video locally and runs the AI, while a cloud dashboard lets you view and manage every location from a browser or the mobile app. It’s a one-time purchase, and you own it. There’s no leasing.
Coram Point comes in several sizes, so the model on your quote depends on how many cameras each site has and how long you need to keep footage:
| Coram Point model | Cameras (video feeds) | Video storage | 
| CP-I-1 | 4 | 30 days | 
| CP-M-1 | 8 | 30, 60 or 90 days | 
| CP-S-1 | 16 | 30, 60 or 90 days | 
| CP-E-1 | 24 | 30, 60 or 90 days | 
| CP-E-2 | 32 | Up to 365 days | 
| CP-X-1 | 64 | Up to 365 days | 
| CP-Y-1 | 80 | Varies; check with Coram | 
You can see the full range on Coram’s Coram Point AI NVR page.
The per-camera licence. This is the recurring part. Each camera connected to the system needs a video licence, and you choose a term of one, three, five or 10 years. The licence count is what grows as you add cameras, so it’s the number to watch over time.
What’s included in the licence
The licence covers more than access to the software. According to Coram, it includes:
- The Coram cloud dashboard, with unlimited user seats
- 24/7 online support
- Software updates for the length of the term
- A 100 per cent hardware warranty during the licence period
Unlimited users is worth noting. Some platforms charge per user, which adds up quickly when security staff, managers and IT all need access.
Coram also lists its security credentials alongside its pricing, including SOC 2 Type II, multi-factor authentication and single sign-on, role-based access, audit logs and data encryption.
What costs extra
Not everything sits inside the standard video licence, so it’s worth asking about these on any quote:
- Safety alerts. Firearm detection, slip-and-fall and PPE alerts are separate licences.
- Continuous cloud backup. Video is stored on the Coram Point by default. Backing everything up to the cloud continuously is a separate paid option.
- Installation. If a partner installs the system, their labour will be on top of the Coram quote.
- Other products. Access control, visitor management and emergency management are part of the same platform but are priced on their own lines.
One more detail: a camera that’s offline still uses its licence, so it pays to keep your camera list tidy.
Can you use the cameras you already have?
This is where Coram’s pricing model differs most from many cloud camera systems. Coram works with existing IP cameras, as long as they support the ONVIF standard and stream video in H.264 or H.265. If your cameras qualify, you don’t need to buy new ones, which can take a big chunk out of the upfront cost.
Older analog, coax and MPEG-only cameras aren’t supported, so check your camera models before you ask for a quote.
For businesses that don’t have IP cameras at all, Coram offers 5MP NDAA-compliant cameras free with the software subscription.
What happens if you stop paying?
Ongoing licences are becoming a familiar story across tech, which is why so many buyers now look for alternatives that don’t require ongoing subscriptions. With security cameras, the bigger question is what you’re left with if you stop.
With Coram, customers who don’t renew keep the Coram Point and any cameras Coram supplied. Coram says it never disables the cameras’ RTSP video streams, so those cameras can be connected to another recording system.
How does Coram’s pricing compare?
Some competitors do publish their prices, which helps put Coram’s model in context.
Verkada, for example, publishes its camera prices and charges a separate licence for every camera. Its one-year camera licence is listed at $249 at 2026 US list price, and its cameras only work with Verkada’s own platform.
Rhombus also publishes pricing, listing its Professional camera licence at US$149 per camera per year on top of the cost of its own cameras.
Coram’s main difference isn’t the licence itself. It’s that you can often keep the cameras you already own and you own the on-site hardware outright. Whether that works out cheaper depends on your camera fleet, so the only fair comparison is to get quotes for the same number of cameras, sites and storage days.
Why the on-site appliance matters
Because Coram records video on site, cameras keep recording even if your internet connection drops. Cloud dashboards are convenient, but as the global IT outage showed, relying entirely on remote systems has risks. Keeping the recording local is part of what you’re paying for with Coram Point.
It’s also why Coram sits in a different category from the home security cameras most of us know. A consumer camera like the one in our Arlo Essential Pan Tilt review is built for a home. Coram is built for organisations managing dozens or hundreds of cameras across multiple sites.
How to get an accurate Coram quote
To get a quote quickly, have these ready:
- The number of sites you need to cover
- How many cameras you have, and their make and model
- How many days of footage you need to keep
- Any extras you want, such as access control, safety alerts or cloud backup
Ask for every item as a separate line, and check the licence term against the yearly cost so you can compare it fairly with other quotes.
Common questions
Does Coram AI publish its pricing?
No. Coram AI pricing is by quote, based on the number of locations, the type of cameras and the days of storage you need.
How long are Coram licences?
Coram sells per-camera video licences on one, three, five or 10-year terms.
Do I need to buy new cameras for Coram?
Not usually. Coram works with existing ONVIF IP cameras that stream in H.264 or H.265. Customers without IP cameras can get free 5MP cameras with the subscription.
Is Coram AI available in Australia?
Coram’s quote form accepts enquiries from Australia and New Zealand. Check with Coram about local availability, installation partners and support for your sites. Some features, such as Coram’s Video Alarms service, are currently available only in the US.
The bottom line
Coram AI doesn’t have a sticker price, but its pricing isn’t a mystery either. You pay once for a Coram Point you own, then a per-camera licence for the term you choose, with extras like safety alerts and cloud backup on top. If you already have compatible IP cameras, that can make Coram a sensible way to add AI search and alerts without starting again from scratch. The best way to find out is to get a quote with your real numbers and compare it line by line.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, cet aspirateur robot Mova noté 5/5 passe sous les 400 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'aspirateur robot Mova P70 Pro Ultra "5 étoiles" à 398,00 € (-14%)
Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, l'aspirateur robot Mova P70 Pro Ultra assure des performances d'aspiration remarquées tout en restant facile à entretenir au quotidien. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : il passe à 398,00 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 14 % et 66,26 € d'économie.
L'aspirateur robot Mova P70 Pro Ultra utilise des patins de lavage et un système de serpillières relevables pour adapter son nettoyage à chaque type de sol. Conçu pour éliminer les taches tout en aspirant la poussière, l'appareil s'était distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo grâce à son efficacité globale.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Mova P70 Pro Ultra descend à 398,00 € chez Amazon, soit environ 14 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours fixé à 464,26 €. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 66,26 €.
Une aspiration efficace et un entretien automatisé par la station
Lors de notre test complet, cet aspirateur robot a obtenu la note maximale à ce jour dans nos tests avec 5 étoiles sur 5. Ses performances d'aspiration capturent la poussière courante sans difficulté sur l'ensemble des sols durs. Sa station d'accueil prend en charge la recharge, le vidage automatique du bac à poussière, le remplissage en eau du réservoir ainsi que le lavage et le séchage des serpillières, ce qui évite d'intervenir manuellement après chaque cycle de nettoyage.
Mova P70 Pro Ultra
Points forts
- Performances d'aspiration.
- Facile à entretenir.
- Robot configurable dans ses moindres détails.
Points faibles
- Obstacle contourné au plus large.
- Les plinthes et les coins pourraient être mieux aspirés.
- Application touffue.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une personnalisation avancée pour compenser quelques écarts le long des murs
Le logiciel de gestion donne accès à de très nombreux paramètres de configuration pour ajuster les débits d'eau ou les puissances d'aspiration selon chaque pièce. Le Mova P70 Pro Ultra a tendance à contourner les obstacles au plus large et laisse parfois de la poussière au niveau des plinthes ou des coins, une concession sans gravité pour les logements aux pièces dégagées.
DJI Romo P : l'autre option face au Mova P70 Pro Ultra
Le DJI Romo P s'appuie sur une cartographie précise et une application particulièrement ergonomique, associées à une station d'entretien complète. En contrepartie, il montre des limites sur les taches incrustées et sur les surfaces comme les tapis épais, ce qui se traduit par une note actuelle de 3,5/5.
Le DJI Romo P se montre plus à l'aise sur l'évitement d'obstacles, mais il coûte 101,00 € de plus que le Mova P70 Pro Ultra qui conserve une note actuelle de 5/5 et une efficacité supérieure sur les taches tenaces.
DJI Romo P
Points forts
- Navigation efficace.
- App complète, mais simple à maîtriser.
- Entretien facile grâce à la station.
Points faibles
- Manque de puissance d'aspiration.
- En difficulté face aux taches très incrustées.
- Sac à poussière compliqué à recycler.

articles.title: « Des crimes graves » : Huawei reconnu coupable de fraude, de blanchiment et d’espionnage aux États-Unis
articles.text:
Ce 24 novembre 2026, un procès de 11 semaines contre Huawei s’est achevé à New York. Au total, 12 chefs d’accusation ont été retenus contre le géant chinois. L’entreprise chinoise a été acquittée pour deux d’entre eux, à savoir association de malfaiteurs et entrave à la justice. En revanche, elle a été reconnue coupable pour les dix autres, et autant dire qu’ils sont lourds.
Huawei reconnu coupable de 10 chefs d’accusation
Comme le rapporte Bloomberg, Huawei a notamment été reconnu coupable de fraude bancaire, de blanchiment d’argent et de vol de secrets industriels appartenant à des entreprises américaines, comme Cisco, T-Mobile ou encore Motorola. L’entreprise chinoise aurait ainsi mis en place un véritable système de vol de secrets commerciaux pendant une période de 20 ans, avec notamment des détournements de code source et de technologies de concurrents.
Huawei a également été reconnu coupable d’avoir violé des sanctions américaines en menant des activités commerciales illégales en Iran, via sa filiale Skycom, spécialisée dans les télécommunications. L’entreprise chinoise aurait dissimulé ses liens avec Skycom auprès de banques comme HSBC afin de pouvoir continuer à mener ses activités en Iran.
Pour Tysen A. Duva, procureur général adjoint de la division pénale du ministère américain de la Justice, la conclusion de ce procès est claire : « Pendant plus de deux décennies, Huawei a bâti un empire sur la fraude, le pillage et le mensonge et les crimes de l’entreprise ont menacé le système financier américain […] et porté atteinte à notre sécurité intérieure ». De son côté, James Barnacle, chef du bureau du FBI à New York, a qualifié les chefs d’accusation retenus de « crimes graves », et a déclaré : « Le succès de Huawei repose sur la tromperie et le vol, et le FBI n’hésitera jamais à poursuivre ceux qui profitent de la loi ».
Rappelons que Washington envisage de nouvelles restrictions envers Nvidia à la suite de l’affaire Jensen Huang. Il est désormais fort probable que Huawei suive le même chemin.
Le géant chinois estime ces accusations sans fondement
L’entreprise chinoise s’est particulièrement félicitée d’avoir été acquittée de deux chefs d’accusation (association de malfaiteurs et entrave à la justice). En ce qui concerne les 10 autres chefs d’accusation retenus, elle considère qu’ils ne sont tout simplement pas fondés. Dans un communiqué, Huawei explique que les accusations retenues sont « sans base factuelle ou fondement juridique ». Le géant chinois l’affirme : « aucun tribunal n’a jamais reconnu la responsabilité de Huawei pour détournement délibéré de propriété intellectuelle, et l’entreprise n’a jamais été condamnée à verser des dommages-intérêts pour détournement de secrets d’affaires ».
De son côté, le porte-parole du ministère chinois des Affaires étrangères, Guo Jiakun, a dénoncé un acharnement et a déclaré que son pays « s’oppose fermement à la répression et à l’endiguement des entreprises chinoises par les États-Unis ».
Quoi qu’il en soit, Huawei risque désormais de sérieuses amendes. L’entreprise a d’ores et déjà fait part de son intention de faire appel.

articles.title: Qué electrodomésticos consumen más energía y cómo reducir la factura de luz en casa
articles.text:
La nevera, la secadora, el horno eléctrico, la lavadora y la plancha figuran entre los electrodomésticos que más energía consumen en casa, aunque el impacto final sobre la factura de luz depende de la potencia, el tiempo de uso y los hábitos de cada familia. Identificar qué equipos permanecen conectados durante más horas permite detectar dónde conviene actuar primero.
El consumo eléctrico no depende solo de los aparatos más grandes. Una secadora puede gastar mucha energía en poco tiempo, mientras una nevera mantiene un gasto continuo durante todo el día. Conocer esa diferencia ayuda a ajustar rutinas, aprovechar programas eficientes y evitar gastos innecesarios sin dejar de utilizar los equipos necesarios en el hogar.
La potencia y el tiempo explican el consumo
La fórmula básica para entender el gasto energético es sencilla: consumo igual a potencia multiplicada por tiempo de uso. Un aparato de alta potencia puede elevar la factura aunque se utilice pocos minutos, mientras otro menos exigente puede acumular consumo si permanece encendido de forma constante.
También importa la frecuencia. La lavadora, por ejemplo, puede tener un impacto moderado si se utiliza pocas veces por semana y con carga completa. El gasto crece cuando se realizan ciclos pequeños, se selecciona agua caliente o se repiten lavados innecesarios. El hábito tiene tanto peso como el electrodoméstico.
La eficiencia del equipo es otro factor. Un aparato antiguo puede necesitar más electricidad para realizar la misma tarea que uno moderno. Sin embargo, reemplazarlo no siempre es la primera medida necesaria: ajustar la temperatura, evitar el uso en vacío y revisar el mantenimiento puede reducir el consumo sin una compra inmediata.
La nevera consume poco por hora, pero funciona siempre
La nevera suele estar entre los principales consumos mensuales porque funciona las 24 horas. Aunque su potencia no sea comparable a la de una secadora o un horno, su actividad continua hace que represente una parte relevante de la factura eléctrica.
Regular correctamente la temperatura permite evitar un esfuerzo innecesario del motor. Una puerta mal cerrada, juntas deterioradas, acumulación de hielo o exceso de alimentos que bloquean la circulación del aire pueden obligar al equipo a trabajar durante más tiempo.
También conviene no introducir alimentos muy calientes y limpiar la parte trasera cuando acumule polvo. Estas medidas favorecen la ventilación y el rendimiento. Mantener la nevera en buenas condiciones puede reducir el gasto sin cambiar la forma de conservar los alimentos.
Secadora, horno y plancha concentran picos de gasto
La secadora encabeza las listas de consumo intensivo. Utiliza resistencias eléctricas para producir calor y puede gastar una cantidad elevada de energía durante cada ciclo. Secar la ropa al aire libre o en un espacio ventilado reduce su uso y permite reservarla para días de lluvia o cargas urgentes.
El horno eléctrico y la cocina eléctrica también requieren atención. Ambos combinan alta potencia con tiempos de funcionamiento prolongados. Aprovechar el calor residual, cocinar varias preparaciones al mismo tiempo y evitar abrir el horno con frecuencia son prácticas que ayudan a controlar el gasto.
La plancha presenta un consumo alto, aunque puntual. Reunir varias prendas en una sola sesión evita que el aparato deba calentarse repetidas veces. Separar la ropa por tipo de tejido y comenzar por las prendas que requieren menor temperatura permite organizar mejor el uso.
Lavadora y microondas dependen de cómo se utilicen
La lavadora tiene un consumo medio, pero aumenta si se usan ciclos con agua caliente o si se enciende varias veces para pocas prendas. Utilizarla con carga completa y seleccionar programas eco ayuda a reducir la electricidad y el agua empleados en cada lavado.
El microondas requiere bastante potencia, pero durante períodos breves. Por eso su impacto suele ser menor que el de un horno eléctrico. Para calentar cantidades pequeñas o descongelar alimentos, puede representar una alternativa con menor gasto.
Televisores, consolas, cargadores y otros dispositivos electrónicos tienen un consumo individual reducido, aunque pueden sumar si permanecen conectados en modo de espera. Desconectar equipos que no se utilizan o emplear regletas con interruptor permite cortar ese gasto acumulado.
Las estimaciones generales sirven como guía, pero cada hogar tiene necesidades distintas. El número de personas, el clima, el tipo de cocina, la antigüedad de los equipos y las horas de uso modifican el resultado final.
Reducir la factura de luz comienza por revisar las rutinas diarias: usar la lavadora llena, limitar la secadora, ajustar la nevera, activar los modos eco y evitar el consumo en espera. Medir el uso real de cada aparato permite pasar de una lista general a decisiones basadas en lo que ocurre dentro de cada hogar.

articles.title: Zu viel versprochen: Warum Ubisoft wegen eines Piratenspiels verklagt wird
articles.text:
Zu viel versprochen: Warum Ubisoft wegen eines Piratenspiels verklagt wird
Die Juristen des französischen Spieleriesen Ubisoft haben eine vielzitierte Aussage von Firmenchef Yves Guillemot über ein neues Game vor Gericht als reine Werbeübertreibung eingestuft. Das berichtet der Journalist Stephen Totilo in seinem Newsletter Game File. Konkret sprachen die Anwälte von „Puffery“ – also von einer allgemeinen, subjektiven Anpreisung ohne konkrete Tatsachenbehauptung, wie sie in der Werbung üblich ist. Guillemot hatte den Titel „Skull and Bones“, ein Piratenabenteuer, als „AAAA“-Titel bezeichnet, also als besonders hochwertig. Wie sich herausstellte, war es das Game aber nicht.
Hintergrund der Affäre ist eine Klage aus dem Jahr 2025. Ein US-Amerikaner warf Ubisoft vor, Verbraucher mit den Aussagen zu „Skull and Bones“ in die Irre geführt und damit gegen das Verbraucherschutzgesetz des Bundesstaats Kansas verstoßen zu haben. Weit kam die Klage jedoch nicht: Der Kläger scheiterte mit mehreren Anträgen, seit September ist das Verfahren eingestellt.
„Quadruple-A“ für 70 US-Dollar
Dennoch zeigen die nun veröffentlichten Gerichtsaussagen, wie Ubisoft offenbar wirklich dachte. Guillemot hatte die Formulierung im Februar 2024 in einer Telefonkonferenz zu den Quartalszahlen benutzt. Dort verteidigte er den Preis von 70 US-Dollar für das Piratenspiel. Auf die Frage, ob ein Free-to-Play-Modell nicht besser zu einem Live-Service-Game passe – also zu einem Titel, der über Jahre mit neuen Inhalten versorgt wird –, verwies er auf den Umfang.
„Es ist ein wirklich vollwertiges Triple … Quadruple-A-Spiel, das auf lange Sicht liefern wird“, sagte Guillemot laut einem Transkript des Calls. Mit dem „AAAA“ wollte Guillemot das Spiel noch über die übliche Blockbuster-Kategorie „AAA“ stellen. Geerntet hat das dann vor allem Spott.
Zehn Jahre Entwicklung, ein Flop
„Skull and Bones“ erschien im Februar 2024 nach über zehn Jahren Entwicklungszeit, mehreren Verschiebungen und einem kompletten Neustart der Entwicklung. Bei Kritikern und Spielern fiel der Titel durch. Das verantwortliche Studio Ubisoft Singapur hat seitdem ein Remake von „Assassin’s Creed Black Flag“ entwickelt.
Ubisoft ließ das Verfahren des Spielers von Kansas nach Kalifornien verlegen. Dort kam der Fall dann nicht mehr voran. Das Register des Bundesgerichts in Los Angeles verzeichnet am 9. September eine freiwillige Einstellung – angestoßen vom Kläger oder von beiden Parteien. Ein Gericht hat über die Vorwürfe damit nie entschieden. Die peinliche „AAAA“-Aussage bleibt in den Büchern.

articles.title: Cognition’s new engineers aren’t even downloading code anymore — they build entirely through Devin
articles.text:
Cognition’s new engineers aren’t even downloading code anymore — they build entirely through Devin
Some engineers joining Cognition no longer set up local development environments. Instead, Devin has become their primary interface for software development.
Speaking to Patrick O’Shaughnessy on Tuesday’s episode of Invest Like the Best, Cognition co-founder and CEO Scott Wu describes how the company’s internal engineering practices have changed as coding agents have become more capable.
No terminal, no download
“The funniest moment for me, I would say, was actually around like four or five months ago when we started to realize that new engineers that joined our team just didn’t even download the code on their computer,” Wu says. “Like they didn’t pull up a terminal. They didn’t run a command line or anything.”
“new engineers that joined our team just didn’t even download the code on their computer … They didn’t run a command line or anything.”
Over roughly a year, Cognition doubled its engineering headcount while increasing its rate of merged pull requests 20-fold, Wu says. That amounts to approximately ten times as many merged pull requests per engineer, despite the company’s already extensive use of AI coding tools a year earlier.
Perhaps more significant, Wu estimates, is that approximately 90% of Cognition’s internal Devin usage is now automated in some form.
When Devin runs itself
Wu cites incident response as an example of Cognition’s automated Devin workflows, where an error can trigger an investigation before an on-call engineer intervenes.
“It doesn’t involve a human saying, ‘Hey, Devin, I need you to go work on this thing’ to kick it off.”
“It doesn’t involve a human saying, ‘Hey, Devin, I need you to go work on this thing’ to kick it off,” Wu says.
Although Wu does not specify whether the 90% figure represents session count, token consumption, or another metric, automated execution has implications for compute provisioning and budget allocation as inference demand becomes less dependent on individual developer activity.
Cognition has already introduced hierarchical budgets for Devin, which give enterprises spending controls across organizational levels.
250,000 pull requests monthly
Wu says one of Cognition’s largest banking customers was on track to merge 250,000 pull requests with Devin in October. Until a few months earlier, the entire organization had been merging approximately 400,000 pull requests per month.
The bank has approximately 80,000 engineering personnel, according to Wu, and only a fraction of the organization had been fully onboarded to Devin at the time of the interview.
Separately, Citi CEO Jane Fraser says during the bank’s third-quarter earnings call that 14,000 engineers use Devin.
Neither Cognition’s internal figures nor the banking customer’s projected PR volume account for the complexity of individual changes. Wu does not provide corresponding data on change failure rates or review workloads, metrics that would help establish whether the rest of the SDLC has kept pace with implementation.
The disparity between implementation and review capacity has already prompted vendors such as CodeRabbit to expand into agentic change management.
Wu argues that enterprise adoption also requires engineering leaders to reconsider their roadmaps and organizational structures to accommodate additional implementation capacity.
Watching the agent swarms
The shift from individual background agents to swarms is a particular concern for Wu because monitoring becomes more difficult when multiple agents work together.
Cognition has been exploring this execution model with its recently introduced Devin Bots, persistent agents that manage other agents’ work.
Wu stresses the need to catch unintended agent behavior early and limit what agents can access, especially when workflows run without an engineer supervising them.
The engineering skill ceiling hasn’t changed
“The barrier to entry has for sure gotten a lot lower,” Wu says. “However, I think the skill ceiling and, you know, a lot of the particular skill sets that you need are still very much the same as they always have been.”
“I think people who can do that really well have always been valuable and now they’re just 10 times more valuable.”
For Wu, writing code is only one part of software engineering. Engineers still have to figure out what an incomplete or ambiguous specification actually means and make architectural decisions that could affect the business for years, even if an agent handles the implementation.
“I think people who can do that really well have always been valuable and now they’re just 10 times more valuable,” Wu says.

articles.title: A private 231-inch workspace that fits in your pocket
articles.text:
RayNeo's GT AR glasses are $249 for Black Friday, a big-screen workspace you can give every remote and traveling employee for under $250
A plug-and-play virtual display for hybrid teams
Equipping a remote or traveling team with a second screen usually means buying, shipping, and carrying monitors. RayNeo's GT AR glasses skip all three.
They weigh 68g, connect over one USB-C cable, and give any compatible laptop, tablet, or phone a private virtual display of up to 231 inches. This Black Friday and Cyber Monday, they are available for $249 on Amazon (was $329), a saving of $80 per pair. You can also grab a unit on RayNeo's official website for the same price.
The GT offers three virtual screen sizes: 136, 201, and 231 inches. Its Steady, Pinned, and Follow modes let each person place the screen where they want it. You can keep things compact when you want focus, or scale up when you are working across spreadsheets, long documents, or a crowded slide deck. The display is Full HD at 1920 × 1080, delivered by a 0.6-inch Micro-OLED panel with a 46-degree field of view. That is plenty for documents, email, presentations, and video calls. It is not a 4K, multi-monitor replacement, and it does not pretend to be, but as a single large, sharp screen that goes wherever you go, it does the job well.
Plug-and-play display glasses that give any laptop or phone a private virtual screen of up to 231 inches. Rated 4.0 out of 5 from 235 reviews on Amazon.
A lightweight AR device featuring 120Hz micro-OLED displays, up to 1,200 nits of brightness, 3840Hz dimming, adjustable nose pads, and virtual screens reaching 231 inches.
Why businesses should look at them
The pitch is a portable screen that doesn't cost desk space, luggage space, or setup time. For hybrid and remote staff, it means a large display at a kitchen table or a co-working desk without buying and shipping a monitor. For frequent travelers such as sales teams and consultants, it brings a big screen for documents, spreadsheets and video to hotels, airports and trains. It also suits hot-desking offices, where people can carry their own screen from desk to desk.
The glasses give you a personal view of your screen, and the optional Sound Tube cuts sound leakage by up to 80%, which helps when you're handling documents in public.
For IT teams, the setup is simple. There's no computing box and no software to install on compatible devices, and the glasses support Windows and Mac laptops, Android phones, iPads and iPhone 15 and later, so a mixed fleet shouldn't be a problem.
Comfort matters for all-day use, and at 68g with adjustable nose pads, the GT is light enough for long sessions. The micro-OLED displays run at 120Hz with up to 1,200 nits of perceived brightness, and 3840Hz dimming is designed to reduce flicker.
What it costs a team
At $249 a pair, ten staff members cost $2,490, which is $800 less than the list price of $3,290. Adding Amazon's 2-year protection plan at $24.99 per pair brings the cost to about $274 a seat. Amazon also lists a 3-year plan at $33.99, and returns are open until January 31, 2027, so a small pilot carries little risk.
Before you roll it out
These are display glasses, not computers, so each device needs USB-C with DisplayPort output, and devices without it need an adapter. The lenses sit at a fixed 64mm IPD, and the 3DoF tracking follows head rotation but not walking around a room. RayNeo markets the GT mainly for entertainment, so features such as multi-screen setups or fleet management aren't advertised.
Price Context
At $249, the GT is well below its $329 regular price. It launched in September at a $299 sale price, so this is $50 lower than the launch deal. It's also cheap for what it offers, since XREAL and VITURE glasses with spatial tracking often cost more than $400.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the RayNeo GT if... you manage remote, hybrid, or traveling staff and want an affordable pilot of a portable large-screen workspace.

articles.title: Friedrich Nietzsche, filósofo: “A menudo contradecimos una opinión cuando en realidad solo nos resulta desagradable el tono con que fue expresada”
articles.text:
Friedrich Nietzsche constató que uno de los problemas de las conversaciones es que a veces odiamos la opinión de alguien por el tono que usa. “A menudo contradecimos una opinión cuando en realidad solo nos resulta desagradable el tono con que fue expresada”, escribió en el aforismo 303 de Humano, demasiado humano. Así aparece en el libro.
Se publicó en 1878. Por entonces, el filósofo alemán se alejaba del pensamiento de Schopenhauer. También estaba en peores términos con Richard Wagner (de quien había sido amigo). En la obra analizó las motivaciones de los seres humanos y puso en cuestión la idea de que nuestras opiniones vienen de un proceso racional por encima de los afectos.
Es entonces cuando hace esta observación sobre el tono. Podemos contradecir una opinión aunque realmente lo que desagrade sea el tono de la persona que afirma algo. Es una de las reacciones habituales, aunque Nietzsche no afirma que sean la mayoría de los casos de desacuerdo.
Asoció las creencias con el temperamento. En el aforismo 608 escribió que buscamos inconscientemente principios y doctrinas que se adapten a nuestro modo de ser. Incluso podemos decir después que son estas ideas las que han dado forma a nuestro carácter (aunque Nietzsche dijo lo contrario).
En el 571 escribió también que cuando nos hacen una pregunta, de pronto la primera opinión que tenemos es la que suele ser habitual en nuestro grupo/posición/origen. Para Nietzsche esto no necesariamente era una opinión propia.
Una de las cosas que estudia la psicología es el sesgo de confirmación. Se trata de la tendencia a buscar información que confirme nuestras expectativas previas. Al mismo tiempo, se descarta o no se busca la información que refute esas expectativas. Esto no quiere decir que rechacemos una idea por el tono que utiliza la persona que la presenta.
También escribió sobre la rigidez de las convicciones. En el aforismo 637 escribió que las opiniones nacen de pasiones, pero también que se endurecen gracias a la pereza del pensamiento. En el 483 escribió: “Las convicciones son enemigos más peligrosos de la verdad que las mentiras”. Pueden verse ambos pasajes en el primer volumen.
Qué permite afirmar la psicología sobre el tono
El tono es uno de los aspectos que tenemos en cuenta para interpretar a la otra persona. Existe una famosa regla (la 7-38-55) de Albert Mehrabian. Él mismo explica que sus porcentajes están basados en unos experimentos sobre la comunicación de sentimientos y actitudes. En su explicación de “Silent Messages” aclara que estos porcentajes no pueden aplicarse en otros casos. Por ejemplo, el 38 % no es el porcentaje de contribución de la voz en cualquier tipo de conversación.
Uno de los aspectos que se estudia en psicología es la reactancia ante amenazas a la libertad, como explica una revisión de Christina Steindl y cols. Esto no quiere decir que cuando la otra persona sube el tono dejemos de procesar las palabras que dice.
Por otro lado, hay que tener en cuenta que cuando se cita a algún personaje conocido, es importante ser preciso. En este caso, en el aforismo de Nietzsche se plantea el problema de confundir opinión y desagrado por el tono. Además, en el 484 añade una observación sobre nuestro juicio. Escribió que somos más críticos con el pensador que plantea algo que nos desagrada. Sin embargo, sería más lógico aplicar ese rigor a lo que nos gusta.
Foto | Wikimedia Commons, Nataliya Vaitkevich en Pexels
