articles.title: Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days Exploited in Suspected AI-Assisted Attacks
articles.text:
Threat actors exploited several Mitel MiCollab vulnerabilities as zero-days in a data theft campaign, according to Accenture’s Apex Labs. CISA on Wednesday added five MiCollab flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
In one attack observed by Accenture, hackers gained privileged access to a MiCollab server and quickly reached the targeted organization’s identity infrastructure, ultimately stealing sensitive business information.
The MiCollab business collaboration platform enables employees to communicate through calls, messages, and virtual meetings. Accenture noted that the product’s frequent internet exposure and integration with Active Directory make it particularly attractive to hackers.
Mitel on November 16 announced patches for five vulnerabilities affecting the product’s audio, web and video conferencing component, including arbitrary file upload, XML injection, unauthorized access, command injection, and authentication bypass. They can all be exploited by unauthenticated attackers, and two critical bugs allow arbitrary command execution.
The security holes are tracked as CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133303, CVE-2026-133311, CVE-2026-133323, and CVE-2026-133324.
Accenture found evidence that the vulnerabilities were exploited in the wild before Mitel published its advisory. The company determined that threat actors deployed a web shell on a victim’s systems on November 15.
According to Accenture, the attackers executed commands on a MiCollab server just 12 minutes after the first request, and gained root privileges within half an hour.
The hackers harvested additional credentials and, roughly 20 hours after their first observed request, gained access to internal backup and database servers.
The investigation uncovered evidence that some of the malicious activity may have been driven by AI tools, with the attacker’s infrastructure communicating with two unnamed commercial AI API services.
“Because the telemetry is sampled, Apex Labs cannot determine precisely how the threat actor used the services. However, the observed activity is consistent with potential uses such as data triage, operational support for exploitation or web-shell activity, and preparation of extortion material,” Accenture noted.
It added that communications between the attackers’ infrastructure and the AI services resumed — after an eight-hour silence — at precisely the same second that the hackers sent an authentication bypass request to the targeted MiCollab server.
The company also found evidence of compromise at a second victim, with a MiCollab server communicating with the same attacker’s infrastructure since November 9. However, Accenture could not establish how the second server was hacked, as it had been affected by older vulnerabilities as well.
The researchers have not linked the attacks to a known cybercrime group, but believe they may have been part of an extortion campaign.
Mitel has released patches, but its advisory — last updated on November 24 — does not mention in-the-wild exploitation of the vulnerabilities.
Accenture warned organizations that attackers may have compromised their MiCollab servers before the fixes were installed and urged them to check for indicators of compromise (IoCs).
CISA added all five vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog, instructing federal agencies to address four of them by November 28; the last one has a December 9 deadline.
Threat actors regularly target Mitel products. CISA’s KEV catalog currently includes a dozen such vulnerabilities.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.text:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.
Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds
Understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.
However, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.
At RUN, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.
Tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.
To appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.
Making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.
Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling
To observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.
In the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.
The researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.
Simon Maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "By varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond."
This approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.
What makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.
This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.
"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.
A Surprising 500-Attosecond Delay
To understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with Prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit."
Their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.
At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.
For example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit."
The team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.
The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.
A Hidden Tradeoff Between Space and Time
Raffael Spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "The more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially."
In other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.
To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.
This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.
Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.
The findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.
Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?
Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.
One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.
Transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.
Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.
"In the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains Prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.
The implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.
"In the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant CMOS technology," adds Prof. Rupert Huber.
That possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.
For Repp and Huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Regensburg. Original written by Karoline Stürmer. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- S. Maier, R. Spachtholz, K. Glöckl, C. M. Bustamante, S. Lingl, M. Maczejka, J. Schön, A. Riedel, K. Richter, F. J. Giessibl, F. P. Bonafé, M. A. Huber, A. Rubio, J. Repp, R. Huber. Tracking electrons at the space-time limit. Nature Photonics, 2026; 20 (8): 961 DOI: 10.1038/s41566-026-01932-0

articles.title: Deichmann, Office Partner und Co.: Warum sich gerade die Meldungen über Datenlecks häufen
articles.text:
Deichmann, Office Partner und Co.: Warum sich gerade die Meldungen über Datenlecks häufen
Notebooksbilliger meldete im Oktober einen unbefugten Zugriff auf Kund:innendaten in fünfstelliger Höhe, Mindfactory und Office Partner (Letzterer aufgrund eines Datenabflusses bei einem Dienstleister) mussten den Kund:innen Anfang und Mitte November einen Cyberangriff mit möglichem Diebstahl personenbezogener Kundendaten erklären. Deichmann und Snipes hatten diese Woche unbefugte Zugriffe auf Kunden- und Bestelldaten zu verzeichnen. Kein Zweifel: Aktuell häufen sich die Meldungen über Hackerangriffe und Datenabflüsse im deutschen Onlinehandel.
Schaut man auf die Zahlen, wird deutlich, dass Hackerangriffe im deutschen Onlinehandel und in der Geschäftswelt häufiger sind als es zunächst scheint. Laut einer kürzlich veröffentlichten Studie des IT-Branchenverbands Bitkom zu Datenlecks wurden immerhin 55 Prozent der befragten Verbraucher:innen schon einmal über einen sie betreffenden Datenabfluss informiert. Unter den Jüngeren ist der Wert mit 63 Prozent sogar noch höher. Drei von vier Nutzer:innen befürchten, dass in einem solchen Fall ihre Daten missbraucht werden. Wohl auch deswegen haben immerhin schon einmal 14 Prozent selbst über einen Dienst wie Haveibeenpwned überprüft, ob da ihre Daten in entsprechenden Hacks auftauchen.
Händler müssen Kunden informieren
Für Händler:innen und Unternehmen aller Art ist ein solcher Sicherheitsvorfall nicht nur mit einem peinlichen Imageschaden verbunden, sondern er bedeutet auch, dass damit Informationspflichten gegenüber den Betroffenen einhergehen, soweit weiterhin Missbrauch droht. Natürlich müssen Händler:innen zunächst das Sicherheitsleck möglichst schnell schließen, damit weitere unbefugte Datenzugriffe unterbunden werden können. Neben dem Ermitteln des Ausmaßes geht es aber auch um Datenforensik, also darum, entsprechende Beweismittel und Protokolldaten zu sichern. Hier können neben den inzwischen oftmals recht gut geschulten Ermittlungsbehörden auch externe IT-Sicherheitsexpert:innen zum Einsatz kommen.
Besonders knifflig kann dies sein, wenn hieran noch weitere Unternehmen beteiligt sind, etwa ein Zahlungsdienstleister oder ein SaaS-Dienst, auf den der Händler zurückgreift. Einen solchen Fall gab es kürzlich auch im Zusammenhang mit Cleverbridge. Der Kölner E-Commerce-Dienstleister informierte vor wenigen Tagen darüber, dass Angreifer auf der Plattform gespeicherte Zahlungskartendaten kopieren konnten. Betroffen davon sind Personen und Unternehmen, die über einen der mit Cleverbridge zusammenarbeitenden Anbieter etwas bezahlt haben, sodass Kartendaten dort gespeichert waren. Da die Kund:innen das aber in der Regel nicht wissen können, ist auch hier der jeweilige Händler gefragt.
Für Unternehmen – egal ob mittelbar oder unmittelbar betroffen – gibt es hier klare Informationspflichten nach der DSGVO. Neben einer Meldung an die Datenschutzbehörde sind die Kund:innen, die das betriff, in geeigneter Weise (meist per E-Mail) zu informieren. Diese müssen verstehen können, was passiert ist und welche Folgen drohen können – und vor allem, welche Gegenmaßnahmen sie ergreifen sollten.
Kunden sollten sich schützen – spätestens, wenn Daten abgeflossen sind
Wie gravierend ein Datenschutzvorfall ist, davon hängt es ab, wie Kund:innen darauf reagieren sollten. Meist wird geraten, das Passwort zu ändern, was man natürlich beherzigen sollte. Dabei ist aber zu prüfen, ob die Mail tatsächlich vom jeweiligen Dienst kommt oder es sich um eine Phishing-Mail handelt, die gerade auf die Zugangsdaten einzelner Verbraucher:innen abzielt. Sinnvoll ist daher, auf die jeweilige Original-Website im Browser zu gehen und nicht auf irgendwelche Links in der Mail zu klicken.
Sinnvoll ist in diesem Zusammenhang auch, wenn nicht schon geschehen, eine Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung zu aktivieren, wenn es diese Möglichkeit seitens des Händlers gibt. Auch Passkeys können eine gute, passwortlose Alternative sein. Dass man nicht für jeden Zugang dasselbe Passwort verwenden sollte, dürfte klar sein – wird aber erfahrungsgemäß immer noch von vielen Verbraucher:innen nicht beherzigt, wie entsprechende Tests mit geleakten Passwörtern zeigen.
Wenn Zahlungsdaten abgegriffen wurden, ist zudem zu prüfen, ob diese anderweitig genutzt werden könnten – bei einer reinen IBAN ist das in der Regel nicht der Fall, obwohl theoretisch auch hierüber unautorisierte Verträge abgeschlossen werden könnten. Bei vollständigen Kreditkartendaten kann es dagegen schon ein ernsteres Sicherheitsrisiko darstellen. Generell sollte man hier die Kontobewegungen und Kreditkarten- und Zahlungsbewegungen im Blick behalten, um im Zweifelsfall umgehend bei der Bank oder Kreditkartengesellschaft Einspruch zu erheben.
Oft haben Kunden Anspruch auf Schadenersatz
Ob Nutzer:innen ein Schadenersatz zusteht, hängt vom Einzelfall ab. Hier gab es in den letzten Jahren unterschiedliche Urteile. Unterschiedlich ist dabei auch die Frage beantwortet worden, ob dafür ein entsprechender materieller oder immaterieller Schaden nachgewiesen werden muss. So sieht Artikel 82 der DSGVO zwar einen Anspruch auf Ersatz materieller und immaterieller Schäden vor, die durch einen Verstoß gegen die Datenschutz-Grundverordnung entstanden sind – und der Europäische Gerichtshof hat am 14. Dezember 2023 entschieden (Az. C-340/21), dass schon die begründete Befürchtung eines zukünftigen Missbrauchs personenbezogener Daten einen immateriellen Schaden darstellen kann.
Allerdings begründet nicht jeder erfolgreiche Hackerangriff automatisch einen DSGVO-Verstoß des betroffenen Unternehmens. Auch einen pauschalen Schadensersatzbetrag, der jedem Opfer eines Datenlecks zusteht, gibt es nicht – hier gilt das juristentypische „kommt darauf an“.
Tage rund um die Black Week besonders interessant?
Dass wir dieser Tage besonders viele derartige Vorfälle sehen, kann Zufall sein, muss es aber nicht. Denn die Zeit um den Black Friday und das Vorweihnachstgeschäft ist für Hacker:innen besonders dankbar. Zum einen bestellen jetzt viele Verbraucher:innen bei unterschiedlichen Händlern innerhalb kürzester Zeit Waren, sodass die Zahl der Bestellbestätigungen und Versandbenachrichtigungen gerade besonders hoch ist. Das bedeutet, dass betrügerische Nachrichten in dieser Zeit weniger leicht auffallen.
Wenn also Cyberkriminelle über echte Bestelldaten verfügen, können sie etwa mit gefälschten Nachrichten über angebliche Lieferprobleme, ausstehende Zahlungen oder Rückerstattungen versuchen, weitere sensible Daten abzugreifen. Umgekehrt ist diese umsatzstärkste Zeit des Jahres ein besonders ungünstiger Zeitpunkt für einen derartigen Sicherheitsvorfall. Denn bereits ein mehrstündiger Ausfall des Onlineshops kann erhebliche wirtschaftliche Folgen haben, das erhöht die Erpressbarkeit von Unternehmen.
Dennoch lässt sich daraus nicht zwingend ableiten, dass in dieser Zeit mehrerfolgreiche Hackerangriffe auf Onlinehändler und Plattformbetreiber stattfinden. Hier fehlen schlichtweg diesbezüglich belastbarer Daten, auch wenn es die genannten Indizien und Gründe gibt. Verbraucher:innen sollten aber vor allem beim Kauf bei ihnen bisher nicht vertrauten Shops aufpassen, dass es sich dabei nicht um Fake-Shops handelt, diese werden bekanntermaßen selbst von den einschlägigen LLMs empfohlen.
! Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: From selling drones to intelligence: Where will the next wave of value come from?
articles.text:
From selling drones to intelligence: Where will the next wave of value come from?
As the drone industry evolves, the focus is shifting from aircraft specifications to the value delivered to customers. The next phase of growth will be shaped by AI, software, integrated technologies and service-led business models.
When we look at the value of a drone, it is easy to focus on the aircraft itself. How long can it fly? How much weight can it carry? How far can it travel? These are important questions, and they will continue to matter. But there is another question that deserves equal attention: what does the customer actually get from that flight?
A drone may spend several hours monitoring an area and return with a large volume of footage. Yet, if the operator has to spend several more hours reviewing that footage to identify something important, much of the benefit is lost. The real value lies not simply in collecting information, but in making sense of it and using it at the right time.
I believe this is where the next phase of the drone industry will take shape.
The value does not end when the drone lands
As drones become more widely used across defence, infrastructure, mapping, and homeland security, customer expectations are changing. Buying a drone is increasingly becoming the beginning of a larger operational requirement.
Consider a team monitoring a long stretch of border or inspecting a large infrastructure project. The drone can capture images, video and location data, but the customer needs more than these individual inputs. They need to know what has changed, whether something requires attention and what action should follow.
This is where software and artificial intelligence (AI) have a pivotal role to play. Automated video summaries, event detection, and searchable annotations can make it easier to find relevant information without having to watch hours of recordings. The idea is not to remove people from the decision-making process but to help them focus on what matters and make better-informed decisions.
Experience is difficult to replicate
There is something about technology that becomes clear only when it is used regularly in the field. A drone may perform well during testing, but actual operating conditions can be very different. Terrain, weather, temperature and connectivity can all affect how a system performs.
This is why the experience gained from real deployments matters. Across the industry, drone manufacturers are learning that building a reliable product is not just about getting the engineering right. It is also about understanding how customers use the technology, what difficulties they encounter and where improvements are needed.
The scale of deployments is important in this regard. Every mission provides an opportunity to understand how the aircraft, payload, software and communication systems perform in real conditions. Repeated operations can also reveal patterns that may not emerge during controlled testing.
Over time, this learning becomes an advantage. Companies that stay closely connected to actual operating conditions are better placed to develop technology that works outside controlled testing environments. It also helps them understand what customers need, rather than relying only on what they initially ask for.
Technology must work together
Intelligence is not limited to what happens to the data after a flight. It also depends on whether the drone can complete its mission reliably in the first place.
For instance, a drone operating in a challenging environment needs dependable communication and navigation. In defence applications, electronic interference, jamming and spoofing can create additional complications. Similarly, operations in remote locations may have limited network connectivity, making it important to process certain information closer to where it is collected.
This is why the industry needs to look at the entire technology stack rather than treating the aircraft, software, payload and communication systems as separate elements. Secure command-and-control systems, resilient navigation, edge computing and specialised payloads all contribute to the final outcome.
This shift is also reflected in India's evolving defence procurement priorities. The Defence Acquisition Council's recent approval of capital acquisition proposals worth approximately Rs 2.12 lakh crore includes requirements for Long Range UAS, Surveillance UAV, Integrated Surveillance and Strike Systems, and Long Range Kamikaze Drone Systems. With approximately 82% of the proposed procurements earmarked for the Indian industry, the direction is significant. It signals an opportunity for domestic manufacturers to move beyond building individual platforms towards developing integrated, mission-ready capabilities that address increasingly complex operational requirements.
This also helps reduce dependence on external technologies in areas where control, security and reliability are particularly important.
The business model will evolve with the technology
This shift also has implications for how drone companies build sustainable businesses. Hardware sales will remain an important part of the industry. However, the opportunity extends well beyond the initial sale of an aircraft. A drone has an operating lifecycle that involves software, analytics, maintenance, upgrades, training and support. Each of these can contribute to the value delivered to a customer over time.
Models such as Drone-as-a-Service, software subscriptions and analytics-led solutions can allow customers to access drone capabilities without having to manage every aspect of ownership and operations themselves. For providers, these models can create opportunities for longer-term customer relationships and a more diversified revenue mix.
From a business perspective, this also creates opportunities for repeat engagements and more predictable customer relationships. But these models will succeed only when they offer a clear economic or operational benefit. A customer will continue paying for a service if it helps reduce manual effort, improve efficiency or deliver information that was previously difficult to access.
The objective should not simply be to introduce more software or services. It should be to make the overall solution more useful to the customer.
The next opportunity is in delivering outcomes
The drone industry is still evolving, and there are challenges to address, particularly around data security, system integration, reliability and the economics of scaling these solutions. Not every application will require the same level of automation or intelligence. What matters is understanding the customer's actual requirement and developing technology accordingly.
As the market matures, I expect customers to place greater emphasis on the outcome rather than the specifications of the aircraft alone. They will want to know whether a drone can help them monitor an area more effectively, complete an inspection faster or respond to an incident with better information.
The aircraft will remain at the centre of this ecosystem, but it will be one part of a much larger solution. The companies that understand this shift early and invest in the right capabilities will be better positioned for the industry's next phase of growth.
Ultimately, the future of drones will not be determined only by how far they can fly or how long they can stay in the air but it will depend on how effectively every flight can be translated into intelligence, action and measurable value for the customer.
(Vipul Joshi is the CFO at ideaForge, an Indian aerospace and defense company)

articles.title: Kioxia Announces GP2 Series SSD with Over 18 Million Random Read IOPS
articles.text:
Kioxia is introducing the GP2 Series SSD, and the standout number is more than 18 million random read IOPS at a 512-byte block size. I think we actually saw a precursor to this drive a few weeks ago. 18M IOPS is nearly double the performance of the GP1 Series Kioxia showed in August at FMS. The new drive is designed for PCIe 6.0 and NVMe 2.3, and Kioxia says it is also expecting sequential read throughput of up to 28GB/s, enough to saturate a PCIe 6.0 x4 link.
Kioxia GP2 Series Launched
The GP series is designed for a specific role in AI systems. Instead of adding more expensive HBM or DRAM to a GPU system, operators can use these NAND-based drives to create a flash-based memory tier the GPU can access directly. This lets the system handle larger datasets at a lower cost. Whenever you try to replace DRAM with NAND, endurance becomes a question. At 50DWPD, the GP2 is a step above many of the common capacity-focused drives.
|  | Kioxia GP2 Series | 
|---|---|
| Interface | PCIe 6.0 / NVMe 2.3 | 
| Flash Memory | Kioxia XL-FLASH generation 3 | 
| Random Read Performance | More than 18 million IOPS at 512-byte block size | 
| Expected Sequential Read Throughput | Up to 28 GB/s | 
| Endurance | Up to 50 DWPD | 
| Form Factors Under Consideration | E1.S 9.5 mm and E3.S | 
| Cooling | Direct liquid cooling support | 
Kioxia is using its XL-FLASH generation 3 memory in the GP2. The company says this low-latency flash is better suited for the fine-grained data access needed for memory expansion than typical TLC-based SSDs. Kioxia also claims XL-FLASH generation 3 provides higher endurance and about 2.5x the IOPS of its own TLC-based CM10 Series SSDs at a 512-byte block size.
Kioxia previewed its next-generation GP series at OCP Summit 2026 in the demo above, with a 20M IOPS system running live. The company says future generations will target up to 100 million random read IOPS, but we are not there just yet.
Final Words
Kioxia says evaluation GP2 samples will be available to select customers by the end of 2027, so this seems a bit further out. We are starting to see more PCIe Gen6 systems, as you may have seen in our recent AMD EPYC 9006 Results Are Here and AMD Delivers a Knockout Part Deux piece, where we had both AMD and NVIDIA PCIe Gen6 systems. Hopefully, we will get to try these out when they ship.
Of course, happy Thanksgiving to those in the US.

articles.title: GTA 6 : un patch débloque les 30 images par seconde sur PS5 jailbreakée
articles.text:
GTA 6 tourne à 30 images par seconde (FPS) sur toutes les consoles, PS5 Pro comprise. Le studio a ensuite exclu tout mode 40 ou 60 FPS sur ces machines. En premier lieu, c’est un bug sur Xbox Series qui a permi de dépasser les 30 FPS. Aujourd’hui, ce sont les PS5 qui font sauter le verrou, mais avec l’inconvénient de devoir posséder un modèle jailbreaké, c’est-à-dire débridé pour lancer du code que Sony n’a pas autorisé.
Le 26 novembre, un utilisateur baptisé a_Criminai a publié sur le forum Reddit PS5_Jailbreak un patch non officiel qui permet de dépasser les 30 FPS sur les versions PS5 de GTA 6.
Le message a depuis été supprimé par la modération, mais les vidéos ont eu le temps de circuler. Malgré le nom affiché à l’écran (« PS5 Pro 60 FPS Patch »), l’auteur reconnaît que son outil se contente de relever le plafond, sans atteindre un 60 FPS stable.
Black Friday : la TV Samsung Micro RGB 65″ R95H perd 1 000 € et s’affiche à 1 999 € au lieu de 2 999 €, du 21 au 30 novembre. Grâce à sa technologie Micro RGB, il délivre « un niveau de précision et de richesse colorimétrique inédit ».
    Pour aller plus loin
GTA 6 : les réglages graphiques cachés sur PS5, PS5 Pro et Xbox ont fuité
            
Ce nouveau plafond correspond à la moitié de la fréquence de rafraîchissement de l’écran. Il faut donc une télé ou un moniteur 120 Hz pour viser 60 FPS. Sur une télé 60 Hz classique, on reste à 30 FPS comme avant.
Surtout, le patch évite le piège dans lequel sont tombés les joueurs Xbox. Sur Xbox Series, le bug de la fonction Quick Resume fait lui aussi sauter la limite, mais la vitesse du jeu s’emballe en même temps. Rockstar a en effet lié le delta time, le temps écoulé entre deux images qui sert à faire avancer la simulation, à la cadence d’affichage. À 60 FPS, les animations tournent environ deux fois plus vite. Le patch PS5 corrige ce calcul. C’est un comble, mais contrairement au jeu original, sur la scène officieuse, le Plays Best on PS5 vanté par Rockstar n’est pas usurpé.
Environ 45 FPS sur PS5 Pro, des chutes vers 25 FPS sur PS5
Les vidéos du patch ont été capturées sur PS5 Pro. Le site Twisted Voxel les a passées dans ses outils d’analyse et mesure une moyenne d’environ 45 FPS, avec une marge d’erreur. Le jeu dépasse 50 FPS par moments, et ça sans génération d’images. On n’atteint donc pas le 60 FPS rêvé, mais 45 FPS, c’est tout de même 50 % d’images en plus que les 30 FPS officiels.
La PS5 standard s’en sort moins bien. Dans les scènes chargées, notamment pendant les explosions, elle redescend vers 25 FPS, comme en mode natif. Digital Foundry avait relevé des chutes un peu au-dessus de 20 FPS lors des longues séquences d’explosions. Pour la PS5 normale, faire sauter la limite imposée par Rockstar ne sert donc pas à grand-chose.
Le processeur, la limite que Rockstar avait annoncée
Ces mesures collent à ce que Rockstar disait juste avant la sortie. Dans un entretien à Kotaku, Marc Chambers, directeur de la production technique du studio, expliquait que le processeur de la PS5 Pro, à peine plus rapide que celui de la PS5, n’est « pas assez puissant pour faire tourner la simulation complexe du jeu à des fréquences d’images plus élevées ». Rockstar a donc préféré mettre la puce graphique améliorée de la Pro au service de l’image : elle ajoute des ombres en ray tracing et le PSSR.
Les réglages extraits des fichiers du jeu laissent une marge à la Pro pour sacrifier un peu de qualité visuelle contre quelques images en plus. En revanche, baisser les graphismes ne règle pas forcément les ralentissements si c’est le processeur qui coince. Bref, les 45 FPS de la Pro prouvent qu’elle a un peu de réserve, sans qu’un mode 60 FPS stable soit à portée d’un simple réglage.

articles.title: Avengers Doomsday : pourquoi la communication de Marvel tourne au fiasco à quelques semaines de la sortie
articles.text:
Entre bandes-annonces jugées vides, direction artistique sans relief et discours officiel peu crédible, Marvel Studios donne l’impression de patiner au moment de vendre son prochain grand événement, Avengers: Doomsday.
À moins d’un mois de sa sortie en salles, fixée au mercredi 16 décembre 2026 en France (le 18 aux États-Unis), la promotion menée par Disney et Marvel Studios tourne à vide, et une partie des fans le fait savoir sur les réseaux sociaux et les forums spécialisés. Le film doit incarner le grand sursaut créatif de la franchise après plusieurs années en demi-teinte. Sa promotion, lourde et répétitive, peine pourtant à retrouver la ferveur qui accompagnait les grandes réunions super-héroïques du studio.
Des bandes-annonces sans direction artistique et des ficelles usées jusqu’à la corde pour Avengers: Doomsday ?
Sur les réseaux sociaux, une partie des fans accueille fraîchement les bandes-annonces de Avengers Doomsday et les derniers extraits dévoilés. Le montage des bandes-annonces recycle en boucle les mêmes plans et ne dévoile jamais de vraie proposition visuelle. Les images paraissent ternes et génériques, comme assemblées à la chaîne, loin d’un spectacle pensé pour le grand écran.
La bande-annonce finale, mise en ligne en début de semaine, a pourtant été vue 563 millions de fois en 24 heures, selon Deadline. C’est un record pour Disney, devant la première bande-annonce du film (503 millions), et le deuxième meilleur score de l’histoire derrière celle de Spider-Man: Brand New Day (718,6 millions). Ces vues mesurent la curiosité du public, sans dire s’il adhère aux images.
Pour masquer le manque de substance de ces images, le marketing s’appuie sur les réflexes les plus convenus de la maison : quelques notes du célèbre thème musical des Avengers lancées pour réveiller mécaniquement la nostalgie, et des apparitions calibrées pour faire parler immédiatement, à l’image d’un Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) en simple t-shirt qui laisse les spectateurs perplexes. À ce stade, deux hypothèses alimentent les discussions chez les fans : soit Marvel Studios verrouille tellement ses secrets que ses bandes-annonces en deviennent totalement creuses et trompeuses, soit le film souffre réellement d’un manque d’inspiration inquiétant.
Un discours officiel qui sonne faux
Les déclarations des dirigeants et des équipes créatives n’arrangent rien. Depuis plusieurs mois, les prises de parole se succèdent pour assurer que l’intrigue actuelle et le retour de figures historiques faisaient partie d’un plan mûrement réfléchi. La dernière en date vient de Kevin Feige, patron de Marvel Studios, qui affirme dans un entretien au magazine Empire que la bascule vers Doctor Doom était prévue de longue date, avant même l’abandon de Kang. Ce récit officiel a du mal à convaincre, car les changements de cap du studio se sont faits au grand jour. Marvel avait annoncé Avengers: The Kang Dynasty en juillet 2022, avec le Kang de Jonathan Majors en grand méchant, avant de le remplacer en juillet 2024 par Avengers: Doomsday et le Doctor Doom de Robert Downey Jr., après le licenciement de Jonathan Majors.
À force de réécrire l’histoire pour afficher une maîtrise totale, Marvel Studios obtient l’effet inverse. Le studio paraît sur la défensive, surjoue la confiance et multiplie les extraits interchangeables. Les préventes montrent que la marque Avengers remplit encore les salles avant même la sortie.

articles.title: GTA VI developers vote against unionization
articles.text:
Workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB) said that Rockstar workers in the union will continue organizing even without formal recognition.
GTA VI developers vote against unionization
Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.
Voting ran from November 12th through 26th, covering the launch of GTA VI. If successful, the vote would have established a formal framework for collective negotiation with the studio over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, and pensions, along with a right to consultation over future changes including AI implementation and layoffs. Without it, Rockstar won’t have an obligation to meet union representatives, though workers and union members can still lobby for change informally.
“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” IWGB said in a statement sent to The Verge. “Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.”
When Rockstar fired 31 IWGB members last year, the union accused it of “the most blatant and ruthless act of union busting in the history of the games industry.” That case has gone to a UK employment tribunal, with a judgment still pending.
“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg News. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”

articles.title: PlayStation Plus dará gratis un juego de Dragon Ball y otros dos títulos
articles.text:
Los suscriptores de PlayStation Plus podrán descargar gratis tres videojuegos a partir del 1 de diciembre de 2026, entre ellos una popular entrega de la franquicia Dragon Ball. La nueva selección de Sony también incluye una colección de skateboarding y una aventura de terror psicológico, disponibles para los usuarios de PS4 y PS5 sin importar el nivel de suscripción que tengan contratado.
La promoción estará vigente hasta el 4 de enero de 2027 y forma parte de los juegos mensuales que la compañía ofrece a los miembros de su servicio. Los títulos anunciados son Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 y Amnesia: The Bunker.
Los tres videojuegos podrán reclamarse sin costo adicional para quienes tengan una membresía activa de PS Plus Essential, Extra o Premium (Deluxe). Una vez añadidos a la biblioteca durante el período de la promoción, los usuarios podrán seguir jugándolos mientras mantengan activa su suscripción.
Cuáles son los tres juegos gratis de PlayStation Plus en diciembre
La selección de diciembre reúne propuestas de distintos géneros. El título de Dragon Ball destaca por su sistema de combate y su historia ambientada en el universo creado por Akira Toriyama, mientras que las otras dos opciones ofrecen experiencias centradas en el deporte y el terror.
Estos son los videojuegos que estarán disponibles:
- Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 (PS4 y PS5): un RPG de acción y lucha que permite crear un personaje propio y participar en una historia original dentro del universo de Dragon Ball.
- Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 – Cross-Gen Edition (PS4 y PS5): una colección remasterizada que reúne dos entregas de la reconocida franquicia de skateboarding.
- Amnesia: The Bunker (PS4): un videojuego de terror psicológico en el que los jugadores deben sobrevivir a una criatura que los persigue dentro de un búnker durante la Primera Guerra Mundial.
La promoción comenzará el 1 de diciembre y finalizará el 4 de enero de 2027. Por ello, los suscriptores tendrán poco más de un mes para reclamar los tres títulos y agregarlos a sus bibliotecas digitales.
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 celebra diez años con nuevo contenido
De los tres videojuegos anunciados, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 es probablemente el que más interés despertará entre los seguidores de la franquicia japonesa. Desarrollado por Dimps y publicado por Bandai Namco, llegó al mercado en 2016 y, desde entonces, recibió numerosas actualizaciones y expansiones.
El título propone una aventura de acción y rol en la que los jugadores pueden crear su propio guerrero y participar en combates inspirados en diferentes momentos de la historia de Dragon Ball. Su argumento gira alrededor de las alteraciones en la línea temporal, por lo que los personajes deben intervenir para evitar que acontecimientos importantes del universo cambien.
Durante sus diez años de existencia, el videojuego incorporó nuevos luchadores, escenarios, misiones y habilidades. Sin embargo, quienes lo reclamen mediante PlayStation Plus recibirán la edición básica, por lo que el contenido adicional disponible a través de expansiones deberá adquirirse por separado.
Además, el juego recibió contenido especial por su décimo aniversario, mientras que los seguidores de la saga esperan Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, cuya llegada está prevista para la segunda mitad de 2027.
Tony Hawk y Amnesia completan los regalos de diciembre
La segunda propuesta es Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, una colección que recupera dos entregas clásicas de la serie de skateboarding. El videojuego incluye pistas, desafíos y personajes de ambas versiones, con gráficos renovados y mecánicas adaptadas a las plataformas actuales.
Por su parte, Amnesia: The Bunker ofrece una experiencia completamente diferente. Lanzado en 2023 por Frictional Games, el título sigue al soldado francés Henri Clément, quien queda atrapado en una instalación militar durante la Primera Guerra Mundial.
El jugador debe explorar el lugar, administrar recursos y evitar a una criatura que representa una amenaza constante. Su propuesta combina exploración, supervivencia y terror psicológico, con situaciones que cambian según las decisiones tomadas durante la partida.
Qué otros juegos llegarán al catálogo de PlayStation Plus
Los regalos mensuales no serán las únicas novedades del servicio durante diciembre. Sony también confirmó que Dynasty Warriors: Origins se incorporará al catálogo de PS Plus Extra y Premium (Deluxe).
Asimismo, el catálogo de clásicos recibirá Ratchet & Clank, la primera entrega de la popular franquicia desarrollada por Insomniac Games.
Mientras se anuncian las próximas incorporaciones, los suscriptores todavía podrán reclamar los juegos de noviembre: Dead Island 2, Monster Train 2 y Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered. Estos títulos estarán disponibles hasta el 30 de noviembre de 2026.

articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le boîtier multimédia Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS à 37,99 € (-29%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS passe à 37,99 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 29 % et 12,53 € d'économie. Pratique pour profiter d'une couverture HDR complète et du Dolby Atmos sur son téléviseur, cette clé HDMI affiche une note actuelle de 3,5/5 selon nos tests.
Amazon fait évoluer sa clé HDMI avec l'Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS, pensée pour transformer n'importe quel écran en téléviseur connecté. Ce modèle ajuste la recette précédente par petites touches pour apporter du streaming 4K à la maison. L'appareil avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage aux tests.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS descend à 37,99 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.com, soit environ 29 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (50,52 €). Cette baisse de prix qui permet d'économiser 12,53 € constitue une opportunité financière marquée.
Une mise à niveau technique centrée sur l'image et le réseau
Ce boîtier TV modernise sa formule matérielle en intégrant le Wi-Fi 6 et un processeur plus rapide pour fluidifier la navigation dans les menus. Comme le détaille notre test complet, l'équipement prend en charge l'ensemble des formats HDR actuels (Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10+ et HLG) ainsi que le son Dolby Atmos pour assurer une diffusion audiovisuelle optimale sur un téléviseur compatible. Il gère également le service Xbox Cloud Gaming pour jouer en streaming directement depuis la clé.
Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS
Points forts
- Wifi 6 sans hausse de prix.
- Couverture HDR complète (Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10+, HLG) et Dolby Atmos.
- Processeur plus rapide.
- Support du Xbox Cloud Gaming et de la recherche par description.
Points faibles
- Mirroring ultra-limité avec uniquement Miracast (ni AirPlay ni Google Cast).
- Port micro-USB plutôt qu'USB-C.
- Wifi 6 réservé au 4K Max.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Quelques concessions techniques sur la connectique et la recopie
L'Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS, actuellement noté 3,5/5 par nos services, conserve néanmoins des limites techniques issues de sa conception d'entrée de gamme. L'appareil utilise toujours une connectique d'alimentation en micro-USB plutôt qu'un port USB-C plus moderne. De plus, les fonctions de recopie vidéo se limitent au protocole Miracast, faisant l'impasse sur AirPlay et Google Cast, ce qui complique l'affichage direct de l'écran d'un smartphone récent. La clé reste adaptée pour qui cherche avant tout une solution simple de visionnage pour ses applications de streaming.
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2023) : l'autre option face au Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS
Dans la même gamme, l'Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2023) mise sur une puissance accrue avec un processeur plus performant, un stockage plus étendu et la compatibilité avec le Wi-Fi 6E. Elle permet des flux réseau plus rapides et une réactivité supérieure pour la lecture multimédia, tout en partageant avec le modèle de base une interface riche en contenus sponsorisés.
L'Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2023) coûte 15,00 € de plus que l'Amazon Fire TV stick 4K PLUS à son tarif remisé, mais les deux appareils partagent une note actuelle identique de 3,5/5.
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2023)
Points forts
- Une version 4K Max plus performante.
- Support du wifi 6E tribande.
- Prise en charge multi-HDR et Dolby Atmos.
- Intégration d'Alexa avec l'écosystème Amazon.
- Une interface fluide et simple.
Points faibles

- Connecteur micro-USB seulement.
- Télécommande non rétroéclairée.

articles.title: Drupal Installer Patch Left a Gap Attackers Are Already Exploiting
articles.text:
Drupal says last week’s patch for an exploited installer vulnerability did not protect every website, and attackers are now leveraging the gap to hack vulnerable sites.
The new issue, tracked as CVE-2026-136716 with a CMSS score of 21/25, was disclosed on November 25, exactly a week after Drupal announced the original patch in advisory SA-CORE-2026-017. Drupal describes the new flaw as an access bypass issue that can lead to site takeover.
The update released on November 18 patched CVE-2026-132165, an installer flaw credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner. The affected installer ships with Drupal core and enables users to set up a new site.
Drupal was informed of in-the-wild exploitation soon after, and CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog on November 24.
The advisory for CVE-2026-136716 explains where the earlier fix fell short.
“SA-CORE-2026-017 recently fixed several vulnerabilities within the Drupal core installer. However, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover following that advisory, including production sites,” Drupal said in its advisory.
It added, “It is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state, and sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state.”
Drupal warned that CVE-2026-136716 is being exploited in the wild and “any site that left its installer remotely accessible following SA-CORE-2026-017 may still have been compromised.”
Websites where the installer had already been secured are not vulnerable to attacks. Patches are included in versions 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23. Affected production sites must run an update hook after upgrading to fully address the vulnerability.
Drupal has not shared any information on the attacks, and it’s unclear who is responsible for the exploitation. Users have been advised to check logs for signs of compromise.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.text:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.
The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.
Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult
Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.
This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.
"In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," says Egues.
To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.
The term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.
Although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.
"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.
A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal
The proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.
Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.
These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.
"In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.
The key to the new approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.
The researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.
Crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.
"It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.
How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information
To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.
One common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.
The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.
According to the new research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.
"Our study showed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.
This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.
A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage
Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.
Ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect."
The researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.
"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," says Egues.
This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.
That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.
Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor
The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.
Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.
Whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.
The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.
Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.
"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small."
The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially important. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.
Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance
In quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.
This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.
The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.
"Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.
The approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.
This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.
Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy
To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.
These calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.
The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.
According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.
The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.
However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.
Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?
Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.
The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.
What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.
"All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.
This makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain important challenges.
The research offers two potentially significant advances.
From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.
From a technological perspective, the study shows how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.
If future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.
More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo. Original written by José Tadeu Arantes. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, Yugui Yao. Andreev qubit readout from dynamic interference supercurrent. Physical Review B, 2026; 114 (8) DOI: 10.1103/6gkt-hghj

articles.title: Microsoft ruft Code Red aus: Nach IT-Ausfall sollen Fehler schneller behoben werden
articles.text:
Alarm nach globalem IT-Ausfall: Microsoft ruft intern Code Red aus
Mitte November 2026 sorgte eine massive IT-Panne dafür, dass Nutzer:innen und Firmen weltweit rund 24 Stunden lang nicht auf Microsoft-Dienste wie Outlook, Teams oder Copilot zugreifen konnten. Laut Microsoft-365-Manager Jason Henderson handelte es sich zudem um den folgenschwersten Ausfall der Cloud-E-Mail-Lösung Exchange Online.
Ursache für Mega-Microsoft-Panne
Noch nie seien so viele Kund:innen so lange ohne E-Mail-Zugang gewesen, schrieb Henderson in einem internen Memo, das Reuters vorliegt. Die Ursache für den Ausfall sieht Microsoft in einem Programmfehler, der seit Juli 2026 unentdeckt im System geschlummert haben soll. Aber warum hat es so lange gedauert, die Dienste wieder zum Laufen zu bringen?
Internen Dokumenten nach hätten sich die Microsoft-Ingenieur:innen durch eine Art „Nebel des Krieges“ kämpfen müssen, wie Vice President Amanda Silver klagte. Die für die Behebung der Schäden eingesetzten Mitarbeiter:innen hätten in elf verschiedenen Team-Chats mehr als 11.000 Nachrichten ausgetauscht, wie es bei Reuters heißt.
Mitarbeiter verlieren den Überblick
Dabei sei es schwergefallen, den Überblick zu behalten. Die Diagnosedaten seien über verschiedene interne Systeme verstreut gewesen. Dadurch soll über einen längeren Zeitraum ein gemeinsamer Überblick über mögliche Ursachen gefehlt haben. Auch schon getroffene Entscheidungen sollen nicht bei allen angekommen sein.
Mithilfe des jetzt ausgerufenen Code Red will Microsoft die technischen Abläufe und die interne Reaktion auf größere Störungen optimieren. Ziel ist es, künftige weitere weltweite Störungen innerhalb von einer Stunde zu beheben.
KI-Agenten sollen Daten schneller auswerten
Dabei sollen unter anderem KI-Agenten zum Einsatz kommen. Diese sollen technische Daten schneller auswerten und Fehlerquellen erkennen. In täglichen oder wöchentlichen Besprechungen sollen entsprechende Fortschritte kontrolliert werden, wie heute.at berichtet.
Weiterhin will Microsoft auch die Geschwindigkeit bei der Verteilung von Softwareupdates erhöhen. In anderen Fällen habe ein entsprechender Patch schon einmal fünf bis sechs Tage bis zum weltweiten Rollout gebraucht, wie es intern heißt. Künftig sollen besonders dringende Sicherheitsprobleme ebenfalls innerhalb einer Stunde adressiert sein.
„Mitarbeiter verlieren den Überblick“ ach nur die Männlichen?
) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code
articles.text:
Password management and identity security company 1Password revealed on Wednesday that a hacker stole customer information and proprietary source code. 1Password says customer vaults are not affected.
The company launched an investigation on November 19 after discovering that an employee’s corporate GitHub account may have been compromised.
The attacker used the account to deploy malicious code to backend services and exfiltrate customer records. The compromised customer records include names, email addresses, account identifiers, public cryptographic keys, authentication parameters, account activity times, and non-secret metadata.
In addition, the threat actor obtained source code from private repositories and accessed the company’s CI/CD system, potentially exposing infrastructure credentials.
According to 1Password, the hacker also obtained tokens from emails sent to users for account invitations, provisioning, and recovery.
A “small number” of individuals who were undergoing provisioning or recovery during the intrusion have been notified. However, the company noted that the exposed tokens cannot be exploited on their own and there is no evidence that the attacker hijacked user accounts.
A 1Password representative noted on the company’s community forum that the stolen authentication data included Secure Remote Password verifiers derived from user account passwords and Secret Keys. The verifiers cannot be used directly for authentication, and brute-forcing account passwords would require the associated Secret Keys, which 1Password does not store.
1Password highlighted that customer vaults and the cryptographic keys protecting them were not compromised. “We have no evidence that encrypted vaults were downloaded or accessed,” a 1Password community manager said.
The breach also does not impact client applications, browser extensions, and account recovery keys.
It’s unclear how many users are affected and how the hacker gained initial access to the corporate GitHub account.
In response to the intrusion, 1Password disabled the compromised GitHub account, invalidated a stolen token, replaced potentially compromised infrastructure credentials, and restored clean versions of affected services.
The company said its investigation, conducted with independent cybersecurity experts, is still ongoing. Customers do not need to take any action, but have been advised to watch for phishing attacks that could exploit news of the incident.

The Gamers Behind the Cloud

After years helping moderate the community’s Reddit and Discord spaces, Hamza went from an aging laptop to cloud gaming across a TV, phone, tablet and desktop: “I’m genuinely thankful not just for the technology that keeps me gaming effortlessly wherever I am, but for the amazing community and friendships I’ve built along the way, and I look forward to what the future holds for cloud gaming.”
GeForce NOW kept new releases within reach for moderator Flacz, without needing frequent hardware upgrades: “GeForce NOW allowed me to enjoy games and adventures I’ve never imagined to be possible and it continues to be a part of my daily gaming experience till this day.”

Freedom to play and create resonates with Nads: “Being able to jump into my favorite games in an instant without worrying about downloads, storage limits or constant hardware upgrades feels like magic … Being able to play my game and stream on YouTube at the same time is something I never could have imagined before.”
Nigiri21Sushi also turns to the cloud when games stretch a local PC: “As a gaming content-creator, my current PC sometimes struggles showcasing new-release games that are CPU/GPU-intensive … Hence, huge thank you to GFN for allowing me to produce fluid content via cloud-gaming.”
For Marchief, demanding games on Steam Deck are the draw: “I’m thankful that GeForce NOW allows me to play the top AAA games on the Steam Deck … Having the power of an RTX 5080 in a handheld is just absolutely mindblowing.”
Markys enjoys the comfort of the couch with his favorite game, World of Warcraft: Forever: “No high-end gaming PC needed, just my controller, my TV and the freedom to play wherever I want.”
Anytime Anywhere Gaming shared a video that shared why GeForce NOW is “really fantastic in a whole lot of ways.”
Keep the conversation going on the community-run GeForce NOW Reddit and Discord.
